verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते । ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥
verses.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
verses.line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
verses.misuse: Not 'stop caring how things turn out'. Peace comes from releasing the grip, not from indifference.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verses.sanskrit_display: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥
verses.translation: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, even in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,
verses.line: Hate no one. Be friendly and kind, free of 'mine' and ego, steady in pain and joy, and forgiving.
verses.misuse: Forgiving is not excusing harm or staying in danger; you can forgive and still keep your distance.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
verses.translation: One from whom the world does not shrink and who does not shrink from the world, who is free from elation, impatience, fear and agitation, is dear to me.
verses.line: Unsettle no one, be unsettled by no one, free of elation, resentment, fear and agitation.
verses.misuse: Not disturbing others doesn't mean never disagreeing; it means not causing needless harm.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verses.sanskrit_display: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥
verses.translation: One who is the same to enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, and free from attachment,
verses.line: The same to friend and foe, in respect and insult, heat and cold, pleasure and pain.
verses.misuse: Being the same in insult doesn't mean tolerating abuse; it means your worth isn't decided by it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
verses.translation: to whom blame and praise are equal, who is silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to me.
verses.line: Praise and blame weigh the same. Quiet, content with what comes, rooted in steadiness, not status.
verses.misuse: Not 'never ask for credit'. You can advocate for yourself without letting praise or blame define you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna names the three gates to self-ruin and how to live instead.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
verses.translation: Threefold is the gate of hell that destroys the self: desire, anger and greed. Therefore one should give up these three.
verses.line: Desire, anger and greed: three gates to self-ruin. Close all three.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verses.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verses.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verses.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks about faith outside the rules; Krishna explains faith follows nature.
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत । श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
verses.translation: Everyone's faith follows their nature, Bharata. A person is made of faith; as a person's faith is, so is that person.
verses.line: You are made of what you deeply believe. As your faith is, so are you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
verses.translation: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
verses.line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥
verses.translation: That which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from the clarity of one's own understanding, is called sattvic happiness.
verses.line: Some joy tastes like poison at first and like nectar in the end. That joy is worth it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
verses.translation: The happiness that comes from contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is called rajasic.
verses.line: Some pleasure tastes like nectar at first and poison in the end. Know which kind you're choosing.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verses.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verses.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verses.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verses.translation: Thus I have declared to you this knowledge, more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
verses.line: I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज । अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
verses.translation: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.
verses.line: Lean on me alone. I will free you from every wrong. Don't worry.
verses.misuse: This is not 'do nothing' or 'ignore your duties'. Krishna says it to a man about to act; it lifts fear, not responsibility.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचअशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे । गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.
verses.line: You grieve for what doesn't need your grief, while talking like you know better.
verses.misuse: Not 'don't cry' or 'your grief is wrong'. It opens a teaching on what in us does not die; grief still deserves time.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
verses.translation: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes on to another body. The steady person is not bewildered by this.
verses.line: Childhood, youth, old age: the body keeps changing. The wise aren't thrown by the next change.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः । आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥
verses.translation: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
verses.line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
verses.misuse: Bearing passing discomfort is not putting up with harm or abuse; those are not weather to wait out.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणोन हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
verses.translation: It is never born and never dies; having been, it will not cease to be. Unborn, eternal, constant and ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain.
verses.line: The self was never born and never dies. It is not killed when the body is.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to skip mourning or to take loss lightly; it is comfort about what remains.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहायनवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि । तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
verses.translation: Just as a person casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so the embodied self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.
verses.line: As we drop worn-out clothes and put on new ones, the self leaves a worn body for a new one.
verses.misuse: Not a way to brush off someone else's grief with 'they've just changed clothes'.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च । तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.translation: Death is certain for the one who is born, and birth is certain for the one who dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
verses.line: Whatever is born will die, and what dies is born again. Don't torment yourself over the unavoidable.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to stop caring for the sick or to rush someone's mourning.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna reminds Arjuna of his duty as a warrior and what retreat would cost him.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verses.translation: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, then engage in the fight. Done this way, you will incur no wrong.
verses.line: Hold pleasure and pain, gain and loss, win and defeat as equal. Then step in and act.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verses.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verses.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verses.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verses.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verses.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
verses.translation: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
verses.line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
verses.misuse: Even in success and failure doesn't mean indifferent to them; learn from both without being thrown.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
verses.translation: One joined to this understanding casts off both good and bad results here. So devote yourself to yoga; yoga is skill in action.
verses.line: Yoga is skill in action: doing the work well, without being bound by it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः । वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: One whose mind is not shaken by sorrow, who has no craving for pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.
verses.line: Unshaken in sorrow, not craving in joy, free of clinging, fear and anger: that is a steady mind.
verses.misuse: A steady mind still feels; it just isn't run by sorrow, fear or anger.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
verses.translation: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on every side, a person withdraws the senses from their objects, his wisdom is firmly set.
verses.line: Like a tortoise pulling in its limbs, draw your senses back from what pulls at them.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
verses.translation: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
verses.line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
verses.translation: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the ruin of understanding; and with understanding ruined, a person is lost.
verses.line: Anger clouds judgement, clouded judgement loses memory, lost memory wrecks reason, and then you fall.
verses.misuse: Not 'never feel anger'. It warns about anger that takes over judgement, not about naming wrongs.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
verses.translation: For the undisciplined there is no understanding and no steady contemplation. Without contemplation there is no peace, and for the one without peace, where is happiness?
verses.line: Without inner discipline there's no clarity; without clarity, no peace; and without peace, where is happiness?

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verses.sanskrit_display: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
verses.translation: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
verses.line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठंसमुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वेस शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
verses.translation: As waters enter the ocean, which is ever being filled yet stays unmoved within its shores, so the one into whom all desires enter in the same way finds peace, not the one who craves desires.
verses.line: Rivers pour into the ocean and it stays full and still. Let desires enter you the same way.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
verses.translation: Whatever a great person does, others do the same. Whatever standard that person sets, the world follows.
verses.line: Whatever a respected person does, others copy. The standard you set is the one people follow.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verses.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verses.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verses.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion; all-devouring and greatly harmful. Know this to be the enemy here.
verses.line: It's desire, which turns into anger when blocked. Never satisfied, it is the real enemy here.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verses.sanskrit_display: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
verses.translation: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
verses.line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
verses.translation: In whatever way people approach me, in that same way I receive them. People follow my path in every way, Partha.
verses.line: However people come to me, I meet them there. Every path, in its own way, leads to me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
verses.translation: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
verses.line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verses.sanskrit_display: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
verses.translation: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
verses.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
verses.translation: The person of faith, devoted to it and with senses controlled, gains knowledge. Having gained knowledge, he soon reaches supreme peace.
verses.line: Trust, commitment and self-control bring understanding, and understanding soon brings peace.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, Bharata, then I bring myself forth.
verses.line: Whenever goodness declines and wrong rises up, I come forth, Krishna promises.
verses.misuse: Not 'wait for rescue'. Many read it as a call to be the force that restores what is right.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verses.sanskrit_display: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः । लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
verses.translation: One who acts offering all actions to the Supreme, giving up attachment, is not touched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is not wet by water.
verses.line: Like a lotus leaf in water, do your work without letting the mess soak in.
verses.misuse: Staying unstained isn't staying silent about wrongdoing at work; you can act and still keep your peace.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verses.sanskrit_display: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥
verses.translation: The enjoyments born of contact are wombs of sorrow; they have a beginning and an end, Kaunteya. The wise do not delight in them.
verses.line: Pleasures born of contact have a beginning and an end and breed sorrow. The wise don't stake their joy there.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verses.sanskrit_display: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
verses.translation: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
verses.line: Whoever can ride out the surge of desire and anger, here and now, is steady and happy.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥
verses.translation: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who keeps awake too long, Arjuna.
verses.line: Balance isn't for those who eat too much or too little, or sleep too much or too little.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
verses.translation: For one who is moderate in food and recreation, measured in effort at work, moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
verses.line: Moderate in food and rest, in work and play, in sleep and waking: that's how sorrow eases.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
verses.translation: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker: that is the image used for the yogi of controlled mind practising union with the self.
verses.line: Like a lamp in a windless place that doesn't flicker: that's a settled mind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
verses.translation: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self.
verses.line: Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
verses.translation: One who, by comparison with himself, sees the same everywhere, Arjuna, whether in pleasure or in pain, is considered the highest yogi.
verses.line: Feel others' joy and pain as if they were your own. That is the highest practice.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verses.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verses.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
verses.line: Yes, the mind is restless and hard to hold. But practice and letting go can train it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचपार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Partha, there is no ruin for him either in this world or the next. No one who does good, my friend, ever comes to grief.
verses.line: Whoever does good never comes to ruin, my friend. Not here, not after.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verses.sanskrit_display: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verses.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verses.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verses.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verses.sanskrit_display: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥
verses.translation: For one who has conquered himself, the self is the friend of the self. But for one who has not, the self acts with hostility, like an enemy.
verses.line: Master yourself and you become your own best friend. Don't, and your own mind works against you like an enemy.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verses.sanskrit_display: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
verses.translation: For one who has conquered himself and is at peace, the higher self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
verses.line: Self-mastered and calm, you stay centred in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, praise and insult.
verses.misuse: Staying steady under insult is not accepting mistreatment; you can stay calm and still speak up.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on worship for rewards and worship without desire.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
verses.translation: To those who think of me alone and worship me, ever devoted, I bring what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
verses.misuse: Not 'God will pay the bills, so don't plan'. Trust eases worry; it doesn't replace effort or prudence.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
verses.translation: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
verses.line: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: whatever is offered with love, I accept.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
verses.translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
verses.line: Even Arjuna, the finest archer alive, froze when the fight was against his own people.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
verses.sanskrit_display: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
verses.translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verses.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
verses.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.setting: Sanjaya reports to the blind king the moment Arjuna gives up before the battle.
verses.sanskrit_display: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
verses.line: Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, too overwhelmed to go on.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on devotees who find joy together and the light he gives them.
verses.sanskrit_display: तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः । नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥
verses.translation: Out of compassion for them, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
verses.line: Out of compassion, I live in their hearts and clear the darkness with the lamp of understanding.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna names the chief glories in which the divine shows itself.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful, know that it springs from a spark of my splendour.
verses.line: Whatever shines with excellence, beauty or power, see it as a spark of the divine.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna, as Time, tells Arjuna the outcome is already set and urges him to act.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्वजित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् । मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेवनिमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् ॥
verses.translation: Therefore stand up and win glory; conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me; be merely the instrument, ambidextrous archer.
verses.line: It's already set in motion. Rise and do your part; be the instrument.
verses.misuse: 'Be the instrument' is not 'I'm not responsible for what I do'. You still choose and answer for your actions.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Having seen Krishna's cosmic form, Arjuna realises how casually he treated his closest friend.
verses.sanskrit_display: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तंहे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति । अजानता महिमानं तवेदंमया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥ यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसिविहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु । एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षंतत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever I said rashly, thinking of you as a friend, 'O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend', not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or affection, and whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while at play, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in company, I ask your forgiveness for it, immeasurable one.
verses.line: I treated you casually, as just a friend, never seeing how great you were.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna, shaken by the cosmic vision, asks Krishna to forgive his years of casual familiarity.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायंप्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् । पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युःप्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥
verses.translation: So, bowing and prostrating my body, I ask your grace, adorable Lord. As a father with his son, a friend with his friend, a lover with the beloved, please bear with me.
verses.line: Bear with me as a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved.
verses.misuse: Asking for forgiveness is not demanding it; the other person still decides.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna tells Arjuna that only undivided devotion sees him.
verses.sanskrit_display: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः । निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥
verses.translation: One who works for me, holds me as the highest, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without enmity towards any being, comes to me, Pandava.
verses.line: Work for the divine, love it, drop clinging, and hold no hatred towards any being.
verses.misuse: No hatred doesn't mean no boundaries; you can wish someone no harm and still keep away.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verses.sanskrit_display: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verses.translation: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on doing work for my sake. Even by doing actions for me, you will reach perfection.
verses.line: If even practice is too hard, just do your work for my sake. That alone takes you far.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥
verses.translation: If you cannot do even this, then taking refuge in my yoga and with self restrained, give up the fruit of all actions.
verses.line: And if even that's beyond you, then simply let go of the results of what you do.
verses.misuse: Letting go of results is not giving up on goals or planning; it's releasing the anxious grip.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verses.sanskrit_display: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
verses.translation: ever content, steady in practice, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding given to me, that devotee of mine is dear to me.
verses.line: Always content, self-disciplined, firm in resolve, heart and mind given to the divine: such a person is dear to me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
verses.translation: One who expects nothing, is pure, capable, unconcerned and untroubled, who has given up all self-centred undertakings, that devotee of mine is dear to me.
verses.line: Wanting nothing extra, clean within and without, capable, unbothered, not chasing every new venture: dear to me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥
verses.translation: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has let go of both good and bad, and is full of devotion, is dear to me.
verses.line: Not swinging between thrill and hate, grief and craving, letting go of 'good' and 'bad' outcomes: dear to me.
verses.misuse: Not feeling grief is not the goal; the verse is about not being swept away by it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् । अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥
verses.translation: If you cannot fix your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me by the yoga of practice, Dhananjaya.
verses.line: If you can't keep your mind fixed yet, then reach for it through regular practice.

verses.collection: Gita 13: The Field and Its Knower
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verses.sanskrit_display: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् । विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
verses.translation: One who sees the Supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the undying within the dying, truly sees.
verses.line: Whoever sees the same undying presence in all beings, even as they perish, truly sees.

verses.collection: Gita 13: The Field and Its Knower
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verses.sanskrit_display: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् । न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
verses.translation: Seeing the Lord equally present everywhere, one does not injure the self by the self, and so reaches the highest goal.
verses.line: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, you stop wounding yourself through yourself.

verses.collection: Gita 13: The Field and Its Knower
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the body as a field, and what true knowledge consists of.
verses.sanskrit_display: अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् । आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः ॥
verses.translation: Humility, freedom from pretence, non-violence, patience, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control,
verses.line: No need for status, no pretence, no harm, patience, straightness, respect for teachers, purity, steadiness, self-control.
verses.misuse: Patience and humility aren't silence in the face of mistreatment.

verses.collection: Gita 13: The Field and Its Knower
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the body as a field, and what true knowledge consists of.
verses.sanskrit_display: इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च । जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् ॥
verses.translation: detachment from sense objects, absence of ego, and seeing clearly the pain and flaw in birth, death, old age and sickness,
verses.line: Not chasing pleasures, not puffed up, and clear-eyed about birth, death, old age and illness.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
verses.sanskrit_display: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
verses.translation: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving: these arise when rajas increases, best of the Bharatas.
verses.line: When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव । न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: One who does not hate clarity, activity or delusion when they arise, Pandava, nor longs for them when they cease,
verses.line: Don't hate your moods when they come, or long for them when they go.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः । तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥
verses.translation: who is the same in pain and pleasure, at home in the self, to whom a clod, a stone and gold are alike, who is the same to the pleasant and the unpleasant, steady, the same in blame and praise,
verses.line: Even in pain and pleasure, at ease in yourself; earth, stone and gold the same; praise and blame alike.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥
verses.translation: the same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, who has given up all self-driven undertakings: such a person is said to have gone beyond the qualities.
verses.line: The same in respect and disrespect, to friend and foe, letting go of the need to start everything: free.
verses.misuse: Not 'tolerate disrespect'. It means your steadiness doesn't depend on how others treat you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचअभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study, austerity and uprightness,
verses.line: Fearlessness, a clean heart, steady learning, generosity, self-control, study and straightforwardness.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
verses.sanskrit_display: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः । कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥
verses.translation: Clinging to immeasurable worries that end only at death, taking the enjoyment of desires as the highest aim, convinced that this is all,
verses.line: Clinging to worries that only end at death, they believe owning and enjoying is all there is.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
verses.sanskrit_display: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः । ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥
verses.translation: bound by hundreds of ties of hope, given over to desire and anger, they strive to amass wealth by unjust means for the enjoyment of desires.
verses.line: Tied by a hundred ropes of hope, pushed by desire and anger, they pile up wealth by any means.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
verses.sanskrit_display: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् । इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥
verses.translation: 'This I have gained today; this desire I shall fulfil. This wealth is mine, and this too shall be mine.'
verses.line: 'I got this today, I'll get that next. This is mine, and more will be mine.' The mind of more.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् । दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
verses.translation: non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, peace, absence of slander, compassion for beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness,
verses.line: No harm, truthfulness, no anger, no gossip, compassion for all, no greed, gentleness, modesty, no fidgeting.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
verses.sanskrit_display: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता । भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥
verses.translation: vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice and from excessive pride: these belong to one born with the divine nature, Bharata.
verses.line: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, no malice, no arrogance: the marks of a good nature.
verses.misuse: Forgiveness here is a strength, not an obligation to stay in harm's way.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
verses.sanskrit_display: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च । अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥
verses.translation: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to one born with the demonic nature, Partha.
verses.line: Show-off, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance: the marks of a nature heading the wrong way.
verses.misuse: A mirror for yourself, not a label to throw at others.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verses.sanskrit_display: मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः । भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint and purity of feeling: this is called austerity of the mind.
verses.line: A calm mind, gentleness, quiet, self-restraint and a clean heart: that is discipline of mind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् । क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥
verses.translation: Austerity practised to gain respect, honour and reverence, and with show, is called rajasic; it is unstable and fleeting.
verses.line: Effort made for respect, status or show is shaky and doesn't last.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verses.sanskrit_display: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे । देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
verses.translation: A gift given because it is right to give, to one who does nothing in return, at the right place and time and to a worthy person, is called sattvic.
verses.line: Give because giving is right, to someone who can't repay you, at the right time and place.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः । दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
verses.translation: But a gift given in expectation of a return, or with a view to reward, or given reluctantly, is called rajasic.
verses.line: Giving to get something back, or giving grudgingly, isn't really giving.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः । यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥
verses.translation: It is not possible for an embodied being to give up action entirely. But one who gives up the fruit of action is called a renouncer.
verses.line: No one with a body can give up action completely. Letting go of the payoff is the real renouncing.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on the five causes behind every action.
verses.sanskrit_display: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
verses.translation: The seat, the doer, the various instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fifth, providence: these are the five causes of every action.
verses.line: Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.
verses.misuse: Not 'it wasn't my fault'. You own your part; you just aren't the only cause.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
verses.translation: The doer who is undisciplined, vulgar, obstinate, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating, is called tamasic.
verses.line: Careless, crude, stubborn, deceitful, spiteful, lazy, gloomy and always putting things off: the dull kind of doer.
verses.misuse: A mirror for your own habits, not a label for anyone with depression or burnout.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये । बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
verses.translation: The understanding that knows action and withdrawal, what should and should not be done, what is to be feared and what not, bondage and freedom, that understanding is sattvic, Partha.
verses.line: Clear judgement knows when to act and when to wait, what to fear, and what frees you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verses.sanskrit_display: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
verses.translation: Each person, devoted to his own work, attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to his own work finds perfection.
verses.line: Devoted to your own work, you reach fulfilment. Here's how.
verses.misuse: Not 'stay in the job your community or birth assigned'. 'Your own work' means the work that fits your nature.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verses.sanskrit_display: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
verses.translation: By worshipping, through his own work, Him from whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.
verses.line: Doing your own work well can be your worship of the source of all life.
verses.misuse: Work as worship doesn't mean overwork or tolerating exploitation.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verses.sanskrit_display: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verses.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
verses.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
verses.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on the steadiness of one established in knowledge.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् । विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
verses.translation: Having given up ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, free from the sense of 'mine' and peaceful, one becomes fit to be one with Brahman.
verses.line: Let go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness. Without 'mine', you become peaceful.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on the steadiness of one established in knowledge.
verses.sanskrit_display: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
verses.translation: Become one with Brahman, serene in self, one neither grieves nor craves. The same to all beings, one gains supreme devotion to me.
verses.line: Serene within, they neither grieve nor crave, and treat all beings alike.
verses.misuse: Not 'don't grieve'. It describes a serenity that grows, not a rule against sorrow.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि । अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥
verses.translation: Fixing your mind on me, you will cross over all obstacles by my grace. But if out of ego you will not listen, you will perish.
verses.line: Heart turned to the divine, you'll cross every obstacle. Refuse out of ego, and you'll be lost.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
verses.translation: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
verses.line: Take refuge in the divine with all your being. By that grace you'll find supreme peace.
verses.misuse: Surrender is trust, not giving up your judgement or your effort.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna's doubts end; Sanjaya closes the dialogue.
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्जुन उवाचनष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत । स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥
verses.translation: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed and I have regained my memory through your grace, Achyuta. I stand firm, my doubts gone. I will do as you say.
verses.line: My confusion is gone, my clarity is back. I stand firm, free of doubt, and I'll act.
verses.misuse: Not blind obedience: Krishna told him to reflect and choose (18.63), and Arjuna acts from his own clarity.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् । स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
verses.translation: One who gives up work because it is painful, out of fear of bodily strain, performs rajasic renunciation and does not gain its fruit.
verses.line: Dropping a duty just because it's hard or you fear the strain isn't freedom. It gains you nothing.
verses.misuse: Not 'never quit'. Leaving for good reasons is wise; this warns against fleeing out of fear alone.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
verses.translation: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; nor will there ever be a time when all of us cease to be.
verses.line: There was never a time when you, I, or anyone here did not exist, and never will be.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
verses.translation: The steady person whom these do not disturb, who stays the same in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for immortality.
verses.line: The one who stays the same in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom.
verses.misuse: Steadiness is not numbness or hiding what you feel.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः । न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
verses.translation: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, and wind does not dry it.
verses.line: No weapon cuts it, no fire burns it, no water wets it, no wind dries it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत । अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
verses.translation: Beings are unseen in their beginning, seen in their middle, and unseen again in their end, Arjuna. What is there to lament in this?
verses.line: We come from the unseen and return to it; only the middle is visible. Why break over that?
verses.misuse: Grief is natural; the verse widens the frame, it doesn't forbid tears.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
verses.translation: Do not give in to this unmanliness, Partha; it does not become you. Throw off this petty weakness of heart and rise, scorcher of enemies.
verses.line: This smallness of heart isn't who you are. Shake it off and stand up.
verses.misuse: Not 'feelings are weakness' or 'man up'. It is a friend reminding you of your strength, said once, then explained for 700 verses.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
verses.translation: Here, Arjuna, the resolute mind is one-pointed. But the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.
verses.line: A decided mind is single and focused. An undecided mind splits into endless branches.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय । बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
verses.translation: Action done for its rewards is far inferior to action done with a steady mind. Seek refuge in that understanding; those who work only for the fruit are to be pitied.
verses.line: Working only for the payoff makes you poor inside. Take shelter in clear understanding.
verses.misuse: Not 'ambition is wrong'. It's about not letting rewards be the only reason you work.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verses.translation: When your understanding, now confused by conflicting things you have heard, stands firm and unmoving in deep stillness, then you will attain yoga.
verses.line: Pulled by conflicting advice, the mind wobbles. When it settles and stays still, you've arrived.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान् । आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: When a person gives up all the desires of the mind and is content in the self by the self, then he is called one of steady wisdom.
verses.line: When you stop chasing every desire and find contentment within yourself, your wisdom becomes steady.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् । नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
verses.translation: One who is without attachment anywhere, who neither rejoices on meeting good nor hates on meeting bad, has wisdom that is firmly set.
verses.line: Good news doesn't inflate them, bad news doesn't embitter them. That's steady wisdom.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verses.sanskrit_display: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयोयद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
verses.translation: Nor do we know which is better for us, to fight or not, or whether we will win or they will. The very people after whose death we would not wish to live stand facing us.
verses.line: I can't tell which is better, or even what winning would look like.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
verses.translation: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is striving, Arjuna.
verses.line: Even a wise, striving person can be dragged off by restless senses. Don't be surprised; be ready.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् । आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥
verses.translation: But a disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, attains clarity and calm.
verses.line: Move through the world with your senses in hand, free of grabbing and pushing away, and you find calm.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
verses.translation: When the mind runs after the roving senses, it carries away one's understanding, as the wind carries a boat away on the water.
verses.line: When the mind chases a wandering sense, it is swept off like a boat in the wind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति ॥
verses.translation: The person who gives up all desires and moves about free from longing, without the sense of 'mine' and without ego, attains peace.
verses.line: Drop the cravings, the sense of 'mine' and the 'I' that keeps score. That's where peace is.
verses.misuse: Dropping 'mine' is about possessiveness, not about loving your people less.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
verses.translation: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
verses.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verses.sanskrit_display: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
verses.translation: With these seemingly mixed words you confuse my mind. Tell me decisively that one thing by which I may reach the highest good.
verses.line: Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
verses.translation: Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. And looking to the welfare of the world, you too should act.
verses.line: Janaka and others reached fulfilment through action. Keep working, if only for the good of the world.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन । नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
verses.translation: There is nothing in the three worlds, Partha, that I must do, nothing unattained that I need to attain, and yet I continue to act.
verses.line: I have nothing left to gain anywhere, Krishna says, and still I keep working.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verses.sanskrit_display: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् । जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन् ॥
verses.translation: The wise should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action. Working steadily themselves, they should encourage others in all their work.
verses.line: Don't unsettle people who are still learning by doing. Do the work well alongside them and show them.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥
verses.translation: All actions are done by the qualities of nature, but the one deluded by ego thinks, 'I am the doer.'
verses.line: Countless forces do the work; the ego, fooled, says 'I did it all'.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verses.sanskrit_display: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा । निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
verses.translation: Surrendering all actions to me, with your mind on the inner self, free from hope and the sense of 'mine', fight with your fever gone.
verses.line: Hand your work to something higher, drop the 'mine' and the hoping, and act with the fever gone.
verses.misuse: Surrender here means letting go of anxious grasping, not handing over your judgement or responsibility.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verses.sanskrit_display: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि । प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
verses.translation: Even a wise person acts according to his own nature. Beings follow their nature; what will mere repression do?
verses.line: Even wise people move as their nature moves them. Brute suppression achieves little.
verses.misuse: Not 'I can't change, it's my nature'. The next verse says not to come under the sway of likes and dislikes.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verses.sanskrit_display: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ । तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
verses.translation: Attraction and aversion to sense objects lie seated in every sense. Do not come under their power; they are your enemies on the way.
verses.line: Liking and disliking lie in wait behind every sense. Don't let either take the wheel.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
verses.translation: Arjuna said: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against his will, as if pushed by force?
verses.line: Why do I do the wrong thing even when I don't want to, as if something forces me?

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
verses.translation: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so is this wisdom covered by desire.
verses.line: Like smoke over fire, dust on a mirror, desire covers your clear sight.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verses.sanskrit_display: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते । न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
verses.translation: Not by refraining from action does a person reach freedom from action, nor by mere renunciation does one attain perfection.
verses.line: You don't get free by not starting, and you don't get perfect by just walking away.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना । जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
verses.translation: Thus knowing that which is higher than the intellect, steadying the self by the self, slay, mighty-armed one, this enemy in the form of desire, so hard to overcome.
verses.line: Knowing what is higher in you, steady yourself with yourself and defeat the desire that's hard to beat.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् । कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥
verses.translation: No one can remain even for a moment without doing something; everyone is made to act, helplessly, by the qualities born of nature.
verses.line: No one can stay without acting, even for a moment. Your nature keeps moving you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् । इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
verses.translation: One who restrains the organs of action but sits dwelling in the mind on sense objects is deluded and is called a hypocrite.
verses.line: Holding back your hands while your mind keeps feasting on the craving is self-deception.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥
verses.translation: Having given up attachment to the fruit of action, ever content and dependent on nothing, though fully engaged in action, he does nothing at all.
verses.line: Content and leaning on no one's approval, fully busy, and yet inwardly at rest.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna lists the many forms of offering people make.
verses.sanskrit_display: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥
verses.translation: The act of offering is Brahman, the offering is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire of Brahman. Brahman is reached by one who sees Brahman in every action.
verses.line: The offering, the giver, the fire, the act: see the sacred in all of it, and you reach the sacred.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verses.sanskrit_display: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
verses.translation: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you will cross over all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.
verses.line: Even if you were the worst wrongdoer of all, the raft of wisdom would carry you across.
verses.misuse: Not 'understanding cancels the harm done to others'; it frees you to change and make amends.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verses.sanskrit_display: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
verses.translation: The ignorant, faithless person of doubting mind perishes. For the doubting self there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
verses.line: A mind that doubts everything finds no happiness here or anywhere.
verses.misuse: Questioning is welcome in the Gita; Arjuna asks constantly. This is about corrosive doubt that blocks every step.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः । छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥
verses.translation: Therefore, cutting with the sword of knowledge this doubt in your heart born of ignorance, take refuge in yoga, and stand up, Bharata.
verses.line: Cut the doubt in your heart with clear understanding, then stand up and act.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥
verses.translation: To protect the good, to destroy wrongdoing, and to firmly establish dharma, I take birth age after age.
verses.line: To protect the good, end the harm, and set right what's broken, I appear age after age.
verses.misuse: Not a licence to punish people you judge wicked; the work of setting right belongs to the divine and to justice.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verses.sanskrit_display: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
verses.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
verses.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
verses.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verses.sanskrit_display: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
verses.translation: The wise see with an equal eye a learned and humble Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and one who eats dog-meat.
verses.line: The wise see the same self in a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verses.sanskrit_display: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
verses.translation: One should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant nor be troubled on getting what is unpleasant. Steady in understanding and undeluded, the knower of Brahman abides in Brahman.
verses.line: Don't get carried away by good news or crushed by bad. Keep your understanding steady.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verses.sanskrit_display: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
verses.translation: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
verses.line: Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, briefly describing meditation and the peace it brings.
verses.sanskrit_display: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् । सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥
verses.translation: Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all the worlds, and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
verses.line: The divine is the well-wisher of every being, you included. Knowing this, you find peace.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks whether giving up action or acting selflessly is better; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति । निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: Know him to be ever a renouncer who neither hates nor desires. Free from the pairs of opposites, mighty-armed one, he is easily released from bondage.
verses.line: The one who neither resents nor craves is the real renouncer, wherever they live.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on who is truly a renouncer.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचअनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: One who does the work that ought to be done, without depending on its fruit, is the renouncer and the yogi; not the one who gives up the sacred fire or gives up action.
verses.line: The real renouncer does the work that's needed without leaning on its rewards, not the one who quits.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥
verses.translation: Having gained it, one thinks no other gain greater; established in it, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow.
verses.line: Find the gain beyond all gains, and even heavy sorrow can't shake you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥
verses.translation: Know that to be yoga: the breaking of contact with sorrow. This yoga should be practised with determination and with an undespairing mind.
verses.line: Yoga is unhooking from sorrow. Practise it with resolve and a heart that doesn't lose hope.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
verses.translation: Little by little one should come to rest, with understanding held steady; fixing the mind on the self, one should think of nothing else.
verses.line: Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
verses.translation: One who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me: I am never lost to him, and he is never lost to me.
verses.line: See me in everything and everything in me, and I never lose you, nor you me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
