verses.sanskrit_display: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥
verses.translation: Yoga is hard to reach for one whose self is uncontrolled, in my view. But one whose self is controlled and who strives can reach it by the right means.
verses.line: Without self-control it's hard. With sincere effort and the right means, it's within reach.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
verses.translation: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
verses.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verses.sanskrit_display: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
verses.translation: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a broken cloud, without support, mighty-armed one, bewildered on the path to Brahman?
verses.line: Fallen from both sides, does he scatter like a torn cloud, with nowhere to stand?

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु । साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥
verses.translation: One who is even-minded towards well-wishers, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, relatives, the good and the wicked, excels.
verses.line: Friend, enemy, stranger, relative, saint or wrongdoer: the one who sees all with an even mind stands highest.
verses.misuse: Even-minded is not naive; you can treat someone fairly and still keep a boundary.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the divine within all things.
verses.sanskrit_display: बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् । धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥
verses.translation: Of the strong, I am the strength free from desire and passion. In beings, I am desire that is not contrary to dharma, best of the Bharatas.
verses.line: In the strong, I am strength without greed or grasping. In all, I am desire that stays within what's right.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on why people miss the divine and who turns to it.
verses.sanskrit_display: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन । आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥
verses.translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.
verses.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks seven questions about the self and death; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥
verses.translation: Whatever state of being a person remembers when leaving the body at the end, to that he goes, Kaunteya, always shaped by that state.
verses.line: Whatever you keep thinking about shapes who you become, right to the end.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks seven questions about the self and death; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥
verses.translation: Therefore remember me at all times, and fight. With mind and understanding offered to me, you will surely come to me.
verses.line: So remember the divine at all times, and keep doing your work.
verses.misuse: 'Fight' here means do your rightful work; it is not a call to pick battles.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, Kaunteya, do it as an offering to me.
verses.line: Whatever you do, eat, give or endure, do it as an offering.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः । ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥
verses.translation: I am the same to all beings; none is hateful to me and none dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.
verses.line: I am the same towards all; no one is hated, no one favoured. Those who love me live in me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् । साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥
verses.translation: Even if one of very bad conduct worships me with undivided devotion, he should be regarded as good, for he has resolved rightly.
verses.line: Even if you've done great wrong, the moment you turn wholeheartedly, count yourself among the good.
verses.misuse: Not 'devotion erases harm done to others'; turning around still includes making amends.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति । कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥
verses.translation: He soon becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. Kaunteya, declare it boldly: my devotee never perishes.
verses.line: Such a person soon turns good and finds lasting peace. Mark it: no one devoted to me is ever lost.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna names the chief glories in which the divine shows itself.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
verses.translation: I am the self, Gudakesha, seated in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of beings.
verses.line: I am the self seated in every heart: the beginning, middle and end of all beings.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on devotees who find joy together and the light he gives them.
verses.sanskrit_display: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
verses.translation: With minds fixed on me and lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and delighted.
verses.line: Their minds on me, they talk of me with each other, and find joy and contentment in it.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna, shown Krishna's cosmic form, is overwhelmed by its scale.
verses.sanskrit_display: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णंव्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् । दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्माधृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥
verses.translation: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colours, mouths wide open, with huge fiery eyes, my inner self trembles, Vishnu, and I find neither courage nor peace.
verses.line: Seeing something too big to take in, my heart trembles and I can't find steadiness or calm.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Overwhelmed by the cosmic vision, Arjuna asks to see Krishna's familiar form again.
verses.sanskrit_display: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वाभयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे । तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपंप्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥
verses.translation: I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me only that form of yours, God; be gracious, Lord of gods, refuge of the world.
verses.line: I'm thrilled and terrified at once. Show me the familiar face again.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna calms the frightened Arjuna and returns to his familiar form.
verses.sanskrit_display: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावोदृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् । व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वंतदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥
verses.translation: Do not be afraid or bewildered at seeing this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and glad at heart, see again that same familiar form of mine.
verses.line: Don't be afraid or confused by what you've seen. Let the fear go and look again with a calm heart.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verses.sanskrit_display: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः । ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
verses.translation: Restraining all the senses, even-minded everywhere, rejoicing in the welfare of all beings, they too reach me.
verses.line: Senses in hand, even-minded everywhere, glad in the good of all beings: they reach me too.

verses.collection: Gita 13: The Field and Its Knower
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verses.sanskrit_display: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना । अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥
verses.translation: Some see the self in the self by the self through meditation; others by the path of knowledge; and others by the yoga of action.
verses.line: Some find the truth by meditation, some by thinking it through, some by selfless work.

verses.collection: Gita 13: The Field and Its Knower
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verses.sanskrit_display: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते । तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
verses.translation: Others, not knowing this, worship having heard it from others; they too cross beyond death, devoted to what they have heard.
verses.line: Others, not knowing these paths, learn by listening to others, and they too cross over.

verses.collection: Gita 13: The Field and Its Knower
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
verses.translation: As the all-pervading sky, because of its subtlety, is not stained, so the self, present in every body, is not stained.
verses.line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
verses.sanskrit_display: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥
verses.translation: Darkness, inertia, heedlessness and delusion: these arise when tamas increases, joy of the Kurus.
verses.line: When dullness rules: darkness, sluggishness, carelessness and confusion.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते । गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥
verses.translation: who sits like one unconcerned, unshaken by the qualities, who knows 'it is only the qualities moving' and stays firm without wavering,
verses.line: Sit like a witness, unshaken, knowing it's just moods moving through, and stay steady.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
verses.sanskrit_display: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥
verses.translation: Know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings. It binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep, Bharata.
verses.line: Dullness, born of ignorance, ties you down through carelessness, laziness and too much sleep.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on his power sustaining the world and dwelling in every heart.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च । वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥
verses.translation: I am seated in the hearts of all. From me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I alone am what is to be known by all the Vedas; I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
verses.line: I am seated in every heart. Memory, knowledge and their fading come from me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes worldly life as an upside-down tree to be cut with detachment.
verses.sanskrit_display: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः । द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥
verses.translation: Free from pride and delusion, with the fault of attachment conquered, ever dwelling in the self, desires turned away, freed from the pairs called pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that eternal state.
verses.line: Free of pride and delusion, past the pull of attachment, the steady reach what doesn't fade.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on the individual soul as a part of the divine.
verses.sanskrit_display: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः । मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥
verses.translation: An eternal part of me becomes the living soul in the world of the living, and draws to itself the mind and the five senses that rest in nature.
verses.line: Every living being is an eternal part of me, says Krishna.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
verses.sanskrit_display: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
verses.translation: 'I am rich and well-born. Who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice': so they say, deluded by ignorance.
verses.line: 'I'm rich, well-born; who else is like me?' So speaks the deluded mind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः । यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
verses.translation: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and against the rules.
verses.line: Self-important, stubborn, drunk on money and status, they give for show.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna names the three gates to self-ruin and how to live instead.
verses.sanskrit_display: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः । आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
verses.translation: Released from these three gates of darkness, Kaunteya, a person does what is good for the self and so reaches the highest goal.
verses.line: Freed from these three dark gates, you do what's truly good for you and reach the highest.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
verses.sanskrit_display: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता । मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥
verses.translation: The divine nature leads to freedom, the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve, Pandava; you are born with the divine nature.
verses.line: Good qualities free you; harsh ones bind. Don't worry; you were born with the good.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verses.sanskrit_display: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः । परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
verses.translation: Austerity performed out of foolish obstinacy, with self-torture, or to harm another, is called tamasic.
verses.line: Discipline done through stubborn self-torment, or to harm another, is the dark kind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verses.sanskrit_display: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः । रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
verses.translation: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheerfulness, that are flavourful, soothing, nourishing and agreeable, are dear to the sattvic.
verses.line: Food that builds life, strength, health, cheer and calm: that's the food of a clear mind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते । त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥
verses.translation: The wise renouncer, full of clarity and free of doubt, does not hate disagreeable work nor cling to agreeable work.
verses.line: The wise don't hate unpleasant work or cling to pleasant work. Doubts gone, they just do it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते । अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥
verses.translation: The knowledge by which one sees one imperishable being in all beings, undivided in the divided, know that knowledge to be sattvic.
verses.line: Clear understanding sees one undivided life in all beings, though they appear separate.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् । अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: Action that is obligatory, done without attachment, without love or hatred, by one who does not crave its fruit, is called sattvic.
verses.line: Good action is steady, done without clinging, not driven by like or dislike, or by what you'll get.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः । क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥
verses.translation: But action done by one seeking desires, or with ego, or with great strain, is called rajasic.
verses.line: Work done with huge strain, for ego or pleasure, is the restless kind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् । मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: Action undertaken out of delusion, without regard to consequence, loss, injury to others, or one's own ability, is called tamasic.
verses.line: Action begun in confusion, without weighing consequences, cost, harm or your own capacity, is dark action.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः । हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
verses.translation: The doer who is passionate, eager for the fruits of work, greedy, harmful, impure, and swayed by joy and sorrow, is called rajasic.
verses.line: Hungry for results, greedy, willing to harm, unclean, tossed by joy and grief: the restless kind of doer.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च । अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
verses.translation: The understanding by which one wrongly knows right and wrong, what should and should not be done, that understanding, Partha, is rajasic.
verses.line: A mind clouded by restlessness can't quite tell right from wrong, or what to do from what to avoid.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता । सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
verses.translation: The understanding which, wrapped in darkness, thinks wrong is right and sees all things in reverse, Partha, is tamasic.
verses.line: A mind wrapped in darkness takes wrong for right and sees everything upside down.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः । योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
verses.translation: The firmness by which one holds the workings of the mind, breath and senses through unwavering yoga, that firmness, Partha, is sattvic.
verses.line: True resolve holds mind, breath and senses steady through unwavering practice.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन । प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
verses.translation: But the firmness by which one holds to duty, pleasure and wealth with attachment, craving their fruits, Arjuna, that firmness, Partha, is rajasic.
verses.line: Clinging to duty, pleasure and wealth for what they'll bring you is restless resolve.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च । न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
verses.translation: The firmness by which a dull-minded person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and pride, that firmness, Partha, is tamasic.
verses.line: Stubbornly holding on to sleep, fear, grief, despair and pride is the dark kind of resolve.
verses.misuse: Not a judgement on depression or grief; it names the habit of clinging to them as if they were safety.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥
verses.translation: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, best of the Bharatas: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, and in which one reaches the end of sorrow.
verses.line: There is a joy you grow into through practice, one that brings sorrow to an end.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः । निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
verses.translation: The happiness that deludes the self in the beginning and in the end, arising from sleep, laziness and heedlessness, is called tamasic.
verses.line: Pleasure from sleep, laziness and carelessness dulls you from start to finish.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on the steadiness of one established in knowledge.
verses.sanskrit_display: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः । नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥
verses.translation: One whose understanding is unattached everywhere, who has mastered himself and is free from desire, reaches through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.
verses.line: Unattached everywhere, self-mastered, free of craving: that's the highest freedom.
verses.misuse: Unattached is not uncaring; it doesn't ask you to step back from family or friends.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः । बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
verses.translation: Mentally resigning all actions to me, holding me as the highest, relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.
verses.line: Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च । कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् ॥
verses.translation: But even these actions should be done giving up attachment and fruits. This, Partha, is my definite and highest view.
verses.line: Even good work should be done without clinging to it or its rewards. That's my settled view.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥
verses.translation: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.
verses.line: Mind on me, heart devoted to me, you will come to me. I promise: you are dear to me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते । मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
verses.translation: Renunciation of obligatory action is not proper. Its abandonment out of delusion is declared tamasic.
verses.line: Walking away from a real responsibility out of confusion is the darkest kind of letting go.
verses.misuse: Not 'you can never leave'. Leaving thoughtfully is different from abandoning out of confusion.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.setting: Sanjaya's closing words to the blind king, after narrating the whole dialogue.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
verses.translation: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is Partha, the archer, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and sound policy. This is my conviction.
verses.line: Where wisdom and skilled effort stand together, there is fortune, victory, wellbeing and steady justice.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन । सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥
verses.translation: When necessary work is done simply because it ought to be done, Arjuna, giving up attachment and the fruit, that renunciation is considered sattvic.
verses.line: Do what must be done because it must be done, letting go of clinging and the payoff.
verses.misuse: Not 'never question your duties'. Choose them wisely, then do them without clinging.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः । उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
verses.translation: The unreal has no lasting being, and the real never ceases to be. Those who see the truth have seen the final word on both.
verses.line: What is unreal never truly lasts; what is real never stops being.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचकुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Where has this faintness of heart come upon you in this crisis, Arjuna? It is not fitting for the noble, it does not lead upward, and it brings disgrace.
verses.line: Where did this weakness come from, at the very moment it matters most?
verses.misuse: Not shaming fear; it's the opening of a long, patient answer.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते । तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.translation: It is called unmanifest, unthinkable and unchanging. Knowing it to be so, you should not grieve.
verses.line: It is unseen, beyond thought, unchanging. Knowing this, ease your grief.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.translation: And even if you think of it as constantly being born and constantly dying, still, mighty-armed one, you should not grieve like this.
verses.line: Even if you believe life simply begins and ends, there's still no need to be crushed by grief.
verses.misuse: Grief is human; this asks you not to be destroyed by it, not to stop feeling it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verses.sanskrit_display: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत । तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.translation: The self dwelling in the body of every being is eternal and can never be slain, Bharata. Therefore you should not grieve for any creature.
verses.line: The self within every body can never be destroyed. So don't grieve for any creature as lost.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to hurry anyone through mourning a person or a pet.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् । व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
verses.translation: For those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away by such talk, a resolute, settled understanding does not arise.
verses.line: Chasing comfort and power, the mind can never settle into a single purpose.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन । निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥
verses.translation: The Vedas deal with the three qualities; rise above them, Arjuna. Be free from the pairs of opposites, always steady in goodness, free from the urge to acquire and keep, and possessed of the self.
verses.line: Rise above the pull of opposites. Stay centred, not obsessed with getting and keeping.
verses.misuse: Not 'don't save or plan'; it's about not being consumed by getting and holding.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
verses.translation: When your understanding crosses the mire of delusion, you will grow indifferent to all that you have heard and all that is yet to be heard.
verses.line: When your mind clears the fog, you'll tire of all you've heard and all you're yet to hear.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः । रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥
verses.translation: Objects fall away from one who abstains from them, but the taste for them remains. Even the taste falls away once the Supreme is seen.
verses.line: Staying away from a craving dims it, but the taste lingers until something higher replaces it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः । वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
verses.translation: Restraining them all, one should sit disciplined, intent on me. For one whose senses are under control, wisdom is firmly set.
verses.line: Gather the senses in, sit steady with your mind on what's highest. Mastery of the senses steadies wisdom.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
verses.translation: In that clarity all sorrows come to an end; for one whose mind is clear, understanding soon becomes steady.
verses.line: When the mind clears, sorrows start to dissolve, and understanding settles quickly.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
verses.translation: What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; and where all beings are awake, that is night for the seeing sage.
verses.line: What the crowd sleeps through, the wise stay awake to. What the crowd chases, the wise see past.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verses.sanskrit_display: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
verses.translation: This is the state of Brahman, Partha. Having reached it, one is not deluded. Abiding in it even at the hour of death, one attains the peace of Brahman.
verses.line: Rooted in this steadiness, you aren't lost, even at the very end.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
verses.translation: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
verses.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on the cycle of offering that sustains the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
verses.translation: Nourish the gods with this, and may the gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you will attain the highest good.
verses.line: Nourish one another, and together you'll reach the highest good.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on the cycle of offering that sustains the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः । भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
verses.translation: The good who eat what remains after the offering are freed from all faults. But the wicked who cook only for themselves eat sin.
verses.line: Those who share first are freed; those who cook only for themselves feed on wrong.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
verses.translation: But for the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and content in the self alone, there is nothing that must be done.
verses.line: One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verses.sanskrit_display: सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत । कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ॥
verses.translation: As the unwise act with attachment to their work, Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, wishing to hold the world together.
verses.line: Work as hard as the ambitious do, but for everyone's good, not your own grip on results.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥
verses.translation: Knowledge is covered, Kaunteya, by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, an insatiable fire.
verses.line: Desire is a fire that never gets enough. It quietly covers even the wise person's clarity.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ । पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
verses.translation: Therefore, best of the Bharatas, first control the senses, then cast off this wrongdoer that destroys knowledge and discernment.
verses.line: So start with the senses. Get them in hand, then let go of the desire that wrecks clear thinking.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
verses.translation: The senses are said to be higher than the body; higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; and higher than the intellect is the self.
verses.line: Senses are strong, the mind stronger, clear judgement stronger still, and your true self strongest of all.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन । कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
verses.translation: But one who controls the senses by the mind, Arjuna, and without attachment engages the organs of action in the yoga of action, excels.
verses.line: Better: guide your senses with your mind and get to work, without being hooked.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः । बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥
verses.translation: Freed from passion, fear and anger, absorbed in me and taking refuge in me, many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, have come to my being.
verses.line: Many have dropped craving, fear and anger, been refined by wisdom, and found their way home.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः । अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥
verses.translation: One must understand what action is, what wrong action is, and what inaction is; the way of action is deep.
verses.line: What to do, what to avoid, when to hold back: the way of action is deep.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः । स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
verses.translation: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people; he is disciplined and does all his work.
verses.line: See the stillness inside activity and the activity inside stillness, and you're truly wise.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
verses.sanskrit_display: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verses.translation: Without hope, with mind and self controlled, giving up all possessiveness, doing only bodily action, he incurs no fault.
verses.line: Expecting nothing, mind steady, letting go of possessiveness, you can work without being stained.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन । ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥
verses.translation: As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.
verses.line: As a blazing fire turns wood to ash, real understanding burns away the hold of past actions.
verses.misuse: Not a way to skip accountability; amends still matter.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते । तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥
verses.translation: There is nothing in this world as purifying as knowledge. One perfected in yoga finds it in oneself in due time.
verses.line: Nothing here cleanses like understanding, and with steady practice you find it within, in time.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verses.sanskrit_display: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥
verses.translation: Actions do not bind one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts are cut away by knowledge, and who is self-possessed, Dhananjaya.
verses.line: Doubts cut away by understanding, steady within, your actions stop binding you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verses.sanskrit_display: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि । योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥
verses.translation: With body, mind, intellect and even the senses alone, the yogis act without attachment, for the purification of the self.
verses.line: Wise people work with body, mind and heart, not for gain, but to become clearer within.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verses.sanskrit_display: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः । निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥
verses.translation: Even here the world is conquered by those whose minds are established in evenness. Brahman is flawless and the same in all; so they are established in Brahman.
verses.line: Those whose minds rest in evenness have already won, right here in this life.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks whether giving up action or acting selflessly is better; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचसंन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ । तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥
verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Renunciation and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good. But of the two, the yoga of action is better than renunciation of action.
verses.line: Stepping back and acting selflessly both lead to good, but of the two, acting is better.
verses.misuse: Not 'never rest or retire'; it prefers engaged, selfless work over withdrawal.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verses.sanskrit_display: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
verses.translation: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light is within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman.
verses.line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verses.sanskrit_display: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः । छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
verses.translation: Seers whose faults are destroyed, whose doubts are cut away, who are self-controlled and delight in the welfare of all beings, attain the peace of Brahman.
verses.line: Doubts cut away, mind mastered, they give themselves to the good of all beings and find peace.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, briefly describing meditation and the peace it brings.
verses.sanskrit_display: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः । विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥
verses.translation: The sage whose senses, mind and intellect are controlled, who is intent on freedom, and from whom desire, fear and anger have gone, is truly free forever.
verses.line: Senses, mind and judgement in hand, free of desire, fear and anger: that person is already free.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥
verses.translation: When the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, becomes still, and one sees the self by the self, one is content in the self.
verses.line: When the mind finally goes still, you see yourself as you are, and you're content.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥
verses.translation: Supreme happiness comes to the yogi whose mind is calm, whose passions are stilled, who is free from wrong and one with Brahman.
verses.line: A calm mind, its turmoil settled, finds the highest happiness.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
verses.translation: One whose self is joined in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self; he sees the same everywhere.
verses.line: See yourself in every being and every being in yourself, and you see the same everywhere.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
verses.translation: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
verses.line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verses.sanskrit_display: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥
verses.translation: There he regains the understanding of his former life, and from there strives again, more than before, for perfection, joy of the Kurus.
verses.line: What you learned before isn't lost. You pick it up again and push on harder.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verses.sanskrit_display: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
verses.translation: By that former practice he is carried on, even against his will. Even one who merely wishes to know yoga goes beyond the ritual word.
verses.line: Past practice carries you forward, even when you don't feel like it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
verses.translation: But the yogi who strives with diligence, cleansed of faults, perfected through many births, then reaches the highest goal.
verses.line: The one who keeps at it, steadily, over a long time, gets there.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verses.sanskrit_display: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥
verses.translation: The yogi whose self is satisfied with knowledge and understanding, who is unshakeable, master of the senses, to whom a clod, a stone and gold are the same, is called steadfast.
verses.line: To the settled mind, a lump of earth, a stone and a bar of gold are worth the same.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to neglect money or family finances; it is about not being ruled by them.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on worship of other deities.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति । तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever form any devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that very faith of his unshakeable.
verses.line: Whatever form someone chooses to worship with faith, I make that faith steady.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on those who miss him and those who know him.
verses.sanskrit_display: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
verses.translation: Through the delusion of the pairs of opposites, arising from desire and aversion, Bharata, all beings fall into confusion at birth, scorcher of enemies.
verses.line: From the pull of want and push of dislike comes the confusion that traps every being.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna on steady remembrance and the cycles of creation.
verses.sanskrit_display: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना । परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥
verses.translation: With a mind disciplined by the practice of yoga and not straying to anything else, meditating constantly, one goes to the supreme divine Person, Partha.
verses.line: With a mind trained by practice and not wandering elsewhere, you reach what you meditate on.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥
verses.translation: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow to me. Having joined yourself to me, with me as your goal, you will come to me.
verses.line: Fix your mind on me, love me, honour me, bow to me. Joined this way, you come to me.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The Aitareya on the three births of a person, beginning with pregnancy.
verses.sanskrit_display: तत्स्त्रिया आत्मभूयं गच्छति। यथा स्वमङ्गं तथा। तस्मादेनां न हिनस्ति । साऽस्यैतमात्मानमत्र गतं भावयति ॥ सा भावयित्री भावयितव्या भवति। तं स्त्री गर्भ बिभर्ति। सोऽग्र एव कुमारं जन्मनोऽग्रेऽधिभावयति।
verses.translation: It becomes one with the woman, like a part of her own body, so it does not harm her. She nourishes this self of his that has come into her. She who nourishes must herself be nourished. The woman carries the child; the father cares for the child from birth onward.
verses.line: She who nourishes the child must herself be nourished.

verses.speaker: Maitreyi and Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Yajnavalkya, leaving home, offers to divide his property between his two wives.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा होवाच मैत्रेयी यन्नु म इयं भगोः सर्वा पृथिवी वित्तेन पूर्णा स्यात् कथं तेनामृता स्यामिति । नेति होवाच याज्ञवल्क्यो यथैवोपकरणवतां जीवितं तथैव ते जीवितꣳ स्यादमृतत्वस्य तु नाऽऽशाऽस्ति वित्तेनेति ॥
verses.translation: Maitreyi said: 'Sir, if this whole earth full of wealth were mine, would I become immortal by it?' 'No,' said Yajnavalkya. 'Your life would be like the life of the well-off. There is no hope of immortality through wealth.'
verses.line: 'If the whole earth's wealth were mine, would it make me deathless?' 'No. Wealth buys comfort, not that.'

verses.speaker: Maitreyi
verses.setting: Maitreyi's reply to the offer of property.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा होवाच मैत्रेयी येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम् । यदेव भगवान्वेद तदेव मे ब्रूहीति ॥
verses.translation: Maitreyi said: 'What should I do with that which will not make me immortal? Tell me, sir, what you know.'
verses.line: What would I do with something that cannot save me? Teach me what you know instead.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya and Janaka
verses.setting: King Janaka, rich and learned, comes down from his seat to the sage.
verses.sanskrit_display: स होवाच यथा वै सम्राण् महान्तमध्वानमेष्यन्रथं वा नावं वा समाददीतैवमेवैताभिरुपनिषद्भिः समाहितात्माऽस्यसि एवं वृन्दारक आढ्यः सन्नधीतवेद उक्तोपनिषत्क इतो विमुच्यमानः क्व गमिष्यसीति । नाहं तद् भगवन् वेद यत्र गमिष्यामीत्यथ वै तेऽहं तद्वक्ष्यामि यत्र गमिष्यसीति । ब्रवीतु भगवानिति ॥
verses.translation: He said: 'Your Majesty, as a man setting out on a long journey would take a chariot or a ship, so you have equipped yourself with these teachings. You are honoured and wealthy, you have studied the Vedas and heard the Upanishads. When you leave this world, where will you go?' 'I do not know, sir, where I shall go.' 'Then I will tell you where you will go.' 'Tell me, sir.'
verses.line: 'You are rich and learned. When you die, where will you go?' The king said, 'I don't know.'

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Janaka asks what light a person lives by.
verses.sanskrit_display: अस्तमित आदित्ये याज्ञवल्क्य चन्द्रमस्यस्तमिते शान्तेऽग्नौ किञ्ज्योतिरेवायं पुरुष इति । वागेवास्य ज्योतिर्भवतीति वाचैवायं ज्योतिषास्ते पल्ययते कर्म कुरुते विपल्येतीति । तस्माद्वै सम्राड् अपि यत्र स्वः पाणिर्न विनिर्ज्ञायतेऽथ यत्र वागुच्चरत्युपैव तत्रन्येतीत्येवमेवैतद् याज्ञवल्क्य ॥ अस्तमित आदित्ये याज्ञवल्क्य चन्द्रमस्यस्तमिते शान्तेऽग्नौ शान्तायां वाचि किञ्ज्योतिरेवायं पुरुष इत्यात्मैवास्य ज्योतिर्भवत्यात्मनैवायं ज्योतिषाऽऽस्ते पल्ययते कर्म कुरुते विपल्येतीति ॥
verses.translation: 'When the sun has set, Yajnavalkya, and the moon has set, and the fire has gone out, what light does a person have?' 'Speech is then his light; for when one cannot even see one's own hand, where a voice is heard, there one goes.' 'And when speech too is silent?' 'Then the self is his light. By the light of the self he sits, goes about, works and returns.'
verses.line: When sun, moon and fire are gone and even voices fall silent, the self is your light.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Yajnavalkya on how a person becomes what they are.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथो खल्वाहुः काममय एवायं पुरुष इति स यथाकामो भवति तत्क्रतुर्भवति यत्क्रतुर्भवति तत्कर्म कुरुते यत्कर्म कुरुते तदभिसम्पद्यते ॥
verses.translation: And so they say: a person is made of desire. As his desire is, so is his will; as his will is, so is his deed; and whatever deed he does, that he becomes.
verses.line: As your desire, so your will; as your will, so your deeds; as your deeds, so you become.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Verses on knowing the self, continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: इहैव सन्तोऽथ विद्मस्तद्वयं न चेदवेदिर्महती विनष्टिः । ये तद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्त्यथेतरे दुःखमेवापियन्ति ॥
verses.translation: While we are still here, we may know it. If we do not, great is the loss. Those who know it become immortal; the rest go only to sorrow.
verses.line: While we are still here, let us know it. Not knowing it is the great loss.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Verses on knowing the self, continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: तमेव धीरो विज्ञाय प्रज्ञां कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणः । नानुध्यायाद्बहूञ्छब्दान् वाचो विग्लापनꣳ हि तदिति ॥
verses.translation: Knowing that one alone, let the wise seeker cultivate understanding. Let him not brood over many words, for that only wearies the voice.
verses.line: Know the one thing, and let wisdom grow from it. Don't brood over many words; that only tires you.

verses.speaker: Prajapati
verses.setting: Prajapati's three kinds of children ask him for teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रयाः प्राजापत्याः प्रजापतौ पितरि ब्रह्मचर्यमूषुर्देवा मनुष्या असुरा उषित्वा ब्रह्मचर्यं देवा ऊचुर्ब्रवीतु नो भवानिति । तेभ्यो हैतदक्षरमुवाच द इति व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुर्दाम्यतेति न आत्थेत्योमिति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति ॥ अथ हैनं मनुष्या ऊचुर्ब्रवीतु नो भवानिति । तेभ्यो हैतदेवाक्षरमुवाच द इति व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुर्दत्तेति न आत्थेत्योमिति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति ॥ अथ हैनमसुरा ऊचुर्ब्रवीतु नो भवानिति । तेभ्यो हैतदेवाक्षरमुवाच द इति व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुर्दयध्वमिति न आत्थेत्योमिति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति । तदेतदेवैषा दैवी वागनुवदति स्तनयित्नुर्द द द इति दाम्यत दत्त दयध्वमिति । तदेतत्त्रयꣳ शिक्षेद् दमं दानं दयामिति ॥
verses.translation: The gods, humans and demons, the three children of Prajapati, lived with their father as students. The gods asked for teaching; he said the syllable 'Da' and asked if they understood. 'Be self-controlled (damyata),' they said. 'Yes.' The humans asked; 'Da.' 'Give (datta),' they said. 'Yes.' The demons asked; 'Da.' 'Be compassionate (dayadhvam),' they said. 'Yes.' The divine voice of thunder repeats it: Da Da Da: be self-controlled, give, be compassionate. One should learn these three: self-control, giving, compassion.
verses.line: The thunder says Da Da Da: be self-controlled, be giving, be compassionate.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A prayer chanted at the start of a Vedic hymn.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथातः पवमानानामेवाभ्यारोहः । स वै खलु प्रस्तोता साम प्रस्तौति । स यत्र प्रस्तुयात् तदेतानि जपेदसतो मा सद् गमय तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय मृत्योर्माऽमृतं गमयेति ।
verses.translation: Now the chanting of the purifying verses. When the priest begins the hymn, one should recite: From the unreal lead me to the real. From darkness lead me to light. From death lead me to immortality.
verses.line: Lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to the deathless.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The creation story: last of all, dharma is made.
verses.sanskrit_display: स नैव व्यभवत् तच्छ्रेयो रूपमत्यसृजत धर्मम् । तदेतत्क्षत्रस्य क्षत्रं यद्धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्मात् परं नास्त्यथो अबलीयान् बलीयाꣳसमाशꣳसते धर्मेण यथा राज्ञैवम् । यो वै स धर्मः सत्यं वै तत् तस्मात्सत्यं वदन्तमाहुर्धर्मं वदतीति धर्मं वा वदन्तꣳ सत्यं वदतीत्येतद्ध्येवैतदुभयं भवति ॥
verses.translation: Still he did not flourish. So he created a higher form, dharma. Dharma is the power over power; nothing is higher than dharma. Through dharma even a weak man can stand up to a strong one, as with the help of a king. That dharma is truth. So people say of one who speaks truth, 'He speaks dharma,' and of one who speaks dharma, 'He speaks truth.' Both are the same.
verses.line: Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.

verses.speaker: Shandilya
verses.setting: The teaching of Shandilya.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत । अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुरस्मिꣳल्लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत ॥
verses.translation: All this is Brahman; from it all arises, into it all dissolves, in it all breathes; so one should meditate on it calmly. A person is made of resolve. As one's resolve is in this world, so one becomes on departing. So let one form a resolve.
verses.line: A person is made of resolve. As you resolve in this life, so you become. So resolve well.

verses.speaker: Jabala
verses.setting: A boy asks his mother his lineage before seeking a teacher.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा हैनमुवाच नाहमेतद्वेद तात यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि बह्वहं चरन्ती परिचारिणी यौवने त्वामलभे साहमेतन्न वेद यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि जबाला तु नामाहमस्मि सत्यकामो नाम त्वमसि स सत्यकाम एव जाबालो ब्रवीथा इति ॥
verses.translation: She said to him: 'I do not know your lineage, my child. In my youth I moved about a great deal as a serving woman, and then I had you. So I do not know your lineage. My name is Jabala and your name is Satyakama. Just say you are Satyakama Jabala.'
verses.line: His mother said, 'I don't know your father's line. I am Jabala, you are Satyakama. Say exactly that.'

verses.speaker: Haridrumata Gautama
verses.setting: The teacher's response to the boy's honesty.
verses.sanskrit_display: तꣳ होवाच नैतदब्राह्मणो विवक्तुमर्हति समिधꣳ सोम्याहरोप त्वा नेष्ये न सत्यादगा इति तमुपनीय कृशानामबलानां चतुःशता गा निराकृत्योवाचेमाः सोम्यानुसंव्रजेति
verses.translation: He said to him: 'No one but a true brahmin could speak so plainly. Bring fuel, dear one; I will take you as a student, for you have not swerved from the truth.' Having initiated him, he picked out four hundred thin, weak cows and said, 'Follow these, dear one.'
verses.line: Only someone truly noble could speak this plainly. You have not swerved from truth; I will teach you.

verses.speaker: Satyakama
verses.setting: Satyakama is given four hundred weak cows to tend.
verses.sanskrit_display: ता अभिप्रस्थापयन्नुवाच नासहस्रेणावर्तेयेति स ह वर्षगणं प्रोवास ता यदा सहस्रꣳ सम्पेदुः ॥
verses.translation: As he drove them off he said, 'I will not return until they are a thousand.' He lived away for years, until they had become a thousand.
verses.line: Given four hundred weak cows, he said, 'I won't come back until they are a thousand.' He stayed years.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: A son returns from twelve years of study, full of himself.
verses.sanskrit_display: स ह द्वादशवर्ष उपेत्य चतुर्विꣳशतिवर्षः सर्वान्वेदानधीत्य महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्ध एयाय तꣳह पितोवाच ॥ श्वेतकेतो यन्नु सोम्येदं महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्धोऽस्युत तमादेशमप्राक्ष्यः येनाश्रुतꣳ श्रुतं भवत्यमतं मतमविज्ञातं विज्ञातमिति कथं नु भगवः स आदेशो भवतीति ॥
verses.translation: He went at twelve and returned at twenty-four, having studied all the Vedas, conceited, proud of his learning, stiff. His father said: 'Shvetaketu, since you are so conceited, so proud of your learning, so stiff, did you ask for that teaching by which the unheard becomes heard, the unthought becomes thought, the unknown becomes known?' 'How could there be such a teaching, sir?'
verses.line: Shvetaketu came home proud of his learning. His father asked: did you learn what makes everything else make sense?

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: Uddalaka explains sleep to his son.
verses.sanskrit_display: स यथा शकुनिः सूत्रेण प्रबद्धो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा बन्धनमेवोपश्रयत एवमेव खलु सोम्य तन्मनो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा प्राणमेवोपश्रयते प्राणबन्धनꣳ हि सोम्य मन इति ॥
verses.translation: As a bird tied by a string flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down at the very place it is tied, so, dear one, the mind flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down on the breath; for the mind is tied to the breath.
verses.line: Like a bird on a string, the mind flies everywhere, finds no rest, and returns to the breath.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: The refrain closing each of Uddalaka's lessons.
verses.sanskrit_display: स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदꣳ सर्वं तत्सत्यꣳ स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो इति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
verses.translation: That which is the subtle essence: this whole world has it as its self. That is the truth. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu. 'Teach me more, sir.' 'So be it, dear one.'
verses.line: That subtle essence is the self of all that is. That is truth. You are that, Shvetaketu.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: After the lesson of the living tree whose branches dry when life leaves them.
verses.sanskrit_display: एवमेव खलु सोम्य विद्धीति होवाच जीवापेतं वाव किलेदं म्रियते न जीवो म्रियते इति स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदꣳ सर्वं तत्सत्यꣳ स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो इति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
verses.translation: 'Know it to be just so, dear one,' he said. 'This body dies when life has left it; life itself does not die. That which is the subtle essence, this whole world has it as its self. That is the truth. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu.'
verses.line: The body dies when life leaves it. Life itself does not die.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: The lesson of the banyan seed.
verses.sanskrit_display: न्यग्रोधफलमत आहरेतीदं भगव इति भिन्द्धीति भिन्नं भगव इति किमत्र पश्यसीत्यण्व्य इवेमा धाना भगव इत्यासामङ्गैकां भिन्द्धीति भिन्ना भगव इति किमत्र पश्यसीति न किंचन भगव इति ॥ तꣳ होवाच यं वै सोम्यैतमणिमानं न निभालयस एतस्य वै सोम्यैषोऽणिम्न एवं महान्यग्रोधस्तिष्ठति श्रद्धत्स्व सोम्येति ॥
verses.translation: 'Bring a fig from the banyan tree.' 'Here it is, sir.' 'Break it.' 'It is broken, sir.' 'What do you see?' 'These tiny seeds, sir.' 'Break one of them.' 'It is broken, sir.' 'What do you see?' 'Nothing at all, sir.' He said: 'That subtle essence you cannot see, dear one: from that very essence this great banyan stands. Have faith, dear one.'
verses.line: Break a banyan seed and you find nothing. From that unseen nothing, a great tree stands. Have faith.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: The lesson of salt in water.
verses.sanskrit_display: लवणमेतदुदकेऽवधायाथ मा प्रातरुपसीदथा इति स ह तथा चकार तꣳ होवाच यद्दोषा लवणमुदकेऽवाधा अङ्ग तदाहरेति तद्धावमृश्य न विवेद ॥ यथा विलीनमेवाङ्गास्यान्तादाचामेति कथमिति लवणमिति मध्यादाचामेति कथमिति लवणमित्यन्तादाचामेति कथमिति लवणमित्यभिप्रास्यैतदथ मोपसीदथा इति तद्ध तथा चकार तच्छश्वत्संवर्तते तꣳ होवाचात्र वाव किल तत्सोम्य न निभालयसेऽत्रैव किलेति ॥
verses.translation: 'Put this salt in water and come to me in the morning.' He did so. The father said, 'Bring me the salt you put in the water last night.' He felt for it and could not find it, for it had dissolved. 'Sip from the top. How is it?' 'Salty.' 'From the middle?' 'Salty.' 'From the bottom?' 'Salty.' 'Throw it away and come to me.' He did, and said, 'It is always there.' The father said, 'You do not see it here, dear one, yet it is right here.'
verses.line: Salt dissolved in water can't be seen, yet every sip tastes of it. What you can't see is still here.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: The lesson of the man from Gandhara.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा सोम्य पुरुषं गन्धारेभ्योऽभिनद्धाक्षमानीय तं ततोऽतिजने विसृजेत्स यथा तत्र प्राङ्वोदङ्वाधराङ्वा प्रत्यङ्वा प्रध्मायीताभिनद्धाक्ष आनीतोऽभिनद्धाक्षो विसृष्टः ॥ तस्य यथाभिनहनं प्रमुच्य प्रब्रूयादेतां दिशं गन्धारा एतां दिशं व्रजेति स ग्रामाद्ग्रामं पृच्छन्पण्डितो मेधावी गन्धारानेवोपसम्पद्येतैवमेवेहाचार्यवान्पुरुषो वेद तस्य तावदेव चिरं यावन्न विमोक्ष्येऽथ सम्पत्स्य इति ॥
verses.translation: As a man brought blindfolded from Gandhara and left in a deserted place might wander east or north or south, crying, 'I was brought here blindfolded and left blindfolded,' and someone removes his blindfold and says, 'Gandhara is that way, go that way,' and asking from village to village, informed and sensible, he reaches Gandhara; so a person who has a teacher comes to know.
verses.line: Lost and blindfolded, you need someone to point the way; then ask village by village until you're home.

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada, master of every science, comes to Sanatkumara.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविदेवास्मि नात्मविच्छ्रुतꣳ ह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्यस्तरति शोकमात्मविदिति सोऽहं भगवः शोचामि तं मा भगवाञ्छोकस्य पारं तारयत्विति तꣳ होवाच यद्वै किंचैतदध्यगीष्ठा नामैवैतत् ॥
verses.translation: 'Sir, I know only the texts; I do not know the self. I have heard from people like you that one who knows the self crosses beyond sorrow. I am in sorrow, sir. Please take me across.' He said to him: 'Whatever you have studied is only name.'
verses.line: I have learned so much, yet I am sad. I know words, not myself. Help me cross this sorrow.

verses.speaker: Sanatkumara
verses.setting: A step in Sanatkumara's ladder: faith rests on steadiness, steadiness on action.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा वै करोत्यथ निस्तिष्ठति नाकृत्वा निस्तिष्ठति कृत्वैव निस्तिष्ठति कृतिस्त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्येति कृतिं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verses.translation: When one acts, one becomes steadfast. One does not become steadfast without acting; only by acting does one become steadfast. So action itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand action.'
verses.line: Steadiness comes from doing. No one becomes steady without acting; act, and steadiness follows.

verses.speaker: Sanatkumara
verses.setting: The summit of Sanatkumara's teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verses.translation: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The infinite alone is happiness. So the infinite must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand the infinite.'
verses.line: Happiness is in the vast. There is no happiness in the small.

verses.speaker: Prajapati's teaching (narrator)
verses.setting: On the self in the heart that we visit nightly in deep sleep without knowing it.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनृतापिधानास्तद्यथापि हिरण्यनिधिं निहितमक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्युपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुरेवमेवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहरहर्गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः ॥
verses.translation: As people who do not know the spot walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold buried in the ground and do not find it, so all these creatures go day after day into that world of Brahman and do not find it, for they are carried away by untruth.
verses.line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Opening verse of the Isha, the shortest principal Upanishad.
verses.sanskrit_display: ॐ ईशा वास्यमिदꣳ सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् । तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम् ॥
verses.translation: All of this, whatever moves in this moving world, is pervaded by the Lord. Enjoy it by letting go. Do not covet; whose is wealth, after all?
verses.line: Everything is held by the divine. Enjoy by letting go; do not covet. Whose wealth is it, really?
verses.misuse: Not a call to neglect your finances; it is about how you hold what you have.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Follows the call to enjoy by letting go: how to live and work.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतꣳ समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥
verses.translation: Doing your work here, you may wish to live a hundred years. For you there is no other way than this: done in this spirit, action does not cling to a person.
verses.line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The Isha on seeing one life in all beings.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मन्येवानुपश्यति । सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं ततो न विजुगुप्सते ॥
verses.translation: One who sees all beings in the self, and the self in all beings, no longer shrinks away from anyone.
verses.line: See yourself in everyone and everyone in yourself, and you stop recoiling from people.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Nachiketa has refused wealth and long life; Yama begins teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीर:। श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद् वृणीते ॥
verses.translation: The good and the pleasant both come to a person. The wise one examines them and tells them apart. The wise chooses the good over the pleasant; the dull chooses the pleasant, for getting and keeping.
verses.line: The good and the pleasant both knock. The wise choose the good; the foolish grab the pleasant.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: The rousing call that closes the chariot teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत । क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥
verses.translation: Arise! Awake! Go to the great ones and learn. Sharp as a razor's edge, hard to cross, is that path, say the wise.
verses.line: Arise, awake! Find the wise and learn. The path is sharp as a razor's edge, hard to cross.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Yama's chariot image of the human being.
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मानँ रथितं विद्धि शरीरँ रथमेव तु । बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥ इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयांस्तेषु गोचरान् । आत्मेन्द्रिय मनोयुक्त भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
verses.translation: Know the self as the rider, the body as the chariot, the intellect as the charioteer and the mind as the reins. The senses, they say, are the horses, and the things of the world are the roads they run on.
verses.line: You are the rider, your body the chariot, your intellect the driver, your mind the reins.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Yama on why we miss what is within.
verses.sanskrit_display: पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयम्भूस्तस्मात्पराङ्पश्यति नान्तरात्मन्। कश्चिद्धीरः प्रत्यगात्मानमैक्षदावृत्तचक्षुरमृतत्वमिच्छन् ॥
verses.translation: The self-existent one made the senses face outward, so a person looks outward, not within. A rare wise one, seeking the deathless, turned the gaze inward and saw the self.
verses.line: Our senses face outward, so we look out. A rare wise person turns the gaze inward.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: Rules of conduct for a renunciant.
verses.sanskrit_display: नात्यर्थं सुखदुःखाभ्यां शरीरमुपतायेत् । स्तूयमानो न तुषेत निन्दितो न शपेत्परान् ॥
verses.translation: Let him not torment the body too much for the sake of pleasure or pain. Praised, let him not gloat; blamed, let him not curse others.
verses.line: Don't wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. Praised, don't gloat; blamed, don't curse others.

verses.speaker: Indra
verses.setting: Indra on attention behind every sense.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि प्रज्ञापेता वाङ्नाम किंचन प्रज्ञपयेदन्यत्र मे मनोऽभूदित्याह नाहमेतन्नाम प्राज्ञासिषमिति न हि प्रज्ञापेतः प्राणो गन्धं कंचन प्रज्ञपयेदन्यत्र मे मनोऽभूदित्याह नाहमेतं गन्धं प्राज्ञासिषमिति नहि
verses.translation: Without attention, speech conveys no word at all. A person says, 'My mind was elsewhere; I did not catch that word.' Without attention, breath conveys no smell. A person says, 'My mind was elsewhere; I did not notice that smell.'
verses.line: Without attention, nothing reaches us. We say, 'Sorry, my mind was elsewhere; I didn't catch that.'

verses.speaker: Shvetaketu and Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: A patron asks Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer; he goes to his father.
verses.sanskrit_display: स होवाच नाहमेतद्वेद हन्ताचार्यं प्रच्छानीति स ह पितरमासाद्य पप्रच्छेतीति स होवाचाहमप्येतन्न वेद सदस्येव वयं स्वाध्यायमधीत्य हरामहे यन्नः परे ददत्येह्युभौ गमिष्याव इति ॥
verses.translation: He said, 'I do not know this. Let me ask my teacher.' He went to his father and asked. The father said, 'I too do not know it. We have studied the Veda and take what others give us. Come, let us both go.'
verses.line: 'I don't know either,' the father told his son. 'Let's both go and learn, as students.'

verses.speaker: Nidagha
verses.setting: Nidagha on ego.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहंकारवशादापदहंकाराद्दुराधयः । अहंकारवशादीहा नाहंकारात्परो रिपुः ॥
verses.translation: From ego come misfortunes; from ego come troubles of the mind; from ego come cravings. There is no enemy greater than ego.
verses.line: Trouble comes from ego, anxiety comes from ego, craving comes from ego. There is no greater enemy.

verses.speaker: Nidagha
verses.setting: Nidagha on his wandering mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा ॥
verses.translation: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.
verses.line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.

verses.speaker: Nidagha
verses.setting: Nidagha on how hard the mind is to master.
verses.sanskrit_display: अप्यब्धिपानान्महतः सुमेरून्मूलनादपि । अपि वह्न्यशनाद्ब्रह्मन्विषमश्चित्तनिग्रहः ॥
verses.translation: Harder than drinking up the ocean, harder than uprooting Mount Meru, harder even than swallowing fire, is the mastery of the mind.
verses.line: Drinking the ocean, uprooting a mountain, swallowing fire: mastering the mind is harder than all of these.

verses.speaker: Nidagha
verses.setting: Nidagha on how everything passes.
verses.sanskrit_display: आपदः क्षणमायान्ति क्षणमायान्ति सम्पदः । क्षणं जन्माथ मरणं सर्वं नश्वरमेव तत् ॥
verses.translation: Misfortunes come in a moment; good fortune comes in a moment; birth in a moment, then death. All of it is passing.
verses.line: Hard times arrive in a moment; good times arrive in a moment. Everything passes.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu begins his answer to Nidagha.
verses.sanskrit_display: मोक्षद्वारे द्वारपालश्चत्वारः परिकीर्तिताः । शमो विचारः सन्तोषश्चतुर्थः साधुसङ्गमः ॥ एकं वा सर्वयत्नेन सर्वमुत्सृज्य संश्रयेत् । एकस्मिन्वशगे यान्ति चत्वारोऽपि वशं गताः ॥
verses.translation: Four gatekeepers are named at the door of freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment, and the company of good people. Take refuge in even one of them with full effort, setting all else aside; when one is won, all four come under your control.
verses.line: Freedom has four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. Win one, and the others follow.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on calm (shama).
verses.sanskrit_display: यानि दुःखानि या तृष्णा दुःसहा ये दुराधयः । शान्तचेतःसु तत्सर्वं तमोऽर्केष्विव नश्यति ॥
verses.translation: Whatever sorrows, whatever craving, whatever unbearable anxieties there are, all of them vanish in calm minds, as darkness vanishes before the sun.
verses.line: Sorrow, craving and unbearable anxiety all vanish in a calm mind, like darkness before the sun.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on calm, continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: न रसायनपानेन न लक्ष्म्यालिङ्गितेन च । न तथा सुखमाप्नोति शमेनान्तर्यथा जनः ॥
verses.translation: Not by drinking elixirs, not by the embrace of Lakshmi, does a person find such happiness as by calm within.
verses.line: No elixir and no fortune brings the happiness that inner calm brings.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on the nature of the mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि चञ्चलताहीनं मनः क्वचन दृश्यते । चञ्चलत्वं मनोधर्मो वह्नेर्धर्मो यथोष्णता ॥
verses.translation: A mind without restlessness is nowhere to be seen. Restlessness is the nature of the mind, as heat is the nature of fire.
verses.line: A mind without restlessness is nowhere to be found. Restlessness is its nature, as heat is fire's.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on self-reliance.
verses.sanskrit_display: तृष्णाग्राहगृहीतानां संसारार्णवपातिनाम् । आवर्तैरूह्यमानानां दूरं स्वमन एव नौः ॥ मनसैव मनश्छित्त्वा पाशं परमबन्धनम् । भवादुत्तारयात्मानं नासावन्येन तार्यते ॥
verses.translation: For those seized by the crocodile of craving and falling into the ocean of worldly life, swept along by its whirlpools, one's own mind is the boat. Cutting with the mind the mind's noose, the strongest of bonds, lift yourself across; no one else can carry you over.
verses.line: Use the mind to cut the mind's own noose. Lift yourself out; no one else can do it for you.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on effort.
verses.sanskrit_display: परमं पौरुषं यत्नमास्थादाय सृद्यमम् । यथाशास्त्रमनुद्वेगमाचरन्को न सिद्धिभाक् ॥
verses.translation: Taking up supreme effort and steady striving, acting according to sound guidance and without anxiety, who would not succeed?
verses.line: With full effort, steady work, good guidance and no panic, who would not succeed?

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on handling the world's give and take.
verses.sanskrit_display: अतो निदाघ तत्त्वज्ञ व्यवहारेषु संसृतेः । नष्टं नष्टमुपेक्षस्व प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपाहर ॥
verses.translation: So, Nidagha, knower of truth, in the dealings of worldly life, let go of whatever is lost, and take up whatever comes.
verses.line: Let what is lost go. Take up what comes.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on removing flaws.
verses.sanskrit_display: तण्डुलस्य यथा चर्म यथा ताम्रस्य कालिमा । नश्यति क्रियया विप्र पुरुषस्य तथा मलम् ॥ जीवस्य तण्डुलस्येव मलं सहजमप्यलम् । नश्यत्येव न सन्देहस्तस्मादुद्योगवान्भवेत् ॥
verses.translation: As the husk of rice and the tarnish of copper are removed by work, so is a person's impurity. A person's impurity, like the husk on rice, may be natural, yet it surely goes; there is no doubt. So be industrious.
verses.line: Rice sheds its husk and copper its tarnish through work. Your flaws can go too, so keep at it.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
