verses.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verses.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verses.sanskrit_display: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verses.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verses.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on the large-hearted person.
verses.sanskrit_display: अयं बन्धुरयं नेति गणना लघुचेतसाम् । उदारचरितानां तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् ॥
verses.translation: 'This one is my own, that one is not': this is how the small-minded reckon. For those of generous character, the whole earth is one family.
verses.line: 'Ours' and 'theirs' is how small minds count. For the large-hearted, the whole earth is family.

verses.speaker: Shakayanya
verses.setting: Verses on the mind near the end of the teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: चित्तमेव हि संसारस्तत्प्रयत्नेन शोधयेत् । यच्चित्तस्तन्मयो भवति गुह्यमेतत्सनातनम् ॥
verses.translation: The mind itself is the world we wander in; so purify it with effort. What one's mind dwells on, that one becomes. This is the ancient secret.
verses.line: Your mind is your world; clean it with care. What your mind dwells on, you become.

verses.speaker: Shakayanya
verses.setting: Verses on the mind, continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: समासक्तं यदा चित्तं जन्तोर्विषयगोचरे । यद्येवं ब्रह्मणि स्यात्तत्को न मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥
verses.translation: If a person's mind were as attached to Brahman as it is attached to the objects of the senses, who would not be freed from bondage?
verses.line: If the mind clung to the highest as tightly as it clings to things, who would not be free?

verses.speaker: Shakayanya
verses.setting: Verses on the mind, concluded.
verses.sanskrit_display: मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः । बन्धाय विषयासक्तं मुक्त्यै निर्विषयं स्मृतमिति ॥
verses.translation: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and of liberation for human beings: attached to objects, it binds; free of objects, it liberates.
verses.line: The mind alone binds or frees us: hooked on things, it binds; free of them, it liberates.

verses.speaker: Mahadeva (Shiva)
verses.setting: Shiva's answer when Maitreya asks for the highest truth.
verses.sanskrit_display: स होवाच महादेवः ॥ देहो देवालयः प्रोक्तः स जीवः केवलः शिवः । त्यजेदज्ञाननिर्माल्यं सोऽहम्भावेन पूजयेत् ॥
verses.translation: Mahadeva said: The body is called a temple; the living being in it is Shiva alone. Cast off ignorance like yesterday's flower offerings, and worship with the sense 'I am He.'
verses.line: Your body is a temple, and the life within it is divine. Toss out ignorance like yesterday's flowers.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras answers Shaunaka's question.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मै स होवाच । द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्मयद्ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति परा चैवापरा च॥ तत्रापरा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्ववेदः शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो ज्योतिषमिति । अथ परा यया तदक्षरमधिगम्यते ॥
verses.translation: He said: two kinds of knowledge are to be known, so the knowers of Brahman say: the higher and the lower. The lower is the four Vedas, phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, metre and astronomy. The higher is that by which the imperishable is reached.
verses.line: There are two kinds of knowledge: the lower, all our learning and skills; the higher, knowing what never perishes.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on what achievement cannot buy.
verses.sanskrit_display: परीक्ष्य लोकान् कर्मचितान् ब्राह्मणो निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन । तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत् समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठम् ॥
verses.translation: Having examined the worlds won by work, a seeker should grow dispassionate: what is not made cannot be gained by what is made. To know it, let him go, fuel in hand, to a teacher who is learned and rooted in Brahman.
verses.line: Having seen what work can win, know this: what is not made cannot be gained by making. Find a teacher.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: The image of the two birds.
verses.sanskrit_display: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते । तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्यो अभिचाकशीति ॥
verses.translation: Two birds, inseparable companions, cling to the same tree. One of them eats the sweet fruit; the other, not eating, simply watches.
verses.line: Two birds, close friends, sit on one tree. One eats the sweet fruit; the other just watches.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on truth as the path.
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । येनाऽऽक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत् सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥
verses.translation: Truth alone wins, not falsehood. By truth the divine path is laid out, by which the sages, their desires fulfilled, travel to where the highest treasure of truth is.
verses.line: Truth alone wins, not falsehood. Truth lays the road that the wise walk.
verses.misuse: Truth wins in the long run; it is not a promise of quick victory.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: A catechism of definitions: 'What is caste?'
verses.sanskrit_display: जातिरिति च न चर्मणो न रक्तस्य न मांसस्य न चास्थिनः । न जातिरात्मनो जातिर्व्यवहारप्रकल्पिता ।
verses.translation: And what is caste? It is not of the skin, nor of the blood, nor of the flesh, nor of the bones. The self has no caste; caste is a convention made for worldly dealings.
verses.line: Caste is not in skin, blood, flesh or bone. The self has no caste; caste is a social convention.

verses.speaker: Sukesha
verses.setting: Sukesha recalls refusing to bluff a prince.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथ हैनं सुकेशा भारद्वाजः पप्रच्छ । भगवन् हिरण्यनाभः कौसल्यो राजपुत्रो मामुपेत्यैतं प्रश्नमपृच्छत । षोडशकलं भारद्वाज पुरुषं वेत्थ । तमहं कुमारमब्रुवं नाहमिमं वेद । यद्यहमिममवेदिषं कथं ते नावक्ष्यमिति । समूलो वा एष परिशुष्यति योऽनृतमभिवदति तस्मान्नार्हम्यनृतं वक्तुम् । स तूष्णीं रथमारुह्य प्रवव्राज । तं त्वा पृच्छामि क्वासौ पुरुष इति ॥
verses.translation: Sukesha asked: 'Sir, Hiranyanabha, a prince of Kosala, came and asked me: do you know the person of sixteen parts? I told the boy: I do not know him. If I knew him, why would I not tell you? Whoever speaks untruth dries up to the root; so I cannot tell a lie. He silently mounted his chariot and left. Now I ask you: where is that person?'
verses.line: I told him plainly, 'I do not know.' Whoever speaks falsehood dries up to the very root.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The Upanishad sets out to measure joy.
verses.sanskrit_display: सैषाऽऽनन्दस्य मीमाꣳसा भवति । युवा स्यात्साधुयुवाऽध्यायकः । आशिष्ठो दृढिष्ठो बलिष्ठः । तस्येयं पृथिवी सर्वा वित्तस्य पूर्णा स्यात् । स एको मानुष आनन्दः । ते ये शतं मानुषा आनन्दाः । स एको मनुष्यगन्धर्वाणामानन्दः । श्रोत्रियस्य चाकामहतस्य ।
verses.translation: Now an inquiry into joy. Let there be a young man, good, well read, quick, firm and strong, and let this whole earth full of wealth be his: that is one measure of human joy. A hundred human joys make one joy of the human gandharvas, and so too is the joy of a learned one untouched by desire.
verses.line: Give a good young man health, learning and the whole earth's wealth: one human joy. The desireless already hold more.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: What falls away for one who knows that joy.
verses.sanskrit_display: एतꣳह वाव न तपति । किमहꣳसाधु नाकरवम् । किमहं पापमकरवमिति ।
verses.translation: Such a one is no longer tormented by the thought: why did I not do good? Why did I do wrong?
verses.line: Free in that joy, one no longer agonises: 'Why didn't I do right? Why did I do wrong?'
verses.misuse: Not a licence to stop caring about harm done; it frees you from self-torment so you can make amends.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Bhrigu's final discovery after four returns to his father.
verses.sanskrit_display: आनन्दो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात्। आनन्दाध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । आनन्देन जातानि जीवन्ति । आनन्दं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । सैषा भार्गवी वारुणी विद्या । परमे व्योमन्प्रतिष्ठिता ।स य एवं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति ।
verses.translation: He understood that joy is Brahman. From joy these beings are born, by joy they live once born, and into joy they enter at death. This is the wisdom of Bhrigu and Varuna, established in the highest space. Whoever knows this becomes established.
verses.line: At last Bhrigu saw: from joy all beings are born, by joy they live, into joy they return.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The graduation address as a student leaves to start family life.
verses.sanskrit_display: वेदमनूच्याचार्योन्तेवासिनमनुशास्ति । सत्यं वद । धर्मं चर । स्वाध्यायान्मा प्रमदः ।
verses.translation: Having taught the Veda, the teacher instructs the student: Speak the truth. Practise what is right. Do not neglect your study.
verses.line: Speak the truth. Do what is right. Never stop learning.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The most quoted lines of the graduation address.
verses.sanskrit_display: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव ।
verses.translation: Do not neglect your duties to the gods and the ancestors. Let your mother be a god to you. Let your father be a god to you. Let your teacher be a god to you. Let your guest be a god to you.
verses.line: Treat your mother as divine, your father as divine, your teacher as divine, your guest as divine.
verses.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean accepting mistreatment or giving up your own conscience.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The graduation address on giving.
verses.sanskrit_display: नो इतराणि । ये के चारुमच्छ्रेयाꣳसो ब्राह्मणाः । तेषां त्वयाऽऽसनेन प्रश्वसितव्यम् । श्रद्धया देयम् । अश्रद्धयाऽदेयम् । श्रिया देयम् । ह्रिया देयम् । भिया देयम् । संविदा देयम् ।
verses.translation: Not the other things. Whoever are better than us, offer them a seat and refreshment. Give with faith; do not give without faith. Give generously. Give with modesty. Give with respect. Give with understanding.
verses.line: Give with faith, not without it. Give generously, give modestly, give with respect, give with understanding.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The teacher's advice for when the rules run out.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथ यदि ते कर्मविचिकित्सा वा वृत्तविचिकित्सा वा स्यात् ॥ ये तत्र ब्राह्मणाः संमर्शिनः । युक्ता आयुक्ताः । अलूक्षा धर्मकामाः स्युः । यथा ते तत्र वर्तेरन् । तथा तत्र वर्तेथाः । अथाभ्याख्यातेषु । ये तत्र ब्राह्मणाः संमर्शिनः । युक्ता आयुक्ताः । अलूक्षा धर्मकामाः स्युः । यथा ते तेषु वर्तेरन् । तथा तेषु वर्तेथाः । एष आदेशः । एष उपदेशः ।
verses.translation: Now, if you are ever unsure about an action or about conduct, look to the thoughtful people there: devoted, independent, not harsh, lovers of what is right. As they would act, so should you act. And towards people under accusation, act as such people would. This is the instruction, this is the teaching.
verses.line: When unsure what to do, ask how thoughtful, gentle, fair-minded people would act, and do that.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Advice on keeping up practice.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथापकृष्टं शैवालं क्षणमात्रं न तिष्ठति । आवृणोति तथा माया प्राज्ञं वापि पराङ्मुखम् ॥
verses.translation: As moss pushed aside does not stay away even a moment, so illusion covers again even a wise person who turns away.
verses.line: Push moss aside and it closes back at once. So confusion returns to the wise who look away.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: One of a series of marks of a person free while living.
verses.sanskrit_display: साधुभिः पूज्यमानेऽस्मिन्पीड्यमानेऽपि दुर्जनैः । समभावो भवेद्यस्य स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥
verses.translation: Whether honoured by the good or harassed by the wicked, one who stays the same is called free while living.
verses.line: Praised by the good or harassed by the cruel, the free person stays the same.
verses.misuse: Staying even does not mean staying in a harmful situation.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: On past actions already in motion.
verses.sanskrit_display: ज्ञानोदयात्पुरारब्धं कर्म ज्ञानान्न नश्यति । अदत्त्वा स्वफलं लक्ष्यमुद्दिश्योत्सृष्टबाणवत् ॥ व्याघ्रबुद्ध्या विनिर्मुक्तो बाणः पश्चात्तु गोमतौ । न तिष्ठति भिनत्त्येव लक्ष्यं वेगेन निर्भरम् ॥
verses.translation: Action that began before knowledge dawned is not destroyed by knowledge without yielding its fruit, like an arrow released at its target. An arrow loosed at what looked like a tiger does not stop when you see it is a cow; it flies on and strikes the target with force.
verses.line: An arrow already shot does not stop because you changed your mind. Past actions run their course.
verses.misuse: Facing consequences is not punishment for being bad; it is how actions work.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The second birth: raising a child.
verses.sanskrit_display: स यत्कुमारं जन्मनोऽग्रेऽधिभावयत्यात्मानमेव तद्भावयत्येषं लोकानां सन्तत्या । एवं सन्तता हीमे लोकास्तदस्य द्वितीयं जन्म ॥
verses.translation: When he cares for the child from birth onward, he is caring for himself, for the continuation of these worlds; that is how they continue. That is his second birth.
verses.line: Caring for your child, you care for yourself. Through them you are born a second time.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The third birth: the parent's passing.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोऽस्यायमात्मा पुण्येभ्यः कर्मभ्यः प्रतिधीयते । अथास्यायामितर आत्मा कृतकृत्यो वयोगतः प्रैति । स इतः प्रयन्नेव पुनर्जायते तदस्य तृतीयं जन्म ॥
verses.translation: This self of his, the child, is put in his place to carry on good works. Then his other self, the parent, having done what was to be done and grown old, departs; departing from here, he is born again. That is his third birth.
verses.line: The child takes up the good work; the parent, duties done and years full, departs and is born again.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Yajnavalkya's teaching to Maitreyi on love.
verses.sanskrit_display: स होवाच न वा अरे पत्युः कामाय पतिः प्रियो भवत्यात्मनस्तु कामाय पतिः प्रियो भवति । न वा अरे जायायै कामाय जाया प्रिया भवत्यात्मनस्तु कामाय जाया प्रिया भवति । न वा अरे पुत्राणां कामाय पुत्राः प्रिया भवन्त्यात्मनस्तु कामाय पुत्राः प्रिया भवन्ति ।
verses.translation: He said: 'It is not for the love of the husband that a husband is dear, but for the love of the self that a husband is dear. It is not for the love of the wife that a wife is dear, but for the love of the self. It is not for the love of the sons that sons are dear, but for the love of the self that sons are dear.'
verses.line: A husband is not dear for the husband's sake, but for the self within. So too wife and children.
verses.misuse: This is not 'love is selfish'; it says we love the one self shining in the other.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: At King Janaka's debate, Kahola asks about the self.
verses.sanskrit_display: या ह्येव पुत्रैषणा सा वित्तैषणा या वित्तैषणा सा लोकैषणोभे ह्येते एषणे एव भवतस्तस्माद्ब्राह्मणः पाण्डित्यं निर्विद्य बाल्येन तिष्ठासेत् । बाल्यं च पाण्डित्यं च निर्विद्याथ मुनिरमौनं च मौनं च निर्विद्याथ ब्राह्मणः ।
verses.translation: The desire for sons is the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is the desire for worlds; both are just desires. So a wise man, having done with learning, should seek to live like a child. Having done with both childlike simplicity and learning, he becomes a sage; having done with both silence and its absence, he becomes a true knower.
verses.line: Wanting children, wanting money, wanting status: it is one desire. Learn, then live with a child's simplicity.

verses.speaker: Gargi Vachaknavi
verses.setting: Gargi rises a second time in a hall full of men to question the champion.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा होवाचाहं वै त्वा याज्ञवल्क्य यथा काश्यो वा वैदेहो वोग्रपुत्र उज्ज्यं धनुरधिज्यं कृत्वा द्वौ बाणवन्तौ सपत्नातिव्याधिनौ हस्ते कृत्वोपोत्तिष्ठेदेवमेवाहं त्वा द्वाभ्यां प्रश्नाभ्यामुपोदस्थाम् । तौ मे ब्रूहीति । पृच्छ गार्गीति ॥
verses.translation: She said: 'Yajnavalkya, as a warrior from Kashi or Videha strings his unstrung bow and rises with two piercing arrows in hand, so I rise before you with two questions. Answer them for me.' 'Ask, Gargi.'
verses.line: As a warrior strings her bow with two sharp arrows, Gargi rose before the assembly with two questions.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Yajnavalkya's answer to Gargi.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो वा एतदक्षरं गार्ग्यविदित्वाऽस्मिꣳल्लोके जुहोति यजते तपस्तप्यते बहूनि वर्षसहस्राण्यन्तवदेवास्य तद्भवति लोको भवति यो वा एतदक्षरं गार्ग्यविदित्वाऽस्माल्लोकात्प्रैति स कृपणोऽथ य एतदक्षरं गार्गि विदित्वाऽस्माल्लोकात्प्रैति स ब्राह्मणः ॥
verses.translation: Gargi, whoever in this world performs rituals, makes offerings and practises austerity for many thousands of years without knowing this imperishable, all that work of his comes to an end. Whoever leaves this world without knowing this imperishable is pitiable. Whoever leaves this world knowing it is a true knower.
verses.line: Years of effort without knowing what lasts all come to an end. To leave life without knowing it is poverty.

verses.speaker: Gargi Vachaknavi
verses.setting: Gargi, having tested Yajnavalkya, addresses the hall.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा होवाच ब्राह्मणा भगवन्तस्तदेव बहु मन्येध्वं यदस्मान्नमस्कारेण मुच्येध्वं न वै जातु युष्माकमिमं कश्चिद्ब्रह्मोद्यं जेतेति ततो ह वाचक्नव्युपरराम ॥
verses.translation: She said: 'Venerable brahmins, count it a great thing if you get away from him with a bow. None of you will ever defeat him in talk about Brahman.' Then Gargi Vachaknavi fell silent.
verses.line: Gargi told the assembly: none of you will beat him; be glad to bow and leave.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Yajnavalkya ends the debate with verses comparing a person to a tree.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्वृक्षो वृक्णो रोहति मूलान्नवतरः पुनः मर्त्यः स्विन्मृत्युना वृक्णः कस्मान्मूलात्प्ररोहति ॥
verses.translation: If a tree is cut down, it grows again from its root, newer still. When a mortal is cut down by death, from what root does he grow again?
verses.line: A felled tree sprouts again from its root. When death fells a person, from what root do they grow?

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Yajnavalkya on what happens at death.
verses.sanskrit_display: तद्यथा तृणजलायुका तृणस्यान्तं गत्वाऽन्यमाक्रममाक्रम्यात्मानमुपसꣳहरत्येवमेवायमात्मेदꣳ शरीरं निहत्याविद्यां गमयित्वाऽन्यमाक्रममाक्रम्याऽऽत्मानमुपसꣳहरति ॥
verses.translation: As a caterpillar, reaching the end of a blade of grass, takes hold of another and draws itself over to it, so this self, having left this body behind and let go of ignorance, takes hold of another support and draws itself over.
verses.line: Like a caterpillar at a grass tip, the self lets go of one body only after grasping the next.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Yajnavalkya on death, continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: तद्यथा पेशस्कारी पेशसो मात्रामपादायान्यन्नवतरं कल्याणतरꣳ रूपं तनुत एवमेवायमात्मेदꣳ शरीरं निहत्याविद्यां गमयित्वाऽन्यन्नवतरं कल्याणतरꣳ रूपं कुरुते पित्र्यं वा गान्धर्वं वा दैवं वा प्राजापत्यं वा ब्राह्मं वाऽन्येषां वा भूतानाम् ॥
verses.translation: As a goldsmith takes a piece of gold and fashions another form, newer and more beautiful, so this self, leaving this body behind and letting go of ignorance, makes for itself another form, newer and more beautiful.
verses.line: As a goldsmith reshapes old gold into a newer, lovelier form, so the self takes a new and finer form.

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Verses on knowing the self.
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मानं चेद्विजानीयादयमस्मीति पूरुषः किमिच्छन्कस्य कामाय शरीरमनुसञ्ज्वरेत् ॥
verses.translation: If a person knew the self as 'I am this', then wanting what, and for whose sake, would he fret after the body?
verses.line: Once you know who you really are, what is left to want, and for whose sake would you fret?

verses.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verses.setting: Yajnavalkya's closing words to Janaka.
verses.sanskrit_display: तदेतदृचाभ्युक्तम् । एष नित्यो महिमा ब्राह्मणस्य न वर्धते कर्मणा नो कनीयान् । तस्यैव स्यात् पदवित्तं विदित्वा न लिप्यते कर्मणा पापकेनेति । तस्मादेवंविच्छान्तो दान्त उपरतस्तितिक्षुः समाहितो भूत्वाऽऽत्मन्येवाऽऽत्मानं पश्यति सर्वमात्मानं पश्यति
verses.translation: This is said in a verse: This eternal greatness of the knower neither grows by deeds nor shrinks. Let one know its nature; knowing it, one is not stained by wrong action. So one who knows this, calm, self-controlled, withdrawn, patient and collected, sees the self in himself and sees everything as the self.
verses.line: Calm, self-controlled, quiet within, patient and collected: that is how you come to see clearly.
verses.misuse: Patience here is inner steadiness, not tolerating mistreatment.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The famous verse on fullness that opens Book 5.
verses.sanskrit_display: ॐ पूर्णमदः पूर्णमिदं पूर्णात्पूर्णमुदच्यते । पूर्णस्य पूर्णमादाय पूर्णमेवावशिष्यते । ॐ३ खं ब्रह्म खं पुराणं वायुरं खमिति ह स्माऽऽह कौरव्यायणीपुत्रो । वेदोऽयम्ं ब्राह्मणा विदुर्वेदैनेन यद्वेदितव्यम् ॥
verses.translation: That is whole; this is whole. From the whole, the whole arises. Taking the whole from the whole, the whole remains. Om. Brahman is space, the ancient space, the airy space, said the son of Kauravyayani. This is the Veda the brahmins know; by it one knows what is to be known.
verses.line: That is whole, this is whole. Take the whole from the whole, and the whole remains.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The creation story: the first being, alone.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोऽबिभेत् तस्मादेकाकी बिभेति । स हायमीक्षां चक्रे यन्मदन्यन्नास्ति कस्मान्नु बिभेमीति । तत एवास्य भयं वीयाय । कस्माद्ध्यभेष्यत् द्वितीयाद्वै भयं भवति ॥
verses.translation: He was afraid; that is why one who is alone is afraid. Then he thought: 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' At that his fear left him. What was there to fear? Fear arises only from a second.
verses.line: Alone, he was afraid. Then he asked: since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?

verses.speaker: Seer (quoting Yajnavalkya)
verses.setting: The first being, alone, longs for another.
verses.sanskrit_display: स वै नैव रेमे तस्मादेकाकी न रमते । स द्वितीयमैच्छत् स हैतावानास यथा स्त्रीपुमाꣳसौ सम्परिष्वक्तौ । स इममेवाऽऽत्मानं द्वेधाऽपातयत् । ततः पतिश्च पत्नी चाभवताम् । तस्मादिदमर्धबृगलमिव स्व इति ह स्माऽऽह याज्ञवल्क्यस्तस्मादयमाकाशः स्त्रिया पूर्यत एव । ताꣳ समभवत् ततो मनुष्या अजायन्त ॥
verses.translation: He found no delight; that is why one who is alone finds no delight. He longed for a second. He became as large as a man and woman embracing, and split himself in two; from that came husband and wife. So, said Yajnavalkya, each of us is like a half. That is why this space is filled by a wife.
verses.line: Alone, he found no joy and longed for another. So, said Yajnavalkya, each of us is like a half.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: How a householder becomes a 'world' for others.
verses.sanskrit_display: यन्मनुष्यान्वासयते यदेभ्योऽशनं ददाति तेन मनुष्याणामथ यत्पशुभ्यस्तृणोदकं विन्दति तेन पशूनां यदस्य गृहेषु श्वापदा वयाꣳस्या पिपीलिकाभ्य उपजीवन्ति तेन तेषां लोको
verses.translation: By housing people and giving them food, he becomes a world for people. By finding grass and water for animals, he becomes a world for animals. When beasts, birds and even ants live off his house, he becomes a world for them.
verses.line: Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A line from the opening teaching on Om.
verses.sanskrit_display: तेनोभौ कुरुतो यश्चैतदेवं वेद यश्च न वेद । नाना तु विद्या चाविद्या च यदेव विद्यया करोति श्रद्धयोपनिषदा तदेव वीर्यवत्तरं भवतीति खल्वेतस्यैवाक्षरस्योपव्याख्यानं भवति ॥
verses.translation: Both the one who knows and the one who does not know perform the act. But knowledge and ignorance are different. Whatever is done with knowledge, with faith and with inner understanding becomes more powerful.
verses.line: Whatever you do with knowledge, faith and real understanding becomes far more powerful.

verses.speaker: Ghora Angirasa
verses.setting: Life described as a sacrifice; these are its true gifts.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथ यत्तपो दानमार्जवमहिꣳसा सत्यवचनमिति ता अस्य दक्षिणाः ॥
verses.translation: And discipline, generosity, straightforwardness, non-harming and truthful speech: these are its gifts to the priests.
verses.line: Self-discipline, giving, honesty, non-harm and truthful speech: these are the real offerings of a life.

verses.speaker: Satyakama
verses.setting: The teacher asks the boy his lineage.
verses.sanskrit_display: तꣳ होवाच किंगोत्रो नु सोम्यासीति स होवाच नाहमेतद्वेद भो यद्गोत्रोऽहमस्म्यपृच्छं मातरꣳ सा मा प्रत्यब्रवीद्बह्वहं चरन्ती परिचरिणी यौवने त्वामलभे साहमेतन्न वेद यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि जबाला तु नामाहमस्मि सत्यकामो नाम त्वमसीति सोऽहꣳ सत्यकामो जाबालोऽस्मि भो इति ॥
verses.translation: He asked him, 'What is your lineage, dear one?' He said, 'I do not know my lineage, sir. I asked my mother, and she told me: in my youth I moved about a great deal as a serving woman and had you; I do not know your lineage. My name is Jabala and yours is Satyakama. So I am Satyakama Jabala, sir.'
verses.line: Asked his lineage, the boy did not invent one. He repeated his mother's words: 'I am Satyakama Jabala.'

verses.speaker: Satyakama
verses.setting: Satyakama returns, taught along the way by a bull, fire, a swan and a diver bird.
verses.sanskrit_display: ब्रह्मविदिव वै सोम्य भासि को नु त्वानुशशासेत्यन्ये मनुष्येभ्य इति ह प्रतिजज्ञे भगवाꣳस्त्वेव मे कामे ब्रूयात् ॥ श्रुतꣳह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्य आचार्याद्धैव विद्या विदिता साधिष्ठं प्रापतीति तस्मै हैतदेवोवाचात्र ह न किंचन वीयायेति वीयायेति ॥
verses.translation: 'You shine like one who knows Brahman, dear one. Who has taught you?' 'Others than men,' he admitted. 'But I wish that you, sir, would teach me, for I have heard from people like you that knowledge learned from a teacher best reaches its goal.' So the teacher taught him that very knowledge, and nothing was left out.
verses.line: Though nature had taught him, he still asked his teacher: knowledge learned from a teacher goes deepest.

verses.speaker: Prajapati
verses.setting: The senses quarrel over which of them is greatest.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथ ह प्राणा अहꣳश्रेयसि व्यूदिरेऽहꣳश्रेयानस्म्यहꣳ श्रेयानस्मीति ॥ ते ह प्राणाः प्रजापतिं पितरमेत्योचुर्भगवन्को नः श्रेष्ठ इति तान्होवाच यस्मिन्व उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं पापिष्ठतरमिव दृश्येत स वः श्रेष्ठ इति ॥
verses.translation: The senses quarrelled about who was best, each saying, 'I am best, I am best.' They went to their father Prajapati and asked, 'Sir, who is the best of us?' He said, 'The one whose departure leaves the body looking worst off is the best among you.'
verses.line: The senses argued over who was greatest. The answer: the one whose absence hurts the whole body most.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: Shvetaketu returns humiliated by a king's questions and blames his father.
verses.sanskrit_display: पञ्च मा राजन्यबन्धुः प्रश्नानप्राक्षीत्तेषां नैकंचनाशकं विवक्तुमिति स होवाच यथा मा त्वं तदैतानवदो यथाहमेषां नैकंचन वेद यद्यहमिमानवेदिष्यं कथं ते नावक्ष्यमिति ॥
verses.translation: 'That fellow of the warrior class asked me five questions, and I could not answer even one.' The father said, 'As you have put them to me, I do not know a single one of them. If I had known them, how could I not have told you?'
verses.line: The father admitted, 'I don't know one of these answers. If I knew, wouldn't I have taught you?'

verses.speaker: Gautama (Uddalaka)
verses.setting: The father goes to the king to learn; the king offers wealth instead.
verses.sanskrit_display: स होवाच तवैव राजन्मानुषं वित्तं यामेव कुमारस्यान्ते वाचमभाषथास्तामेव मे ब्रूहीति स ह कृच्छ्री बभूव ॥
verses.translation: He said, 'Let human wealth remain with you, O king. Tell me the very words you spoke to my son.' The king was troubled.
verses.line: Offered wealth, the father said, 'Keep your riches. Just teach me what you asked my son.'

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: Five learned householders come to Uddalaka for teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: स ह सम्पादयांचकार प्रक्ष्यन्ति मामिमे महाशाला महाश्रोत्रियास्तेभ्यो न सर्वमिव प्रतिपत्स्ये हन्ताहमन्यमभ्यनुशासानीति ॥
verses.translation: He thought: 'These great householders, great scholars, will question me, and I will not be able to answer everything. Let me direct them to another teacher.'
verses.line: Knowing he could not answer everything, the sage sent his visitors to a better teacher.

verses.speaker: The visiting scholars
verses.setting: The king offers gifts; the visitors steer back to why they came.
verses.sanskrit_display: ते होचुर्येन हैवार्थेन पुरुषश्चरेत्तꣳहैव वदेदात्मानमेवेमं वैश्वानरꣳ सम्प्रत्यध्येषि तमेव नौ ब्रूहीति ॥
verses.translation: They said: 'A person should state the very purpose for which he has come. You know the universal self; teach that to us.'
verses.line: State plainly the purpose you came for.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: After a fifteen-day fast Shvetaketu cannot recall his learning; after eating, he can.
verses.sanskrit_display: तꣳ होवाच यथा सोम्य महतोऽभ्याहितस्यैकमङ्गारं खद्योतमात्रं परिशिष्टं तं तृणैरुपसमाधाय प्राज्वलयेत्तेन ततोऽपि बहु दहेत् ॥ एवꣳ सोम्य ते षोडशानां कलानामेका कलातिशिष्टाभूत्सान्नेनोपसमाहिता प्राज्वाली तयैतर्हि वेदाननुभवस्यन्नमयꣳहि सोम्य मन आपोमयः प्राणस्तेजोमयी वागिति तद्धास्य विजज्ञाविति विजज्ञाविति ॥
verses.translation: 'As a single ember the size of a firefly, left from a great fire, can be fed with straw and made to blaze and burn far more, so, dear one, of your sixteen parts one was left. Fed with food, it blazed up, and with it you now recall the Vedas. For the mind is made of food, breath of water, speech of heat.' And he understood.
verses.line: A tiny ember, fed with straw, blazes again. Fed well, a depleted mind remembers everything.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: The lesson of the rivers.
verses.sanskrit_display: इमाः सोम्य नद्यः पुरस्तात्प्राच्यः स्यन्दन्ते पश्चात्प्रतीच्यस्ताः समुद्रात्समुद्रमेवापियन्ति स समुद्र एव भवति ता यथा तत्र न विदुरियमहमस्मीयमहमस्मीति ॥
verses.translation: These rivers, dear one, flow, the eastern ones to the east and the western ones to the west. From the sea they come and into the sea they go, and become the sea itself. There they do not know, 'I am this river, I am that one.'
verses.line: Rivers flowing east and west all become the sea, and no longer say 'I am this one.'

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: The lesson of the dying man.
verses.sanskrit_display: पुरुषꣳ सोम्योतोपतापिनं ज्ञातयः पर्युपासते जानासि मां जानासि मामिति तस्य यावन्न वाङ्मनसि सम्पद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस्तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायां तावज्जानाति ॥
verses.translation: Relatives gather around a man who is gravely ill and ask, 'Do you know me? Do you know me?' As long as his speech has not merged into mind, mind into breath, breath into heat and heat into the highest, he knows them.
verses.line: Family gathers at the bedside asking, 'Do you know me?' He knows them, until speech returns into mind.

verses.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verses.setting: The last lesson: the ordeal of the heated axe.
verses.sanskrit_display: पुरुषꣳ सोम्योत हस्तगृहीतमानयन्त्यपहार्षीत्स्तेयमकार्षीत्परशुमस्मै तपतेति स यदि तस्य कर्ता भवति तत एवानृतमात्मानं कुरुते सोऽनृताभिसंधोऽनृतेनात्मानमन्तर्धाय परशुं तप्तं प्रतिगृह्णाति स दह्यतेऽथ हन्यते ॥ अथ यदि तस्याकर्ता भवति ततेव सत्यमात्मानं कुरुते स सत्याभिसन्धः सत्येनात्मानमन्तर्धाय परशुं तप्तं प्रतिगृह्णाति सन दह्यतेऽथ मुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: They bring a man with his hands bound: 'He has stolen, he has committed theft; heat the axe for him.' If he did it, he makes himself false; covering himself with falsehood, he grasps the heated axe, is burned and is punished. If he did not do it, he makes himself true; covering himself with truth, he grasps the heated axe, is not burned and is released.
verses.line: Covered in truth, the accused held the red-hot axe and was not burned. The liar was.
verses.misuse: An ancient ordeal used as a picture of how truth protects; not a literal test.

verses.speaker: Sanatkumara
verses.setting: The next step: action rests on happiness.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा वै सुखं लभतेऽथ करोति नासुखं लब्ध्वा करोति सुखमेव लब्ध्वा करोति सुखं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यमिति सुखं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verses.translation: When one finds happiness, one acts. No one acts without finding happiness; only by finding happiness does one act. So happiness itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand happiness.'
verses.line: We act only when we find joy in it. Understand the joy, and action follows.

verses.speaker: Sanatkumara
verses.setting: Sanatkumara on what people call greatness.
verses.sanskrit_display: गोअश्वमिह महिमेत्याचक्षते हस्तिहिरण्यं दासभार्यं क्षेत्राण्यायतनानीति नाहमेवं ब्रवीमि ब्रवीमीति होवाचान्योह्यन्यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठित इति ॥
verses.translation: Here people call cows and horses greatness, elephants and gold, servants and wives, fields and houses. I do not say so, I do not say so, for each of these rests on something else.
verses.line: People call cattle, gold, land and houses greatness. I don't. Each of those depends on something else.

verses.speaker: Virochana
verses.setting: After 32 years with Prajapati, Virochana goes home with a half-truth.
verses.sanskrit_display: विरोचनोऽसुराञ्जगाम तेभ्यो हैतामुपनिषदं प्रोवाचात्मैवेह महय्य आत्मा परिचर्य आत्मानमेवेह महयन्नात्मानं परिचरन्नुभौ लोकाववाप्नोतीमं चामुं चेति ॥
verses.translation: Virochana, content at heart, went to the asuras and taught them this teaching: 'The body alone is to be worshipped here, the body alone is to be tended. Worshipping the body and tending it, one wins both worlds, this one and the next.'
verses.line: Virochana taught his people: only the body matters; pamper it and you win everything.
verses.misuse: This is the mistaken teaching in the story; caring for your health is fine.

verses.speaker: Indra
verses.setting: Indra, unlike Virochana, stops halfway home with a doubt.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथ हेन्द्रोऽप्राप्यैव देवानेतद्भयं ददर्श यथैव खल्वयमस्मिञ्छरीरे साध्वलंकृते साध्वलंकृतो भवति सुवसने सुवसनः परिष्कृते परिष्कृत एवमेवायमस्मिन्नन्धेऽन्धो भवति स्रामे स्रामः परिवृक्णे परिवृक्णोऽस्यैव शरीरस्य नाशमन्वेष नश्यति नाहमत्र भोग्यं पश्यामीति ॥
verses.translation: But Indra, before he reached the gods, saw this danger: 'Just as this self is well adorned when the body is well adorned, well dressed when it is well dressed, so it will be blind when the body is blind, lame when it is lame, crippled when it is crippled, and will perish when the body perishes. I see no good in this.'
verses.line: Indra stopped halfway home: if I am the body, I go blind when it does. There's no good in this.

verses.speaker: Prajapati
verses.setting: Indra returns with his doubt.
verses.sanskrit_display: एवमेवैष मघवन्निति होवाचैतं त्वेव ते भूयोऽनुव्याख्यास्यामि वसापराणि द्वात्रिꣳशतं वर्षाणीति स हापराणि द्वात्रिꣳशतं वर्षाण्युवास तस्मै होवाच ॥
verses.translation: 'So it is, Maghavan,' he said. 'I will explain it to you further. Live here another thirty-two years.' He lived there another thirty-two years.
verses.line: 'You are right,' his teacher said. 'I will explain more. Stay another thirty-two years.' Indra stayed.

verses.speaker: Prajapati
verses.setting: Prajapati's final teaching to Indra.
verses.sanskrit_display: मघवन्मर्त्यं वा इदꣳ शरीरमात्तं मृत्युना तदस्यामृतस्याशरीरस्यात्मनोऽधिष्ठानमात्तो वै सशरीरः प्रियाप्रियाभ्यां न वै सशरीरस्य सतः प्रियाप्रिययोरपहतिरस्त्यशरीरं वाव सन्तं न प्रियाप्रिये स्पृशतः ॥
verses.translation: Maghavan, this body is mortal, held by death. It is the dwelling of the deathless, bodiless self. The embodied self is held by pleasure and pain; for one in the body there is no escape from pleasure and pain. But pleasure and pain do not touch one who is free of the body.
verses.line: As long as you take yourself to be the body, pleasure and pain will keep their grip.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Closing verse of the Chhandogya: the shape of a good householder's life.
verses.sanskrit_display: तधैतद्ब्रह्मा प्रजापतयै उवाच प्रजापतिर्मनवे मनुः प्रजाभ्यः आचार्यकुलाद्वेदमधीत्य यथाविधानं गुरोः कर्मातिशेषेणाभिसमावृत्य कुटुम्बे शुचौ देशे स्वाध्यायमधीयानो धर्मिकान्विदधदात्मनि सर्वैन्द्रियाणि सम्प्रतिष्ठाप्याहिꣳसन्सर्व भूतान्यन्यत्र तीर्थेभ्यः स खल्वेवं वर्तयन्यावदायुषं ब्रह्मलोकमभिसम्पद्यते न च पुनरावर्तते न च पुनरावर्तते ॥
verses.translation: Brahma told this to Prajapati, Prajapati to Manu, Manu to the people. One who has studied the Veda in a teacher's house, doing the teacher's work in his spare time, returns home, lives as a householder in a clean place, keeps studying, raises virtuous children, draws all his senses into the self, and harms no living being except where sanctioned: living this way all his life, he reaches the world of Brahman and does not return.
verses.line: Keep learning, keep a clean home, raise good children, gather your senses inward, and harm no living being.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A prayer near the end of the Isha, spoken as life draws to a close.
verses.sanskrit_display: हिरण्मयेन पात्रेण सत्यस्यापिहितं मुखम् । तत्त्वं पूषन्नपावृणु सत्यधर्माय दृष्टये ॥
verses.translation: The face of truth is covered by a golden vessel. Uncover it, O Pushan, so that I, who hold to truth, may see.
verses.line: Truth's face is hidden behind a golden lid. Lift it, so I can see what is real.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Closing prayer of the Isha.
verses.sanskrit_display: अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् । युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमौक्तिं विधेम ॥
verses.translation: O Agni, lead us by the good path to true wealth, O god who knows all our ways. Keep crooked wrongdoing away from us. We offer you our fullest words of reverence.
verses.line: Lead us by the good path. Keep crooked dealing far from us.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Continues verse 6 on seeing oneness.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मैवाभूद्विजानतः । तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वमनुपश्यतः ॥
verses.translation: For the one who knows, in whom all beings have become the self, what confusion, what sorrow can there be, seeing oneness everywhere?
verses.line: When you see the same life in everyone, where is there room for confusion or grief?

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Nachiketa's first boon: that his father be at peace and not angry with him.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथापुरस्ताद्भविताप्रतीत औदालकिरारुणिर्मत्प्रसृष्टः । सुखꣳरात्रीःशयितावीतमन्युस्त्वांददृशिवान्मृत्युमुखात्प्रमुक्तम्॥
verses.translation: Your father, Auddalaki Aruni, will know you as before, by my leave. He will sleep peacefully at night, his anger gone, when he sees you released from the jaws of death.
verses.line: Your father will know you again, sleep well at night, his anger gone, when he sees you home.

verses.speaker: Nachiketa
verses.setting: A boy watches his father give away worn-out cows as a show of piety.
verses.sanskrit_display: स होवाच पितर तत कस्मै मां दास्यसीति। द्वितीयं तृतीयं तꣳहोवाच मृत्युवे वा ददामीति ॥
verses.translation: He said to his father, 'Father, to whom will you give me?' He asked a second time, and a third. His father said, 'To Death I give you.'
verses.line: A boy asks his father three times, 'To whom will you give me?' The angry answer: 'To Death.'

verses.speaker: Nachiketa
verses.setting: Nachiketa reflects as he leaves for Death's house.
verses.sanskrit_display: बहूनामेमि प्रथमो बहूनामेमि मध्यमः । किꣳस्त्रिद्यमस्य कर्तव्यं यन्मयाद्य करिष्यति ॥
verses.translation: Among many I go first; among many I go in the middle. What can Yama have to do that he will do with me today?
verses.line: Among many I have gone first, among many in the middle. What can Death really do with me today?

verses.speaker: Nachiketa
verses.setting: Nachiketa urges his regretful father to keep his word.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य यथा परे । सस्यमिव मत्यैः पच्यते सस्यमिवाजायते पुनः ॥
verses.translation: Look back at how those before us fared; look ahead at how those after us will fare. Like grain a mortal ripens, and like grain is born again.
verses.line: Look at those before us and those to come: like grain, we ripen, fall and spring up again.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Yama on the self within changing bodies.
verses.sanskrit_display: अशरीरँ शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् । महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥
verses.translation: Knowing the self as bodiless within bodies, steady among the unsteady, great and all-pervading, the wise one does not grieve.
verses.line: Knowing what stays steady inside all that changes, the wise do not grieve.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Yama on how the self is found.
verses.sanskrit_display: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यः तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूꣳ स्वाम् ॥
verses.translation: This self is not reached by lectures, nor by intellect, nor by much learning. It is reached by the one it chooses; to that one the self reveals its own form.
verses.line: Not by lectures, intellect or much study is the self reached; it opens to the one it chooses.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Yama on what blocks understanding.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाविरतो दुश्चरितामाशान्तो ना समाहितः । नाशान्त मानसो वापि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात् ॥
verses.translation: One who has not turned away from wrong conduct, who is not calm, not collected, whose mind is not at peace, cannot reach it by cleverness alone.
verses.line: No amount of cleverness helps if you have not stopped wrong habits and calmed your mind.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: The chariot image continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥
verses.translation: For one who lacks understanding, whose mind is never held steady, the senses run out of control like a driver's wild horses. For one who has understanding, whose mind is always steady, the senses obey like good horses.
verses.line: Without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses; with a steady mind, they run like trained ones.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Follows the turn inward.
verses.sanskrit_display: पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बालास्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् । अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते ॥
verses.translation: The immature chase outward pleasures and walk into the wide-spread net of death. The wise, knowing what is deathless, do not look for the lasting among things that pass.
verses.line: The immature chase outward pleasures into death's wide net. The wise don't seek permanence in passing things.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Yama on the inner self and the world's pain.
verses.sanskrit_display: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुः न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः । एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥
verses.translation: Just as the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by the flaws the eyes see outside, so the one inner self of all beings is not stained by the sorrow of the world; it stands apart.
verses.line: The sun shows every flaw yet stays untouched. Your deepest self stays untouched by the world's sorrow.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Yama on the light behind all lights.
verses.sanskrit_display: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥
verses.translation: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine, much less this fire. When that shines, everything shines after it; by its light all this is lit.
verses.line: There the sun does not shine, nor moon or stars. By its light alone, everything else shines.

verses.speaker: Yama
verses.setting: Near the close of Yama's teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः । अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम् ॥
verses.translation: When all the knots of the heart are cut, here in this life, the mortal becomes immortal. This much is the whole teaching.
verses.line: When the knots of the heart are cut, even here, a mortal becomes deathless. That is the whole teaching.

verses.speaker: Indra
verses.setting: Indra on the knower behind experience.
verses.sanskrit_display: न वाचं विजिज्ञासीत वक्तारं विद्यान्न गन्धं विजिज्ञासीत घ्रातारं विद्यान्न रूपं विजिज्ञासीत रूपविदं विद्यान्न शब्दं विजिज्ञासीत श्रोतारं विद्यान्नान्नरसं विजिज्ञासीतान्नरसविज्ञातारं विद्यान्न कर्म विजिज्ञासीत कर्तारं विद्यान्न सुखदुःखे विजिज्ञासीत सुखदुःखयोर्विज्ञातारं विद्यान्नानन्दं रतिं प्रजातिं विजिज्ञासीतानन्दस्य रतेः प्रजातेर्विज्ञातारं विद्यान्नेत्यां विजिज्ञासीतैतारं विद्यान्न
verses.translation: One should not seek to know speech; one should know the speaker. Not smell, but the one who smells; not form, but the one who sees it; not sound, but the hearer; not taste, but the one who tastes. Not action, but the doer; not pleasure and pain, but the one who knows pleasure and pain; not delight, but its knower; not movement, but the mover.
verses.line: Don't chase your pleasures and pains. Know the one who feels them.

verses.speaker: A dying father and his son
verses.setting: The father's last gift: passing on his faculties to his son.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखदुःखे मे त्वयि दधानीति पिता सुखदुःखे ते मयि दध इति पुत्र आनन्दं रतिं प्रजाइं मे त्वयि दधानीति पिता आनन्दं रतिं प्रजातिं ते मयि दध इति पुत्र इत्यां मे त्वयि दधानीति पिता इत्यां ते मयि दध इति पुत्रो
verses.translation: 'I place my joys and sorrows in you,' says the father. 'I take your joys and sorrows into me,' says the son. 'I place my pleasure, delight and power of begetting in you,' says the father. 'I take them into me,' says the son. 'I place my going in you,' says the father. 'I take your going into me,' says the son.
verses.line: The dying father says, 'I place my joys and sorrows in you.' The son replies, 'I take them.'

verses.speaker: Nidagha
verses.setting: Young Nidagha, back from pilgrimage, pours out his disillusionment.
verses.sanskrit_display: तरवोऽपि हि जीवन्ति जीवन्ति मृगपक्षिणः । स जीवति मनो यस्य मननेनोपजीवति ॥
verses.translation: Trees also live; animals and birds also live. That person truly lives whose mind lives by reflection.
verses.line: Trees live, animals and birds live. Truly alive is the one whose mind lives by reflection.

verses.speaker: Nidagha
verses.setting: Nidagha's lament continues.
verses.sanskrit_display: भारो विवेकिनः शास्त्रं भारो ज्ञानं च रागिणः । अशान्तस्य मनो भारो भारोऽनात्मविदो वपुः ॥
verses.translation: Scripture is a burden to the undiscerning, knowledge a burden to the passionate, the mind a burden to the restless, the body a burden to one who does not know the self.
verses.line: Books weigh on the undiscerning, knowledge on the obsessed, the mind on the restless, the body on the self-unaware.

verses.speaker: Nidagha
verses.setting: Nidagha on craving.
verses.sanskrit_display: यां यामहं मुनिश्रेष्ठ संश्रयामि गुणश्रियम् । तां तां कृन्तति मे तृष्णा तन्त्रीमिव कुमूषिका ॥
verses.translation: Whatever good quality I take refuge in, great sage, craving cuts it away, as a mouse gnaws through a string.
verses.line: Every good quality I take up, craving gnaws through, like a mouse chewing a string.

verses.speaker: Nidagha
verses.setting: Nidagha on craving, continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: पदं करोत्यलङ्घ्येऽपि तृप्ता विफलमीहते । चिरं तिष्ठति नैकत्र तृष्णा चपलमर्कटी ॥
verses.translation: It sets foot even where no one can go; even when satisfied it strives in vain; it never stays long in one place: craving is a restless monkey.
verses.line: Craving is a restless monkey: never in one place, never satisfied, reaching even where it cannot go.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on people of steady goodness.
verses.sanskrit_display: नापदि ग्लानिमायान्ति निशि हेमाम्बुजं यथा । नेहन्ते प्रकृतादन्यद्रमन्ते शिष्टवर्त्मनि ॥
verses.translation: In adversity they do not wilt, as the golden lotus does not close at night. They want nothing beyond what is at hand and delight in the path of the good.
verses.line: Good people do not wilt in hard times, like a golden lotus that stays open at night.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on calm, continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: मातरीव परं यान्ति विषमाणि मृदूनि च । विश्वासमिह भूतानि सर्वाणि शमशालिनि ॥
verses.translation: All beings, the harsh and the gentle alike, come to trust the person who is calm, as they would trust a mother.
verses.line: Everyone, gentle or fierce, comes to trust a calm person, the way we trust a mother.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu defines contentment.
verses.sanskrit_display: अप्राप्तं हि परित्यज्य सम्प्राप्ते समतां गतः । अदृष्टखेदाखेदो यः सन्तुष्ट इति कथ्यते ॥ नाभिनन्दत्यसम्प्राप्तं प्राप्तं भुङ्क्ते यथेप्सितम् । यः स सौम्यसमाचारः सन्तुष्ट इति कथ्यते ॥
verses.translation: One who lets go of what has not come, stays even with what has come, and is untouched by gain or loss is called content. One who does not long for what is not attained, and enjoys what has come as it comes, gentle in conduct, is called content.
verses.line: Contentment: not pining for what hasn't come, enjoying what has, staying even either way.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on the words that bind.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं ब्रह्मेति नियतं मोक्षहेतुर्महात्मनाम् । द्वे पदे बन्धमोक्षाय निर्ममेति ममेति च । ममेति बध्यते जन्तुर्निर्ममेति विमुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: 'I am Brahman': this conviction is the cause of freedom for great souls. Two words bring bondage and freedom: 'mine' and 'not mine'. With 'mine' a creature is bound; with 'not mine' it is freed.
verses.line: Two words bind or free you: 'mine' and 'not mine.' With 'mine,' we are bound.
verses.misuse: Not a call to stop caring for family; it is about clinging.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu's shortest verse.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनास्थैव हि निर्वाणं दुःखमास्थापरिग्रहः ॥
verses.translation: Non-clinging alone is freedom; clinging is sorrow.
verses.line: Not clinging is freedom. Clinging is sorrow.
verses.misuse: Not clinging is not the same as not caring.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on craving.
verses.sanskrit_display: धीरोऽप्यतिबहुज्ञोऽपि कुलजोऽपि महानपि । तृष्णया बध्यते जन्तुः सिंहः श‍ृङ्खलया यथा ॥
verses.translation: However brave, however learned, however well born, however great, a person is bound by craving, as a lion is bound by a chain.
verses.line: Brave, learned, well born or great, anyone can be chained by craving, like a lion on a chain.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Shuka is kept waiting at King Janaka's gate, then tested with luxury.
verses.sanskrit_display: ते भोगास्तानि भोज्यानि व्यासपुत्रस्य तन्मनः । नाजह्वुर्मन्दपवनो बद्धपीठमिवाचलम् ॥ केवलं सुसमः स्वच्छो मौनी मुदितमानसः । सम्पूर्ण इव शीतांशुरतिष्ठदमलः शुकः ॥
verses.translation: Those pleasures and those foods did not move the mind of Vyasa's son, as a gentle breeze cannot move a mountain on its base. Only even, clear, silent and glad of heart, complete like the full moon, pure Shuka remained.
verses.line: Ignored for days, then pampered with luxury, Shuka stayed the same, steady as a mountain in a breeze.

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on the mark of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनागतानां भोगानामवाञ्छनमकृत्रिमम् । आगतानां च संभोग इति पण्डितलक्षणम् ॥
verses.translation: Not longing for pleasures yet to come, and enjoying those that have come: this, unforced, is the mark of the wise.
verses.line: Not pining for pleasures still to come, and enjoying the ones already here: that is wisdom.

verses.speaker: King Brihadratha
verses.setting: The king's plea after listing everything that passes.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥
verses.translation: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
verses.line: Like a frog in a dark well, I am stuck in this life. Show me the way out.

verses.speaker: King Brihadratha
verses.setting: A king who has handed over his kingdom asks a sage what is real.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वं चेदं क्षयिष्णु पश्यामो यथेमे दंशमशकादयस्तृणवन्नश्यतयोद्भूतप्रध्वंसिनः ॥
verses.translation: We see that all this perishes, like gnats and mosquitoes, like grass and trees that spring up and wither.
verses.line: Everything perishes, like gnats and mosquitoes, like grass that springs up and withers.

verses.speaker: Mahadeva (Shiva)
verses.setting: Shiva redefines religious practice.
verses.sanskrit_display: अभेददर्शनं ज्ञानं ध्यानं निर्विषयं मनः। स्नानं मनोमलत्यागः शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः ॥
verses.translation: Seeing no difference is knowledge; a mind free of objects is meditation; giving up the mind's dirt is bathing; restraint of the senses is purity.
verses.line: True knowledge is seeing no difference. Meditation is a mind at rest. Real bathing is washing the mind.

verses.speaker: Shaunaka
verses.setting: A wealthy householder comes formally to a teacher with one question.
verses.sanskrit_display: शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥
verses.translation: Shaunaka, the great householder, approached Angiras in the proper way and asked: 'Sir, what is that which, when known, makes all this known?'
verses.line: Shaunaka asked: what is the one thing which, once known, makes everything else make sense?

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on people satisfied with ritual and status.
verses.sanskrit_display: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितं मन्यमानाः । जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥
verses.translation: Living in ignorance, wise in their own eyes, thinking themselves learned, the deluded go round and round, stumbling, like the blind led by the blind.
verses.line: Wise in their own eyes, the deluded go round in circles, like the blind led by the blind.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: The archer image for inner focus.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रणवो धनुः शारो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते । अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत् तन्मयो भवेत् ॥
verses.translation: Om is the bow, the self is the arrow, and Brahman is called the target. It must be hit by one who is undistracted; like the arrow, one becomes one with it.
verses.line: Focus like an archer: steady, undistracted, until you and your target become one.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: The fruit of seeing the highest.
verses.sanskrit_display: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरे ॥
verses.translation: The knot of the heart is cut, all doubts are dispelled and one's deeds wear away, when that which is both high and low is seen.
verses.line: When you see the highest, the heart's knot loosens, every doubt is cut, old deeds lose their grip.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: The two birds, continued.
verses.sanskrit_display: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनिशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥
verses.translation: On the same tree a person sits sunk, grieving, bewildered by his own helplessness. When he sees the other, the content lord, and his greatness, his sorrow leaves him.
verses.line: The bird that eats grieves, lost in its helplessness. When it sees the calm one beside it, grief falls away.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on how the wise live.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन् विद्वान् भवते नातिवादी । आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ॥
verses.translation: This is the life that shines through all beings. Knowing it, the wise one does not talk over others. Delighting in the self, playing in the self, yet active, such a one is the best of the knowers of Brahman.
verses.line: Knowing this, the wise stop arguing. Their joy is within, and they stay fully active.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on desire.
verses.sanskrit_display: कामान् यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र । पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः ॥
verses.translation: One who desires, brooding on desires, is born here and there by those desires. But for one whose desire is fulfilled, who is whole in himself, all desires dissolve right here.
verses.line: Chase desires and they keep giving birth to more. Be whole within, and they dissolve here and now.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on effort.
verses.sanskrit_display: नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात् तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् । एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वांस्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्मधाम ॥
verses.translation: This self is not won by the weak, nor through carelessness, nor by austerity without a true aim. But the wise one who strives by these means enters the home of Brahman.
verses.line: This is not won by the weak or the careless. Whoever strives wisely gets there.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on the end of separateness.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय । तथा विद्वान् नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥
verses.translation: As flowing rivers disappear into the sea, giving up name and form, so the knower, freed from name and form, goes to the divine person beyond the beyond.
verses.line: As rivers lose their names in the sea, so the wise, freed of name and form, merge in the highest.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The catechism of definitions continues.
verses.sanskrit_display: स्वर्ग इति च सत्संसर्गः स्वर्गः । नरक इति च असत्संसारविषयजनसंसर्ग एव नरकः ॥
verses.translation: What is heaven? The company of the good is heaven. What is hell? Contact with the false world and with people lost in its objects is hell.
verses.line: Heaven is good company. Hell is keeping company with what is hollow and the people lost in it.

verses.speaker: Pippalada
verses.setting: End of Pippalada's first answer.
verses.sanskrit_display: तेषामसौ विरजो ब्रह्मलोको न येषु जिह्ममनृतं न माया चेति ॥
verses.translation: That stainless world of Brahman belongs to those in whom there is no crookedness, no falsehood and no deceit.
verses.line: The pure world belongs to those with no crookedness, no lying and no trickery in them.

verses.speaker: Pippalada
verses.setting: The senses boast that they keep the body going; breath decides to show them.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोऽभिमानादूर्ध्वमुत्क्रामत इव तस्मिन्नुत्क्रामत्यथेतरे सर्व एवोत्क्रामन्ते तस्मिंश्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रतिष्ठन्ते । तद्यथा मक्षिका मधुकरराजानमुत्क्रामन्तं सर्व एवोत्क्रमन्ते तस्मिंष्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रातिष्टन्त एवं वाङ्मनष्चक्षुः श्रोत्रं च ते प्रीताः प्राणं स्तुन्वन्ति ॥
verses.translation: Out of pride, breath seemed to rise to leave the body, and as it rose all the others had to rise; as it settled, they all settled. As bees all fly out when their queen flies out and settle when she settles, so did speech, mind, eye and ear. Pleased, they praised breath.
verses.line: When the life-breath rose to leave, all the senses had to follow, like bees after their queen.

verses.speaker: Pippalada
verses.setting: Six seekers arrive with questions; the sage makes them wait.
verses.sanskrit_display: तान्ह स ऋषिरुवाच भूय एव तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया संवत्सरं संवत्स्यथ यथाकामं प्रश्नान् पृच्छत यदि विज्ञास्यामः सर्वं ह वो वक्ष्याम इति ॥
verses.translation: The sage said to them: 'Live here one more year with discipline, self-restraint and faith. Then ask whatever you wish. If we know, we will tell you all of it.'
verses.line: Stay a year in discipline and faith, then ask. If I know, I will tell you everything.

verses.speaker: Seekers of Brahman
verses.setting: Opening questions of the Shvetashvatara.
verses.sanskrit_display: किं कारणं ब्रह्म कुतः स्म जाता जीवाम केन क्व च सम्प्रतिष्ठा । अधिष्ठिताः केन सुखेतरेषु वर्तामहे ब्रह्मविदो व्यवस्थाम् ॥
verses.translation: What is the cause? Is it Brahman? From where are we born? By what do we live? Where do we finally rest? Under whose rule, O knowers of Brahman, do we pass through joys and sorrows?
verses.line: Where did we come from? What keeps us alive? Where do we go? Who governs our joys and sorrows?

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: On how the self is found.
verses.sanskrit_display: तिलेषु तैलं दधिनीव सर्पिरापः स्रोतःस्वरणीषु चाग्निः । एवमात्माऽत्मनि गृह्यतेऽसौसत्येनैनं तपसायोऽनुपश्यति ॥
verses.translation: As oil in sesame seeds, butter in curd, water in springs and fire in fire-sticks, so is the self found within oneself by one who seeks it with truth and discipline.
verses.line: Like oil in sesame or butter in curd, what you seek is already within. Sincere effort brings it out.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: On the joy at the heart of things.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्वै तत् सुकृतम् रसो वै सः रसꣳह्येवायं लब्ध्वाऽऽनन्दी भवति ।
verses.translation: That which is well made is the essence itself. Having found that essence, a person becomes joyful.
verses.line: It is the very flavour of life. Whoever tastes it is filled with joy.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The famous verse closing the Brahmananda Valli.
verses.sanskrit_display: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्। न बिभेति कुतश्चनेति ।
verses.translation: That from which words turn back, along with the mind, not reaching it: whoever knows the joy of Brahman fears nothing at all.
verses.line: Where words and thoughts turn back unable to reach: whoever knows that joy fears nothing.

verses.speaker: Varuna
verses.setting: A son asks his father to teach him what is ultimate.
verses.sanskrit_display: भृगुर्वै वारुणिः । वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तस्मा एतत्प्रोवाच । अन्नं प्राणं चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनो वाचमिति । तꣳहोवाच । यतो वा इमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । येन जातानि जीवन्ति। यत्प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्ति। तद्विजिज्ञासस्व । तद्ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ॥
verses.translation: Bhrigu, son of Varuna, went to his father and said, 'Sir, teach me Brahman.' He told him: food, breath, eye, ear, mind, speech. Then he said: 'That from which these beings are born, by which they live once born, and into which they enter at death: seek to know that. That is Brahman.' Bhrigu practised disciplined reflection.
verses.line: Bhrigu asked his father to teach him. 'Seek that from which all is born and to which all returns.'

verses.speaker: Varuna
verses.setting: Each time Bhrigu returns with an answer, his father sends him back.
verses.sanskrit_display: अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तꣳहोवाच । तपसा ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासस्व । तपो ब्रह्मेति ।
verses.translation: 'Sir, teach me Brahman.' He said to him: 'Seek to know Brahman by disciplined reflection. Disciplined reflection is Brahman.'
verses.line: His father did not hand him answers: 'Seek it through disciplined reflection. That effort is the way.'

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: Vows that follow Bhrigu's discovery.
verses.sanskrit_display: अन्नं न निन्द्यात् । तद्व्रतम् । प्राणो वा अन्नम् । शरीरमन्नादम् । प्राणे शरीरं प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
verses.translation: Do not speak ill of food; that is a vow. Breath is food, the body eats food; the body rests on breath and breath rests in the body.
verses.line: Never speak ill of food. Treat that as a vow.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The hospitality vow.
verses.sanskrit_display: सदाचारप्रदर्शनम् । ब्रह्मानन्दानुभवःन कञ्चन वसतौ प्रत्याचक्षीत । तद्व्रतम् । तस्माद्यया कया च विधया बह्वन्नं प्राप्नुयात् ।
verses.translation: Turn no one away from your home; that is a vow. So one should gather plenty of food by whatever means, for people say of such a person: food is ready for him.
verses.line: Turn no one away from your door. Make that a vow, and keep enough to share.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: A list of what must go alongside lifelong learning.
verses.sanskrit_display: ऋतं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। सत्यं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। तपश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। दमश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च।
verses.translation: Right conduct, along with study and teaching. Truth, along with study and teaching. Discipline, along with study and teaching. Self-control, along with study and teaching.
verses.line: Do what is right, speak truth, keep discipline, and never stop learning and teaching.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The graduation address continues.
verses.sanskrit_display: आचार्याय प्रियं धनमाहृत्य प्रजातन्तुं मा व्यवच्छेत्सीः । सत्यान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । धर्मान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । कुशलान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । भूत्यै न प्रमदितव्यम् । स्वाध्यायप्रवचनाभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् ॥
verses.translation: Having brought your teacher the gift he values, do not cut off the line of your family. Do not drift from truth. Do not drift from what is right. Do not neglect your wellbeing. Do not neglect your prosperity. Do not neglect study and teaching.
verses.line: Do not drift from truth or duty. Do not neglect your wellbeing, your prosperity, or your learning.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The teacher's surprising humility.
verses.sanskrit_display: यान्यनवद्यानि कर्माणि । तानि सेवितव्यानि । नो इतराणि । यान्यस्माकꣳसुचरितानि । तानि त्वयोपास्यानि ॥
verses.translation: Whatever actions are blameless, those you should do, and not others. Whatever good conduct is ours, that you should follow.
verses.line: Do only what is blameless. Follow what is good in us, your teachers, and not the rest.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit_display: मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि । किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥
verses.translation: One who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.
verses.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
verses.misuse: This is about inner freedom; it does not deny real constraints or problems that need action.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit_display: निरपेक्षो निर्विकारो निर्भरः शीतलाशयः । अगाधबुद्धिरक्षुब्धो भव चिन्मात्रवासनः ॥
verses.translation: Be free of expectation, unchanging, self-reliant, cool at heart, deep in understanding and unshaken, resting in pure awareness alone.
verses.line: Be free of expectations, steady, self-reliant and cool at heart: deep, and impossible to rattle.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's first answer to King Janaka's question: how does one become free?
verses.sanskrit_display: मुक्तिमिच्छसि चेत्तात विषयान् विषवत्त्यज । क्षमार्जवदयातोषसत्यं पीयूषवद् भज ॥
verses.translation: If you want freedom, my son, shun the objects of craving as you would poison, and take in forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth as you would nectar.
verses.line: Treat craving like poison. Drink forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth like nectar.
verses.misuse: Forgiveness here is a quality you grow, not a duty to excuse ongoing harm.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि । अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥
verses.translation: If you set the body apart and rest in awareness, then this very moment you will be happy, at peace and free of bondage.
verses.line: Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं कर्तेत्यहंमानमहाकृष्णाहिदंशितः । नाहं कर्तेति विश्वासामृतं पीत्वा सुखी भव ॥
verses.translation: You have been bitten by the great black snake of the ego that says 'I am the doer'. Drink the nectar of trust that says 'I am not the doer', and be happy.
verses.line: 'Everything depends on me' is a snakebite. The antidote is trusting you are not the only doer.
verses.misuse: Not being the only doer does not mean you are not responsible for what you do.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tells Janaka what has never given the mind rest.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्र यत्र भवेत्तृष्णा संसारं विद्धि तत्र वै । प्रौढवैराग्यमाश्रित्य वीततृष्णः सुखी भव ॥
verses.translation: Wherever there is craving, know that the endless round is there. Take up mature dispassion, be free of craving, and be happy.
verses.line: Wherever craving lives, the treadmill runs. Let go of the craving, and be happy.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tells Janaka what has never given the mind rest.
verses.sanskrit_display: अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा । एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥
verses.translation: Enough of wealth, of desire, even of good deeds. In this wilderness of life the mind never found rest in them.
verses.line: Money, pleasure, even good deeds: none of them ever gave this mind rest.
verses.misuse: Not against good deeds; it says they cannot be the source of inner rest.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra lists the certainties that make the wise calm.
verses.sanskrit_display: चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी । तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥
verses.translation: One who knows for certain that suffering here is born of worry and nothing else is free of it, happy, at peace, and unattached everywhere.
verses.line: Suffering is born of worry, nothing else. Free of worry, you are happy and at peace.
verses.misuse: Real problems still need attention; this is about the extra pain rumination adds.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
verses.translation: In you, the boundless ocean, let the waves of the world rise or fall by their own nature. You neither grow nor shrink.
verses.line: Let the waves of the world rise or fall. You, the ocean, neither gain nor lose.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit_display: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
verses.translation: Do not stir your mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. Be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self.
verses.line: Don't churn your mind with plans and second thoughts. Be still and rest in yourself.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to avoid decisions; decide, then stop churning.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit_display: मोक्षो विषयवैरस्यं बन्धो वैषयिको रसः । एतावदेव विज्ञानं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verses.translation: Liberation is losing your taste for the objects of craving; bondage is relishing them. That is all there is to know; now do as you wish.
verses.line: Freedom is losing your taste for what hooks you; bondage is savouring it. That's all you need to know.
verses.misuse: 'Do as you wish' assumes the craving is gone; it is not a licence.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit_display: न त्वं देहो न ते देहो भोक्ता कर्ता न वा भवान् । चिद्रूपोऽसि सदा साक्षी निरपेक्षः सुखं चर ॥
verses.translation: You are not the body, nor is the body yours; you are not the doer or the enjoyer. You are awareness itself, the ever-present witness, needing nothing. Live happily.
verses.line: You are not your body or your achievements. You are the awareness watching it all. Live lightly.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit_display: रागद्वेषौ मनोधर्मौ न मनस्ते कदाचन । निर्विकल्पोऽसि बोधात्मा निर्विकारः सुखं चर ॥
verses.translation: Liking and disliking belong to the mind, and you are never the mind. You are awareness itself, free of thought-forms and unchanging. Live happily.
verses.line: Liking and disliking belong to the mind. You are not your mind.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit_display: गुणैः संवेष्टितो देहस्तिष्ठत्यायाति याति च । आत्मा न गन्ता नागन्ता किमेनमनुशोचसि ॥
verses.translation: The body, made of nature's qualities, comes, stays and goes. The Self neither comes nor goes. Why grieve for it?
verses.line: The body comes and goes; what you truly are does not. Why grieve so?
verses.misuse: Grief is natural; this offers perspective, not a rule against mourning.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
verses.translation: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
verses.line: Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.
verses.misuse: Not against effort; against the anxious straining that rides on it.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: हातुमिच्छति संसारं रागी दुःखजिहासया । वीतरागो हि निर्दुःखस्तस्मिन्नपि न खिद्यति ॥
verses.translation: The attached person wants to escape the world to get away from pain. The one free of attachment has no pain and is not troubled even while in it.
verses.line: Running away won't free you from pain. Free of clinging, you can be at peace right where you are.
verses.misuse: Not advice to stay somewhere harmful; it says escape alone won't fix inner restlessness.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra describes the person who has truly understood.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्तु भोगेषु भुक्तेषु न भवत्यधिवासितः । अभुक्तेषु निराकाङ्क्षी तदृशो भवदुर्लभः ॥
verses.translation: One who doesn't keep dwelling on pleasures already enjoyed, nor pine for pleasures not yet had, is rare in this world.
verses.line: Rare is the person who doesn't replay old pleasures or pine for new ones.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: न धावति जनाकीर्णं नारण्यमुपशान्तधीः । यथातथा यत्रतत्र सम एवावतिष्ठते ॥
verses.translation: The calm mind does not run off to crowded places or to the forest. Whatever and wherever, it stays the same.
verses.line: A calm mind doesn't need the crowd or the forest. It is the same wherever it is.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्जयित्वाखिलान् अर्थान् भोगानाप्नोति पुष्कलान् । न हि सर्वपरित्यागमन्तरेण सुखी भवेत् ॥
verses.translation: One may earn every kind of wealth and enjoy abundant pleasures, but without letting go of everything, no one is happy.
verses.line: You can earn everything and enjoy everything, and still not be happy until you let go.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्तव्यदुःखमार्तण्डज्वालादग्धान्तरात्मनः । कुतः प्रशमपीयूषधारासारमृते सुखम् ॥
verses.translation: For one whose heart is scorched by the blazing sun of 'things I must do', where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?
verses.line: When 'I still have to do this' burns you up inside, only a rain of calm brings relief.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: न शान्तिं लभते मूढो यतः शमितुमिच्छति । धीरस्तत्त्वं विनिश्चित्य सर्वदा शान्तमानसः ॥
verses.translation: The confused person never finds peace, because he is trying to get it. The wise, clear about the truth, is always calm.
verses.line: Chasing calm keeps it away. Seeing clearly, the wise are calm without trying.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः । कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥
verses.translation: The fool is restless even when doing nothing; the skilful one stays calm even when doing everything that needs doing.
verses.line: A restless mind is agitated even doing nothing; a skilled one stays calm doing everything.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखमास्ते सुखं शेते सुखमायाति याति च । सुखं वक्ति सुखं भुङ्क्ते व्यवहारेऽपि शान्तधीः ॥
verses.translation: He sits happily, sleeps happily, comes and goes happily, speaks and eats happily: calm-minded even in daily affairs.
verses.line: Sit, sleep, come, go, talk and eat at ease. Calm can live inside ordinary days.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति । धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥
verses.translation: He does not pray for gain, nor grieve over loss. The steady one's cool mind is filled as if with nectar.
verses.line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: न प्रीयते वन्द्यमानो निन्द्यमानो न कुप्यति । नैवोद्विजति मरणे जीवने नाभिनन्दति ॥
verses.translation: Praised, he is not pleased; blamed, he is not angry. He neither dreads death nor clings to life.
verses.line: Praise doesn't inflate you, blame doesn't enrage you, death doesn't frighten you. That is freedom.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tests the newly awakened Janaka: if you really know, why do you still chase things?
verses.sanskrit_display: चेष्टमानं शरीरं स्वं पश्यत्यन्यशरीरवत् । संस्तवे चापि निन्दायां कथं क्षुभ्येत् महाशयः ॥
verses.translation: One who watches his own active body as if it were someone else's: how could praise or blame disturb such a large-hearted person?
verses.line: Watch yourself as you'd watch anyone else, and praise or blame stops shaking you.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tests the newly awakened Janaka: if you really know, why do you still chase things?
verses.sanskrit_display: विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे । सोऽहमस्मीति विज्ञाय किं दीन इव धावसि ॥
verses.translation: Knowing 'I am That in which this world rises like waves on the sea', why do you run around like a beggar?
verses.line: You are the ocean these waves rise in. Why run around like a beggar for more?

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's shortest definition of bondage and freedom, given to Janaka.
