verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो हि दिष्टमुपासीत निर्विचेष्टः सुखं स्वपन् / अवसीदेत्सुदुर्बुद्धिरामो घट इवोदके
verses.translation: The fool who just waits on fate, doing nothing and sleeping comfortably, sinks like an unbaked clay pot in water.
verses.line: Wait on fate and do nothing, and you'll dissolve like an unbaked clay pot in water.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi describes a farmer who ploughs and sows, then waits for rain.
verses.sanskrit_display: वृष्टिश्चेन्नानुगृह्णीयादनेनास्तत्र कर्षकः / यदन्यः पुरुषः कुर्यात्तत्कृतं सफलं मया तच्चेदं फलमस्माकमपराधो न मे क्वचित् / इति धीरोऽन्ववेक्ष्यैव नात्मानं तत्रगर्हयेत्
verses.translation: If the rain does not favour him, the farmer is not to blame. He tells himself: 'Whatever anyone could have done, I have done.' If the result is still this, the fault is not mine. Seeing this, the wise do not condemn themselves.
verses.line: You ploughed and sowed. If the rain didn't come, that isn't your failure. Don't condemn yourself.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verses.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verses.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verses.sanskrit_display: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verses.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verses.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Gandhari
verses.setting: Gandhari turns first on her husband, who has indulged their son for years.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वं ह्येवात्र भृशं गर्ह्यो धृतराष्ट्र सुतप्रियः / यो जानन्पापतामस्य तत्प्रज्ञामनुवर्तसे
verses.translation: You are the one most to blame here, Dhritarashtra, so fond of your son: you know his wrongdoing and still follow his lead.
verses.line: A parent who sees a child's wrong and still goes along with it shares the blame.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Gandhari
verses.setting: Queen Gandhari is called into court to reason with her son Duryodhana, who has rejected peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मानमेव प्रथमं द्वेष्यरूपेण योजयेत् / ततोऽमात्यानमित्रांश्च न मोघं विजिगीषते
verses.translation: First take your own self in hand, as you would an opponent. Then you won't fail to win over your advisers and your rivals.
verses.line: Win the contest with yourself first. Then winning over others becomes possible.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Gandhari
verses.setting: Queen Gandhari is called into court to reason with her son Duryodhana, who has rejected peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: न लोभादर्थसंपत्तिर्नराणामिह दृश्यते / तदलं तात लोभेन प्रशाम्य भरतर्षभ ॥
verses.translation: No one in this world gains real wealth through greed. Enough of greed, my son. Be at peace.
verses.line: Greed has never made anyone truly rich. Enough of it, my child. Be at peace.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit_display: अलातं तिन्दुकस्येव मुहूर्तमपि हि ज्वल / मा तुषाग्निरिवानर्चिर्धूमायस्व जिजीविषुः
verses.translation: Like a torch of tinduka wood, blaze, even if only for a moment. Do not smoulder without flame like a fire of husks, just to stay alive.
verses.line: Blaze like a torch, even for a moment. Don't just smoulder to stay alive.
verses.misuse: About wholehearted effort, not reckless risk or burnout.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit_display: अलब्ध्वा यदि वा लब्ध्वा नानुशोचति पण्डितः / आनन्तर्यं चारभते न प्राणानां धनायते
verses.translation: Whether he wins or fails, the wise person does not keep grieving. He starts on the next task at once and does not hoard his own life.
verses.line: Win or lose, don't keep grieving. Start the next thing right away.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit_display: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verses.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verses.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit_display: पुत्र नात्मावमन्तव्यः पूर्वाभिरसमृद्धिभिः / अभूत्वा हि भवन्त्यर्था भूत्वा नश्यन्ति चापरे / अमर्षेणैव चाप्यर्था नारब्धव्याः सुबालिशैः
verses.translation: Son, don't look down on yourself because of past failures. Fortunes that never were come to be, and fortunes that were are lost. But don't start things out of mere resentment, like a fool.
verses.line: Don't look down on yourself because of past failures. Fortunes come and go, and can come again.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्
verses.translation: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
verses.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: दश धर्मं न जानन्ति धृतराष्ट्र निबोध तान् / मत्तः प्रमत्त उन्मत्तः श्रान्तः क्रुद्धो बुभुक्षितः त्वरमाणश्च लुब्धश्च भीतः कामी च ते दश / तस्मादेतेषु भावेषु न प्रसञ्जेत पण्डितः
verses.translation: Ten people do not know what is right, Dhritarashtra; hear who they are: the drunk, the careless, the deranged, the exhausted, the angry, the starving, the hurried, the greedy, the frightened and the lustful. So a wise person does not let himself be caught in these states.
verses.line: Don't decide when you are angry, exhausted, hungry, rushed, greedy or afraid; right and wrong blur then.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: न वैरमुद्दिपयति प्रशान्तं / न दर्पमारोहति शान्तिमेति / न दुर्गतोऽस्मीति करोत्यकार्यं / तमार्यशीलं परमाहुरार्याः
verses.translation: He does not rekindle a quarrel that has died down, does not climb onto his pride, stays calm, and does not do wrong telling himself 'I am in a bad way': the noble call such conduct the best.
verses.line: Don't rake up settled quarrels, don't ride your pride, and don't excuse wrongdoing because times are hard.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षिप्रं विजानाति चिरं श्रृणोति / विज्ञाय चार्यं भजते न कामात् / नासंपृष्टो व्युपयुङ्क्ते परार्थे / तत्प्रज्ञानं प्रथमं पण्डितस्य
verses.translation: He understands quickly, listens patiently, acts on understanding and not on impulse, and does not meddle in other people's affairs unasked: this is the first mark of a wise person.
verses.line: Understand quickly, listen long, act from judgement not impulse, and stay out of others' business unless asked.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाप्राप्यमभिवाञ्छन्ति नष्टं नेच्छन्ति शोचितुम् / आपत्सु च न मुह्यन्ति नराः पण्डितबुद्धयः
verses.translation: The wise do not long for what cannot be had, do not choose to keep grieving over what is lost, and do not lose their heads in misfortune.
verses.line: Don't chase what can't be had, don't keep mourning what is gone, and don't lose your head in trouble.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verses.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verses.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते
verses.translation: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
verses.line: Don't swell with praise or burn at a slight; stay deep and still like a river pool.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: संसारयति कृत्यानि सर्वत्र विचिकित्सते / चिरं करोति क्षिप्रार्थे स मूढो भरतर्षभ
verses.translation: He drags out what needs doing, doubts everything, and is slow where speed is needed: such a person is a fool, best of the Bharatas.
verses.line: Stretching tasks out, doubting everything, going slow when speed matters: that is what foolishness looks like.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: परं क्षिपति दोषेण वर्तमानः स्वयं तथा / यश्च क्रुध्यत्यनीशानः स च मूढतमो नरः
verses.translation: One who blames another for a fault he himself has, and one who rages when he has no power to act, is the greatest of fools.
verses.line: Blaming others for your own fault, or raging where you have no power, is the height of folly.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: एकः क्षमावतां दोषो द्वितीयो नोपपद्यते / यदेनं क्षमया युक्तमशक्तं मन्यते जनः सोऽस्य दोषो न मन्तव्यः क्षमा हि परमं बलम् / क्षमा गुणो ह्यशक्तानां शक्तानां भूषणं क्षमा
verses.translation: The forgiving have one fault and no second: people take a forgiving person to be weak. That should not be counted against him, for forgiveness is the greatest strength. In the weak it is a virtue; in the strong it is an ornament.
verses.line: People may mistake your forgiveness for weakness. It isn't. Forgiveness is the greatest strength.
verses.misuse: Forgiving is not the same as staying in harm's way or excusing abuse.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: षड्दोषाः पुरुषेणेह हातव्या भूतिमिच्छता / निद्रा तन्द्री भयं क्रोध आलस्यं दीर्घसूत्रता
verses.translation: Six faults must be given up by anyone who wants to prosper: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
verses.line: Six habits block every rise: oversleeping, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: आरोग्यमानृण्यमविप्रवासः / सद्भिर्मनुष्यैः सह संप्रयोगः / स्वप्रत्यया वृत्तिरभीतवासः / षट् जीवलोकस्य सुखानि राजन्
verses.translation: Health, freedom from debt, living at home, the company of good people, a livelihood of one's own, and living without fear: these, O king, are the six joys of this world.
verses.line: Health, no debt, home, good people, work of your own, a life without fear: that is real happiness.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: ईर्षुर्धृणी नसन्तुष्टः क्रोधनो नित्यशङ्कितः / परभाग्योपजीवी च षडेते नित्यदुःखिताः
verses.translation: The envious, the scornful, the discontented, the short-tempered, the ever-suspicious, and one who lives off another's fortune: these six are always unhappy.
verses.line: Envy, scorn, discontent, short temper, constant suspicion, living off others' luck: six sure roads to misery.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: तथैव योगविहितं यत्तु कर्म न सिध्यति / उपाययुक्तं मेधावी न तत्र ग्लपयेन्मनः
verses.translation: And if a task undertaken with the right means and done with proper method still does not succeed, the wise person should not let his mind sink over it.
verses.line: If you did it the right way and it still failed, don't let your mind sink.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: आक्रोशपरिवादाभ्यां विहिंसन्त्यबुधा बुधान् / वक्ता पापमुपादत्ते क्षममाणो विमुच्यते
verses.translation: Fools wound the wise with abuse and slander. The one who speaks takes on the wrong; the one who bears it patiently is set free.
verses.line: When someone abuses you, the wrong stays with the speaker; the one who bears it walks free.
verses.misuse: Bearing an insult calmly does not mean accepting ongoing abuse.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् / वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम्
verses.translation: A forest pierced by arrows or felled by the axe grows back; but a wound made by cruel, ugly words does not heal.
verses.line: A forest cut down grows back. A wound made with harsh words does not heal.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: न देवा यष्टिमादाय रक्षन्ति पशुपालवत् / यं तु रक्षितुमिच्छन्ति बुद्ध्या संयोजयन्ति तम्
verses.translation: The gods do not guard a person with a stick in hand, the way a herdsman guards cattle. Whomever they wish to protect, they endow with good judgement.
verses.line: The gods don't stand guard with a stick; whom they protect, they give clear judgement.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: तृणोल्कया ज्ञायते जातरूपं / वृत्तेन भद्रो व्यवहारेण साधुः / शूरो भयेष्वर्थकृच्छ्रेषु धीरः / कृच्छ्रेष्वापत्सु सुहृदश्चारयश्च
verses.translation: Gold is known by a flame of straw; a good person by conduct, an honest one by dealings, a brave one in danger, a steady one in money troubles, and friends and enemies in hard times.
verses.line: Gold shows in fire, character in conduct, courage in danger, and true friends in hard times.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: दिवसेनैव तत्कुर्याद्येन रात्रौ सुखं वसेत् / अष्टमासेन तत्कुर्याद्येन वर्षाः सुखं वसेत् पूर्वे वयसि तत्कुर्याद्येन वृद्धः सुखं वसेत् / यावज्जीवं तु तत्कुर्याद्येन प्रेत्य सुखं वसेत्
verses.translation: Do during the day what lets you sleep in peace at night; do in the eight dry months what lets you live comfortably through the rains. Do in youth what makes old age comfortable, and do all your life what brings peace after death.
verses.line: Do today what lets you sleep tonight, and in youth what lets you rest in old age.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: न तन्मित्रं यस्य कोपाद्बिभेति / यद्वा मित्रं शङ्कितेनोपचर्यम् / यस्मिन्मित्रे पितरीवाश्वसीत / तद्वै मित्रं सङ्गतानीतराणि
verses.translation: That is no friend whose anger you fear, or whom you must approach warily. A friend is one you can trust as you trust a father; the rest are mere acquaintances.
verses.line: If you fear someone's anger or must tiptoe around them, they are not really your friend.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते रूपं सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते बलम् / सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते ज्ञानं सन्तापाद्व्याधिमृच्छति अनवाप्यं च शोकेन शरीरं चोपतप्यते / अमित्राश्च प्रहृष्यन्ति मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः
verses.translation: Brooding destroys beauty, brooding destroys strength, brooding destroys understanding, brooding brings on illness. Grief does not get you what you want; it only wears out the body and gladdens your enemies. Do not give your mind to grief.
verses.line: Brooding drains your looks, strength and judgement, makes you ill, and changes nothing. Don't give your mind to it.

verses.speaker: Dhritarashtra asks; Vidura answers
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्रमिदं मनः / यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते नान्यत्र विद्यातपसो नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् / नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्यामि तेऽनघ
verses.translation: Dhritarashtra: 'Everything is always unsettled, and this mind is always unsettled. Wise one, tell me of the state that is free from unrest.' Vidura: 'I see no peace for you apart from learning and discipline, apart from mastering the senses, apart from giving up greed.'
verses.line: Peace comes from learning, discipline, mastering your senses, and letting go of always wanting more.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: अव्याधिजं कटुकं शीर्षरोगि / पापानुबन्धं परुषं तीक्ष्णमुष्णम् / सतां पेयं यन्न पिबन्त्यसन्तो / मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य
verses.translation: It is bitter without being a medicine, it gives you a headache, it leads to wrongdoing; it is harsh, sharp and hot. The good drink it down; the bad cannot. That is anger. Drink it, great king, and be at peace.
verses.line: Anger is a bitter drink the wise swallow and the foolish can't. Swallow it and find peace.
verses.misuse: Swallowing anger means not acting it out, not denying a real hurt.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यदभीक्ष्णं निषेवते / तदेवापहरत्येनं तस्मात्कल्याणमाचरेत्
verses.translation: Whatever a person keeps doing, in action, thought or word, is what carries him away. So keep doing what is good.
verses.line: What you repeat in deed, thought and word is what shapes you. So repeat what is good.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: न वृद्धिर्बहुमन्तव्या या वृद्धिः क्षयमावहेत् / क्षयोऽपि बहुमन्तव्यो यः क्षयो वृद्धिमावहेत्
verses.translation: A gain that brings loss should not be valued; a loss that brings gain should be valued.
verses.line: Don't prize a gain that leads to loss; value a loss that leads to growth.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: आर्जवेन नरं युक्तमार्जवात्सव्यपत्रपम् / अशक्तं मन्यमानास्तु धर्षयन्ति कुबुद्धयः
verses.translation: A person who is straightforward, and modest because of it, is taken for weak by small-minded people, and they push him around.
verses.line: Small minds mistake your honesty and modesty for weakness, and try to push you around.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to stop being straightforward; a reason to hold firm boundaries.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि / पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम् / न जातु कामान्न भयान्न लोभा- / द्धर्मं जह्याज्जीविस्यापि हेतोः
verses.translation: Here is the highest thing I can tell you, the purest and most valuable: never abandon what is right, not out of desire, not out of fear, not out of greed, not even to save your life.
verses.line: Never give up what is right, not for desire, not from fear, not for money.

verses.speaker: Sanatsujata
verses.setting: The sage Sanatsujata answers King Dhritarashtra's questions about death and the self.
verses.sanskrit_display: योऽन्यथा सन्तमात्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते / किं तेन न कृतं पापं चोरेणात्मापहारिणा
verses.translation: One who is one thing but presents himself as another: what wrong has that thief not committed, who robs his own self?
verses.line: Pretending to be someone you're not is theft, and what you steal is yourself.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वोच्छेदे च यतते वैरस्यान्तविधित्सया / जयो वैरं प्रसृजति दुःखमास्ते पराजितः सुखं प्रशान्तः स्वपिति हित्वा जयपराजयौ / जातवैरश्च पुरुषो दुःखं स्वपिति नित्यदा
verses.translation: Victory breeds hostility, and the defeated live in pain. The one at peace, who has set aside winning and losing, sleeps well.
verses.line: Winning breeds resentment and losing breeds pain. Drop the scorecard, and you'll sleep in peace.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit_display: आख्यातारश्च विद्यन्ते पुमांश्चेद्विद्यते कुले / न चापि वैरं वैरेण केशव व्युपशाम्यति हविषाऽग्निर्यथा कृष्ण भूय एवाभिवर्धते / अतोऽन्यथा नास्ति शान्तिर्नित्यमन्तरमन्ततः
verses.translation: Hostility is never ended by hostility, Keshava. It only grows, like fire fed with ghee.
verses.line: Hostility never ends hostility. It only grows, like a fire fed with ghee.
verses.misuse: Ending a feud does not require pretending the wrong never happened.

verses.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Brihaspati counsels Indra on how to hold authority among difficult people.
verses.sanskrit_display: मृदुमप्यवमन्यन्ते तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः / मातीक्ष्णो मा मृदुर्भूस्त्वं तीक्ष्णो भव मृदुर्भव
verses.translation: People look down even on the gentle, and they shrink from the harsh. Do not be only harsh, do not be only soft: be firm when firmness is needed and gentle when gentleness is.
verses.line: People walk over the soft and fear the harsh. Be firm when it's needed, gentle when it's needed.
verses.misuse: Firmness here means clarity, not cruelty.

verses.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
verses.setting: The sage warns the deposed prince against resenting others' success.
verses.sanskrit_display: सहस्व श्रियमन्येषां यद्यपि त्वयि नास्ति सा / अन्यत्रापि सतीं लक्ष्मीं कुशला भुञ्जते नराः / अभिनिष्यन्दते देही श्रीभूतश्च द्विषज्जनात्
verses.translation: Bear the good fortune of others, even though it is not with you. Wise people know how to enjoy good fortune even when it belongs to someone else; good fortune drains away from the one who resents.
verses.line: Make peace with other people's success, even when you lack it. The wise can enjoy good fortune that isn't theirs.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which duty matters most; Bhishma names honouring parents and teachers.
verses.sanskrit_display: मातापित्रोर्गुरूणां च पूजा बहुमता मम / अत्र वर्तन्नरो लोकान्यशश्च महदश्नुते
verses.translation: Honouring one's mother, father and teachers is, I think, the highest duty. One who lives this way wins the worlds and great renown.
verses.line: Of all duties, honouring your mother, father and teachers stands among the highest.
verses.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean obeying them into harm; verses 108.4-5 (obey even against dharma) are deliberately left out.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma on public slander, answering Yudhishthira's question about being insulted in an assembly.
verses.sanskrit_display: परिवादं ब्रुवाणो हि दुरात्मा वै महाजने / प्रकाशयति दोषान्स्वान्सर्पः फणमिवोन्नतम्
verses.translation: The person who speaks ill of others in front of a crowd only puts his own faults on display, the way a snake raises its hood.
verses.line: Whoever runs others down in public only puts their own faults on display.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Yudhishthira asks how a calm person should respond when a loud fool insults him in public.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रकृत्या हि प्रशंसन्वा निन्दन्वा किं करिष्यति / वने काक इवाबुद्धिर्वाश्यमानो निरर्थकम्
verses.translation: Whether such a person praises you or blames you, what difference can it make? It is like a senseless crow cawing in the forest, meaning nothing.
verses.line: Whether a careless person praises or blames you, what can it do? It's a crow cawing in the forest.
verses.misuse: Fair criticism is worth hearing; this is about mindless abuse.

verses.speaker: Palita the mouse (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Trapped between a cat, an owl and a mongoose, the mouse Palita thinks through whom to trust.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रेष्ठो हि पण्डितः शत्रुर्न च मित्रमपण्डितः / अमित्रे खलु मार्जारे जीवितं संप्रतिष्ठितम्
verses.translation: A wise enemy is better than a foolish friend.
verses.line: A wise opponent is better than a foolish friend.

verses.speaker: Bharadvaja (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: A sage advises King Shatrunjaya on what really works with both soft and hard people.
verses.sanskrit_display: मृदुनैव मृदुं हन्ति मृदुना हन्ति दारुणम् / नासाध्यं मृदुना किंचित्तस्मात्तीक्ष्णतरो मृदुः
verses.translation: With gentleness one overcomes the gentle, and with gentleness one overcomes the harsh. Nothing is impossible for gentleness; that is why gentleness is said to be sharper than harshness.
verses.line: Gentleness wins over both the gentle and the harsh. It is sharper than harshness.

verses.speaker: The male pigeon (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: A male pigeon, not knowing a fowler has caught his mate, waits for her through a storm.
verses.sanskrit_display: धर्मार्थकामकालेषु भार्या पुंसः सहायिनी / विदेशगमने चास्य सैव विश्वासकारिका
verses.translation: In right living, in work and in love, a wife is a man's partner. When he goes to a foreign land, she is the one he can trust.
verses.line: A partner shares your values, your work and your joys. Far from home, they're the one you trust.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Bhima urges Yudhishthira to enjoy the kingdom; Yudhishthira answers that wanting more never ends.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाह्ना पूरयितुं शक्यां न मासैर्भरतर्षभ / अपूर्यां पूरयन्निच्छामायुषाऽपि न शक्नुयात्
verses.translation: You are trying to fill what can never be filled. Not in a day, not in months, not even in a whole lifetime could you fill it.
verses.line: Desire can't be filled in a day, a month, or a whole lifetime. Stop trying to fill it.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma closes the story of Gautama, who killed the kind crane that had sheltered and enriched him.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुतः कृतघ्नस्य यशः कुतः स्थानं कुतः सुखम् / अश्रद्धेयः कृतघ्नो हि कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः
verses.translation: Where is a good name for the ungrateful, where is a place to stand, where is happiness? No one can trust an ungrateful person.
verses.line: Ingratitude costs you trust, and without trust there's no peace or standing anywhere.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma closes the story of Gautama, who killed the kind crane that had sheltered and enriched him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्थाद्वा मित्रलाभाद्वा मित्रलाभो विशिष्यते / सुलभा मित्रतोऽर्थास्तु मित्रेण यतितुं क्षमम्
verses.translation: Between gaining money and gaining a friend, gaining a friend is better. Money comes easily through friends, and with a friend you can attempt anything.
verses.line: A good friend is worth more than money. Money comes and goes; a friend helps you face anything.

verses.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: The brahmin explains to King Senajit why loss hurts so much.
verses.sanskrit_display: किंचिदेव ममत्वेन यदा भवति कल्पितम् / तदेव परितापाय नाशे संपद्यते तदा
verses.translation: Whatever a person begins to think of as 'mine', that very thing becomes a source of anguish when it is lost.
verses.line: Whatever you start calling 'mine' becomes a source of pain the day you lose it.

verses.speaker: Medhavin
verses.setting: A young man named Medhavin tells his father not to put off what matters, because time is running out.
verses.sanskrit_display: को हि जानाति कस्याद्य मृत्युकालो भविष्यति / युवैव धर्मशीलः स्यादनित्यं खलु जीवितम् / कृते धर्मे भवेत्कीर्तिरिह प्रेत्य च वै सुखम्
verses.translation: Who knows whose time of death will come today? Live rightly while you are still young; life is uncertain.
verses.line: No one knows which day is their last. Live well now, while you still can.

verses.speaker: Medhavin
verses.setting: A young man named Medhavin tells his father not to put off what matters, because time is running out.
verses.sanskrit_display: मृत्युनाभ्याहतो लोको जरया परिवारितः / अहोरात्राः पतन्त्येते ननु कस्मान्न बुध्यसे / अमोघा रात्रयश्चापि नित्यमायान्ति यान्ति च
verses.translation: The world is struck by death and hemmed in by old age, and the days and nights keep falling like arrows. Why don't you wake up to it?
verses.line: Days and nights keep falling away. Wake up to how short this is.

verses.speaker: Shampaka (quoted by Bhishma)
verses.setting: A brahmin named Shampaka, who lost everything, tells Bhishma why having little brought him peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: आकिञ्चन्ये च राज्ये च विशेषः सुमहानयम् / नित्योद्विग्नो हि धनवान्मृत्योरास्यगतो यथा
verses.translation: Between having nothing and having a kingdom there is this great difference: the rich man is always anxious, as if he were in the jaws of death.
verses.line: The more you hold, the more you fear losing. Wealth can come with constant anxiety.
verses.misuse: Not a case against earning a living or providing for family; it is about the anxiety that comes with clinging.

verses.speaker: Shampaka (quoted by Bhishma)
verses.setting: A brahmin named Shampaka, who lost everything, tells Bhishma why having little brought him peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: नात्यक्त्वा सुखमाप्नोति नात्यक्त्वा विन्दते परम् / नात्यक्त्वा चाभयः शेते त्यक्त्वा सर्वं सुखी भवेत्
verses.translation: Without letting go, no one finds happiness; without letting go, no one reaches the highest; without letting go, no one sleeps free of fear. Let go of everything and be happy.
verses.line: Without letting go, there's no happiness and no fearless sleep.

verses.speaker: King Janaka (quoted by Bhishma)
verses.setting: King Janaka's famous saying on freedom from possessiveness, quoted by Bhishma.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनन्तमिव मे वित्तं यस्य मे नास्ति किंचन / मिथिलायां प्रदीप्तायां न मे दह्यति किंचन
verses.translation: My wealth seems endless, because nothing at all is mine. If all of Mithila were burning, nothing of mine would burn.
verses.line: My wealth feels endless because nothing is 'mine'. If my whole city burned, nothing of mine would burn.
verses.misuse: Not 'don't care for anything'; care without clutching.

verses.speaker: Bodhya
verses.setting: The calm sage Bodhya tells King Yayati about one of his six teachers: an osprey.
verses.sanskrit_display: सामिषं कुररं दृष्ट्वा वध्यमानं निरामिषैः / आमिषस्य परित्यागात्कुररः सुखमेधते
verses.translation: Seeing an osprey with meat in its beak, the birds without meat attack it. By dropping the meat, the osprey is left to live in peace.
verses.line: The bird holding the scrap of meat gets attacked. Drop it, and you're left in peace.

verses.speaker: The Ajagara sage
verses.setting: A wandering sage who lives like the python, taking what comes, explains his contentment to Prahlada.
verses.sanskrit_display: न सन्निपतितं धर्म्यमुपभोगं यदृच्छया / प्रत्याचक्षे न चाप्येनमनुरुध्ये सुदुर्लभम्
verses.translation: I do not refuse a rightful pleasure that comes to me on its own, nor do I go chasing after one that is hard to get.
verses.line: I don't refuse good things that come to me, and I don't chase what's hard to get.

verses.speaker: Indra, disguised as a jackal
verses.setting: The jackal tells Kashyapa that getting more will not cure his discontent.
verses.sanskrit_display: न तृप्तिः प्रियलाभेऽस्ति तृष्णा नाद्भिः प्रशाम्यति / संप्रज्वलति सा भूयः समिद्भिरिव पावकः
verses.translation: There is no satisfaction in getting what you want. Craving is not put out by water; it only blazes up more, like a fire fed with fuel.
verses.line: Getting what you want doesn't satisfy. Craving grows like a fire fed with more wood.

verses.speaker: Bali
verses.setting: Indra, now king of the gods, finds his fallen rival Bali living as a donkey and mocks him.
verses.sanskrit_display: न त्वेतदनुरूपं ते यशसो वा कुलस्य च / समृद्धार्थोऽसमृद्धार्थं यन्मां कत्थितुमिच्छसि
verses.translation: It does not suit your reputation or your family that you, who have everything, should wish to boast over me, who have lost it.
verses.line: Gloating over someone who has fallen says more about you than about them.

verses.speaker: Bali
verses.setting: Indra, now king of the gods, finds his fallen rival Bali living as a donkey and mocks him.
verses.sanskrit_display: न तु विक्रमकालोऽयं शान्तिकालोऽयमागतः / कालः स्थापयते सर्वं कालः पचति वै तथा
verses.translation: This is not a time for putting forth strength; a time for calm has come. Time sets everything in place, and time ripens everything.
verses.line: Not every season is for pushing. Some are for calm. Time ripens everything.
verses.misuse: A season for calm is not a reason to accept injustice.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Vyasa
verses.setting: The sage Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira, who wants to starve himself to death in grief.
verses.sanskrit_display: संयोगा विप्रयोगाश्च जातानां प्राणिनां ध्रुवम् / बुद्धुदा इव तोयेषु भवन्ति न भवन्ति च
verses.translation: For every living being, meeting and parting are certain. Like bubbles on water, they appear and are gone.
verses.line: Meeting and parting come to everyone. Like bubbles on water, they rise and they vanish.

verses.speaker: Tuladhara
verses.setting: Tuladhara, a merchant, teaches the proud ascetic Jajali what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वेषां यः सुहृन्नित्यं सर्वेषां च हिते रतः / कर्मणा मनसा वाचा स धर्मं वेद जाजले
verses.translation: Jajali, the one who is always a friend to all, devoted to the good of all, in action, thought and word, is the one who truly knows dharma.
verses.line: The one who is a friend to everyone, in action, thought and word, truly knows what is right.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verses.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verses.sanskrit_display: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verses.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verses.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verses.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to bear the loss of family and wealth.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्वासे क्व च गमिष्यामि कोऽन्वहं किमिहास्थितः / कस्मात्किमनुशोचेयमित्येवं स्थापयेन्मनः
verses.translation: 'Where was I before? Where will I go? Who am I, really, and why am I here? Why should I grieve, and for what?' Ask these, and steady the mind.
verses.line: In grief, ask: where did I come from, where am I going, who am I? Let that steady you.
verses.misuse: These questions are for steadying grief, not for dismissing it; mourning is natural.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verses.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to bear the loss of family and wealth.
verses.sanskrit_display: नायमत्यन्तसंवासो लभ्यते जातु केनचित् / अपि स्वेन शरीरेण किमुतान्येन केनचित्
verses.translation: No one ever gets to live together with anyone forever, not even with one's own body, let alone with anyone else.
verses.line: No one gets to stay with anyone forever, not even with their own body.

verses.speaker: Chirakari
verses.setting: Ordered to kill his mother, Chirakari first weighs what a father is.
verses.sanskrit_display: मुच्यते बन्धनात्पुरुषं फलं वृक्षान्प्रमुच्यते / क्लिश्यन्नपि सुतस्नेहैः पिता पुत्रं न मुञ्चति
verses.translation: A grown person is freed from his bonds as fruit drops from the tree. But a father, even suffering through his love, never lets go of his child.
verses.line: Children grow and leave like fruit from a tree. A father's love, even when it hurts him, never lets go.

verses.speaker: Chirakari
verses.setting: Ordered to kill his mother, Chirakari slowly weighs what a mother is.
verses.sanskrit_display: पुत्रपौत्रोपपन्नोपि जननीं यः समाश्रितः / अपि वर्षशतस्यान्ते स द्विहायनवच्चरेत्
verses.translation: Even with sons and grandsons around him, someone who still has his mother to turn to lives like a two-year-old, even at a hundred.
verses.line: Whoever still has their mother to turn to is a little child, even at a hundred.

verses.speaker: Chirakari
verses.setting: Ordered to kill his mother, Chirakari slowly weighs what a mother is.
verses.sanskrit_display: समर्थं वाऽसमर्थं वा कृशं वाप्यकृशं तथा / रक्षत्येव सुतं माता नान्यः पोष्टा विधानतः
verses.translation: Capable or not, thin or well-fed, a mother protects her child. No one else nurtures like that.
verses.line: Strong or weak, thriving or struggling, a mother protects her child. No one nurtures like that.

verses.speaker: Gautama
verses.setting: Gautama returns, remorseful, realising his rage against his wife came from jealousy.
verses.sanskrit_display: ईर्ष्याजं व्यसनं प्राहुस्तेन चैवोर्ध्वरेतसः / ईर्ष्यया त्वहमाक्षिप्तो मग्नो दुष्कृतसागरे
verses.translation: They say ruin is born of jealousy; even ascetics fall to it. Jealousy threw me into a sea of wrongdoing.
verses.line: Jealousy can drown even a disciplined person. Mine threw me into a sea of wrongs.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Gautama orders his son Chirakari, 'the slow one', to kill his mother; the son deliberates, and saves them all.
verses.sanskrit_display: एवं सर्वेषु कार्येषु विमृश्य पुरुषस्ततः / चिरेण निश्चयं कृत्वा चिरं न परितप्यते
verses.translation: So, in every matter, a person should think it over and decide slowly; then he does not suffer regret for long.
verses.line: Think it over and decide slowly, and you'll spend far less time in regret.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Narada (retold by Krishna)
verses.setting: Narada consoles King Srinjaya, whose only son has died, by telling of sixteen great kings who also died.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखदुःखैरहं त्वं च प्रजाः सर्वाश्च सृञ्जय / अविमुक्ता मरिष्यामस्तत्र का परिदेवना
verses.translation: Srinjaya, you, I and all creatures will die without being freed from joy and sorrow. So why such lament?
verses.line: You, I and everyone will die, all of us still mixed with joy and sorrow. You're not alone in this.
verses.misuse: It is not telling a grieving parent to stop crying; the story ends with the son restored.

verses.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
verses.setting: The golden swan tells the Sadhyas who deserves to be called wise.
verses.sanskrit_display: वाचो वेगं मनसः क्रोधवेगं / विधित्सावेगमुदरोपस्थवेगम् / एतान्वेगान्यो विषहेदुदीर्णां / स्तं मन्येऽहं ब्राह्मणं वै मुनिं च
verses.translation: The rush of speech, the surge of anger, the itch to scheme, the urges of belly and body: the one who can withstand these urges when they rise, him I call a true sage.
verses.line: Whoever can ride out the urge to speak, the surge of anger and the itch to grab is truly wise.

verses.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
verses.setting: The golden swan on why criticism can feel louder than praise.
verses.sanskrit_display: न तथा वक्तुमिच्छन्ति कल्याणान्पुरुषे गुणान् / यथैषां वक्तुमिच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यमनुयुञ्जकाः
verses.translation: Fault-finders are never as eager to speak of a person's good qualities as they are to speak of his flaws.
verses.line: Critics never talk about your good qualities as eagerly as they talk about your flaws.

verses.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
verses.setting: The golden swan on what anger costs.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्क्रोधनो यजति यद्ददाति / यद्वा तपस्तप्यति यज्जुहोति / वैवस्वतस्तद्धरतेऽस्य सर्वं / मोघः श्रमो भवति हि क्रोधनस्य
verses.translation: Whatever an angry person offers, gives, endures in discipline or sacrifices, Yama takes it all away. The angry man's labour is wasted.
verses.line: Whatever you do in anger, the good of it is lost. Anger wastes all your effort.

verses.speaker: Sanatkumara (quoted by Narada)
verses.setting: Narada passes on the sage Sanatkumara's teaching to the young Shuka, Vyasa's son.
verses.sanskrit_display: नित्यं क्रोधात्तपो रक्षेच्छ्रियं रक्षेच्च मत्सरात् / विद्यां मानावमानाभ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः
verses.translation: Always guard your discipline from anger and your good fortune from envy; guard your learning from both pride and insult, and guard yourself from carelessness.
verses.line: Guard your effort from anger, your success from envy, your learning from pride, and yourself from carelessness.

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada to Shuka on troubles that affect many people at once.
verses.sanskrit_display: न जानपदिकं दुःखमेकः शोचितुमर्हति / अशोचन्प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम्
verses.translation: No one should sit alone grieving over a trouble that has struck everyone. Instead of grieving, act to remedy it if you see a way.
verses.line: Don't just grieve over a problem everyone faces. If you see a way to fix it, act.

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: The sage Narada comforts the young Shuka with a teaching on grief and contentment.
verses.sanskrit_display: अन्यामन्यां धनावस्थां प्राप्य वैशेषिकीं नराः / अतृप्ता यान्ति विध्वंसं संतोषं यान्ति पण्डिताः
verses.translation: Reaching one level of wealth after another, people remain unsatisfied and come to ruin. The wise come to contentment.
verses.line: Each new level of wealth just reveals the next one. The wise stop and find contentment.

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada to Shuka on why more is never enough.
verses.sanskrit_display: अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायास्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम् / तस्मात्संतोषमेवेह धनं पश्यन्ति पण्डिताः
verses.translation: There is no end to thirst; contentment is the highest happiness. That is why the wise see contentment itself as wealth.
verses.line: There's no end to wanting. Contentment is the highest happiness, and the real wealth.

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: The sage Narada comforts the young Shuka with a teaching on grief and contentment.
verses.sanskrit_display: निमेषमात्रमपि हि वयो गच्छन्न तिष्ठति / स्वशरीरेष्वनित्येषु नित्यं किमनुचिन्तयेत्
verses.translation: Not even for the blink of an eye does life stand still. In a body that is passing, why brood as if things last forever?
verses.line: Life doesn't pause, not even for the blink of an eye. Don't spend it brooding.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: After the war, Yudhishthira, crushed by grief and guilt over the dead, wants to renounce the throne.
verses.sanskrit_display: बहुकल्याणमिच्छन्त ईहन्ते पितरः सुतान् / तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण वन्दनेन तितिक्षया उपवासैस्तथेज्याभिर्व्रतकौतुकमङ्गलैः / लभन्ते मातरो गर्भांस्तान्मासान्दश बिभ्रति
verses.translation: Fathers long for every good thing for their children, and strive for them with discipline, prayer and patience. Mothers, through fasts and vows, conceive them and carry them for ten months.
verses.line: Parents give years of patience, prayer and sacrifice, hoping only for their children's good.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira that relatives are difficult, and still indispensable.
verses.sanskrit_display: निकृतस्य नरैरन्यैर्ज्ञातिरेव परायणम् / नान्यो निकारं सहते ज्ञातिर्ज्ञातेः कदाचन
verses.translation: When others wrong you, your own people are your refuge. No one else will stand up against your humiliation the way family does.
verses.line: When the world wrongs you, family is the refuge. Nobody feels your hurt like they do.

verses.speaker: Narada (quoted by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: ज्ञातीनां वक्तुकामानां कटुकानि लधूनि च / गिरा त्वं हृदयं वाचं शमयस्य मनांसि च
verses.translation: When relatives are about to say bitter or petty things, calm their hearts, their words and their minds with your own words.
verses.line: When relatives are about to say something bitter, calm things down with your own gentle words.

verses.speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: अरणीमग्निकामो वा मथ्नाति दहृयं मम / वाचा दुरुक्तं देवर्षे तन्मां दहति नित्यदा
verses.translation: My heart is churned the way someone wanting fire churns a fire-stick. The harsh words my relatives say keep burning me, day after day.
verses.line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Asked how a person lives long and well, Bhishma describes everyday good conduct.
verses.sanskrit_display: परापवादं न ब्रूयान्नाप्रियं च कदाचन / न मन्युः कश्चिदुत्पाद्यः पुरुषेणि भवार्थिना
verses.translation: Never speak ill of others or say unpleasant things. A person who wants to prosper should never stir up anyone's anger.
verses.line: Don't speak ill of others, and don't go out of your way to provoke anyone's anger.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Asked how a person lives long and well, Bhishma describes everyday good conduct.
verses.sanskrit_display: वृद्धो ज्ञातिस्तथा मित्रमनाथा च स्वसा गुरुः / कुलीनः पण्डित इति रक्ष्या निःस्वः स्वशक्तितः / गृहे वासयितव्यास्ते धन्यमायुष्यमेव च
verses.translation: An aged relative, a friend, a sister with no one to support her, a teacher, a person of good family or learning who has fallen poor: protect them as you are able, and give them a place in your home.
verses.line: An aging relative, a friend in need, a sister with no support: make room for them as you can.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Asked how a person lives long and well, Bhishma describes everyday good conduct.
verses.sanskrit_display: अक्रोधनः सत्यवादी भूतानामविहिंसकः / अनसूयुरजिह्मश्च शतं वर्षाणि जीवति
verses.translation: One who is slow to anger, truthful, harms no living being, does not envy and is not crooked lives a hundred years.
verses.line: Slow to anger, honest, harmless, free of envy and straight with people: that is how to live long.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma on whom one must never mock, in his teaching on good conduct.
verses.sanskrit_display: हीनाङ्गानतिरिक्ताङ्गान्विद्याहीनान्वयोधिकान् / रूपद्रविणहीनांश्च सत्यहीनांश्च नाक्षिपेत्
verses.translation: Never taunt anyone for a missing limb or an extra one, for lack of learning, for age, for lack of looks or money, or for lack of standing.
verses.line: Never mock anyone for their body, their age, their looks, their money or their schooling.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Asked how a person lives long and well, Bhishma describes everyday good conduct.
verses.sanskrit_display: न चाभ्युदितसायी स्यात्प्रायश्चित्ती तथा भवेत् / मातापितरमुत्थाय पूर्वमेवाभिवादयेत् / आचार्यमथवाऽप्यन्तं तथाऽऽयुर्विदन्ते महत्
verses.translation: Don't sleep past sunrise. On rising, first greet your mother and father, and your teacher or another elder; that is how a long life is won.
verses.line: Start the day by greeting your mother and father. Small daily respect adds up to a good life.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how an eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and they him.
verses.sanskrit_display: भ्रातॄणामविभक्तानामुत्थानमपि चेत्सह / न पुत्रभागं विषमं पिता दद्यात्कदाचन
verses.translation: If undivided brothers decide to split the property while the father lives, the father should never give unequal shares.
verses.line: When parents divide what they have, unequal shares plant resentment for a generation. Be fair.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how an eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and they him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अन्धः स्यादन्धवेलायां जडः स्यादपि वा बुधः / परिहारेण तद्ब्रूयाद्यस्तेषां स्याद्व्यतिक्रमः
verses.translation: At times the elder should act blind, or slow, even though he is wise. If a younger one goes wrong, point it out indirectly.
verses.line: Sometimes the wise choice is to not see every mistake. When you must correct someone, do it gently.
verses.misuse: Overlooking small slips is different from ignoring real harm or danger.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how an eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and they him.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रत्यक्षं भिन्नहृदया भेदयेयुर्यथाऽहिताः / `श्रियाऽभितप्तास्तद्भेदान्नभिन्नाः स्युः समाहिताः' / श्रियाऽभितप्ताः कौन्तेय भेदकामास्तथाऽरयः
verses.translation: Outsiders who burn at a family's good fortune try to break it apart, sowing division between brothers. Those who stay close are not divided.
verses.line: People who envy a family's good fortune try to divide it. Don't let them come between you.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how an eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and they him.
verses.sanskrit_display: ज्येष्ठः कुलं वर्धयति विनाशयति वा पुनः / हन्ति सर्वमपि ज्येष्ठः प्रायो दुर्विनयादिह
verses.translation: The eldest can make a family flourish, or destroy it. Usually, when he ruins everything, it is through arrogance.
verses.line: The eldest can make a family flourish or break it, and arrogance is usually what breaks it.

verses.speaker: Desire (the Kama Gita, quoted by Krishna)
verses.setting: Krishna quotes the song of Desire itself, boasting how it survives every attack.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो मां प्रयतते हन्तुं ज्ञात्वा प्रहरणे बलम् / तस्य तस्मिन्प्रहरणे पुनः प्रादुर्भवाम्यहम्
verses.translation: Whoever tries to kill me, relying on the strength of some weapon, finds me reborn in that very weapon.
verses.line: Fight a craving with force alone, and it comes back inside the very thing you fought it with.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna tells the grieving Yudhishthira that his hardest battle, against his own mind, has just begun.
verses.sanskrit_display: लब्ध्वा हि पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां सहस्थावरजङ्गमाम् / ममत्वं यस्य नैव स्यात्किं तया स करिष्यति अथवा वसतः पार्थ वने वन्येन जीवतः / ममता यस्य वित्तेषु मृत्योरांस्ये स वर्तते
verses.translation: Even if someone gains the whole earth with everything on it, what harm can it do him if he has no sense of 'mine'? But one living in the forest on wild food, if he clings to his possessions, is already in death's jaws.
verses.line: It isn't what you have but how tightly you hold it. A mansion can be light, a hut heavy.

verses.speaker: King Ambarisha (quoted in the Anugita)
verses.setting: King Ambarisha, who had defeated every outer enemy, sings of the one he had not: his own greed.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मादेतं सम्यगवेक्ष्य लोभं / निगृह्य धृत्याऽऽत्मनि राज्यमिच्छेत् / एतद्राज्यं नान्यदस्तीह राज्य- / मात्मैव राजा विदितो यथावत्
verses.translation: So, seeing greed clearly for what it is, restrain it with steadiness and seek to rule within yourself. That is the true kingdom, there is no other; the self, rightly understood, is the king.
verses.line: Master your own greed and rule yourself. That is the only kingdom worth having.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Uttanka, furious that the war happened, threatens to curse Krishna for not stopping it.
verses.sanskrit_display: कृतो यत्नो मया पूर्वं सौशाम्ये कौरवान्प्रति / नाशक्यन्त यदा साम्ये ते स्थापयितुमञ्जसा
verses.translation: I made every effort earlier to bring the Kauravas to peace. But they could not be brought to agree, however I tried.
verses.line: I tried hard to make peace. When people refuse to be reconciled, you can't force it.

verses.speaker: Dharma (told by the mongoose)
verses.setting: A mongoose, half its body turned to gold, scoffs at Yudhishthira's grand sacrifice and tells of a poor family's gift.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षुधा निर्णुदति प्रज्ञां धर्मबुद्धिं व्यपोहति / क्षुधापरिगतज्ञानो धृतिं त्यजति चैव ह
verses.translation: Hunger drives out wisdom and pushes aside the sense of right; one overcome by hunger loses even his steadiness.
verses.line: Real need wears down judgement. Be gentle with yourself and others when money is tight.

verses.speaker: Dharma (told by the mongoose)
verses.setting: A mongoose, half its body turned to gold, scoffs at Yudhishthira's grand sacrifice and tells of a poor family's gift.
verses.sanskrit_display: न धर्मः प्रीयते तात दानैर्दत्तैर्महाफलैः / न्यायलब्धैर्यथा सूक्ष्मैः श्रुद्धापूतैः स तुष्यति
verses.translation: Dharma is not pleased by lavish gifts so much as by small ones, honestly earned and given with sincerity.
verses.line: A small gift, honestly earned and sincerely given, is worth more than a lavish one.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Shibi and the dove
verses.speaker: The hawk (Indra in disguise)
verses.setting: A hawk demands the dove King Shibi is sheltering, arguing that rules can clash.
verses.sanskrit_display: गुरुलाघवमाज्ञाय धर्माधर्मविनिश्चये / यतो भूयांस्ततो राजन्कुरु धर्मविनिश्चयम्
verses.translation: When deciding between right and wrong, weigh what is heavier against what is lighter, and choose the course where the greater good lies.
verses.line: When two duties pull against each other, weigh them, and choose the one that does more good.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Twelve-year-old Ashtavakra is stopped at King Janaka's gate because he is 'only a boy'.
verses.sanskrit_display: न ज्ञायते कायवृद्ध्या विवृद्धि- / र्यथाऽष्ठीला शाल्मलेः संप्रवृद्धाः / ह्रस्वोऽल्पकायः फलितो विवृद्धो / यश्चाफलस्तस्य न वृद्धभावः
verses.translation: Growth isn't measured by the size of the body. A short tree that bears fruit has grown; a tall one that bears none has not.
verses.line: Growth isn't size. A small tree bearing fruit has grown more than a tall, empty one.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Bhima and Hanuman
verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman, having humbled his proud younger brother Bhima, sends him off with advice.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि धर्ममविज्ञाय वृद्धाननुपसेव्य च / धर्मो वै वेदितुं शक्यो बृहस्पतिसमैरपि
verses.translation: Without learning what is right and sitting with those who have lived longer, no one can know it, not even someone as wise as Brihaspati.
verses.line: No one, however brilliant, knows what is right without learning and listening to those who've lived it.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
verses.speaker: Nahusha
verses.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं हि दिवि दिव्येन विमानन चरन्पुरा / अभिमानेन मत्तः सन्कंचिन्नान्यमचिन्तयम्
verses.translation: Once I moved through the sky in a celestial chariot, drunk on pride, and gave no thought to anyone else.
verses.line: When I was riding high, drunk on pride, I stopped thinking about anyone but myself.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
verses.speaker: Nahusha
verses.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्यं दमस्तपो योगमहिंसा ज्ञाननित्यता / साधकानि सतां पुंसां न जातिर्नकुलं नृप
verses.translation: Truth, self-control, discipline, steadiness, harmlessness and constant learning are what make a person good, O king, not birth or family.
verses.line: Truth, self-control and kindness make a person good, not their birth or family.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
verses.speaker: Nahusha asks; Yudhishthira answers
verses.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्वचिद्दानप्रयोगाद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते / सत्यवाक्याच्च राजेनद्र क्वचिद्दानं विशिष्यते
verses.translation: Sometimes truth outweighs giving, and sometimes giving outweighs truth. Likewise, harmlessness can matter more than pleasant speech. It depends on what the situation requires.
verses.line: Sometimes honesty matters more than generosity, sometimes the reverse. It depends on what's at stake.

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit_display: न लोके राजते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया / अपिचेह मृजाहीनः कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते
verses.translation: A fool does not shine in the world by praising himself; but a truly accomplished person shines even without polish.
verses.line: Self-praise never made anyone shine; real ability shows even without polish.

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रीण्येव तु पदान्याहुः सतां वृत्तमनुस्मरन् / न चैव द्रुह्येद्दद्याच्च सत्यं चैव सदा वदेत्
verses.translation: Recalling the conduct of the good, the wise name just three steps: never betray anyone, give, and always speak the truth.
verses.line: Good people walk three steps: never betray anyone, give generously, and always tell the truth.

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit_display: वेदस्योपनिषत्सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः / दमस्योपनिषत्त्यागः शिष्टाचारेषु नित्यदा
verses.translation: The essence of the Veda is truth; the essence of truth is self-control; the essence of self-control is letting go. This is always the way of the good.
verses.line: The heart of wisdom is truth; the heart of truth is self-control; the heart of self-control is letting go.

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनसूयुः कृतज्ञश्च कल्याणान्येव सेवते / सुखानि धर्ममर्थं च स्वर्गं च लभते नरः
verses.translation: The person who is free of envy and grateful keeps to what is good, and finds happiness, right living, prosperity and heaven.
verses.line: Let go of envy and stay grateful, and good things keep finding their way to you.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Satyabhama
verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Satyabhama asks Draupadi for a charm to control her husband; Draupadi says control destroys love.
verses.sanskrit_display: उद्विग्नस्य कुतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् / न जातु वशगो भर्ता स्त्रियाः स्यान्मन्त्रकारणात्
verses.translation: How can someone who feels anxious and watched have any peace? And without peace, where is happiness? No husband is ever truly won over by charms and tricks.
verses.line: No one can be at peace while being managed or manipulated. Without peace, love has nowhere to grow.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
verses.setting: Prahlada lists the times when forgiveness is the right answer.
verses.sanskrit_display: अबुद्धिमाश्रितानां तु क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनाम् / न हि सर्वत्र पाण्डित्वं सुलभं पुरुषेण वै
verses.translation: Those who did wrong out of foolishness should be forgiven, for good judgement is not easy for everyone to come by.
verses.line: Forgive people who hurt you out of foolishness. Good judgement isn't easy for anyone.
verses.misuse: Forgiving a mistake is not the same as accepting a pattern of harm.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: In exile, Draupadi urges Yudhishthira to answer injustice with force; he argues for forgiveness.
verses.sanskrit_display: वस्तु क्रोधं समुत्पन्नं प्रज्ञया परिबाधते / तेजस्विनं तं विदुषो मन्यन्ते तत्त्वदर्शिनः
verses.translation: The person who checks anger the moment it rises, using wisdom, is the one the wise call truly powerful.
verses.line: Real strength is catching your anger as it rises and steadying it with good sense.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Kashyapa (quoted by Yudhishthira)
verses.setting: Yudhishthira quotes the sage Kashyapa's verses in praise of forgiveness.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षमा ब्रह्म क्षमा सत्यं क्षमा भूतं च भावि च / क्षमा तपः क्षमा शौचं क्षमयेदं धृतं जगत्
verses.translation: Forgiveness is the sacred; forgiveness is truth; forgiveness is what was and what will be. Forgiveness is discipline and purity. It is forgiveness that holds this world together.
verses.line: Forgiveness is truth, discipline and purity. It is what holds the world together.
verses.misuse: Forgiveness is a strength you choose; no one is owed it as a way to keep hurting you.

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राहुः साप्तपदं मैत्रं बुधास्तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः / मित्रतां च पुरस्कृत्य किंचिद्वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु
verses.translation: The wise, who see what is true, say that walking seven steps together makes people friends. On the strength of that friendship, let me say something; please listen.
verses.line: The wise say that walking seven steps together makes two people friends.

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verses.sanskrit_display: सौहदात्सर्वभूतानां विश्वासो नाम जायते / तस्मात्सत्सु विशेपेण विश्वासं कुरुते जनः
verses.translation: Trust is born from goodwill toward all beings. That is why people place their trust above all in the good.
verses.line: Trust grows out of goodwill. People trust those who wish everyone well.

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verses.sanskrit_display: आर्यजुष्टमिदं वृत्तमिति विज्ञाय शाश्वतम् / सन्तः परार्थं कुर्वाणा नावेक्षन्ति प्रतिक्रियाः
verses.translation: Knowing this to be the noble, timeless way, the good keep working for others' sake without looking for anything in return.
verses.line: Good people help others without keeping score or waiting for something back.
verses.misuse: Helping without keeping score is different from letting others use you; boundaries still matter.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Asked by the Yaksha what makes a person truly learned, Yudhishthira points to action.
verses.sanskrit_display: पठकाः पाठकाश्चैव ये चान्ये शास्त्रचिन्तकाः / सर्वे व्यसनिनो मूर्खा यः क्रियावान्स पण्डितः
verses.translation: Readers, teachers and all others who merely mull over scripture are addicts and fools; the one who acts on it is the truly learned one.
verses.line: Reading and talking about wisdom isn't wisdom. The one who acts on it is wise.
verses.misuse: Not anti-learning; it is against learning that never becomes action.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: व्याख्याता मे त्वया प्रश्ना यथातत्वं परंतप / पुरुषं त्विदानींव्याख्याहि यश्च सर्वधनी नरः तुल्ये प्रियाप्रिये यस् सुखदुःखे तथैव च / अतीतानागते चोभे सवै पुरुष उच्येत
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'You have answered my questions truly. Now tell me who is truly a person, and who possesses every wealth.' Yudhishthira: 'One to whom the pleasant and the unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future are all alike: he is called a true person.'
verses.line: Truly whole is the one who meets pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future with an even mind.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Offered one brother's life, Yudhishthira picks his stepmother's son Nakula over mighty Bhima and Arjuna.
verses.sanskrit_display: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः परमार्थाच्चमे मतम् / आनृशंस्यं चिकीर्षामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु
verses.translation: Kindness is the highest dharma, higher in my view than even the highest gain. I want to act with kindness: let Nakula live, Yaksha.
verses.line: I hold kindness higher than even the greatest advantage.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: किंस्वित्प्रवसतो मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस् च किं मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं मरिष्यतः विद्या प्रवसतो मित्रं भार्या मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस्य भिषङ्भित्रं दानं मित्रं मरिष्यतः
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'Who is the friend of one away from home? Who is the friend of one at home? Who is the friend of the sick? Who is the friend of one about to die?' Yudhishthira: 'Learning is the friend of one abroad; a spouse is the friend at home; the doctor is the friend of the sick; what one has given is the friend of the dying.'
verses.line: Abroad, your learning is your friend; at home, your spouse; when ill, a doctor; at the end, what you gave.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: किंस्विदेकपदं धर्म्यं किंस्विदेकपदं यशः / किंस्विदेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं किंस्विदेकपदं सुखम् दाक्ष्यमेकपदं धर्म्यं दानमेकपदं यशः / सत्यमेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं शीलमेकपदंसुखम्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What single step leads to righteousness? What single step to good name? What single step to heaven? What single step to happiness?' Yudhishthira: 'Competence is the one step to righteousness; giving, to good name; truth, to heaven; good character, to happiness.'
verses.line: Competence is the way to goodness, giving to a good name, truth to heaven, good character to happiness.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: तपः किंलक्षणं प्रोक्तं को दमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / क्षमा च का परा प्रोक्ता का च ह्रीः परिकीर्तिता तपः स्वधर्मवर्तित्वं मनसो दमनं दमः / क्षमा द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वंहीरकार्यनिवर्तनम्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What is called austerity? What is self-restraint? What is the highest forbearance? What is shame?' Yudhishthira: 'Austerity is staying true to one's own duty; restraint is taming the mind; forbearance is bearing life's opposites; shame is turning back from what should not be done.'
verses.line: Real restraint is taming the mind; real patience is bearing life's ups and downs.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: किं ज्ञानं प्रोच्यते राजन्कः शमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / दया च का परा प्रोक्ता किं चार्जवमुदाहृतम् ज्ञानं तत्त्वार्थसम्बोधः शमश्चित्तप्रशान्तता / दयासर्वसुखैपित्वमार्जवं समचित्तता
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What is called knowledge? What is calm? What is the highest compassion? What is straightforwardness?' Yudhishthira: 'Knowledge is understanding things as they truly are; calm is a quiet mind; compassion is wishing happiness for all; straightforwardness is an even mind.'
verses.line: Calm is simply a quiet mind. Compassion is wishing every being well.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: किं स्थैर्यमृषिभिः प्रोक्तं किं च धैर्यमुदाहृतम् / स्नानं च किं परं प्रोक्तं दानं च किमिहोच्यते स्वधर्मे स्थिरता स्थैर्यं धैर्यमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः / स्नानं मनोमलत्यागो दानं वै भूतरक्षणम्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What do the sages call steadiness? What is fortitude? What is the best bath? What is true giving?' Yudhishthira: 'Steadiness is standing firm in one's duty; fortitude is mastery of the senses; the best bath is washing away the mind's impurities; true giving is protecting living beings.'
verses.line: The best bath is washing the mind clean; the truest gift is protecting others.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
verses.speaker: Narrator (Brihadashva)
verses.setting: King Nala, possessed by the spirit of the dice, keeps gambling against his brother.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथायथा हि नृपतिः पुष्करेणैव जीयते / तथातथाऽस्य वै द्यूते रागो भूयोऽभिवर्धते
verses.translation: The more the king kept losing to Pushkara, the more his passion for the dice grew.
verses.line: The more Nala lost, the harder he found it to stop playing.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
verses.speaker: Damayanti
verses.setting: Nala has lost everything at dice; Damayanti follows him into the forest and will not leave.
verses.sanskrit_display: न च भार्यासमं किंचिन्नरस्यार्तस्य भेषजम् / नित्यं हि सर्वदुःखेषु सत्यमेतद्व्रवीमि ते
verses.translation: There is no medicine like a wife for a man in pain, in every kind of sorrow. I tell you this truly.
verses.line: In every sorrow, no medicine works like a partner who stays by your side.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Gandhari
verses.setting: Queen Gandhari is called into court to reason with her son Duryodhana, who has rejected peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: अविधेयानि हीमानि व्यापादयितुमप्यलम् / अविधेया इवादान्ता हयाः पथि कुसारथिम्
verses.translation: Untamed senses are enough to destroy a person, the way unbroken horses can kill a poor charioteer on the road.
verses.line: Untamed urges are like wild horses. Let them run, and they'll wreck the one holding the reins.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Gandhari
verses.setting: Queen Gandhari is called into court to reason with her son Duryodhana, who has rejected peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: अलमर्धं पृथिव्यास्ते महामात्यस्य जीवितुम् / सुहृदां वचने तिष्ठन्यशः प्राप्स्यति भारत
verses.translation: Half the earth is enough for you and your counsellors to live on. Listen to those who wish you well, and you will win a good name.
verses.line: Half is more than enough. Share, and listen to the people who want good things for you.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit_display: उद्यम्य धुरमुत्कर्षेदाजानेयकतं स्मरन् / कुरु सत्वं च मानं च विद्धि पौरुषमात्मनः
verses.translation: Lift the load and pull it forward, remembering how a thoroughbred works. Summon your strength and your self-respect; know the power that is in you.
verses.line: Pick up the load again. Summon your strength and self-respect, and know the power in you.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit_display: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verses.translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
verses.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
verses.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Sanjaya's counsel
verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.setting: Sent by Dhritarashtra, Sanjaya urges Yudhishthira not to go to war for a kingdom.
verses.sanskrit_display: लब्ध्वाऽपीमां पृथिवीं सागरान्तां / जरामृत्यू नैव हि त्वं प्रजह्याः / प्रियाप्रिये सुखदुःखे च राज- / न्नैवं विद्वान्नैव युद्धं कुरु त्वम्
verses.translation: Even if you win this whole earth to the edge of the sea, you will not escape old age and death, or the pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow.
verses.line: Win the whole world and you still won't escape old age, death, joy and sorrow.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: अष्टौ गुमाः पुरुषं दीपयन्ति / प्रज्ञा च कौल्यं च दमः श्रुतं च / पराक्रमश्चाबहुभाषिता च / दानं यथाशक्ति कृतज्ञता च
verses.translation: Eight qualities make a person shine: wisdom, a good upbringing, self-control, learning, courage, speaking little, giving as much as one can, and gratitude.
verses.line: Eight things make a person shine: wisdom, upbringing, self-control, learning, courage, few words, generosity, gratitude.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: न स्वे सुखे वै कुरुते प्रहर्षं / नान्यस्य दुःखे भवति प्रहृष्टः / दत्त्वा न पश्चात्कुरुतेऽनुतापं / स कथ्यते सत्पुरुषार्यशीलः
verses.translation: He does not gloat over his own happiness, takes no pleasure in another's sorrow, and does not regret what he has given: such a person is called good and noble.
verses.line: Don't gloat over your joy, don't enjoy another's pain, and never regret what you gave.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: अभियुक्तं बलवता दुर्बलं हीनसाधनम् / हृतस्वं कामिनं चोरमाविशन्ति प्रजागराः
verses.translation: Sleeplessness takes hold of a weak man attacked by a stronger one, of one without resources, of one who has lost his wealth, of the lustful, and of the thief.
verses.line: Sleepless nights come to the overpowered, the stripped, the craving and the guilty.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: किं नु मे स्यादिदं कृत्वा किं नु मे स्यादकुर्वतः / इति कर्माणि सञ्चिन्त्य कुर्याद्वा पुरुषो न वा
verses.translation: 'What will happen to me if I do this? What will happen if I don't?' Thinking actions through this way, a person should then act, or not act.
verses.line: Before acting, ask two questions: what happens if I do this, and what happens if I don't?

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: य ईर्षुः परवित्तेषु रूपे वीर्ये कुलान्वये / सुखसौभाग्यसत्कारे तस्य व्याधिरनन्तकः
verses.translation: One who envies others their wealth, looks, strength, family, happiness, good fortune or honours suffers from a disease without end.
verses.line: Envying others' wealth, looks, luck or praise is a sickness that never ends.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: जरा रूपं हरति हि धैर्यमाशा / मृत्युः प्राणान्धर्मचर्यामसूया / क्रोधः श्रियं शीलमनार्यसेवा / ह्रियं कामः सर्वमेवाभिमानः
verses.translation: Age steals beauty, craving steals patience, death takes life, envy takes goodness, anger takes prosperity, bad company takes character, lust takes shame, and pride takes everything.
verses.line: Craving steals your patience, anger your fortune, bad company your character, and pride takes everything.

verses.speaker: Vidura, quoting the sage Atreya
verses.setting: Vidura retells a sage's answer to the gods, to calm the anxious King Dhritarashtra.
verses.sanskrit_display: आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः / आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति
verses.translation: When insulted, do not insult back. The anger held in by one who forbears burns up the one who insulted him, and the forbearer gains his merit.
verses.line: Insulted, don't insult back. The one who holds back keeps their worth; the insulter loses his.
verses.misuse: Not a wish for harm to come to the other person; the point is your own restraint.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: महानप्येकजो वृक्षो बलवान्सुप्रतिष्ठितः / प्रसह्य एव वातेन सस्कन्धो मर्दितुं क्षणात् अथ ये सहिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः / ते हि शीघ्रतमान्वातान्सहन्तेन्योन्यसंश्रयात्
verses.translation: A single tree, however great, strong and deep-rooted, can be wrenched out trunk and all by the wind in a moment. But trees that stand together, rooted in a cluster, withstand the fiercest winds by leaning on one another.
verses.line: A lone tree falls to the storm; trees that stand together hold each other up.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: अतिमानोऽतिवादश्च तथाऽत्यागो नराधिप / क्रोधश्चात्मविधित्सा च मित्रद्रोहश्च तानि षट् एत एवासयस्तीक्ष्णाः कृन्तन्त्यायूंषि देहिनाम् / एतानि मानवान्ध्नन्ति न मृत्युर्भद्रमस्तु ते
verses.translation: Excessive pride, talking too much, refusing to give, anger, selfishness and betraying friends: these six are sharp swords that cut short a person's life. It is these that kill people, not death.
verses.line: Arrogance, overtalking, stinginess, anger, selfishness, betraying friends: these, not death, cut a life short.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura warns Dhritarashtra that his sons and the Pandavas need each other, like a forest and its tigers.
verses.sanskrit_display: न स्याद्वनमृते व्याघ्रान्व्याघ्रा न स्युर्ऋते वनम् / वनं हि रक्ष्यते व्याघ्रैर्व्याघ्रान्रक्षति काननम्
verses.translation: There is no forest without tigers, and no tigers without the forest. The tigers protect the forest, and the forest shelters the tigers.
verses.line: No forest without tigers, no tigers without the forest. Families that fight forget they protect each other.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
