verses.sanskrit_display: सन्नियच्छति यो वेगमुत्थितं क्रोधहर्षयोः / स श्रियो भाजनं राजन्यश्चापत्सु न मुह्यति
verses.translation: Whoever reins in the rush of anger and of elation the moment they rise, and does not lose his head in trouble, is the one good fortune favours.
verses.line: Rein in the rush of anger and of excitement alike, and keep your head in trouble.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: करिष्यन्न प्रभाषेत कृतान्येव तु दर्शयेत् / धर्मकामार्थकार्याणि तथा मन्त्रो न भिद्यते
verses.translation: Don't talk about what you are going to do; let people see only what you have done. That way your plans for duty, pleasure and gain are never exposed.
verses.line: Don't announce your plans; let people see your results.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: अप्राप्तकालं वचनं बृहस्पतिरपि ब्रुवन् / लभते बुध्द्यवज्ञानमवमानं च भारत
verses.translation: Even Brihaspati, if he speaks before the right time, earns contempt for his wisdom and is disrespected.
verses.line: Even the wisest voice gets dismissed when it speaks at the wrong moment.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: कृतज्ञं धार्मिकं सत्यमक्षुद्रं दृढभक्तिकम् / जितेन्द्रियं स्थितं स्थित्यां मित्रमित्यभिवाञ्छति
verses.translation: Everyone wants as a friend someone grateful, principled, truthful, big-hearted, loyal, self-controlled and steady.
verses.line: Everyone wants a friend who is grateful, honest, generous, loyal and steady. Be that friend.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: अग्नौ प्रास्तं तु पुरुषं कर्मान्वेति स्वयं कृतम् / तस्मात्तु पुरुषो यत्नाद्धर्मं सञ्चिनुयाच्छनैः
verses.translation: When a person is laid on the pyre, only the deeds he himself did go with him. So gather goodness carefully, a little at a time.
verses.line: In the end only what we did goes with us. Gather goodness slowly, a little each day.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: महान्तमप्यर्थमधर्मयुक्तं / यः मन्त्यजत्यनपाकृष्ट एव / सुखं सुदुःखान्यवमुच्य शेते / जीर्णां त्वचं सर्प इवावमुच्य
verses.translation: One who gives up a great gain that is tainted by wrong, without waiting to be pushed, sleeps at ease, free of sorrows, like a snake that has shed its old skin.
verses.line: Walk away from a big gain that isn't clean, and you'll sleep like a snake that shed its skin.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: कामक्रोधग्राहवतीं पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां नदीम् / नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संतर
verses.translation: Make steadiness your boat and cross the river whose water is the five senses and whose crocodiles are desire and anger.
verses.line: Make steadiness your boat. Cross the river of the senses, where desire and anger wait like crocodiles.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रज्ञावृद्धं धर्मवृद्धं स्वबन्धुं / विद्यावृद्धं वयसा चापि वृद्धम् / कार्याकार्ये पूजयित्वा प्रसाद्य / यः संपृच्छेन्न स मुह्येत्कदाचित्
verses.translation: One who honours and wins over a kinsman mature in wisdom, in goodness, in learning and in years, and asks him what should and should not be done, is never confused.
verses.line: When unsure what to do, respectfully ask someone older and wiser. You won't go astray.

verses.speaker: Sanatsujata
verses.setting: The sage Sanatsujata answers King Dhritarashtra's questions about death and the self.
verses.sanskrit_display: कामानुसारी पुरुषः कामाननु विनश्यति / कामान्व्युदस्य धुनुते यत्किञ्चित्पुरुषो रजः
verses.translation: A person who runs after desires perishes along with them; one who sets desires aside shakes off whatever dust clings to him.
verses.line: Chase every desire and you go down with them; let them go and you shake off the dust.

verses.speaker: Sanatsujata
verses.setting: The sage Sanatsujata answers King Dhritarashtra's questions about death and the self.
verses.sanskrit_display: उभे सत्ये क्षत्रियाद्य प्रवृत्ते / मोहो मृत्युः संमतोऽयं कवीनाम् / प्रमादं वै मृत्युमहं ब्रवीमि / तथाऽप्रमादममृतत्वं ब्रवीमि
verses.translation: Both views are true, O king, and both have been held from the beginning. The wise regard delusion as death. I say that heedlessness is death, and heedfulness is immortality.
verses.line: Drifting through life carelessly is a kind of death; staying awake to it is immortality.

verses.speaker: Sanatsujata
verses.setting: The sage Sanatsujata answers King Dhritarashtra's questions about death and the self.
verses.sanskrit_display: मौनान्न स मुनिर्भवति नारण्यवसनान्मुनिः / स्वलक्षणं तु यो वेद स मुनिः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते
verses.translation: One does not become a sage by keeping silent, nor by living in the forest. One who knows his own true nature is called the best of sages.
verses.line: Silence and retreat don't make you wise. Knowing your own nature does.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुले जातस्य वृद्धस्य परवित्तेषु गृद्ध्यतः / लोभः प्रज्ञानमाहन्ति प्रज्ञा हन्ति हता ह्रियं ह्रीर्हता बाधते धर्मं धर्मो हन्ति हतः श्रियम् / श्रीर्हता पुरुषं हन्ति पुरुषस्याधं वधः
verses.translation: When someone from a good family covets others' wealth, greed kills his judgement; lost judgement kills his sense of shame; lost shame wears away right conduct, and with it goes prosperity, and then the person himself.
verses.line: Greed kills judgement, then shame, then integrity, and finally the person. It always starts small.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit_display: अधनाद्धि निवर्तन्ते ज्ञातयः सुहृदो द्विजाः / अपुष्पादफलाद्वृक्षाद्यथा कृष्ण पतत्रिणः
verses.translation: When a man has no money, relatives, friends and brahmins turn away from him, the way birds leave a tree that has no flowers and no fruit.
verses.line: When money runs out, some friends drift away, like birds leaving a tree with no fruit.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit_display: न तथा बाध्यते कृष्ण प्रकृत्या निर्धनो जनः / यथा भद्रां श्रियं प्राप्य तया हीनः सुखैधितः
verses.translation: Someone born poor does not suffer as much as someone who had good fortune, grew used to comfort, and then lost it.
verses.line: Losing comfort you were used to hurts more than never having had it. Be gentle with yourself.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit_display: स तदाऽऽत्मापराधेन संप्राप्तो व्यसनं महत् / सेन्द्रान्गर्हयते देवान्नात्मानं च कथंचन
verses.translation: Having fallen into great trouble through his own fault, he blames the gods, even Indra, but never himself.
verses.line: When things fall apart through our own fault, we blame everyone except ourselves.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि नः प्रीणयेद्द्रव्यं न देवत्वं कुतः सुखम् / न च सर्वामरैश्वर्यं तव द्रोहेण माधव
verses.translation: No wealth would please us, nor godhood, let alone mere comfort, nor even lordship over all the gods, if it came by betraying you, Madhava.
verses.line: No amount of money or power would make me happy if it came from betraying a friend.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Krishna (speaking for the Pandavas)
verses.setting: Krishna addresses the Kaurava court, asking Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and make peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: वर्तामहे त्वयि च तां त्वं च वर्तस्व नस्तथा / पित्रा स्थापयितव्या हि वयमुत्पथमास्थिताः
verses.translation: We have treated you as a father; treat us the same way. When children go astray, it is the father's duty to set them back on the path.
verses.line: When children go astray, a parent's job is to set them back on the path, not look away.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna addresses the Kaurava court, asking Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and make peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: धर्मज्ञेषु सभासत्सु नेह युक्तमसांप्रतम् / यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः / विद्धो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सभां यत्र प्रपद्यते
verses.translation: Where right is struck down by wrong and truth by falsehood while the assembly looks on, it is the onlookers who are struck down.
verses.line: When wrong crushes right while others watch in silence, the silent are wounded too.

verses.speaker: Bodhya
verses.setting: Bodhya describes another of his teachers to King Yayati: an arrow-maker lost in his work.
verses.sanskrit_display: इषुकारो नरः कश्चिदिपावासक्तमानसः / समीपेनापि गच्छन्तं राजानं नावबुद्धवान्
verses.translation: A certain arrow-maker was so absorbed in his arrow that he did not even notice the king passing right beside him.
verses.line: An arrow-maker was so absorbed in his work, he didn't notice the king walking past.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: पृथ्वी विभाण्डं गगनं पिघानं / सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन / मासर्तुदर्वीपरिघट्टनेन / भूतानि कालः पचतीति वार्ता
verses.translation: With the earth as the pot and the sky as its lid, with the sun as the fire and days and nights as the fuel, stirring with the ladle of months and seasons, Time is cooking all beings: that is the news.
verses.line: The only real news: time is slowly cooking us all, day by day, season by season.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Valmiki has watched a hunter kill one of a pair of cranes; his cry of grief came out as verse.
verses.sanskrit_display: समाक्षरैश्चतुर्भिर्यः पादैर्गीतो महर्षिणा। सोऽनुव्याहरणाद् भूयः शोकः श्लोकत्वमागतः॥
verses.translation: Sung by the sage in four equal lines and repeated again and again, his grief became a shloka, a poem.
verses.line: His grief, said over and over, turned into a poem. Sorrow can become something you make.

verses.speaker: Vishvamitra
verses.setting: After ten years with the celestial Menaka, Vishvamitra wakes up to how far he drifted from his goal.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहोरात्रापदेशेन गताः संवत्सरा दश ॥ काममोहाभिभूतस्य विघ्नोऽयं प्रत्युपस्थितः।
verses.translation: Ten years went by as if they were a single day and night. Lost in desire, this obstacle came and I did not see it.
verses.line: Ten years passed like a single day. Distraction rarely feels like lost time while it is happening.

verses.speaker: Narrator (Shatananda)
verses.setting: Vishvamitra has just cursed a nymph in a fit of temper and lost the merit of years of effort.
verses.sanskrit_display: कोपेन च महातेजास्तपोऽपहरणे कृते। इन्द्रियैरजितै राम न लेभे शान्तिमात्मनः॥ बभूवास्य मनश्चिन्ता तपोऽपहरणे कृते। नैवं क्रोधं गमिष्यामि न च वक्ष्ये कथंचन ॥
verses.translation: In his anger he lost what his effort had earned, and with his senses unmastered he found no peace. Then he resolved: 'I will not give way to anger like this again, and I will not speak in it.'
verses.line: Temper cost him years of work. He resolved: I won't give way to anger again, or speak from it.
verses.misuse: A vow of restraint, not a vow to swallow every hurt in silence.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Valmiki describes the young prince Ram before the crisis of the exile.
verses.sanskrit_display: कदाचिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति । न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया॥
verses.translation: A single kindness done to him, however small, was enough to please him; a hundred wrongs he did not keep in mind, being master of himself.
verses.line: One kindness was enough to please him. A hundred wrongs he did not keep count of.
verses.misuse: Not keeping score is not the same as ignoring a pattern of harm.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram asks Bharata a series of questions on how he is leading.
verses.sanskrit_display: कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिः सह। कच्चित् ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति॥
verses.translation: I hope you do not take counsel all alone, nor with too many people? And that a plan you have decided on does not spread through the land before it is carried out?
verses.line: Don't decide entirely alone, nor with too many voices. Keep plans close until they are ready.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Bharata, ashamed of his mother's scheme, begs forgiveness at Ram's feet.
verses.sanskrit_display: न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरिसूदन। न चापि जननी बाल्यात् त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.translation: I see no fault in you, not the smallest, brother. And you should not blame your mother out of immaturity.
verses.line: I see no fault in you. And don't hold your mother's mistake against her out of youthful anger.
verses.misuse: Not blaming a parent in anger is different from pretending harm did not happen.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: In the forest, Ram learns that his father died months ago, grieving for him.
verses.sanskrit_display: पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्। वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतः कर्णसुखान्यहम्॥
verses.translation: When I did something well, my father used to comfort me with words that were sweet to hear. Where will I hear such words now?
verses.line: When I did well, my father had words for me. Who will say them now?

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram consoles Bharata, who is grieving their father and begging Ram to come home.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्याः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्॥
verses.translation: Every gathering ends in running out, every rise ends in a fall, every meeting ends in parting, and every life ends in death.
verses.line: Whatever is gathered runs out, whatever rises falls, and whatever comes together will part.
verses.misuse: A reason to hold outcomes loosely, not a reason to stop building or caring.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram consoles Bharata, who is grieving their father and begging Ram to come home.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य तु व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कंचन॥ एवं भार्याश्च पुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च वसूनि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः॥
verses.translation: As two pieces of wood meet on the wide ocean and, after some time, drift apart again, so wives, children, relatives and wealth come together and then move away. Their parting is certain.
verses.line: Like two logs that meet on the ocean, people come together for a while and then drift apart.
verses.misuse: Not a case for coldness toward family; a case for treasuring the time together.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: The sceptic Jabali urges Ram to break his word and take the throne; Ram refuses.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुलीनमकुलीनं वा वीरं पुरुषमानिनम्। चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वाशुचिम्॥
verses.translation: Whether a person is noble or not, brave or merely boastful, clean or unclean, it is conduct alone that shows it.
verses.line: Your conduct, not your family or your claims, shows whether you are noble, brave or honest.

verses.speaker: Kaikeyi
verses.setting: The old king begs his favourite queen to say why she is upset; she sets her trap.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रतिज्ञा प्रतिजानीष्व यदि त्वं कर्तुमिच्छसि। अथ ते व्याहरिष्यामि यथाभिप्रार्थितं मया॥
verses.translation: Make me a promise first, if you are willing to do it. Then I will tell you what I want.
verses.line: 'Promise first, then I'll tell you what I want.' Never agree before you know the ask.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Parting at Chitrakoot, Ram asks Bharata to make peace with Kaikeyi.
verses.sanskrit_display: कामाद् वा तात लोभाद् वा मात्रा तुभ्यमिदं कृतम्। न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं वर्तितव्यं च मातृवत्॥
verses.translation: Whether from desire or greed, your mother did this for your sake. Do not hold it in your mind; treat her as a son treats his mother.
verses.line: She did it for you, out of wanting or greed. Don't carry it; treat her as your mother still.
verses.misuse: Not a call to keep an abusive parent close; Ram asks Bharata to drop resentment, not his judgement.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Ram walks out of the palace, having lost the throne he was to receive that morning.
verses.sanskrit_display: न वनं गन्तुकामस्य त्यजतश्च वसुंधराम्। सर्वलोकातिगस्येव लक्ष्यते चित्तविक्रिया॥
verses.translation: As he set out for the forest and gave up the earth, no change could be seen in his mind, as if he stood beyond the world.
verses.line: He had just lost the kingdom, and his mind showed no change at all.
verses.misuse: Calm in loss is not pretending it does not hurt; Ram grieves elsewhere in the story.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram has just accepted fourteen years of exile; one thing still hurts him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अलीकं मानसं त्वेकं हृदयं दहते मम। स्वयं यन्नाह मां राजा भरतस्याभिषेचनम्॥
verses.translation: Only one sorrow burns my heart: that the king did not tell me himself about Bharata's coronation.
verses.line: What hurt most was not the news, but that he didn't tell me himself.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Just told he is exiled, Ram calms his furious brother Lakshman.
verses.sanskrit_display: निगृह्य रोष शोकं च धैर्यमाश्रित्य केवलम्। अवमानं निरस्यैनं गृहीत्वा हर्षमुत्तमम्॥ उपक्लुप्तं यदैतन्मे अभिषेकार्थमुत्तमम्। सर्वं निवर्तय क्षिप्रं कुरु कार्य निरव्ययम्॥
verses.translation: Hold back your anger and grief, lean on steadiness alone, set this insult aside and take up real cheerfulness. Quickly undo the preparations made for my coronation and get on with what needs doing, without fuss.
verses.line: Rein in anger and grief, lean on your steadiness, and set the insult aside.
verses.misuse: Not a call to ignore injustice; it is about choosing your response.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Sita insists on sharing Ram's exile; this is her decision, argued and won.
verses.sanskrit_display: स मामनादाय वनं न त्वं प्रस्थितुमर्हसि। तपो वा यदि वारण्यं स्वर्गो वा स्यात् त्वया सह ।।१०।
verses.translation: You must not leave for the forest without me. Hardship, wilderness or heaven: let it be with you.
verses.line: Hardship, wilderness or heaven: I choose to face it with you.

verses.speaker: Sumitra
verses.setting: Lakshman's mother blesses him as he leaves to share Ram's fourteen years in the forest.
verses.sanskrit_display: लक्ष्मणं त्वेवमुक्त्वासौ संसिद्धं प्रियराघवम्। सुमित्रा गच्छ गच्छेति पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्॥ राम दशरथं विद्धि मां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्। अयोध्यामटवीं विद्धि गच्छ तात यथासुखम्॥
verses.translation: Saying 'Go, go' again and again, Sumitra told him: Think of Ram as your father Dasharatha, of Sita as me, and of the forest as Ayodhya. Go happily, my son.
verses.line: Treat the forest as home, and the people with you as family. Go well, my son.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: From exile, Ram sends Bharata a message about how to treat their ageing father.
verses.sanskrit_display: अतिक्रान्तवया राजा मा स्मैनं व्यपरोरुधः। कुमारराज्ये जीवस्व तस्यैवाज्ञाप्रवर्तनात्॥
verses.translation: The king has grown old; do not push him aside. Live as prince by carrying out his wishes.
verses.line: Your father has grown old. Don't push him aside; let him still feel he leads.

verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: After lashing out at Dasharatha over Ram's exile, Kausalya apologises and explains what grief did to her.
verses.sanskrit_display: शोको नाशयते धैर्यं शोको नाशयते श्रुतम्। शोको नाशयते सर्वं नास्ति शोकसमो रिपुः॥
verses.translation: Grief destroys steadiness, grief destroys learning, grief destroys everything. There is no enemy like grief.
verses.line: Grief wears away your steadiness and your judgement. There is no enemy like it.
verses.misuse: Not a ban on grieving; a warning not to let sorrow make your decisions.

verses.speaker: Dasharatha
verses.setting: Dying of grief, Dasharatha recalls the rash act from his youth that brought him to this.
verses.sanskrit_display: गुरुलाघवमर्थानामारम्भे कर्मणां फलम्। दोषं वा यो न जानाति स बाल इति होच्यते।७।।
verses.translation: Whoever, at the start of an undertaking, does not weigh how serious or slight it is, what it will lead to, and what could go wrong, is called a child.
verses.line: Before you start, weigh what is at stake, where it leads and what could go wrong.

verses.speaker: Bharata
verses.setting: Bharata, away at his uncle's home, returns to find his father has died while he was gone.
verses.sanskrit_display: अम्ब केनात्यगाद् राजा व्याधिना मय्यनागते। धन्या रामादयः सर्वे यैः पिता संस्कृतः स्वयम्॥
verses.translation: Mother, of what illness did the king die while I was away? Blessed are Ram and the others who performed my father's last rites themselves.
verses.line: He died while I was away. Blessed are those who were there to say goodbye.

verses.speaker: Bharata
verses.setting: Bharata learns his father has died while he was away from home.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्व स पाणिः सुखस्पर्शस्तातस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। यो हि मां रजसा ध्वस्तमभीक्ष्णं परिमार्जति॥
verses.translation: Where is my father's gentle hand now, the hand that used to brush the dust off me again and again?
verses.line: Where is that gentle hand that used to brush the dust off me?

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Seeing Bharata's army approach, Lakshman wants to fight; Ram refuses to gain anything at his family's cost.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद् द्रव्यं बान्धवानां वा मित्राणां वा क्षये भवेत्। नाहं तत् प्रतिगृह्णीयां भक्ष्यान् विषकृतानिव॥
verses.translation: Any wealth that would come to me through the ruin of my relatives or friends I would never accept, any more than food laced with poison.
verses.line: Anything gained by ruining family or friends is poisoned food. Don't take it.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Lakshman wants to fight Bharata's approaching army; Ram says the kingdom is not worth wronging anyone.
verses.sanskrit_display: नेयं मम मही सौम्य दुर्लभा सागराम्बरा। नहीच्छेयमधर्मेण शक्रत्वमपि लक्ष्मण॥
verses.translation: This sea-girt earth is not hard for me to win, gentle brother. But I would not want even Indra's throne through wrong.
verses.line: I could win it. But I wouldn't want even heaven's throne if it came through wrongdoing.

verses.collection: Aranya: Sita and Ram on non-violence
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Sita gently questions Ram's vow to fight the forest demons; Ram thanks her before explaining his stand.
verses.sanskrit_display: मम स्नेहाच्च सौहार्दादिदमुक्तं त्वा वचः॥ परितुष्टोऽस्म्यहं सीते न ह्यनिष्टोऽनुशास्यते।
verses.translation: You said this out of love and friendship for me. I am pleased with you, Sita; no one gives advice to someone they do not care about.
verses.line: No one bothers to advise a person they don't care about.
verses.misuse: Not every criticism is care; but honest counsel from people close to you usually is.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Sita is entranced by a deer with a golden, jewelled hide; Lakshman suspects a trick.
verses.sanskrit_display: अस्य मायाविदो माया मृगरूपमिदं कृतम्। भानुमत् पुरुषव्याघ्र गन्धर्वपुरसंनिभम्॥ मृगो ह्येवंविधो रत्नविचित्रो नास्ति राघव। जगत्यां जगतीनाथ मायैषा हि न संशयः॥
verses.translation: This deer's form is the trick of a master of illusion, bright as a city in the clouds. No such jewelled deer exists anywhere on earth, Raghava. It is an illusion, no doubt.
verses.line: No deer like this exists anywhere. If something looks too perfect to be real, it probably isn't.

verses.speaker: Jatayu
verses.setting: The old vulture Jatayu confronts Ravana, who is carrying Sita away.
verses.sanskrit_display: स भारः सौम्य भर्तव्यो यो नरं नावसादयेत्। तदन्नमपि भोक्तव्यं जीर्यते यदनामयम्॥
verses.translation: Carry only the load that does not crush you, friend; eat only the food you can digest without falling ill.
verses.line: Carry only the load that won't crush you; take on only what you can digest.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: After Sita is taken, Ram in fury threatens to destroy the world; Lakshman steadies him.
verses.sanskrit_display: एकस्य नापराधेन लोकान् हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि। ननु जानामि कस्यायं भग्नः सांग्रामिको रथः॥
verses.translation: You should not destroy the worlds for the wrong done by one. Surely we can find out whose broken war chariot this is.
verses.line: Don't punish the whole world for one person's wrong.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: After Sita is taken, Lakshman comforts Ram, who is lost in grief.
verses.sanskrit_display: आश्वसिही नरश्रेष्ठ प्राणिनः कस्य नापदः। संस्पृशन्त्यग्निवद् राजन् क्षणेन व्यपयान्ति च॥
verses.translation: Take heart, best of men. Which living being does trouble not touch? Troubles strike like fire, king, and pass in a moment.
verses.line: Take heart. Trouble touches everyone; it flares up like fire and passes.

verses.collection: Aranya: Sita and Ram on non-violence
verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Entering the Dandaka forest, Sita talks with Ram about duty and restraint.
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मानं नियमैस्तैस्तैः कर्षयित्वा प्रयत्नतः। प्राप्यते निपुणैर्धर्मो न सुखाल्लभते सुखम्॥
verses.translation: The skilful reach what is right by disciplining themselves with effort through many restraints. Happiness is not reached through comfort.
verses.line: Happiness is not reached through comfort. It comes through discipline and effort.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: At Lake Pampa, Lakshman pulls Ram out of despair after Sita has been taken.
verses.sanskrit_display: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
verses.translation: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
verses.line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.

verses.speaker: Tara
verses.setting: Tara urges Vali to make peace with his younger brother instead of fighting him.
verses.sanskrit_display: लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयानेष वानरः॥ तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुरेव ते। नहि तेन समं बन्धुं भुवि पश्यामि कंचन ॥
verses.translation: Your younger brother deserves your care. Near you or far away, he is your own family. I see no relative on earth to equal him.
verses.line: Near or far, your brother is still your family. No one else on earth can take his place.

verses.speaker: Tara
verses.setting: Vali storms out to fight his brother; his wife Tara stops him at the door.
verses.sanskrit_display: साधु क्रोधमिमं वीर नदीवेगमिवागतम्। शयनादुत्थितः काल्यं त्यज मुक्तामिव स्रजम्॥
verses.translation: Let go of this anger that has come on like a river in flood, as you throw off last night's garland when you get up in the morning.
verses.line: Let this anger go, the way you drop last night's garland in the morning.

verses.speaker: Vali
verses.setting: Dying, Vali advises his young son Angada how to conduct himself at his uncle Sugriva's court.
verses.sanskrit_display: न चातिप्रणयः कार्यः कर्तव्योऽप्रणयश्च ते। उभयं हि महादोषं तस्मादन्तरदृग्भव॥
verses.translation: Do not be too familiar, and do not be distant either; both are serious mistakes. So keep a sense of the middle.
verses.line: Don't be too familiar, and don't be cold. Both are mistakes; find the middle.

verses.speaker: Vali
verses.setting: Dying, Vali reflects on how the kingdom came between him and his brother.
verses.sanskrit_display: युगपद् विहितं तात न मन्ये सुखमावयोः। सौहार्दै भ्रातृयुक्तं हि तदिदं जातमन्यथा॥
verses.translation: Brother, it seems we were not meant to have both happiness at once: brotherly love and the kingdom. It turned out otherwise.
verses.line: We couldn't have both, the love between brothers and the kingdom. It went the wrong way.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Ram wants to act now, but the rains have closed every road; Lakshman counsels waiting.
verses.sanskrit_display: शरत्कालं प्रतीक्षस्व प्रावृटकालोऽयमागतः। ततः सराष्ट्र सगणं रावणं तं वधिष्यसि॥
verses.translation: The rainy season has come; wait for autumn. Then you will defeat Ravana with his kingdom and his allies.
verses.line: The rains are here. Wait for autumn. Some seasons are for waiting, not fighting.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verses.sanskrit_display: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उर:स्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verses.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verses.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Sugriva has let his promised search for Sita slide; Hanuman tells him how to face Ram's angry message.
verses.sanskrit_display: आर्तस्य हृतदारस्य परुषं पुरुषान्तरात्। वचनं मर्षणीयं ते राघवस्य महात्मनः॥
verses.translation: You must patiently bear the harsh words of great-hearted Ram, who is in pain and has lost his wife, even when they come to you through another man.
verses.line: When someone in deep pain speaks harshly to you, bear it with patience.
verses.misuse: Patience with a hurting person's outburst, not tolerance of ongoing abuse.

verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Hearing that an angry Lakshman is coming, Sugriva worries aloud to his ministers about his friendship with Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वथा सुकरं मित्रं दुष्करं प्रतिपालनम्। अनित्यत्वात् तु चित्तानां प्रीतिरल्पेऽपि भिद्यते॥
verses.translation: Making a friend is easy in every way; keeping the friendship is hard. Because minds are changeable, affection can break over very little.
verses.line: Making a friend is easy; keeping one is hard. Affection can break over very little.

verses.speaker: Tara
verses.setting: Lakshman storms into Kishkindha, furious at Sugriva's delay; Sugriva's queen Tara meets him calmly.
verses.sanskrit_display: न कोपकालः क्षितिपालपुत्र न चापि कोपः स्वजने विधेयः। त्वदर्थकामस्य जनस्य तस्य प्रमादमप्यर्हसि वीर सोढुम्॥
verses.translation: Prince, this is no time for anger, and anger should not be turned on your own people. Hero, you should bear even the lapse of someone who wants your good.
verses.line: This is no time for anger. Bear the slip of someone who is on your side.
verses.misuse: About lapses by people who mean well, not about repeated mistreatment.

verses.speaker: Tara
verses.setting: Lakshman storms into Kishkindha, furious at Sugriva's delay; Sugriva's queen Tara meets him calmly.
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्त्वयुक्ता हि पुरुषास्त्वद्विधाः पुरुषर्षभ। अविमृश्य न रोषश्य सहसा यान्ति वश्यताम् ॥
verses.translation: Best of men, people of real character, like you, do not suddenly fall under the control of anger without first thinking things over.
verses.line: Strong people don't let anger take over before they have thought things through.

verses.speaker: Angada
verses.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.
verses.sanskrit_display: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
verses.translation: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verses.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.

verses.speaker: Jambavan
verses.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
verses.sanskrit_display: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
verses.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
verses.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?

verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva, who has lost his own wife and kingdom, steadies a grieving Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: व्यसने वार्थकृच्छ्रे वा भये वा जीवितान्तगे। विमृशंश्च स्वया बुद्ध्या धृतिमान् नावसीदति॥
verses.translation: In disaster, in money trouble, in fear, even when life itself is at stake, the steady person who thinks things through with their own mind does not sink.
verses.line: In loss, money trouble or fear, the steady person thinks it through and does not go under.

verses.speaker: Beings of the sky
verses.setting: Having outwitted two monsters mid-flight, Hanuman is praised by those watching from the sky.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥
verses.translation: Whoever has these four, as you do, chief of monkeys, never sinks in his work: steadiness, clear sight, judgement and skill.
verses.line: Steadiness, clear sight, good judgement and skill. With these four, you won't sink at work.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman thanks the mountain for its offer of rest but keeps flying.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वरते कार्यकाले मे अहश्चाप्यतिवर्तते। प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्तरा॥
verses.translation: The time for my work presses on me, and the day is passing. I have given my word: I will not stop on the way.
verses.line: Thank you, but the work is waiting and I promised not to stop halfway.
verses.misuse: Focus is not refusing all rest; Hanuman rests once he lands.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Having searched all of Lanka without finding Sita, Hanuman fights off despair.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥
verses.translation: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
verses.line: Refusing to lose heart is the root of success. Look again where you have not yet looked.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman has found Sita, terrified and alone; he works out how to speak without frightening her.
verses.sanskrit_display: अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यं मानुषं वाक्यमर्थवत्। मया सान्त्वयितुं शक्या नान्यथेयमनिन्दिता ॥
verses.translation: I must speak to her in ordinary human words that carry meaning. There is no other way to comfort this blameless woman.
verses.line: To comfort someone, use their language, not the one that impresses.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Captive for months, Sita hears news of Ram from Hanuman and remembers an old saying.
verses.sanskrit_display: कल्याणी वत गाथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा। एति जीवन्तमानन्दो नरं वर्षशतादपि॥
verses.translation: How true this lovely old saying seems to me: joy comes to a person who stays alive, even if it takes a hundred years.
verses.line: As long as you are still alive, joy can find you again, even after a hundred years.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: After setting Lanka ablaze in fury, Hanuman fears he has harmed Sita and turns on his own anger.
verses.sanskrit_display: धन्याः खलु महात्मानो ये बुद्ध्या कोपमुत्थितम्। निरुन्धन्ति महात्मानो दीप्तमग्निमिवाम्भसा॥
verses.translation: Blessed indeed are the great-hearted who, with good sense, check anger the moment it rises, as water puts out a blazing fire.
verses.line: Blessed are those who use good sense to put out rising anger, the way water puts out fire.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Hanuman returns with news of Sita; Ram has nothing in exile to give him.
verses.sanskrit_display: इदं तु मम दीनस्य मनो भूयः प्रकर्षति। यदिहास्य प्रियाख्यातुर्न कुर्मि सदृशं प्रियम् ॥
verses.translation: What weighs on my mind is this: I, so poor here, cannot do anything equal in return for the one who brought me such good news.
verses.line: It pains me that I can't repay this kindness in kind. So I'll give what I have: a hug.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Lakshman lies near death on the battlefield; Ram remembers what his brother has been to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: शोकार्तस्य प्रमत्तस्य पर्वतेषु वनेषु च॥ विषण्णस्य महाबाहो समाश्वासयिता मम।
verses.translation: In the mountains and forests, when I was grief-stricken, careless and despairing, you were the one who comforted me, mighty brother.
verses.line: In every forest and every low moment, you were the one who lifted me up.

verses.speaker: Mandodari
verses.setting: Over Ravana's body, his queen Mandodari names what really defeated him.
verses.sanskrit_display: इन्द्रियाणि पुरा जित्वा जितं त्रिभुवनं त्वया॥ स्मरद्भिरिव तद्वैरमिन्द्रियैरेव निर्जितः।
verses.translation: Long ago you conquered your senses and so conquered the three worlds. Now, as if remembering that grudge, those same senses have conquered you.
verses.line: You once mastered your desires and won the world. In the end, your desires mastered you.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: After Ravana's death, Hanuman wants to punish the guards who tormented Sita; she refuses.
verses.sanskrit_display: न परः पापमादत्ते परेषां पापकर्मणाम्। समयो रक्षितव्यस्तु सन्तश्चारित्रभूषणाः।॥ पापानां वा शुभानां वा वधार्हाणामथापि वा। कार्य कारुण्यमार्येण न कश्चिन्त्रापराध्यति॥ लोकहिंसाविहाराणां क्रूराणां पापकर्मणाम्। कुर्वतामपि पापानि नैव कार्यमशोभनम् ॥
verses.translation: A good person does not repay wrongdoers in kind; the standard must be kept, for good people are adorned by their conduct. Whether people are wicked or good, or even deserve death, a noble person should be compassionate, for no one is without fault. Even toward the cruel who harm others, one should not act basely.
verses.line: Show compassion even to those who wronged you. No one is without fault.
verses.misuse: Compassion does not mean letting anyone keep hurting you.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Victory won, Vibhishana begs Ram to stay and be honoured in Lanka; Ram only wants to go home.
verses.sanskrit_display: न खल्वेतन्न कुर्यां ते वचनं राक्षसेश्वर। तं तु मे भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं भरतं त्वरते मनः॥ मां निवर्तयितुं योऽसौ चित्रकूटमुपागतः। . शिरसा याचतो यस्य वचनं न कृतं मया॥
verses.translation: It is not that I refuse you, lord of the rakshasas. But my heart hurries me to see my brother Bharata, who came to Chitrakoot to bring me back, and whose plea I did not grant.
verses.line: Thank you, truly. But my heart is in a hurry to see my brother again.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Before arriving, Ram sends Hanuman to read Bharata's face after fourteen years of ruling.
verses.sanskrit_display: संगत्या भरतः श्रीमानराज्येनार्थी स्वयं भवेत्। प्रशास्तु वसुधां सर्वामखिलां रघुनन्दनः॥
verses.translation: If, having held the kingdom so long, the fortunate Bharata now wants it for himself, let him rule the whole earth.
verses.line: If my brother wants to keep what he's been holding, let him have it. I won't fight family for it.

verses.speaker: Bharata
verses.setting: After fourteen years, Bharata places Ram's sandals back on his feet before the whole city.
verses.sanskrit_display: एतत्ते सकलं राज्यं न्यासं निर्यातितं मया॥ अद्य जन्म कृतार्थं मे संवृत्तश्च मनोरथः। यत्त्वां पश्यामि राजानमयोध्यां पुनरागतम्॥
verses.translation: This whole kingdom, which you left in my care, I hand back to you. Today my life has meaning and my wish is fulfilled, now that I see you back in Ayodhya as king.
verses.line: Everything you left in my care, I hand back. Seeing you home makes the long wait worth it.

verses.speaker: Vibhishana
verses.setting: Insulted for urging Ravana to return Sita, Vibhishana leaves the court with these words.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः। अप्रियस्य च पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः॥
verses.translation: O king, people who always say pleasant things are easy to find. Someone who says what is unwelcome but good for you is rare, and so is someone who will listen to it.
verses.line: Flatterers are easy to find. Rare is the one who tells the hard truth, rarer the one who hears it.

verses.speaker: Vibhishana
verses.setting: Insulted for urging peace, Vibhishana leaves his brother's court for good.
verses.sanskrit_display: तन्मर्षयतु यच्चोक्तं गुरुत्वाद्धितमिच्छता। आत्मानं सर्वथा रक्ष पुरीं चेमां सराक्षसाम्। स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सुखी भव मया विना॥
verses.translation: Forgive what I said; I said it for your good, out of respect for you as my elder. Protect yourself and this city. I wish you well. I am leaving. Be happy without me.
verses.line: I said it for your good. I wish you well. I'm leaving. Be happy without me.
verses.misuse: Walking away from family is a last resort after honest counsel fails, not a first response to disagreement.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram's allies suspect Vibhishana, the enemy's brother, is a spy; Ram decides to take him in.
verses.sanskrit_display: सकृदेव प्रपन्नाय तवास्मीति च याचते। अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददाम्येतद्ब्रतं मम॥
verses.translation: Whoever comes to me even once and says 'I am yours', asking for shelter, I give freedom from fear, from every being. This is my vow.
verses.line: Whoever comes once and says 'I'm with you', I will protect. That is my promise.

verses.speaker: Kumbhakarna
verses.setting: Woken in the middle of the war, Kumbhakarna bluntly tells Ravana where his planning went wrong.
verses.sanskrit_display: यः पश्चात्पूर्वकार्याणि कुर्यादैश्वर्यमास्थितः। पूर्वं चोत्तरकार्याणि न स वेद नयानयौ॥
verses.translation: A man in power who does last what should come first, and first what should come last, does not know good policy from bad.
verses.line: Whoever does first what should come last, and last what should come first, lacks judgement.

verses.speaker: Kumbhakarna
verses.setting: A courtier boasts and flatters; Kumbhakarna answers before going out to fight.
verses.sanskrit_display: न मर्षयन्ति चात्मानं संभावयितुमात्मना। अदर्शयित्वा शूरास्तु कर्म कुर्वन्ति दुष्करम्॥
verses.translation: The truly brave do not put up with praising themselves. Without showing off, they do what is hard.
verses.line: The brave don't praise themselves. They quietly do the hard thing.

verses.speaker: Valmiki
verses.setting: Moments after cursing the hunter in a burst of grief, Valmiki stops and reflects on what he said.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्येत्थं ब्रुवतश्चिन्ता बभूव हृदि वीक्षतः। शोकार्तेनास्य शकुनेः किमिदं व्याहृतं मया॥
verses.translation: As he spoke, a worry rose in his heart as he looked on: 'Overcome by grief for this bird, what is this I have said?'
verses.line: Even a sage stops after an outburst and asks: what did I just say?

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Dasharatha refuses to let teenage Ram leave with the sage Vishvamitra; his guru Vasishtha reasons with him.
verses.sanskrit_display: तेषां निग्रहणे शक्तः स्वयं च कुशिकात्मजः। तव पुत्रहितार्थाय त्वामुपेत्याभियाचते॥
verses.translation: Vishvamitra could subdue those demons himself. He has come to ask for your son for your son's own good.
verses.line: Sometimes the person asking you to let your child go is asking for your child's sake.
verses.misuse: Letting a child grow is not handing them to anyone who asks; Dasharatha trusts a proven teacher.

verses.speaker: Kushanabha
verses.setting: A king praises his daughters for refusing to curse the wind-god who had wronged them.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षमा दानं क्षमा सत्यं क्षमा यज्ञाश्च पुत्रिकाः। क्षमा यशः क्षमा धर्मः क्षमायां विष्ठितं जगत्।
verses.translation: Forbearance is giving, forbearance is truth, forbearance is sacrifice, my daughters; forbearance is honour, forbearance is righteousness; the world rests on forbearance.
verses.line: Forbearance is generosity, truth and honour. The world rests on people who can forbear.
verses.misuse: Forbearance means not retaliating, not accepting harm; the daughters had refused the god's advances.

verses.collection: Bala: the descent of the Ganga
verses.speaker: Brahma
verses.setting: Bhagiratha has finished what his great-grandfather, grandfather and father each tried and failed to do.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा त्वया समतिक्रान्ता प्रतिज्ञा पुरुषर्षभ। प्राप्तोऽसि परमं लोके यशः परमसम्मतम्॥
verses.translation: You have carried through the vow they could not keep, best of men. You have earned the highest honour in the world.
verses.line: Three generations tried and failed. You finished it. Effort carried forward is not wasted.

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: A powerful king offers a fortune for the sage's cow, the source of his whole way of life.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाहं शतसहस्रेण नापि कोटिशतैर्गवाम्॥ राजन् दास्यामि शबलां राशिभी रजतस्य वा। न परित्यागमयं मत्सकाशादरिंदम ॥
verses.translation: Not for a hundred thousand cows, not for a billion, not for heaps of silver, O king, will I give up Shabala. She stays with me.
verses.line: Not for any price. Some things are not for sale, however powerful the buyer.

verses.speaker: Narrator (Shatananda)
verses.setting: After his last relapse, Vishvamitra keeps a thousand-year vow of silence; temptations come again.
verses.sanskrit_display: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु काष्ठभूतं महामुनिम्। विघ्नैर्बहुभिराधूतं क्रोधो नान्तरमाविशत्॥
verses.translation: When the thousand years were done the great sage stood still as wood; many obstacles shook him, but anger could not get inside.
verses.line: Many things shook him. Anger could not get in.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: After the wedding, Valmiki describes Ram and Sita's early married life in Ayodhya.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रिया तु सीता रामस्य दारा पितृकृता इति॥ गुणाद् रूपगुणाच्चापि प्रीतिर्भूयोऽभिवर्धते। तस्याश्च भर्ता द्विगुणं हृदये परिवर्तते॥
verses.translation: Sita was dear to Ram as the wife his father chose; yet his love kept growing because of who she was, and in her heart he lived twice over.
verses.line: Love that began by arrangement kept growing because of who each one was.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Valmiki describes the young prince Ram before the crisis of the exile.
verses.sanskrit_display: स च नित्यं प्रशान्तात्मा मृदुपूर्वं च भाषते। उच्यमानोऽपि परुषं नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्यते॥
verses.translation: He was always calm inside and began his words gently. Even when spoken to harshly, he did not answer in kind.
verses.line: He spoke gently first, and when someone spoke harshly, he did not answer in kind.
verses.misuse: Not returning harshness is a choice of strength, not an obligation to accept abuse.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram asks Bharata a series of questions on how he is leading.
verses.sanskrit_display: कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं मदोदयम्। क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्म न दीर्घयसि राघव॥
verses.translation: Having decided on a task that costs little and yields much, do you start it quickly and not delay, Bharata?
verses.line: When a small effort promises a big result, start now. Don't drag it out.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram asks Bharata a series of questions on how he is leading.
verses.sanskrit_display: कच्चित् सहस्रैर्मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम्। पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छेषु कुर्यानिःश्रेयसं महत्॥
verses.translation: Do you prefer one wise person over a thousand fools? In a crisis, a wise person can do great good.
verses.line: One wise adviser is worth more than a thousand fools, especially in a crisis.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram consoles Bharata, who is grieving their father and begging Ram to come home.
verses.sanskrit_display: नन्दन्त्युदित आदित्ये नन्दन्त्यस्तमितेऽहनि। आत्मनो नावबुध्यन्ते मनुष्या जीवितक्षयम्॥
verses.translation: People rejoice when the sun rises and rejoice when the day ends, yet they do not notice their own life wearing away.
verses.line: We cheer each sunrise and each evening, and miss that our days are running out.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: The sceptic Jabali urges Ram to break his word and take the throne; Ram refuses.
verses.sanskrit_display: कामवृत्तोऽन्वयं लोकः कृत्स्नः समुपवर्तते। यद्वृत्ताः सन्ति राजानस्तद्वृत्ताः सन्ति हि प्रजाः॥
verses.translation: If I live by desire, the whole world will follow me, because as the rulers behave, so do the people.
verses.line: People follow the example of those who lead them.

verses.speaker: Bharata
verses.setting: Bharata will rule from a village hut for fourteen years in Ram's name, waiting.
verses.sanskrit_display: भ्रात्रा तु मयि संन्यासो निक्षिप्तः सौहृदादयम्। तमिमं पालयिष्यामि राघवागमनं प्रति॥
verses.translation: My brother has entrusted this to me out of love. I will look after it until Ram comes back.
verses.line: This was entrusted to me out of love. I'll look after it until he returns.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Just told he is exiled, Ram calms his furious brother Lakshman.
verses.sanskrit_display: मा च लक्ष्मण संतापं कार्षीर्लक्ष्या विपर्यये। राज्यं वा वनवासो वा वनवासो महोदयः॥
verses.translation: Lakshman, do not torment yourself over this reversal of fortune. Between the kingdom and life in the forest, the forest may be the greater blessing.
verses.line: Don't torment yourself over a setback. The road you didn't choose may turn out better.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Furious at Ram's exile, Lakshman argues that effort, not fate, should decide.
verses.sanskrit_display: दैवं पुरुषकारेण यः समर्थः प्रबाधितुम्। न दैवेन विपत्रार्थः पुरुषः सोऽवसीदति॥
verses.translation: The person who can push back fate with effort does not lose heart when fate damages his interests.
verses.line: Those who answer bad luck with effort don't lose heart when things go wrong.
verses.misuse: Lakshman is speaking in anger, and Ram chose restraint; take the line about effort, not the urge to fight.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram's mother wants to follow him into exile; he asks her instead to stay and look after his grieving father.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा मयि तु निष्क्रान्ते पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवः॥ श्रमं नावाप्नुयात् किंचिदप्रमत्ता तथा कुरु। दारुणश्चाप्ययं शोको यथैनं न विनाशयेत्॥ राज्ञो वृद्धस्य सततं हितं चर समाहिता।
verses.translation: Take care that when I am gone the king does not wear himself out with grief for his son, that this terrible sorrow does not destroy him. Look after the old king's welfare always.
verses.line: When I'm gone, look after him. Don't let his grief wear him down.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Ram has listed every hardship of forest life to talk Sita out of coming with him.
verses.sanskrit_display: ये त्वया कीर्तिता दोषा वने वस्तव्यतां प्रति। गुणानित्येव तान् विद्धि तव स्नेहपुरस्कृता॥
verses.translation: The hardships you list about living in the forest, know that I see them as blessings, because my love for you goes first.
verses.line: Every hardship you list sounds like a blessing to me, because I'd face it with you.

verses.speaker: Dasharatha
verses.setting: The heartbroken king, bound by his promise, cannot stop Ram going but begs for one more night.
verses.sanskrit_display: मातरं मां च सम्पश्यन् वसेमामद्य शर्वरीम्। तर्पितः सर्वकामैस्त्वं श्वः काल्ये साधयिष्यसि ॥
verses.translation: Stay tonight, see your mother and me. Rest, have everything you want, and set out early tomorrow.
verses.line: Stay tonight. Let your mother and me see you. You can leave in the morning.

verses.speaker: Sumitra
verses.setting: Ram has left for fourteen years; his mother cannot stop weeping, and her co-queen sits with her.
verses.sanskrit_display: निवृत्तवनवासं तं द्रष्टासि पुनरागतम्। जहि शोकं च मोहं च देवि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
verses.translation: You will see him again, back from the forest. Let go of grief and confusion, my queen. I tell you the truth.
verses.line: You will see him again. Let go of this grief.
verses.misuse: Comfort for a long separation, not a promise that every loss will be undone.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Loyal citizens have followed Ram into the wilderness; he slips away at dawn so they will go home.
verses.sanskrit_display: पौरा ह्यात्मकृताद् दुःखाद् विप्रमोच्या नृपात्मजैः। न तु खल्वात्मना योज्या दुःखेन पुरवासिनः॥
verses.translation: Leaders should free people from the troubles they bring on themselves, never pull them into troubles of their own making.
verses.line: Lead people out of their troubles; never drag them into yours.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: From exile, Ram sends his mother a message about living alongside Kaikeyi, the queen who exiled him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अभिमानं च मानं च त्यक्त्वा वर्तस्व मातृषु। अनुराजानमार्यां च कैकेयीमम्ब कारय॥
verses.translation: Set aside pride and self-importance in how you treat my other mothers. And, mother, show Kaikeyi the respect the king gives her.
verses.line: Drop your pride with the rest of the family, even the one who hurt us.
verses.misuse: Respect is not submission; Ram asks his mother not to feed a feud, not to accept mistreatment.

verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: After lashing out at Dasharatha over Ram's exile, Kausalya apologises.
verses.sanskrit_display: जानामि धर्मे धर्मज्ञ त्वां जाने सत्यवादिनम्। पुत्रशोकार्तया तत्तु मया किमपि भाषितम्॥
verses.translation: I know what is right, righteous one, and I know you are truthful. It was in my anguish over my son that I said what I said.
verses.line: I know you are honest. I said those words out of my own pain.

verses.speaker: Dasharatha
verses.setting: Near death, Dasharatha finally tells his wife of the boy he killed by mistake as a young man.
verses.sanskrit_display: तदिदं मेऽनुसम्प्राप्तं देवि दुःखं स्वयंकृतम्। सम्मोहादिह बालेन यथा स्याद् भक्षितं विषम्॥
verses.translation: This sorrow has come to me, my queen, by my own doing, like a child who swallows poison out of ignorance.
verses.line: This sorrow is of my own making, like a child who swallowed poison without knowing.
verses.misuse: Owning a mistake is not deserving endless punishment for it.

verses.speaker: The ascetic's father
verses.setting: Dasharatha confesses to the blind parents that he killed their son; the father answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्येतदशुभं कर्म न स्म मे कथयेः स्वयम्। फलेन्मूर्धा स्म राजन् सद्यः शतसहस्रधा॥
verses.translation: Had you not told us this terrible deed yourself, your head would have shattered into a hundred thousand pieces.
verses.line: Because you told us yourself, you were spared. Confession changes what comes next.
verses.misuse: Confessing is right because it is honest, not because it buys a lighter sentence.

verses.speaker: The ascetic's blind father
verses.setting: Blind old parents hear footsteps and think their son is back with water. It is his killer.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वं गतिस्त्वगतीनां च चक्षुस्त्वं हीनचक्षुषाम्। समासक्तास्त्वयि प्राणाः कथं त्वं नाभिभाषसे॥
verses.translation: You are the refuge of us who have no other; you are the eyes of us who cannot see. Our lives hang on you. Why don't you speak?
verses.line: You are our eyes, our support. Our lives hang on you. Why don't you answer?

verses.speaker: Kaikeyi
verses.setting: Before the maid Manthara works on her fears, Kaikeyi hears Ram will be crowned and is delighted.
verses.sanskrit_display: रामे वा भरते वाहं विशेषं नोपलक्षये। तस्मात्तुष्टास्मि यद्राजा रामं राज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यति॥
verses.translation: I see no difference between Ram and Bharata. So I am glad the king will crown Ram.
verses.line: 'I see no difference between his son and mine. I'm glad for him.' The heart before envy is fed.

verses.speaker: Bharata
verses.setting: Grieving Kausalya accuses Bharata of plotting Ram's exile; he knew nothing of it.
verses.sanskrit_display: आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकल्मषम्। विपुलां च मम प्रीति स्थितां जानासि राघवे॥
verses.translation: Noble lady, why do you blame me, who knew nothing and did nothing wrong? You know how deep my love for Ram is.
verses.line: Why blame me, who knew nothing? You know what I feel for him.

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: On the thirteenth day, Bharata collapses at his father's pyre; the family priest lifts him up.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि भूतेषु प्रवृत्तान्यविशेषतः। तेषु चापरिहार्येषु नैवं भवितुमर्हसि॥
verses.translation: Three pairs come to every creature without exception: hunger and thirst, grief and confusion, old age and death. Since none can be avoided, you should not give way like this.
verses.line: Hunger, grief, old age and death come to every living being. None of us is singled out.
verses.misuse: Grief is natural; this is said to help a mourner stand up, not to forbid tears.

verses.speaker: Bharata
verses.setting: The court offers Bharata the throne his mother schemed for; he refuses before everyone.
verses.sanskrit_display: कथं दशरथाज्जातो भवेद् राज्यापहारकः। राज्यं चाहं च रामस्य धर्म वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
verses.translation: How could a son of Dasharatha steal a kingdom? The kingdom and I both belong to Ram. Speak what is right here.
verses.line: How could I take what belongs to my brother? Some gains I won't accept.

verses.speaker: Guha
verses.setting: Guha sees Bharata's army approach and fears the worst, but he holds back until he knows Bharata's intent.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदि तुष्टस्तु भरतो रामस्येह भविष्यति। इयं स्वस्तिमती सेना गङ्गामद्य तरिष्यति॥
verses.translation: But if Bharata comes in good faith towards Ram, this army may cross the Ganga safely today.
verses.line: Prepare for the worst if you must, but find out their intent before you judge.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Seeing Bharata's army approach, Lakshman assumes the worst; Ram questions his suspicion.
verses.sanskrit_display: विप्रियं कृतपूर्वं ते भरतेन कदा नु किम्। ईदृशं वा भयं तेऽद्य भरतं यद् विशङ्कसे॥
verses.translation: When has Bharata ever done you wrong? What has happened that you now fear and suspect him like this?
verses.line: When has this person ever wronged you? Why suspect them now?

verses.speaker: Maricha
verses.setting: Ordered to help abduct Sita, Maricha makes a last plea to Ravana.
verses.sanskrit_display: निवार्यमाणस्तु मया हितैषिणा न मृष्यसे वाक्यमिदं निशाचर। परेतकल्पा हि गतायुषो नरा हितं न गृह्णन्ति सुहृद्भिरीरितम्॥
verses.translation: Though I try to stop you out of concern for your good, you will not accept my words. People whose time is running out do not take the good advice their friends give.
verses.line: People heading for a fall are the ones who won't take good advice from friends.

verses.speaker: Jatayu
verses.setting: The ancient Jatayu, sixty thousand years old, challenges the young armed Ravana alone.
verses.sanskrit_display: वृद्धोऽहं त्वं युवा धन्वी सरथः कवची शरी। न चाप्यादाय कुशली वैदेहीं मे गमिष्यसि ॥
verses.translation: I am old; you are young, with bow, chariot, armour and arrows. Even so, you will not take Vaidehi from me unharmed.
verses.line: I am old, and you are young and armed. I'll still stand up to you.

verses.speaker: Kabandha
verses.setting: Ram is lost and grieving; Kabandha tells him to seek Sugriva, who has also lost his wife and home.
verses.sanskrit_display: तदवश्यं त्वया कार्यः स सुहृत् सुहृदां वर। अकृत्वा नहि ते सिद्धिमहं पश्यामि चिन्तयन् ॥
verses.translation: You must make him your friend, best of friends. Thinking it over, I see no success for you without it.
verses.line: Find a friend who knows your kind of trouble. You won't get through this alone.

verses.speaker: Shabari
verses.setting: The old ascetic woman Shabari has waited years at Pampa for Ram, as her teachers foretold.
verses.sanskrit_display: एवमुक्ता महाभागैस्तदाहं पुरुषर्षभ। मया तु संचितं वन्यं विविधं पुरुषर्षभ॥ तवार्थे पुरुषव्याघ्र पम्पायास्तीरसम्भवम्।
verses.translation: So the great ones told me, best of men, and for you I have gathered every kind of forest food from the banks of the Pampa.
verses.line: I was told you would come, so I kept gathering for you. Waiting was a kind of preparing.

verses.collection: Aranya: Sita and Ram on non-violence
verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Sita tells Ram the story of a gentle hermit who turned violent from always carrying a sword.
verses.sanskrit_display: एवमेतत् पुरावृत्तं शस्त्रसंयोगकारणम्। अग्निसंयोगवद्धेतुः शस्त्रसंयोग उच्यते॥
verses.translation: This is the old story of what carrying a weapon does: keeping a weapon close is said to change a person, as contact with fire changes wood.
verses.line: Keep a weapon always at hand and it slowly changes you, as fire changes wood.

verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva tells Ram how he tried to apologise to Vali after the misunderstanding at the cave.
verses.sanskrit_display: विषादात्विह मां दृष्ट्वा पौरैर्मन्त्रिभिरेव च॥ अभिषिक्तो न कामेन तन्मे क्षन्तुं त्वमर्हसि।
verses.translation: Seeing me in despair, the citizens and ministers made me king; it was not my wish. Please forgive me for it.
verses.line: It wasn't what I wanted. Please forgive me. Sometimes a rift begins with a misunderstanding.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Sugriva panics on seeing two armed strangers; Hanuman tells him his fear is getting ahead of the facts.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहो शाखामृगत्वं ते व्यक्तमेव प्लवङ्गम। लघुचित्ततयात्मानं न स्थापयसि यो मतौ।। ।॥
verses.translation: Clearly your restless monkey nature is showing, friend: because your mind is so flighty, you cannot settle yourself on a clear thought.
verses.line: Your mind keeps jumping, so you can't settle on a clear thought.

verses.speaker: Vali
verses.setting: Dying, Vali speaks to the brother he drove into exile.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुग्रीव दोषेण न मां गन्तुमर्हसि किल्वषात्। कृष्यमाणं भविष्येण बुद्धिमोहेन मां बलात्॥
verses.translation: Sugriva, do not hold my faults against me. I was dragged by a confusion of mind I could not resist.
verses.line: Don't hold my wrongs against me. I was not thinking clearly.

verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva has won the throne through Vali's death and is overwhelmed with remorse.
verses.sanskrit_display: भ्राता कथं नाम महागुणस्य भ्रातुर्वधं राम विरोचयेत। राज्यस्य दुःखस्य च वीर सारं विचिन्तयन्कामपुरस्कृतोऽपि॥
verses.translation: How could a brother, however greedy, take pleasure in killing a brother of such great worth, once he weighs the joy of a kingdom against this grief?
verses.line: Weigh the prize against the grief of what it cost. No win is worth a brother.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Stuck waiting out the rains, Ram cannot sleep for grief over Sita; Lakshman speaks to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अलं वीर व्यथां गत्वा न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि। शोचते ह्यवसीदन्ति सर्वार्था विदितं हिते॥
verses.translation: Enough, brother. Do not sink into this pain. You know that those who keep grieving lose every purpose they had.
verses.line: Those who keep grieving lose every purpose they had. Don't let sorrow take all of you.
verses.misuse: Not a rule that grief must be cut short; a friend's nudge back towards living.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Sugriva is enjoying his new kingdom and has not begun the search; Ram chooses to give him time.
verses.sanskrit_display: स्वयमेव हि विश्रम्य ज्ञात्वा कालमुपागतम्। उपकारं च सुग्रीवो वेत्स्यते नात्र संशयः॥
verses.translation: Once he has rested, Sugriva will see for himself that the time has come and remember the help he received. I have no doubt.
verses.line: Give people time. Once rested, a good friend remembers what they owe.
verses.misuse: Patience with a friend has limits; when it runs out, Ram sends Lakshman (4.30).

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Comfortable on his new throne, Sugriva has forgotten his promise to Ram; Hanuman reminds him.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो हि कालव्यतीतेषु मित्रकार्येषु वर्तते। स कृत्वा महतोऽप्यान्न मित्रार्थेन युज्यते॥
verses.translation: Whoever acts on a friend's business after its time has passed does not truly serve that friend, even if he does something big.
verses.line: Help that comes after the moment has passed counts for little, however big it is.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Once calmed, Lakshman makes peace with Sugriva and apologises for his outburst.
verses.sanskrit_display: यच्च शोकाभिभूतस्य श्रुत्वा रामस्य भाषितम्। मया त्वं परुषाण्युक्तस्तत् क्षमस्व सखे मम॥
verses.translation: And forgive me, friend, the harsh words I said to you after hearing the grieving Ram.
verses.line: Forgive me, friend, for the harsh words I said while carrying someone else's grief.

verses.speaker: Sage Nishakara
verses.setting: The old vulture Sampati, wings burnt and grounded for ages, is told why he should live on.
verses.sanskrit_display: उत्सहेयमहं कर्तुमद्यैव त्वां सपक्षकम्। इहस्थस्त्वं हि लोकानां हितं कार्यं करिष्यसि॥
verses.translation: I could give you back your wings this very day. But by staying here as you are, you will do something for the good of the world.
verses.line: You are needed exactly where you are, as you are. Your use isn't over.

verses.speaker: Jambavan
verses.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
verses.sanskrit_display: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः परिहीनपराक्रमः। साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं भवान् सर्वगुणान्वितः॥
verses.translation: Now I am old and my strength has faded. This is your time; you have every quality it needs.
verses.line: My strength has faded with age. This is your time, and you have what it takes.

verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva, who has lost his own wife and kingdom, steadies a grieving Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: बालिशस्तु नरो नित्यं वैक्लव्यं योऽनुवर्तते। स मज्जत्यवशः शोके भाराक्रान्तेव नौ ले॥
verses.translation: But the foolish person who keeps giving in to despair sinks helplessly in grief, like an overloaded boat in water.
verses.line: Keep giving in to despair and you sink, like an overloaded boat.

verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva, who has lost his own wife and kingdom, steadies a grieving Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: हितं वयस्यभावेन ब्रूमि नोपदिशामि ते। वयस्यतां पूजयन्मे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.translation: I say this for your good, as a friend; I am not lecturing you. Honour our friendship and do not grieve.
verses.line: I tell you this as a friend, for your good, not to lecture you.

verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Newly bound in friendship, Sugriva tells Ram what a friend means to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: आढ्यो वापि दरिद्रो वा दुःखितः सुखितोऽपि वा। निर्दोषश्च सदोषश्च वयस्यः परमा गतिः॥
verses.translation: Rich or poor, happy or unhappy, faultless or flawed, a friend is one's greatest refuge.
verses.line: Rich or poor, happy or sad, flawed or not, a friend is your greatest refuge.

verses.speaker: Mainaka mountain
verses.setting: Mid-leap over the ocean, a mountain rises to offer Hanuman rest, repaying an old kindness from his father.
verses.sanskrit_display: अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये सागरस्य ममैव च। प्रीतिं प्रीतिमनाः कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि महामते॥
verses.translation: Now that this task has come, great one, it is your turn to let the ocean and me show our gratitude. Please accept it gladly.
verses.line: The time to return a kindness has come. Let me thank you.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Unable to find Sita, Hanuman considers giving up altogether, then chooses to keep going.
verses.sanskrit_display: विनाशे बहवो दोषा जीवन् प्राप्नोति भद्रकम्। तस्मात् प्राणान् धरिष्यामि ध्रुवो जीवति संगमः॥
verses.translation: Giving up brings many harms; one who lives on finds good things. So I will hold on to life; for the living, meeting again is certain.
verses.line: Giving up costs too much. Whoever keeps going finds good things again.
verses.misuse: Hanuman is rejecting despair; anyone in crisis should reach out to someone right away.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Captive in Lanka, Sita answers Ravana's offers of wealth and power.
verses.sanskrit_display: शक्या लोभयितुं नाहमैश्वर्येण धनेन वा। अनन्या राघवेणाहं भास्करेण यथा प्रभा॥
verses.translation: You cannot tempt me with power or wealth. I belong to Raghava as light belongs to the sun.
verses.line: You can't buy me with money or power. Some loyalties are not for sale.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Alone in captivity, Sita fears Ram has forgotten her, then reassures herself.
verses.sanskrit_display: दृश्यमाने भवेत् प्रीतिः सौहृदं नास्त्यदृश्यतः। नाशयन्ति कृतघ्नास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति॥
verses.translation: Love lasts while someone is in sight; out of sight, affection fades. But that is the way of the ungrateful. Ram will not let it fade.
verses.line: 'Out of sight, out of mind' is true only of the ungrateful. Real love survives distance.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman weighs fighting the guards against quietly reaching Sita first.
verses.sanskrit_display: असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते। कश्च निःसंशयं कार्यं कुर्यात् प्राज्ञः ससंशयम्॥
verses.translation: Battles are uncertain, and I don't like a gamble. What wise person would turn a sure task into an unsure one?
verses.line: Don't turn a sure thing into a gamble. Do the certain part first.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman decides how to open the conversation with frightened Sita.
verses.sanskrit_display: इक्ष्वाकूणां वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः। शुभानि धर्मयुक्तानि वचनानि समर्पयन्॥ श्रावयिष्यामि सर्वाणि मधुरां प्रब्रुवन् गिरम्। श्रद्धास्यति यथा सीता तथा सर्वं समादधे॥
verses.translation: I will recite good and true words about Ram, best of the Ikshvakus, speaking gently, and arrange it all so that Sita can trust what she hears.
verses.line: Start gently, with what they love, so they can trust what you say next.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Having found Sita, Hanuman plans what more he can achieve in Lanka before returning.
verses.sanskrit_display: नह्येकः साधको हेतुः स्वल्पस्यापीह कर्मणः। यो ह्यर्थं बहुधा वेद स समर्थोऽर्थसाधने॥
verses.translation: No single means achieves even a small task. The one who knows many ways to the goal is the one able to reach it.
verses.line: No single approach gets even a small job done. Know several ways to your goal.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: After setting Lanka ablaze in fury, Hanuman fears he has harmed Sita and turns on his own anger.
verses.sanskrit_display: ईषत्कार्यमिदं कार्यं कृतमासीन्न संशयः। तस्य क्रोधाभिभूतेन मया मूलक्षयः कृतः॥ विनष्टा जानकी व्यक्तं न ह्यदग्धः प्रदृश्यते। लङ्कायाः कश्चिदुद्देशः सर्वा भस्मीकृता पुरी॥
verses.translation: Burning Lanka was a small thing, no doubt, but overcome by anger I have destroyed the root of my mission. Surely Sita has perished, for no part of Lanka is left unburnt; the whole city is ash.
verses.line: Carried away by anger, I won a small fight and wrecked the very thing I came to do.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: After setting Lanka ablaze in fury, Hanuman fears he has harmed Sita and turns on his own anger.
verses.sanskrit_display: वाच्यावाच्यं प्रकुपितो न विजानाति कर्हिचित्। नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते क्वचित्॥
verses.translation: An angry person never knows what should and should not be said. For the angry, nothing is off limits to do or to say.
verses.line: In anger we lose the sense of what should never be said.

verses.speaker: Vibhishana
verses.setting: Vibhishana goes to Ravana privately to say what the other ministers will not.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रापणे चास्य मन्त्रस्य निवृत्ताः सर्वमन्त्रिणः। अवश्यं च मया वाच्यं यदृष्टमथवा श्रुतम्।। संविधाय यथान्यायं तद्भवान्कर्तुमर्हति॥
verses.translation: All the ministers have held back from telling you this, but I must tell you what I have seen and heard. Weigh it properly, then act.
verses.line: Everyone else held back. I must still say what I have seen and heard.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram consoles Vibhishana after Ravana falls in battle.
verses.sanskrit_display: नैकान्तविजयो युद्धे भूतपूर्वः कदाचन। परैर्वा हन्यते वीरः परान्वा हन्ति संयुगे॥
verses.translation: No one has ever known only victory in war: a fighter either falls to others or brings others down.
verses.line: No one has ever won every battle. Sometimes you win, and sometimes you fall.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Vibhishana hesitates to perform funeral rites for his brother Ravana; Ram urges him to.
verses.sanskrit_display: मरणान्तानि वैराणि निवृतं नः प्रयोजनम्। क्रियतामस्य संस्कारो ममाप्येष यथा तव ॥
verses.translation: Enmity ends with death. Our purpose is achieved. Let his last rites be performed; he is now as much mine as yours.
verses.line: Enmity ends with death. The fight is over; give him his due. He is mine as much as yours.
verses.misuse: About letting a conflict end once it is over, not excusing harm while it continues.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: After the war, Ram publicly voices suspicion of Sita; she answers his harsh words before the assembly.
verses.sanskrit_display: सह संवृद्धभावेन संसर्गेण च मानद। यदि तेऽहं न विज्ञाता हता तेनास्मि शाश्वतम्॥
verses.translation: We grew up together in love and lived together so long. If even so you have not understood me, then I am lost forever.
verses.line: After all these years together, if you still don't know me, that loss is forever.
verses.misuse: This is Sita's protest against unjust suspicion; the app does not endorse the test that follows.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Ram's advisers debate whether to trust Vibhishana; Hanuman gives his view.
verses.sanskrit_display: न वादान्नापि संघर्षानाधिक्यान च कामतः। वक्ष्यामि वचनं राजन्यथार्थं राम गौरवात्॥
verses.translation: I will speak, king, not to argue, not to compete, not to show I know more, and not from my own wishes, but plainly, as the matter deserves, out of respect for you.
verses.line: Speak not to win, compete or show off, but because the matter needs saying.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ravana's brother Vibhishana asks for refuge; Ram's advisers suspect a trap.
verses.sanskrit_display: मित्रभावेन संप्राप्तं न त्यजेयं कथंचन। दोषो यद्यपि तस्य स्यात्सतामेतदगर्हितम्॥
verses.translation: I will never turn away someone who has come in friendship, even if he has faults. Good people see nothing wrong in this.
verses.line: I won't turn away someone who comes in friendship, even if they have faults.
verses.misuse: Openness to people, not ignoring clear warning signs.

verses.speaker: Nala
verses.setting: The army is stuck at the ocean; Nala reveals he can build a bridge, which he had not mentioned.
verses.sanskrit_display: समर्थश्चाप्यहं सेतुं कर्तुं वै वरुणालये। तस्मादद्यैव बध्नन्तु सेतुं वानरपुङ्गवाः॥
verses.translation: I too am able to build a bridge across the ocean. So let the best of the monkeys start building it this very day.
verses.line: I can build this. Let's start today.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: A kind guard, Sarama, offers to spy for Sita; Sita asks only to know what is decided about her.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितं वापि यद्भवेत्। निवेदयेथाः सर्वं तद्वरो मे स्यादनुग्रहः॥
verses.translation: If there is any talk about him, or anything decided at all, tell me everything. That would be the greatest kindness to me.
verses.line: Whatever has been decided, just tell me. Not knowing is the hardest part.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram has disarmed Ravana and broken his crown, but will not kill an exhausted opponent.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रयाहि जानामि रणार्दितस्त्वं प्रविश्य रात्रिंचरराज लङ्काम्। आश्वस्य निर्याहि रथी सधन्वी तदा बलं प्रेक्ष्यसि मे रथस्थः॥
verses.translation: Go. I know you are worn out from fighting. Go back into Lanka, king of the night-walkers. Rest, then come out again with chariot and bow, and you will see my strength.
verses.line: Go and rest. I know you're exhausted. Come back when you're ready.

verses.speaker: Kumbhakarna
verses.setting: Woken to fight a war that is already being lost, Kumbhakarna tells his brother where he went wrong.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रथमं वै महाराज कृत्यमेतदचिन्तितम्। केवलं वीर्यदर्पण नानुबन्धो विचारितः॥
verses.translation: From the start, great king, you never thought this through. Proud of your strength alone, you never weighed where it would lead.
verses.line: Proud of your strength, you never stopped to ask where it would lead.

verses.collection: Uttara: Sita left in the forest
verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Abandoned because of gossip, Sita sends a message back to Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं तु नानुशोचामि स्वशरीरं नरर्षभ॥ यथापवादः पौराणां तथैव रघुनन्दन।
verses.translation: I do not grieve for myself, best of men, so much as for the slander the people are spreading.
verses.line: It isn't the hardship I mind most. It's what people are saying that wasn't true.
verses.misuse: Sita is the one wronged here; the verse names unjust gossip, not her fault.

verses.collection: Uttara: Sita left in the forest
verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Lakshman has carried out Ram's order to leave pregnant Sita at the forest's edge because of public gossip.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा कथं ह्याश्रमे सौम्य वत्स्यामि विजनीकृता। आख्यास्यामि च कस्याहं दुःखं दुःखपरायणा ।।६
verses.translation: How will I live in a hermitage, cut off from everyone I love? To whom will I tell my sorrow, now that sorrow is all I have?
verses.line: Cut off from everyone I love, who will I tell my sorrow to?
verses.misuse: Read as the grief of someone wronged; the app does not endorse the abandonment.

verses.speaker: Valmiki
verses.setting: Valmiki finds Sita weeping alone by the river and brings her to his hermitage.
verses.sanskrit_display: इदमऱ्या प्रतीच्छ त्वं विस्रब्धा विगतज्वरा। यथा स्वगृहमभ्येत्य विषादं चैव मा कृथाः॥ श्रुत्वा तु भाषितं सीता मुनेः परममद्भुतम्। शिरसा वन्द्य चरणौ तथेत्याह कृताञ्जलिः॥
verses.translation: Accept this welcome, trust me and let your fever of worry pass. Think of this as coming to your own home, and do not despair.
verses.line: Trust me and rest. Think of this as your own home.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Grieving, Ram has not held court for four days; he calls in everyone who has been waiting.
verses.sanskrit_display: चत्वारो दिवसाः सौम्य कार्य पौरजनस्य च । अकुर्वाणस्य सौमित्रे तन्मे मर्माणि कृन्तति॥
verses.translation: Four days now I have not attended to the people's business, gentle Lakshman, and it cuts me to the core.
verses.line: Four days of putting off what people needed from me, and it cuts me to the core.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram plans a grand imperial sacrifice; Bharata warns it would bring war on many, and Ram agrees.
verses.sanskrit_display: लोकपीडाकरं कर्म न कर्तव्यं विचक्षणैः। बालानां तु शुभं वाक्यं ग्राह्यं लक्ष्मणपूर्वज। तस्माच्छृणोमि ते वाक्यं साधु युक्तं महाबल।।२०
verses.translation: The wise should not do anything that brings suffering to people. Good advice should be taken even from the young, elder brother of Lakshman; so I accept what you have said as right and fitting.
verses.line: Take good advice even from the young, and do nothing that makes people suffer.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram asks Bharata a series of questions on how he is leading.
verses.sanskrit_display: यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यश्रूणि राघव। तानि पुत्रपशून् घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासतः॥
verses.translation: The tears that fall from the falsely accused destroy the children and herds of a ruler who governs for his own comfort.
verses.line: The tears of the falsely accused bring ruin on the leader who ignored them.

verses.speaker: Manthara
