verses.setting: The maid Manthara sets out to turn Kaikeyi's joy at Ram's coronation into fear and envy.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुभगा किल कौसल्या यस्याः पुत्रोऽभिषेक्ष्यते। यौवराज्येन महता श्वः पुष्येण द्विजोत्तमैः॥
verses.translation: Lucky Kausalya, they say: tomorrow, under the Pushya star, the best of the twice-born will crown her son heir to the great kingdom.
verses.line: 'Lucky her.' Envy often begins as someone counting another person's blessings for you.
verses.misuse: This is the voice of envy, quoted as a warning, not as advice.

verses.collection: Uttara: Sita returns to the earth
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Years later, before the assembly, Ram admits why he abandoned Sita and asks forgiveness.
verses.sanskrit_display: लोकापवादो बलवान्येन त्यक्ता हि मैथिली। सेयं लोकभयाद्ब्रह्मनपापेत्यभिजानता। परित्यक्ता मया सीता तद्भवान्क्षन्तुमर्हति ॥
verses.translation: Public slander is powerful; because of it Maithili was abandoned. I knew she was blameless, yet in fear of the people I left her. Please forgive me.
verses.line: I knew she was innocent, and I gave in to what people said. Please forgive me.
verses.misuse: An admission of a wrong done under social pressure, not a justification of it.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Narada's pride and the monkey face
verses.speaker: Vishnu
verses.setting: Vishnu, asked by the love-struck sage Narada for a handsome face, explains why he won't grant it.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुपथ माग रुज ब्याकुल रोगी। बैद न देइ सुनहु मुनि जोगी॥ एहि बिधि हित तुम्हार मैं ठयऊ। कहि अस अंतरहित प्रभु भयऊ ॥
verses.translation: Listen, sage: when a sick man in distress begs for food that will harm him, the doctor does not give it. In the same way I have resolved to do what is truly good for you.
verses.line: A good doctor won't give the patient what he begs for if it will harm him.
verses.misuse: Not every refusal is for your good; this is a way to reframe, not a reason to accept harm.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Janaka's despair and the bow
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Ram, standing before Shiva's bow, sees Sita's anguish and knows the moment won't wait.
verses.sanskrit_display: देखी बिपुल बिकल बैदेही। निमिष बिहात कलप सम तेही। तृषित बारि बिनु जो तनु त्यागा। मुएँ करइ का सुधा तड़ागा ॥ का बरषा सब कृषी सुखानें। समय चुकें पुनि का पछितानें॥ अस जियँ जानि जानकी देखी। प्रभु पुलके लखि प्रीति बिसेषी ॥
verses.translation: He saw Vaidehi in deep distress, each moment passing like an age. If a thirsty man dies for want of water, what use is a lake of nectar after he is gone? What use is rain when the crops have dried? What use is regret once the moment has passed? Knowing this, he looked at Janaki, and seeing her deep love, he thrilled.
verses.line: What use is rain after the crops have dried? Act while the moment is still here.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: As Lakshman's retorts inflame the furious sage Parashurama, Ram steps in.
verses.sanskrit_display: लखन उतर आहुति सरिस भृगुबर कोपु कृसानु। बढ़त देखि जल सम बचन बोले रघुकुलभानु ॥
verses.translation: Seeing Parashurama's fire of anger rise with each of Lakshman's replies, which fell on it like offerings of ghee, Ram, sun of the Raghu line, spoke words like water.
verses.line: Sharp replies feed an angry fire like ghee. Answer with words like water.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Lakshman, half-teasing, to the raging sage Parashurama.
verses.sanskrit_display: लखन कहेउ हँसि सुनहु मुनि क्रोधु पाप कर मूल। जेहि बस जन अनुचित करहिं चरहिं बिस्व प्रतिकूल ॥
verses.translation: Lakshman laughed and said, 'Listen, sage: anger is the root of wrongdoing. In its grip people do what they shouldn't and set themselves against the whole world.'
verses.line: Anger is the root of wrongdoing; in its grip we do what we shouldn't.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Lakshman to Parashurama, who is enraged that Shiva's bow has been broken.
verses.sanskrit_display: मैं तुम्हार अनुचर मुनिराया। परिहरि कोपु करिअ अब दाया॥ टूट चाप नहिं जुरिहि रिसाने। बैठिअ होइहिं पाय पिराने ॥
verses.translation: Great sage, I am your servant; give up your anger and be kind. A broken bow won't mend because you are angry. You must be tired of standing; do sit down.
verses.line: A broken bow won't mend because you are angry. Sit down.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, opening the Manas, on why the company we keep matters.
verses.sanskrit_display: बिनु सतसंग बिबेक न होई। राम कृपा बिनु सुलभ न सोई॥ सतसंगत मुद मंगल मूला। सोई फल सिधि सब साधन फूला ॥
verses.translation: Without good company there is no clear judgement, and by Ram's grace alone such company comes easily. Good company is the root of joy and well-being; finding it is the fruit, and every other practice is only the flower.
verses.line: Without good company, there is no clear judgement.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Janaka says goodbye to his daughter
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: King Janaka, famous for his detachment, as his daughter Sita leaves home after her wedding.
verses.sanskrit_display: सीय बिलोकि धीरता भागी। रहे कहावत परम बिरागी॥ लीन्हि रायँ उर लाइ जानकी। मिटी महामरजाद ग्यान की ॥
verses.translation: He was known as supremely detached, yet on seeing Sita his composure fled. The king held Janaki to his heart, and the great banks of his wisdom gave way.
verses.line: Known for his calm, he held his daughter close as she left, and all his wisdom gave way.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Sati doubts, tests and hides it
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, after Sati hides the truth from her husband Shiva, on what deceit does to love.
verses.sanskrit_display: जलु पय सरिस बिकाइ देखहु प्रीति कि रीति भलि। बिलग होइ रसु जाइ कपट खटाई परत पुनि ॥
verses.translation: See love's lovely way: water mixed with milk sells at the price of milk. But let the sourness of deceit fall in, and the water separates and the sweetness is gone.
verses.line: Love turns water into milk. One drop of deceit, and it curdles.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Sati and Daksha
verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva, when Sati wants to attend her father's ceremony uninvited, where Shiva is resented.
verses.sanskrit_display: जदपि मित्र प्रभु पितु गुर गेहा। जाइअ बिनु बोलेहुँ न सँदेहा॥ तदपि बिरोध मान जहँ कोई। तहाँ गएँ कल्यानु न होई ॥
verses.translation: It is true that one may go uninvited to the home of a friend, a master, a father or a teacher. Yet where someone holds hostility toward you, no good comes of going there.
verses.line: You may visit family without an invitation. But where there is hostility toward you, going brings no good.
verses.misuse: Not a rule to cut off family; a caution about walking into known hostility.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, opening the Manas, on seeing good and bad in the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: जड़ चेतन गुन दोषमय बिस्व कीन्ह करतार। संत हंस गुन गहहिं पय परिहरि बारि बिकार ॥
verses.translation: The Creator made this world, living and lifeless, a mix of virtues and faults. But the wise, like the swan, take the milk of virtue and leave behind the water of faults.
verses.line: The world is a mix of good and bad. Like the swan, take the milk and leave the water.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
verses.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
verses.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
verses.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Tulsidas on loving our own work
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, introducing his work, on how rarely people rejoice at someone else's rise.
verses.sanskrit_display: जग बहु नर सर सरि सम भाई। जे निज बाढ़ि बढ़हि जल पाई॥ सज्जन सकृत सिंधु सम कोई। देखि पूर बिधु बाढ़इ जोई ॥
verses.translation: Brother, most people in the world are like ponds and rivers: they swell only when their own waters rise. Rare is the good soul who, like the ocean, surges with joy on seeing another's moon grow full.
verses.line: Most of us swell only at our own rise. Rare is the one who surges at another's.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Ram's unease on the eve of his crowning
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, told he alone will be crowned heir, feels uneasy about his brothers.
verses.sanskrit_display: जनमे एक संग सब भाई। भोजन सयन केलि लरिकाई॥ करनबेध उपबीत बिआहा। संग संग सब भए उछाहा ॥ बिमल बंस यहु अनुचित एकू। बंधु बिहाइ बड़ेहि अभिषेकू॥ प्रभु सप्रेम पछितानि सुहाई। हरउ भगत मन कै कुटिलाई ॥
verses.translation: We brothers were born together; we ate, slept and played together as children; ear-piercing, sacred thread and weddings were all celebrated side by side. In this spotless family only this one thing is wrong: that the eldest alone is crowned, leaving his brothers aside. (Tulsidas:) May the Lord's loving regret take the crookedness out of his devotees' hearts.
verses.line: We grew up together, every milestone shared. Why should one brother alone be crowned?

verses.speaker: Sumantra
verses.setting: Sumantra returns alone to the grieving king Dasharath and steadies him.
verses.sanskrit_display: जनम मरन सब दुख सुख भोगा। हानि लाभु प्रिय मिलन बियोगा॥ काल करम बस होहिं गोसाईं। बरबस राति दिवस की नाईं ॥ सुख हरषहिं जड़ दुख बिलखाहीं। दोउ सम धीर धरहिं मन माहीं॥ धीरज धरहु बिबेकु बिचारी। छाड़िअ सोच सकल हितकारी ॥
verses.translation: Birth and death, joy and sorrow, loss and gain, meeting and parting with those we love: these come under the sway of time and action, as surely as night and day. The foolish rejoice in good times and wail in bad; the steady hold both alike in the mind. Hold on to your courage, think with discernment, and let go of worry, you who care for everyone.
verses.line: Gain and loss, meeting and parting come like day and night. The steady hold both alike.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Bharat comes home to grief
verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: Kausalya comforts Bharat, who has come home to find his father dead and his brother exiled.
verses.sanskrit_display: अजहुँ बच्छ बलि धीरज धरहू। कुसमउ समुझि सोक परिहरहू॥ जनि मानहु हियँ हानि गलानी। काल करम गति अघटित जानी ॥
verses.translation: My child, bless you, hold on to courage even now. Seeing that the times are bad, set aside your grief. Knowing that the course of time and karma cannot be turned, don't take this loss as your shame.
verses.line: Hold on, child. The times turned against us. Don't carry this loss as your shame.
verses.misuse: Easing shame is not denying responsibility where it is real.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Vasishtha's counsel to Bharat
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: The sage Vasishtha to Bharat, shattered by his father's death and Ram's exile.
verses.sanskrit_display: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
verses.translation: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
verses.line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Bharat refuses the throne
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat, urged by his teacher and mother to accept the throne, explains why he cannot.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम्ह तौ देहु सरल सिख सोई। जो आचरत मोर भल होई॥ जद्यपि यह समुझत हउँ नीकें। तदपि होत परितोष न जी कें ॥
verses.translation: You give me simple advice, the kind that would do me good if I followed it. Though I understand it well, my heart is not at peace.
verses.line: I understand your advice perfectly. My heart still isn't at peace.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Bharat refuses the throne
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat resolves to go to the forest and face the brother he believes he has wronged.
verses.sanskrit_display: जद्यपि मैं अनभल अपराधी। भै मोहि कारन सकल उपाधी॥ तदपि सरन सनमुख मोहि देखी। छमि सब करिहहिं कृपा बिसेषी ॥
verses.translation: Though I am at fault and guilty, and all this trouble came about because of me, still, seeing me come before him for refuge, Ram will forgive everything and show me special kindness.
verses.line: I am at fault. Still I will go to him face to face, trusting his heart to forgive.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Guha nearly fights Bharat
verses.speaker: Guha
verses.setting: Guha, ready to block Bharat's army at the river, listens to an elder who urges caution.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनि गुह कहइ नीक कह बूढ़ा। सहसा करि पछिताहिं बिमूढ़ा॥ भरत सुभाउ सीलु बिनु बूझें। बड़ि हित हानि जानि बिनु जूझें ॥
verses.translation: Guha said, 'The old man speaks well. Fools act in haste and repent. To fight without knowing Bharat's character and nature would do great harm to our own good.'
verses.line: Fools act in haste and repent. Know someone's nature before you fight them.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Bharadwaj lifts Bharat's shame
verses.speaker: Bharadwaj
verses.setting: The sage Bharadwaj to Bharat, who is consumed by shame over what his mother did.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम्ह गलानि जियँ जनि करहु समुझि मातु करतूति। तात कैकइहि दोसु नहिं गई गिरा मति धूति ॥
verses.translation: Don't eat yourself up with shame remembering your mother's deed. Child, Kaikeyi is not at fault either; the goddess of speech clouded her mind.
verses.line: Don't eat yourself up with shame for what someone else in your family did.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Chitrakoot: Lakshman's anger
verses.speaker: A voice from the sky
verses.setting: Lakshman, convinced Bharat is coming to attack, grabs his bow; a heavenly voice stops him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनुचित उचित काजु किछु होऊ। समुझि करिअ भल कह सबु कोऊ। सहसा करि पाछे पछिताहीं। कहहिं बेद बुध ते बुध नाहीं ॥
verses.translation: Whatever needs doing, right or wrong, think it through first, then act; everyone calls that good. Those who act in haste and regret afterward, the wise say, are not wise at all.
verses.line: Think before you act. Acting in haste and regretting later is not wisdom.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Manthara poisons Kaikeyi's mind
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, finishes turning the queen against Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनत बात मृदु अंत कठोरी। देति मनहुँ मधु माहुर घोरी॥ कहइ चेरि सुधि अहइ कि नाहीं। स्वामिनि कहिहु कथा मोहि पाहीं ॥
verses.translation: Her words were soft to hear but harsh in their outcome, as if she were giving poison dissolved in honey. The maid said, 'Mistress, do you remember the story you once told me?'
verses.line: Some advice is soft to hear and harsh in its end: poison dissolved in honey.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, The brothers meet at Chitrakoot
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot Ram greets the three queens, and goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused his exile.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रथम राम भेंटी कैकेई। सरल सुभायँ भगति मति भेई॥ पग परि कीन्ह प्रबोधु बहोरी। काल करम बिधि सिर धरि खोरी ॥ भेटीं रघुबर मातु सब करि प्रबोधु परितोषु। अंब ईस आधीन जगु काहु न देइअ दोषु ॥
verses.translation: Ram met Kaikeyi first of all, and with his simple nature and devotion soothed her mind. Falling at her feet, he laid the blame on time, karma and fate, and comforted her. Then he met all the mothers and comforted each: 'Mother, the world is in God's hands; we should blame no one.'
verses.line: He went first to the one who had wronged him, and comforted her.
verses.misuse: Forgiving is not pretending the harm didn't happen.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, The family council at Chitrakoot
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha, at the Chitrakoot assembly, asks Ram to decide because those grieving cannot.
verses.sanskrit_display: आरत कहहिं बिचारि न काऊ। सूझ जुआरिहि आपन दाऊ॥ सुनि मुनि बचन कहत रघुराऊ॥ नाथ तुम्हारेहि हाथ उपाऊ ॥
verses.translation: People in distress never speak after weighing things; a gambler sees only his own throw. Hearing the sage, Raghunath said, 'Master, the way forward is in your hands.'
verses.line: People in distress never speak with judgement; the gambler sees only his own throw.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to dismiss people who are hurting; a reason to wait before deciding.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, The family council at Chitrakoot
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat, before the assembly at Chitrakoot, speaks of his elder brother.
verses.sanskrit_display: सिसुपन तें परिहरेउँ न संगू। कबहुँ न कीन्ह मोर मन भंगू॥ मैं प्रभु कृपा रीति जियँ जोही। हारेहूँ खेल जितावहिं मोही ॥
verses.translation: Since childhood I never left his side, and he never once broke my heart. I have seen the way of his kindness: even when I lost at games, he made me win.
verses.line: Since childhood he never broke my heart. Even when I lost at games, he let me win.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, The family council at Chitrakoot
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Bharat, who blames himself for the exile and their father's death.
verses.sanskrit_display: तात जायँ जियँ करहु गलानी। ईस अधीन जीव गति जानी॥ तीनि काल तिभुअन मत मोरें। पुन्यसिलोक तात तर तोरें ॥
verses.translation: Brother, you torment your heart with shame for nothing; know that a soul's course is in God's hands. In my view, all the virtuous of past, present and future, in all three worlds, stand below you.
verses.line: You torment yourself with shame for nothing. In my eyes you stand above them all.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Chitrakoot: Bharat's humility
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat, once Ram and their teacher have reassured him, admits what his dread was made of.
verses.sanskrit_display: अपडर डरेउँ न सोच समूलें। रबिहि न दोसु देव दिसि भूलें॥ मोर अभागु मातु कुटिलाई। बिधि गति बिषम काल कठिनाई ॥
verses.translation: "I was afraid of imagined fears; my worry had no root at all. If one loses one's direction, the sun is not to blame. It was my misfortune, my mother's crookedness, the hard turn of fate and the difficulty of the times..."
verses.line: I was frightened by fears I had imagined. My worry had no root at all.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Janaka's family joins the council
verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: Kausalya, to Sita's mother at Chitrakoot, on Bharat's character.
verses.sanskrit_display: जानउँ सदा भरत कुलदीपा। बार बार मोहि कहेउ महीपा॥ कसें कनकु मनि पारिखि पाएँ। पुरुष परिखिअहिं समयँ सुभाएँ ॥
verses.translation: I have always known Bharat to be the lamp of our family; the king told me so again and again. Gold is known on the touchstone and a gem when a jeweller comes; a person is tested by time and shows his nature.
verses.line: Gold is proved on the touchstone. People are proved by time.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Ram and Bharat settle it
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram asks Bharat to rule in his place for fourteen years.
verses.sanskrit_display: जानि तुम्हहि मृदु कहउँ कठोरा। कुसमयँ तात न अनुचित मोरा॥ होहिं कुठायँ सुबंधु सहाए। ओड़िअहिं हाथ असनिहु के धाए ॥
verses.translation: Knowing you are gentle, I still say something hard; in hard times, brother, it isn't wrong of me. In bad times it is good brothers who help; it is the hands that rise to block a thunderbolt.
verses.line: In bad times, good siblings are the hands that rise to block the blow.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Chitrakoot: Ram to Bharat
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, sending Bharat back to govern Ayodhya in his place, on what a leader should be.
verses.sanskrit_display: मुखिआ मुखु सो चाहिऐ खान पान कहुँ एक। पालइ पोषइ सकल अँग तुलसी सहित बिबेक ॥
verses.translation: A leader should be like the mouth: it alone eats and drinks, yet with good sense it nourishes and sustains every limb of the body.
verses.line: A leader is like the mouth: it takes in, but only to nourish the whole body.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Ram hears he is to be exiled
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, told by Kaikeyi that Bharat will be crowned and he exiled, answers her calmly.
verses.sanskrit_display: भरतु प्रानप्रिय पावहिं राजू। बिधि सब बिधि मोहि सनमुख आजू॥ जौं न जाउँ बन ऐसेहु काजा। प्रथम गनिअ मोहि मूढ़ समाजा ॥
verses.translation: ...and Bharat, dear to me as life, will have the kingdom. Fate is favouring me in every way today. If I would not go to the forest even for such a cause, count me first among fools.
verses.line: My beloved brother gets the throne. Fate is favouring me in every way today.
verses.misuse: Grace in loss is not pretending it doesn't hurt.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Ram hears he is to be exiled
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Kaikeyi hears Ram's plain, gracious words and reads them as cunning.
verses.sanskrit_display: सहज सकल रघुबर बचन कुमति कुटिल करि जान। चलइ जोंक जल बक्रगति जद्यपि सलिलु समान ॥
verses.translation: Raghuvar's words were simple by nature, but the ill-minded queen took them as crooked, as a leech moves crookedly even through still, even water.
verses.line: A twisted mind reads straight words as crooked, as a leech wriggles through still water.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Ram hears he is to be exiled
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Ram, walking to his mother's palace after being exiled, feels lighter, not crushed.
verses.sanskrit_display: नव गयंदु रघुबीर मनु राजु अलान समान। छूट जानि बन गवनु सुनि उर अनंदु अधिकान ॥
verses.translation: Raghuvir's mind was like a newly captured elephant, and the crown like the post it is tethered to. Hearing he must go to the forest, he felt himself set free, and joy rose in his heart.
verses.line: The crown had been a tether. Losing it, he felt like an elephant set free.
verses.misuse: Losing a role can free you; that does not make every loss a gift.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Kausalya lets her son go
verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: Kausalya, choosing not to hold her son back, sends him into exile with her blessing.
verses.sanskrit_display: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥
verses.translation: Thinking this over, I will not insist out of false affection. I bless you, son; only keep the bond of a mother, and don't forget me.
verses.line: I won't hold you back with false affection. Go, son. Just don't forget your mother.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Kausalya lets her son go
verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: Kausalya, as Ram, Sita and Lakshman take leave, wonders if she will live to see them again.
verses.sanskrit_display: फिरिहि दसा बिधि बहुरि कि मोरी। देखिहउँ नयन मनोहर जोरी। सुदिन सुघरी तात कब होइहि। जननी जिअत बदन बिधु जोइहि ॥
verses.translation: O Fate, will my fortune ever turn again? Will I see this lovely pair with my own eyes once more? Son, when will that good day, that blessed hour come, when your mother, still alive, sees your moon-like face again?
verses.line: When will that day come, when your mother, still living, sees your face again?

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
verses.speaker: Sumitra
verses.setting: Sumitra tells her son Lakshman to follow Ram into exile.
verses.sanskrit_display: अवध तहाँ जहँ राम निवासू। तहँइँ दिवसु जहँ भानु प्रकासू॥ जौं पै सीय रामु बन जाहीं। अवध तुम्हार काजु कछु नाहीं ॥
verses.translation: Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives; day is wherever the sun shines. If Sita and Ram really go to the forest, you have nothing to do in Ayodhya.
verses.line: Home is wherever your people are, as day is wherever the sun shines.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Lakshman, keeping watch at night, to Guha who blames Kaikeyi for Ram sleeping on the ground.
verses.sanskrit_display: बोले लखन मधुर मृदु बानी। ग्यान बिराग भगति रस सानी॥ काहु न कोउ सुख दुख कर दाता। निज कृत करम भोग सबु भ्राता ॥
verses.translation: Then Lakshman spoke in a sweet, gentle voice, steeped in knowledge, detachment and devotion: "No one is the giver of another's joy or sorrow, brother. Everyone lives out the fruit of their own actions."
verses.line: No one else is the giver of your joy or sorrow. You live out the fruit of your own actions.
verses.misuse: Not "you deserve your suffering"; it is about not handing your peace to others.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Lakshman, continuing his night talk with Guha, after comparing the world to a dream.
verses.sanskrit_display: अस बिचारि नहिं कीजिअ रोसू। काहुहि बादि न देइअ दोसू॥ मोह निसाँ सबु सोवनिहारा। देखिअ सपन अनेक प्रकारा ॥
verses.translation: Thinking this through, do not give way to anger, and do not blame anyone without reason. Everyone is asleep in the night of delusion, and in sleep they see dreams of many kinds.
verses.line: Think it through: don't give way to anger, and don't blame anyone needlessly.
verses.misuse: Not blaming is not the same as excusing harm.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Kevat washes Ram's feet
verses.speaker: Kevat
verses.setting: The boatman Kevat, having ferried Ram across the Ganga, refuses the ring offered as fare.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथ आजु मैं काह न पावा। मिटे दोष दुख दारिद दावा॥ बहुत काल मैं कीन्हि मजूरी। आजु दीन्ह बिधि बनि भलि भूरी ॥
verses.translation: Lord, what have I not received today? The fire of my faults, sorrows and poverty is put out. I have worked for wages a long time; today Providence has paid me fully and well.
verses.line: I've worked for wages all my life. Today I was paid in full.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Shabari, the forest woman of no rank, on the forms of devotion (seventh and eighth).
verses.sanskrit_display: सातवँ सम मोहि मय जग देखा। मोतें संत अधिक करि लेखा॥ आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा। सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥
verses.translation: The seventh is to see the whole world as filled with me, and to regard good people as greater than me. The eighth is to be content with whatever comes, and never, even in a dream, to look for faults in others.
verses.line: Be content with what comes, and don't go looking for faults in others, not even in your dreams.

verses.collection: Manas: Aranya Kand, Ram and Narada
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, asked by the sage Narada what marks a good person.
verses.sanskrit_display: निज गुन श्रवन सुनत सकुचाहीं। पर गुन सुनत अधिक हरषाहीं॥ सम सीतल नहिं त्यागहिं नीती। सरल सुभाउ सबहि सन प्रीति ॥
verses.translation: They shrink when they hear their own praises and are delighted to hear the praises of others. They are even-tempered and calm, never abandon what is right, are simple by nature and kind to all.
verses.line: Good people squirm at their own praise and light up when others are praised.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Ram consoles Tara
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram consoles Tara, weeping over her husband Bali's body.
verses.sanskrit_display: तारा बिकल देखि रघुराया। दीन्ह ग्यान हरि लीन्ही माया॥ छिति जल पावक गगन समीरा। पंच रचित अति अधम सरीरा ॥ प्रगट सो तनु तव आगे सोवा। जीव नित्य केहि लगि तुम्ह रोवा॥ उपजा ग्यान चरन तब लागी। लीन्हेसि परम भगति बर मागी ॥
verses.translation: Seeing Tara distraught, Raghunath gave her wisdom and took away her delusion: 'This body is made of five elements, earth, water, fire, sky and air, and it is a lowly thing. That body lies here before you, asleep; the self is eternal. For whom are you weeping?' When understanding dawned, she bowed at his feet and asked for the gift of devotion.
verses.line: The body of five elements lies before you; the self lives on. For whom do you weep?
verses.misuse: This is comfort for later, not a reason to stop someone from grieving.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, rainy season similes
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Lakshman, watching the monsoon from Mount Pravarshana.
verses.sanskrit_display: बरषहिं जलद भूमि निअराएँ। जथा नवहिं बुध बिद्या पाएँ। बूँद अघात सहहिं गिरि कैसे। खल के बचन संत सह जैसें ॥
verses.translation: The clouds hang low as they rain, the way the wise bow when they gain learning. The mountains bear the beating of the raindrops the way the good bear the harsh words of the wicked.
verses.line: Mountains take the pounding rain the way steady people take harsh words.
verses.misuse: Bearing words calmly is not the same as accepting mistreatment.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, describing the monsoon to Lakshman, draws a lesson from ponds filling up.
verses.sanskrit_display: समिटि समिटि जल भरहिं तलावा। जिमि सदगुन सज्जन पहिं आवा॥ सरिता जल जलनिधि महुँ जोई। होइ अचल जिमि जिव हरि पाई ॥
verses.translation: Water gathers bit by bit and fills the ponds, as good qualities come one by one to a good person. River water, reaching the ocean, becomes still, as a soul becomes steady on finding Hari.
verses.line: Ponds fill drop by drop. Good qualities gather in a person the same way.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Sugriva forgets his promise
verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva, having forgotten his promise to Ram amid royal comforts, apologises to an angry Lakshman.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथ विषय सम मद कछु नाहीं। मुनि मन मोह करइ छन माहीं। सुनत बिनीत बचन सुख पावा। लछिमन तेहि बहु बिधि समुझावा ॥
verses.translation: Lord, there is no intoxicant like the pleasures of the senses; they cloud even a sage's mind in an instant. Hearing his humble words, Lakshman was pleased and reassured him in many ways.
verses.line: No drink intoxicates like comfort. It can cloud even a wise mind in a moment.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Sampati's burned wings
verses.speaker: Sampati
verses.setting: Sampati, his wings regrown, urges the monkeys who had given up the search.
verses.sanskrit_display: जो नाघइ सत जोजन सागर। करइ सो राम काज मति आगर॥ मोहि बिलोकि धरहु मन धीरा। राम कृपाँ कस भयउ सरीरा ॥
verses.translation: Whoever can leap the hundred-league ocean, wise and capable, will do Ram's work. Look at me and take heart: see what Ram's grace has done to my body.
verses.line: Look at me and take heart. My burned wings have grown back.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Jambavant and Hanuman
verses.speaker: Jambavant
verses.setting: The old bear Jambavant to Hanuman, who sits silent while others say the ocean is too wide.
verses.sanskrit_display: कवन सो काज कठिन जग माहीं। जो नहिं होइ तात तुम्ह पाहीं॥ राम काज लगि तव अवतारा। सुनतहिं भयउ पर्बताकारा ॥
verses.translation: "What task in the world is too hard for you, my son? You were born for Ram's work." Hearing this, Hanuman grew to the size of a mountain.
verses.line: What task in the world is too hard for you? You were made for this.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Sugriva, as they swear friendship by the fire.
verses.sanskrit_display: जे न मित्र दुख होहिं दुखारी। तिन्हहि बिलोकत पातक भारी॥ निज दुख गिरि सम रज करि जाना। मित्रक दुख रज मेरु समाना ॥
verses.translation: Those who are not pained by a friend's pain commit a grave wrong just by being seen. A true friend treats his own mountain of sorrow as a speck of dust, and his friend's speck of sorrow as a mountain.
verses.line: A real friend treats his own troubles as dust and his friend's troubles as a mountain.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman reaches Sita
verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Sita, captive in Lanka, is reached by Hanuman with Ram's ring.
verses.sanskrit_display: हरिजन जानि प्रीति अति गाढ़ी। सजल नयन पुलकावलि बाढ़ी॥ बूड़त बिरह जलधि हनुमाना। भयहु तात मो कहुँ जलजाना ॥
verses.translation: Knowing him to be the Lord's own, her love deepened; her eyes filled and she thrilled. 'Hanuman, I was drowning in a sea of separation, and you became my ship.'
verses.line: I was drowning in a sea of separation, and you became my ship.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman reaches Sita
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram's message to Sita, carried across the sea by Hanuman.
verses.sanskrit_display: कहेहू तें कछु दुख घटि होई। काहि कहौं यह जान न कोई॥ तत्व प्रेम कर मम अरु तोरा। जानत प्रिया एकु मनु मोरा ॥
verses.translation: Telling one's grief lightens it a little. But whom can I tell? No one knows this pain. The truth of the love between you and me, my beloved, only my own heart knows.
verses.line: Speaking of pain lightens it. But whom can I tell? No one knows this ache.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman meets Surasa on the way
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Hanuman, leaping the ocean, is blocked by Surasa, who opens her jaws to swallow him.
verses.sanskrit_display: जस जस सुरसा बदनु बढ़ावा। तासु दून कपि रूप देखावा॥ सत जोजन तेहिं आनन कीन्हा। अति लघु रूप पवनसुत लीन्हा ॥
verses.translation: As Surasa widened her mouth, Hanuman showed a form twice as large. She made her mouth a hundred leagues wide; then Hanuman took a very tiny form.
verses.line: As the obstacle grew, he grew twice as big. Then he made himself tiny and slipped through.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Lankini at the gate of Lanka
verses.speaker: Lankini
verses.setting: Lankini, guardian of Lanka, struck down by Hanuman, recognises him and blesses him.
verses.sanskrit_display: तात स्वर्ग अपबर्ग सुख धरिअ तुला एक अंग। तूल न ताहि सकल मिलि जो सुख लव सतसंग ॥
verses.translation: Friend, put all the joys of heaven and liberation on one side of the scale: together they cannot match the joy of a single moment of good company.
verses.line: All of heaven on one side of the scale can't outweigh one moment in good company.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman, back from Lanka, when Ram asks how he crossed the ocean and burned the city.
verses.sanskrit_display: सो सब तव प्रताप रघुराई। नाथ न कछू मोरि प्रभुताई ॥
verses.translation: "All of it was your glory, Lord. None of it was my own greatness."
verses.line: All of it was your strength, not my greatness.
verses.misuse: Humility about success, not denying your own effort.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Ravana's ministers flatter him as Ram's army arrives; the poet comments.
verses.sanskrit_display: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥
verses.translation: When a minister, a doctor and a teacher speak only to please, out of fear or hope of reward, then the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed.
verses.line: When advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you, the ruin comes quickly.

verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's younger brother, advises him in open court.
verses.sanskrit_display: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥
verses.translation: Even a sole master of the fourteen worlds cannot last if he makes enemies of living beings. A person may be an ocean of virtues and clever too, but if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good.
verses.line: You may be gifted and clever, but even a little greed and people stop calling you good.

verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan keeps advising Ravana after the wise minister Malyavan is thrown out.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुमति कुमति सब कें उर रहहीं। नाथ पुरान निगम अस कहहीं॥ जहाँ सुमति तहँ संपति नाना। जहाँ कुमति तहँ बिपति निदाना ॥
verses.translation: Good sense and bad sense live in every heart; so say the scriptures. Where good sense is, many kinds of prosperity follow; where bad sense is, calamity is sure to come.
verses.line: Good sense and bad sense live in every heart. Which you feed decides what follows.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan, insulted and kicked, leaves his brother's court.
verses.sanskrit_display: रामु सत्यसंकल्प प्रभु सभा कालबस तोरि। मैं रघुबीर सरन अब जाउँ देहु जनि खोरि ॥
verses.translation: Ram is the Lord whose resolve is true, and your court is in the grip of doom. I go now to Raghuvir for refuge; don't blame me.
verses.line: I've said what I had to say. I am leaving now; don't blame me.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Three days at the ocean's edge
verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: At the shore, Ram asks how to cross the ocean, and Vibhishan advises.
verses.sanskrit_display: कह लंकेस सुनहु रघुनायक। कोटि सिंधु सोषक तव सायक॥ जद्यपि तदपि नीति असि गाई। बिनय करिअ सागर सन जाई ॥
verses.translation: Raghunath, though a single arrow of yours could dry up countless oceans, good policy says: first go and ask the ocean politely.
verses.line: Even when you have the power to force it, ask politely first.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: After three days of humble requests the ocean still won't let the army cross; Ram finally turns firm.
verses.sanskrit_display: लछिमन बान सरासन आनू। सोषौं बारिधि बिसिख कृसानु॥ सठ सन बिनय कुटिल सन प्रीति। सहज कृपन सन सुंदर नीति ॥ ममता रत सन ग्यान कहानी। अति लोभी सन बिरति बखानी॥ क्रोधिहि सम कामिहि हरिकथा। ऊसर बीज बएँ फल जथा ॥
verses.translation: "Lakshman, bring my bow and arrows; I will dry up the ocean with fiery shafts. Pleading with the stubborn, friendship with the crooked, fine principles to a born miser, talk of wisdom to someone lost in possessiveness, praise of renunciation to the very greedy, calm to the angry, and holy stories to the lustful: all are like sowing seed in barren soil."
verses.line: Calm advice to an angry person, or detachment to a greedy one, is seed sown in barren soil.
verses.misuse: Firmness after real patience, not permission to bully. The doha 'bhay binu hoi na priti' is deliberately not used.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman finds a friend in Lanka
verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's good-hearted brother, describes his life in Ravana's court.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनहु पवनसुत रहनि हमारी। जिमि दसनन्हि महुँ जीभ बिचारी॥ तात कबहुँ मोहि जानि अनाथा। करिहहिं कृपा भानुकुल नाथा ॥
verses.translation: Son of the wind, hear how I live: like the poor tongue among the teeth. Friend, knowing me to be without support, will the Lord of the Sun dynasty ever show me grace?
verses.line: I live here like the tongue among the teeth.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Ram hurries home
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: After the war Vibhishan begs Ram to rest in Lanka; Ram wants to hurry home.
verses.sanskrit_display: तोर कोस गृह मोर सब सत्य बचन सुनु भ्रात। भरत दसा सुमिरत मोहि निमिष कल्प सम जात ॥
verses.translation: Listen, brother: your treasury and home are truly mine. But remembering Bharat's state, each moment feels like an age to me.
verses.line: All you offer is mine too. But thinking of my brother back home, each moment feels like an age.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Angad in Ravana's court
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram sends young Angad as his envoy to Ravana's court.
verses.sanskrit_display: बहुत बुझाइ तुम्हहि का कहऊँ। परम चतुर मैं जानत अहऊँ॥ काजु हमार तासु हित होई। रिपु सन करेहु बतकही सोई ॥
verses.translation: Why explain much to you? I know you are very capable. Talk with the enemy in a way that gets our work done and is good for him too.
verses.line: Speak with your opponent so the work gets done and it does them good too.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Angad in Ravana's court
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Angad plants his foot in Ravana's court and dares anyone to move it; no one can.
verses.sanskrit_display: भूमि न छाँड़त कपि चरन देखत रिपु मद भाग। कोटि बिघ्न ते संत कर मन जिमि नीति न त्याग ॥
verses.translation: The monkey's foot would not leave the ground, and seeing it, the enemy's pride drained away; just as a good person's mind does not abandon what is right, though a million obstacles come.
verses.line: A good mind doesn't leave what is right, though a million obstacles come.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Lakshman falls; Hanuman brings the mountain
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram at midnight, holding Lakshman struck down in battle, waiting for Hanuman and the herb.
verses.sanskrit_display: सकहु न दुखित देखि मोहि काउ। बंधु सदा तव मृदुल सुभाऊ॥ मम हित लागि तजेहु पितु माता। सहेहु बिपिन हिम आतप बाता ॥
verses.translation: Brother, you could never bear to see me sad; your nature was always gentle. For my sake you left mother and father and bore the forest's cold, heat and wind.
verses.line: You could never bear to see me sad. For me you left home and bore every hardship.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Ravana, on the eve of battle, lectures his wives on wisdom; the poet remarks.
verses.sanskrit_display: तिन्हहि ग्यान उपदेसा रावन। आपुन मंद कथा सुभ पावन॥ पर उपदेस कुसल बहुतेरे। जे आचरहिं ते नर न घनेरे ॥
verses.translation: Ravana gave them sermons on knowledge: he himself was wicked, but his talk was pure and fine. Many are skilled at advising others; those who practise it themselves are not many.
verses.line: Many are skilled at advising others. Few live by the advice themselves.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Vibhishan panics: Ravana has a chariot, Ram stands barefoot. Ram describes the chariot that actually wins.
verses.sanskrit_display: सौरज धीरज तेहि रथ चाका। सत्य सील दृढ़ ध्वजा पताका॥ बल बिबेक दम परहित घोरे। छमा कृपा समता रजु जोरे ॥
verses.translation: Valour and patience are the wheels of that chariot; truth and good conduct are its firm flag and banner. Strength, discernment, self-control and kindness to others are its horses, yoked with the reins of forgiveness, compassion and evenness of mind.
verses.line: Courage and patience are the wheels; truth and character, the flag. That is the chariot that wins.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram comes home
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram introduces his monkey and bear companions to his teacher on returning home.
verses.sanskrit_display: ए सब सखा सुनहु मुनि मेरे। भए समर सागर कहँ बेरे॥ मम हित लागि जन्म इन्ह हारे। भरतहु ते मोहि अधिक पिआरे ॥
verses.translation: Listen, sage: these are all my friends. They were my boats across the ocean of battle. For my sake they staked their lives; they are dearer to me than even Bharat.
verses.line: These friends carried me across the battle. For me they staked their lives.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, The student who would not stand for his teacher
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi's teacher
verses.setting: The gentle teacher whose proud student refused even to rise for him pleads with Shiva to lift the student's curse.
verses.sanskrit_display: तव माया बस जीव जड़ संतत फिरइ भुलान। तेहि पर क्रोध न करिअ प्रभु कृपासिंधु भगवान ॥
verses.translation: This ignorant soul, in the grip of your maya, wanders constantly astray. Ocean of mercy, Lord, do not be angry with him.
verses.line: He is confused and lost. Don't be angry with him.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, The student who would not stand for his teacher
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, many lives later, on the one memory that still stings.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रिजग देव नर जोइ तनु धरउँ। तहँ तहँ राम भजन अनुसरऊँ॥ एक सूल मोहि बिसर न काऊ। गुर कर कोमल सील सुभाऊ ॥
verses.translation: Whatever body I took, animal, god or human, I kept up my devotion to Ram. Yet one thorn never left me: I never forgot my teacher's gentle, kindly nature.
verses.line: One thorn never left me: how gentle the teacher I insulted had been.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Arguing with Lomash
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi recalls arguing endlessly with the sage Lomash until the sage lost his temper.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनु प्रभु बहुत अवग्या किएँ। उपज क्रोध ग्यानिन्ह के हिएँ॥ अति संघरषन जौं कर कोई। अनल प्रगट चंदन ते होई ॥
verses.translation: Lord, listen: even a wise man's heart grows angry when he is slighted again and again. If someone rubs sandalwood too hard, even it will burst into flame.
verses.line: Rub even sandalwood too hard, and it bursts into flame.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Garuda's seven questions
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi answers Garuda's questions: what is the highest virtue, and the gravest wrong?
verses.sanskrit_display: संत उदय संतत सुखकारी। बिस्व सुखद जिमि इंदु तमारी॥ परम धर्म श्रुति बिदित अहिंसा। पर निंदा सम अघ न गरीसा ॥
verses.translation: The rise of the good always brings joy, as moon and sun bring joy to the whole world. The Vedas hold non-harm as the highest duty, and there is no wrong as heavy as slandering others.
verses.line: Non-harm is the highest duty. No wrong weighs as much as slandering others.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Mental diseases (manas rog)
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Garuda's last question is about the diseases of the mind; Kakbhushundi answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥
verses.translation: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
verses.line: Confusion is the root illness. Anger is the bile that keeps your chest burning.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram comes home
verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Back in Ayodhya, Ram notices that Kaikeyi is ashamed to face him.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रभु जानी कैकई लजानी। प्रथम तासु गृह गए भवानी॥ ताहि प्रबोधि बहुत सुख दीन्हा। पुनि निज भवन गवन हरि कीन्हा ॥
verses.translation: The Lord saw that Kaikeyi was ashamed, so he went first to her house, Bhavani, comforted her and gave her great ease. Then he went to his own palace.
verses.line: Seeing her shame, he went to her house first and put her at ease.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, The last day of waiting
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Bharat, with one day left of Ram's fourteen years, still has no word.
verses.sanskrit_display: रहेउ एक दिन अवधि अधारा। समुझत मन दुख भयउ अपारा॥ कारन कवन नाथ नहिं आयउ। जानि कुटिल किधौं मोहि बिसरायउ ॥
verses.translation: Only one day of the appointed time, the support of his life, was left. Thinking of it, Bharat's grief was boundless. 'Why hasn't my Lord come? Has he forgotten me, knowing me to be crooked?'
verses.line: One day left, and still no word. Has he forgotten me?

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, The last day of waiting
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Just as Bharat sinks into despair, Hanuman arrives with news.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम बिरह सागर महँ भरत मगन मन होत। बिप्र रूप धरि पवनसुत आइ गयउ जनु पोत॥1क॥
verses.translation: Bharat's mind was sinking in the ocean of separation from Ram when the son of the wind arrived in a Brahmin's guise, as if a boat had come.
verses.line: Just as he was going under, help arrived like a boat.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and bad people.
verses.sanskrit_display: संत असंतन्हि कै असि करनी। जिमि कुठार चंदन आचरनी॥ काटइ परसु मलय सुनु भाई। निज गुन देइ सुगंध बसाई ॥
verses.translation: The way good and bad people treat each other is like sandalwood and the axe: listen, brother, the axe cuts the sandalwood tree, yet the sandalwood, by its own nature, leaves its fragrance on the axe.
verses.line: The axe cuts the sandalwood, and the sandalwood still leaves its fragrance on the axe.
verses.misuse: Staying kind is not the same as staying within reach of the axe.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, The last day of waiting
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat, hearing from Hanuman that Ram is on his way home.
verses.sanskrit_display: कपि तव दरस सकल दुख बीते। मिले आजुमोहि राम पिरीते॥ बार बार बूझी कुसलाता। तो कहुँ देउँ काह सुन भ्राता ॥ एहि संदेस सरिस जग माहीं। करि बिचार देखेउँ कछु नाहीं॥ नाहिन तात उरिन मैं तोही। अब प्रभु चरित सुनावहु मोही ॥
verses.translation: Seeing you, all my sorrows are over; today I have met my beloved Ram himself. He asked again and again after everyone's welfare. 'Brother, what can I give you? Nothing in the world equals this news; I have thought it over. I can never repay you. Now tell me about my Lord.'
verses.line: Nothing in the world equals this news. I can never repay you.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram on good people and difficult people
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, answering Bharat, describes the marks of a good person.
verses.sanskrit_display: बिषय अलंपट सील गुनाकर। पर दुख दुख सुख सुख देखे पर॥ सम अभूतरिपु बिमद बिरागी। लोभामरष हरष भय त्यागी ॥
verses.translation: They are not greedy for pleasures; they are mines of good conduct and virtue; others' sorrow makes them sad and others' joy makes them glad. They are even-minded, see no one as an enemy, are free of pride and detached, and have let go of greed, rage, elation and fear.
verses.line: A good person is saddened by others' sorrow and gladdened by others' joy.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Bharat, finishing his list of the marks of a good person.
verses.sanskrit_display: ए सब लच्छन बसहिं जासु उर। जानेहु तात संत संतत फुर॥ सम दम नियम नीति नहिं डोलहिं। परुष बचन कबहूँ नहिं बोलहिं ॥ निंदा अस्तुति उभय सम ममता मम पद कंज। ते सज्जन मम प्रानप्रिय गुन मंदिर सुख पुंज ॥
verses.translation: Know that whoever carries all these qualities in their heart is truly good. They never waver from self-control, discipline and right conduct, and never speak a harsh word. Praise and blame are the same to them, and their love is for my feet: such good people, homes of virtue and joy, are dear to me as life.
verses.line: Never speak a harsh word. Let praise and blame land on you the same way.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram sums up his teaching to his brothers in Ayodhya.
verses.sanskrit_display: पर हित सरिस धर्म नहिं भाई। पर पीड़ा सम नहिं अधमाई॥ निर्नय सकल पुरान बेद कर। कहेउँ तात जानहिं कोबिद नर ॥
verses.translation: There is no duty equal to doing good to others, brother, and no baseness equal to causing others pain. This is the verdict of all the scriptures; the wise know it.
verses.line: No duty equals doing good to others, and nothing is lower than causing others pain.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram's address to the citizens
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: King Ram calls the whole city together and tells them how to treat what he says.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोइ सेवक प्रियतम मम सोई। मम अनुसासन मानै जोई॥ जौं अनीति कछु भाषौं भाई। तौ मोहि बरजहु भय बिसराई ॥
verses.translation: "The one who follows my teaching is truly my dear servant. But if I say anything unjust, brothers, put aside your fear and stop me."
verses.line: If I say anything wrong, stop me. Don't be afraid.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram's address to the citizens
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to the citizens, describing the person at peace.
verses.sanskrit_display: बैर न बिग्रह आस न त्रासा। सुखमय ताहि सदा सब आसा॥ अनारंभ अनिकेत अमानी। अनघ अरोष दच्छ बिग्यानी ॥
verses.translation: "Holding no grudge and picking no quarrel, with neither craving nor fear, every direction is joyful to him. He starts nothing out of craving for results, clings to no house, wants no honour, is free of wrongdoing and anger, skilled and wise."
verses.line: No grudges, no quarrels, no craving, no fear: for such a person every direction is joy.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram comes home
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, flying home in the Pushpak, points out Ayodhya to his friends.
verses.sanskrit_display: जद्यपि सब बैकुंठ बखाना। बेद पुरान बिदित जगु जाना॥ अवधपुरी सम प्रिय नहिं सोऊ। यह प्रसंग जानइ कोउ कोऊ ॥ जन्मभूमि मम पुरी सुहावनि। उत्तर दिसि बह सरजू पावनि॥ जा मज्जन ते बिनहिं प्रयासा। मम समीप नर पावहिं बासा ॥
verses.translation: Though everyone praises Vaikuntha, as the Vedas and Puranas say and the world knows, even that is not as dear to me as Avadhpuri; few know this secret. This lovely city is my birthplace; to its north flows the holy Sarayu, by bathing in which people come to dwell near me without effort.
verses.line: Heaven may be praised by all. It isn't as dear to me as the town where I was born.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva, met on the road by the doubt-ridden Garuda, sends him to good company instead of answering.
verses.sanskrit_display: मिलेहु गरुड़ मारग महँ मोही। कवन भाँति समुझावौं तोही॥ तबहिं होइ सब संसय भंगा। जब बहु काल करिअ सतसंगा ॥
verses.translation: You met me on the road; how can I explain it to you in passing? All doubts end only when one spends a long time in good company.
verses.line: Doubts don't end in a passing conversation. They clear with long time in good company.

verses.speaker: Garuda
verses.setting: Garuda, his doubt resolved, thanks Kakbhushundi.
verses.sanskrit_display: जो अति आतप ब्याकुल होई। तरु छाया सुख जानइ सोई॥ जौं नहिं होत मोह अति मोही। मिलतेउँ तात कवन बिधि तोही ॥
verses.translation: Only one scorched by the sun knows the comfort of a tree's shade. Friend, had I not been so deeply confused, how would I ever have met you?
verses.line: Only the one scorched by the sun knows the shade. Without my doubt, I'd never have found you.

verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi tells the ashamed Garuda that his confusion is nothing unusual.
verses.sanskrit_display: मोह न अंध कीन्ह केहि केही। को जग काम नचाव नजेही॥ तृस्नाँ केहि न कीन्ह बौराहा। केहि कर हृदय क्रोध नहिं दाहा ॥
verses.translation: Whom has delusion not blinded? Who in the world has desire not made to dance? Whom has craving not maddened? Whose heart has anger not burned?
verses.line: Who hasn't been blinded, made to dance by desire, maddened by craving, burned by anger?

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi to Garuda
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: The crow-sage Kakbhushundi consoles Garuda, ashamed of his own confusion: no one is immune.
verses.sanskrit_display: मच्छर काहि कलंक न लावा। काहि न सोक समीर डोलावा॥ चिंता साँपिनि को नहिं खाया। को जग जाहि न ब्यापी माया ॥
verses.translation: Whom has envy not stained? Whom has the wind of grief not shaken? Whom has the snake of worry not bitten? Who in the world has not been caught by illusion?
verses.line: Whom has the snake of worry not bitten? You are not the only one.

verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, explaining to Garuda how people misjudge what they see.
verses.sanskrit_display: नयन दोष जा कहँ जब होई। पीत बरन ससि कहुँ कह सोई॥ जब जेहि दिसि भ्रम होई खगेसा। सो कह पच्छिम उयउ दिनेसा ॥ नौकारूढ़ चलत जग देखा। अचल मोह बस आपुहि लेखा॥ बालक भ्रमहिं न भ्रमहिं गृहादी। कहहिं परस्पर मिथ्याबादी ॥
verses.translation: When someone's eyes are diseased, he calls the moon yellow; when someone loses his bearings, he says the sun rose in the west. A man on a moving boat sees the world moving and, deluded, thinks himself still. Children spin round, not the houses, yet they call each other liars.
verses.line: Diseased eyes see a yellow moon. From a moving boat, the shore seems to move.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, on why being humbled can be a kindness.
verses.sanskrit_display: ताते करहिं कृपानिधि दूरी। सेवक पर ममता अति भूरी॥ जिमि सिसु तन ब्रन होई गोसाईं। मातु चिराव कठिन की नाईं ॥ जदपि प्रथम दुख पावइ रोवइ बाल अधीर। ब्याधि नास हित जननी गनति न सो सिसु पीर॥ 74 क॥
verses.translation: So the merciful one removes it, for he loves his servant deeply. When a boil forms on a child's body, the mother has it lanced as if she were hard-hearted. Though the child suffers at first and cries out, the mother, to cure the illness, pays no heed to that pain.
verses.line: A mother has the boil lanced though the child cries. Some humbling is like that.
verses.misuse: Not every pain is for your good; don't use this to excuse harm done to anyone.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Offered every power and pleasure by the child Ram, young Kakbhushundi thinks before choosing.
verses.sanskrit_display: भगति हीन गुन सब सुख ऐसे। लवन बिना बहु बिंजन जैसे॥ भजन हीन सुख कवने काजा। अस बिचारि बोलेउँ खगराजा ॥
verses.translation: Without devotion, all virtues and pleasures are like many dishes without salt. What use is happiness without devotion? Thinking so, I spoke.
verses.line: Every comfort without devotion is like a feast without salt.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, summing up what he learned, on how love grows.
verses.sanskrit_display: जानें बिनु न होइ परतीती। बिनु परतीति होइ नहिं प्रीती॥ प्रीति बिना नहिं भगति दिढ़ाई। जिमि खगपति जल कै चिकनाई ॥
verses.translation: Without knowing his greatness, no trust forms; without trust, no love; and without love, devotion is not firm, just as, king of birds, oil does not stay on water.
verses.line: Without knowing, there is no trust. Without trust, there is no love.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi to Garuda
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi to Garuda on what actually brings rest.
verses.sanskrit_display: कोउ बिश्राम कि पाव तात सहज संतोष बिनु। चलै कि जल बिनु नाव कोटि जतन पचि पचि मरिअ ॥
verses.translation: Can anyone find rest without natural contentment, friend? Can a boat move without water, though you strain and wear yourself out with a million efforts?
verses.line: No one finds rest without contentment, any more than a boat moves without water.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Manu and Shatarupa ask late in life
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: King Manu, who ruled well for a lifetime, sees that old age has come and something essential was missed.
verses.sanskrit_display: होइ न बिषय बिराग भवन बसत भा चौथपन॥ हृदयँ बहुत दुख लाग जनम गयउ हरिभगति बिनु ॥
verses.translation: Old age came while he lived at home, yet the pull of pleasures had not faded. His heart grieved deeply that his life had gone by without devotion to Hari.
verses.line: Old age arrived at home, the cravings stayed, and he grieved for the years spent elsewhere.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Manu and Shatarupa ask late in life
verses.speaker: Manu
verses.setting: Manu, offered any boon after years of austerity, hesitates to ask for what he truly wants.
verses.sanskrit_display: जथा दरिद्र बिबुधतरु पाई। बहु संपति मागत सकुचाई॥ तासु प्रभाउ जान नहिं सोई। तथा हृदयँ मम संसय होई ॥
verses.translation: Like a poor man who finds the wish-fulfilling tree and still hesitates to ask for much, not knowing its power, so doubt rises in my heart.
verses.line: Like a poor man before the wishing tree, we hesitate to ask for what we really want.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, as a king is taken in by an old enemy disguised as a holy man.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुलसी देखि सुबेषु भूलहिं मूढ़ न चतुर नर। सुंदर केकिहि पेखु बचन सुधा सम असन अहि ॥
verses.translation: It is not only fools who are taken in by a fine appearance; the clever are too. Look at the beautiful peacock: its voice is like nectar, and it eats snakes.
verses.line: Even the clever are fooled by a fine look. The peacock sings like nectar and eats snakes.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Kausalya and the child who ran from dinner
verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: Kausalya, shown her newborn's cosmic form, asks him to be simply her baby.
verses.sanskrit_display: माता पुनि बोली सो मति डोली तजहु तात यह रूपा। कीजै सिसुलीला अति प्रियसीला यह सुख परम अनूपा॥ सुनि बचन सुजाना रोदन ठाना होइ बालक सुरभूपा। यह चरित जे गावहिं हरिपद पावहिं ते न परहिं भवकूपा ॥
verses.translation: Then the mother spoke, her mind unsettled: 'Child, put away this form. Play as a little child, so dear to the heart; that joy is beyond compare.' Hearing her, the wise Lord began to cry and became a baby. Those who sing this story reach Hari's feet and do not fall into the well of worldly life.
verses.line: Put away the grand form, child. Just be little with me; there is no joy like it.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Dasharath lets his sons go
verses.speaker: Dasharath
verses.setting: King Dasharath, who had his sons late in life, is asked to send young Ram away with a sage.
verses.sanskrit_display: सब सुत प्रिय मोहि प्रान की नाईं। राम देत नहिं बनइ गोसाईं॥ कहँ निसिचर अति घोर कठोरा। कहँ सुंदर सुत परम किसोरा ॥
verses.translation: All my sons are dear to me as life, and Ram I cannot bring myself to give. Where are those terrible, cruel demons, and where my tender, boyish son?
verses.line: Every child is dear as life, and some partings a parent can hardly bear to make.
verses.misuse: Love that never lets go can hold a child back; in the story he does let Ram go.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Lakshman, when the furious sage Parashurama keeps boasting of his past deeds.
verses.sanskrit_display: सूर समर करनी करहिं कहि न जनावहिं आपु। बिद्यमान रन पाइ रिपु कायर कथहिं प्रतापु ॥
verses.translation: The truly brave prove themselves by what they do in battle; they do not announce themselves. Cowards, finding an enemy in front of them, talk about their own prowess.
verses.line: The capable let their work speak. It is the insecure who keep announcing what they can do.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, opening the Manas, on how company shapes people.
verses.sanskrit_display: सठ सुधरहिं सतसंगति पाई। पारस परस कुधात सुहाई॥ बिधि बस सुजन कुसंगत परहीं। फनि मनि सम निज गुन अनुसरहीं ॥
verses.translation: Even the crooked improve in good company, the way base metal turns to gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone. And if by chance good people fall among bad company, they keep their own nature, like the jewel in a cobra's hood that never takes on its poison.
verses.line: Good company can change the worst of us; the good keep their light even in bad company.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Sati doubts, tests and hides it
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Sati realises Shiva has withdrawn from her after she lied to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: संकर रुख अवलोकि भवानी। प्रभु मोहि तजेउ हृदयँ अकुलानी॥ निज अघ समुझि न कछु कहि जाई। तपइ अवाँ इव उर अधिकाई ॥
verses.translation: Reading Shiva's manner, Sati knew he had left her in his heart, and she was shaken. Knowing the fault was her own, she could say nothing, but inside her heart burned like a potter's kiln.
verses.line: When you know the fault is yours, words fail, and the heart burns quietly like a kiln.
verses.misuse: Guilt is a signal to make amends, not a sentence to burn forever.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: Parvati, after the sages list Shiva's faults and offer her a 'better' match.
verses.sanskrit_display: महादेव अवगुन भवन बिष्नु सकल गुन धाम। जेहि कर मनु रम जाहि सन तेहि तेही सन काम ॥
verses.translation: Grant that Mahadev is a house of faults and Vishnu the home of every virtue. Still, the one a heart has settled on is the one it wants.
verses.line: Others may list the faults. The heart wants the one it has chosen.
verses.misuse: Choosing for yourself still means listening honestly to those who care.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, before beginning his poem, on how people judge their own work.
verses.sanskrit_display: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥ जे पर भनिति सुनत हरषाहीं। ते बर पुरुष बहुत जग नाहीं ॥
verses.translation: Who does not like their own poetry, whether it is rich or utterly flat? But people who are delighted by someone else's work are rare in this world.
verses.line: Everyone loves their own work. Rare is the person who is truly glad about someone else's.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Brihaspati checks Indra's envy
verses.speaker: Brihaspati
verses.setting: The gods' teacher Brihaspati to Indra, who fears Bharat's rising virtue and wants to scheme against him.
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्यसंध प्रभु सुर हितकारी। भरत राम आयस अनुसारी॥ स्वारथ बिबस बिकल तुम्ह होहू। भरत दोसु नहिं राउर मोहू ॥
verses.translation: The Lord is true to his word and kind to the gods, and Bharat follows Ram's wishes. You are anxious for nothing, gripped by self-interest. The fault is not Bharat's; it is your own confusion.
verses.line: You're anxious because of your own interests. The fault isn't theirs; it's your confusion.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Chitrakoot: Ram to Bharat
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram reassures Bharat, who is tormented by guilt over his mother's scheme.
verses.sanskrit_display: कहउँ सुभाउ सत्य सिव साखी। भरत भूमि रह राउरि राखी॥ तात कुतरक करहु जनि जाएँ। बैर पेम नहिं दुरइ दुराएँ ॥
verses.translation: "I tell you truly, with Shiva as witness: the earth stays safe because you hold it. Don't torment yourself with needless doubts, brother. Hostility and love cannot be hidden, however you try."
verses.line: Stop torturing yourself with doubts. Love and hostility cannot be hidden; people know which you carry.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Janaka's family joins the council
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat, asked by Janaka what should be done, explains why he can't judge his own case.
verses.sanskrit_display: आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। सेवाधरमु कठिन जगु जाना॥ स्वामि धरम स्वारथहि बिरोधू। बैरु अंध प्रेमहि न प्रबोधू ॥
verses.translation: The Vedas, scriptures and Puranas say, and the world knows, that the duty of service is hard. Duty to one's master and self-interest pull against each other; hatred is blind, and love has no judgement.
verses.line: Duty and self-interest pull against each other. Hatred is blind, and love can't reason.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Janaka's family joins the council
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Janaka and his court react to Bharat's reply.
verses.sanskrit_display: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सुभाऊ। सहित समाज सराहत राऊ॥ सुगम अगम मृदु मंजु कठोरे। अरथु अमित अति आखर थोरे ॥
verses.translation: Hearing Bharat's words and seeing his nature, Janaka and his court praised him. His words were easy yet deep, gentle yet firm: few in syllables, boundless in meaning.
verses.line: Easy yet deep, gentle yet firm: few words, boundless meaning.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Bharat rules from a hut for fourteen years
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Bharat rules Ayodhya for fourteen years from a hut, taking nothing for himself.
verses.sanskrit_display: तेहिं पुर बसत भरत बिनु रागा। चंचरीक जिमि चंपक बागा॥ रमा बिलासु राम अनुरागी। तजत बमन जिमि जन बड़भागी ॥
verses.translation: Bharat lives in that city without attachment, like a bee in a champak garden. Fortunate lovers of Ram turn from the luxuries of wealth as one turns from vomit.
verses.line: He lived amid the riches like a bee in a champak garden, untouched by them.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Kausalya lets her son go
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Kausalya hears her son must go into exile and is torn between duty and love.
verses.sanskrit_display: धरम सनेह उभयँ मति घेरी। भइ गति साँप छुछुंदरि केरी॥ राखउँ सुतहि करउँ अनुरोधू। धरमु जाइ अरु बंधु बिरोधू ॥
verses.translation: Duty and love together hemmed in her mind; she was like the snake that has seized a muskrat. 'If I insist and keep my son, duty is lost and the brothers fall out...'
verses.line: Caught between duty and love, like a snake that can neither swallow nor let go.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
verses.speaker: Sumitra
verses.setting: Sumitra's parting advice to her son as he leaves home for fourteen years.
verses.sanskrit_display: रागु रोषु इरिषा मदु मोहू। जनि सपनेहुँ इन्ह के बस होहू॥ सकल प्रकार बिकार बिहाई। मन क्रम बचन करेहु सेवकाई ॥
verses.translation: Never, even in a dream, fall under the sway of attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion. Leaving every such distortion behind, serve Sita and Ram with mind, word and deed.
verses.line: A mother's send-off: never let attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion rule you, even in dreams.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Ram and Sumantra
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, when the charioteer Sumantra begs him to return to Ayodhya as the king wished.
verses.sanskrit_display: धरमु न दूसर सत्य समाना। आगम निगम पुरान बखाना॥ मैं सोइ धरमु सुलभ करि पावा। तजें तिहूँ पुर अपजसु छावा ॥
verses.translation: "The scriptures all say there is no duty equal to truth. I have found that duty easily within my reach. If I abandon it, disgrace will spread through all three worlds."
verses.line: There is no duty higher than truth. Abandoning it costs more than anything it saves.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to the dying vulture Jatayu, who gave his life trying to save Sita.
verses.sanskrit_display: परहित बस जिन्ह के मन माहीं। तिन्ह कहुँ जग दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं॥ तनु तिज तात जाहु मम धामा। देउँ काह तुम्ह पूरनकामा ॥
verses.translation: "For those whose minds are ruled by the good of others, nothing in the world is out of reach. Leave this body, friend, and go to my abode; what can I give you, who already have everything?"
verses.line: For someone whose heart is set on the good of others, nothing in the world is out of reach.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Shabari, completing the nine forms of devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: नवम सरल सब सन छलहीना। मम भरोस हियँ हरष न दीना॥ नव महुँ एकउ जिन्ह कें होई। नारि पुरुष सचराचर कोई ॥
verses.translation: The ninth is to be simple and free of guile with everyone, to keep trust in me in your heart, and to be neither elated nor downcast. Whoever has even one of these nine, man or woman or any creature at all...
verses.line: Be simple and without guile with everyone, neither carried away by joy nor crushed by setbacks.

verses.collection: Manas: Aranya Kand, Pampa: Ram to Lakshman
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Lakshman in the spring forest near Pampa lake.
verses.sanskrit_display: तात तीनि अति प्रबल खल काम क्रोध अरु लोभ। मुनि बिग्यान धाम मन करहिं निमिष महुँ छोभ ॥
verses.translation: Brother, three enemies are exceedingly strong: desire, anger and greed. In an instant they unsettle even the minds of sages who are homes of wisdom.
verses.line: Desire, anger and greed can unsettle even the wisest mind in a moment.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Lakshman, as the rains end and autumn clears the sky.
verses.sanskrit_display: उदित अगस्ति पंथ जल सोषा। जिमि लोभहिं सोषइ संतोषा॥ सरिता सर निर्मल जल सोहा। संत हृदय जस गत मद मोहा ॥
verses.translation: Agastya's star rises and dries the water on the roads, as contentment dries up greed. Rivers and lakes shine with clear water, like the heart of a good person freed from pride and confusion.
verses.line: Contentment dries up greed the way the autumn sun dries the puddles.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, describing autumn to Lakshman, as the ponds begin to shrink.
verses.sanskrit_display: पंक न रेनु सोह असि धरनी। नीति निपुन नृप कै जसि करनी॥ जल संकोच बिकल भइँ मीना। अबुध कुटुंबी जिमि धनहीना ॥
verses.translation: With neither mud nor dust, the earth looks like the work of a wise king. As the water shrinks, the fish grow restless, like a thoughtless householder when the money runs out.
verses.line: Fish panic as the pond shrinks, like a careless household when the money runs out.
verses.misuse: Not a judgement on anyone struggling with money; a nudge to plan for dry seasons.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Sampati's burned wings
verses.speaker: Sampati
verses.setting: The old vulture Sampati tells the despairing monkeys how he lost his wings.
verses.sanskrit_display: तेज न सहि सक सो फिरि आवा। मैं अभिमानी रबि निअरावा॥ जरे पंख अति तेज अपारा। परेउँ भूमि करि घोर चिकारा ॥
verses.translation: He (Jatayu) could not bear the sun's heat and turned back; I, being proud, flew on towards the sun. My wings burned in its boundless blaze, and I fell to the earth with a terrible cry.
verses.line: My brother turned back from the sun. I, in my pride, flew closer, and my wings burned.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Sugriva and Bali: brothers split by a misunderstanding
verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva, after Ram promises to help him, sees his feud with his brother Bali differently.
verses.sanskrit_display: बालि परम हित जासु प्रसादा। मिलेहु राम तुम्ह समन बिषादा॥ सपनें जेहि सन होइ लराई। जागें समुझत मन सकुचाई ॥
verses.translation: Bali is in fact my greatest benefactor: through him I met you, who end all sorrow. Now if I fought him even in a dream, I'd feel ashamed on waking.
verses.line: If I fought my brother even in a dream, I'd feel ashamed on waking.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Sugriva on what a friend actually does.
verses.sanskrit_display: जिन्ह कें असि मति सहज न आई। ते सठ कत हठि करत मिताई॥ कुपथ निवारि सुपंथ चलावा। गुन प्रगटै अवगुनन्हि दुरावा ॥
verses.translation: Why do those who lack this natural feeling force themselves into friendships? A friend turns you back from the wrong path and sets you on the right one, makes your good qualities known and keeps your faults to himself.
verses.line: A friend steers you off the wrong path, speaks of your strengths, and keeps your faults private.
verses.misuse: Keeping faults private means discretion, not covering up harm.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Sugriva on the marks of a good friend.
verses.sanskrit_display: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥
verses.translation: He gives and takes without suspicion, always does you good as far as he is able, and in hard times loves you a hundred times more. These, say the scriptures, are the qualities of a good friend.
verses.line: A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Sugriva on the signs of a false friend.
verses.sanskrit_display: आगें कह मृदु बचन बनाई। पाछें अनहित मन कुटिलाई॥ जाकर िचत अहि गति सम भाई। अस कुमित्र परिहरेहिं भलाई ॥
verses.translation: One who says sweet, made-up words to your face but wishes you ill behind your back, with a crooked mind; whose heart moves like a snake, brother: it is best to leave such a false friend.
verses.line: Sweet to your face, harmful behind your back: it is best to walk away from such a friend.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman speaks plainly to Ravana
verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman, bound in Ravana's court, warns him about power that has no root.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम बिमुख संपति प्रभुताई। जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई॥ सजल मूल जिन्ह सरितन्ह नाहीं। बरषि गएँ पुनि तबहिं सुखाहीं ॥
verses.translation: For one turned away from Ram, wealth and power slip away even while held, and having them is like not having them. Rivers with no spring at their source dry up as soon as the rains have passed.
verses.line: Wealth with no deep source is a rain-fed river: gone as soon as the rains stop.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Ravana kicks his brother Vibhishan for urging him to return Sita.
verses.sanskrit_display: उमा संत कइ इहइ बड़ाई। मंद करत जो करइ भलाई॥ तुम्ह पितु सरिस भलेहिं मोहि मारा। रामु भजें हित नाथ तुम्हारा ॥
verses.translation: (Shiva:) Uma, this is the greatness of the good: they do good even to those who harm them. (Vibhishan:) You are like a father to me; strike me if you will. But your good, brother, lies in turning to Ram.
verses.line: The good still wish you well when you strike them.
verses.misuse: Wishing someone well does not mean staying to be hurt; Vibhishan leaves.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman enters Lanka
verses.speaker: Lankini
verses.setting: Lanka's gatekeeper, humbled by Hanuman, sends him into the city with a blessing.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥
verses.translation: Enter the city and do all your work, holding the king of Kosala in your heart. For such a one, poison turns to nectar, enemies become friends, the ocean shrinks to a hoofprint, and fire turns cool.
verses.line: Walk into the hard task carrying what you love in your heart, and even poison turns to nectar.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, when Sugriva suspects Vibhishan is a spy and urges him to be turned away.
verses.sanskrit_display: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा। मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥ भेद लेन पठवा दससीसा। तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा ॥
verses.translation: "A person with a clean mind reaches me; I have no liking for deceit, tricks or fault-finding. Even if Ravana sent him to learn our secrets, there is no fear or loss in it for us, Sugriva."
verses.line: Deceit and tricks win nothing lasting. People with a clean mind are the ones who are trusted.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Vibhishan meets Ram
verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan, newly arrived at Ram's camp, on his years in Ravana's palace.
verses.sanskrit_display: बरु भल बास नरक कर ताता। दुष्ट संग जनि देइ बिधाता॥ अब पद देखि कुसल रघुराया। जौं तुम्ह कीन्हि जानि जन दाया ॥
verses.translation: "Better to live in hell, friend, than to be given the company of the wicked. Now that I have seen your feet, Lord, I am well, since you have shown me kindness, knowing me as your own."
verses.line: Better to live in hell than to be stuck in the company of the cruel.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again
verses.speaker: Prahasta
verses.setting: Prahasta, Ravana's son, leaves after his father rejects his advice and insults him.
verses.sanskrit_display: हित मत तोहि न लागत कैसें। काल बिबस कहुँ भेषज जैसें॥ संध्या समय जानि दससीसा। भवन चलेउ निरखत भुज बीसा ॥
verses.translation: How is it that sound advice doesn't take with you? Like medicine on one in death's grip. Seeing it was evening, Ravana went to his palace, admiring his twenty arms.
verses.line: Good advice won't take on someone set on ruin, like medicine on the dying.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Kumbhakarna fights for a brother he knows is wrong
verses.speaker: Kumbhakarna
verses.setting: Kumbhakarna, going out to fight for Ravana though he knows him wrong, meets Vibhishan, who has joined Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनु भयउ कालबस रावन। सो कि मान अब परम सिखावन॥ धन्य धन्य तैं धन्य विभीषन। भयहु तात निसिचर कुल भूषन ॥
verses.translation: Listen, son: Ravana is in the grip of doom; would he heed good counsel now? Blessed, blessed, blessed are you, Vibhishan; you have become the ornament of our clan.
verses.line: Blessed, blessed are you, brother. You have become the pride of our family.

verses.speaker: Mandodari
verses.setting: Ravana's wife Mandodari pleads with him to give up the war.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथ बयरु कीजे ताही सों। बुधि बल सकिअ जीति जाही सों॥ तुम्हहि रघुपतिहि अंतर कैसा। खलु खद्योत दिनकरहि जैसा ॥
verses.translation: "My lord, pick a quarrel only with someone you can defeat with your wits and strength. Between you and Ram there is the difference between a firefly and the sun."
verses.line: Pick your fights only where your wits and strength can actually win.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Arguing with Lomash
verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva, as the cursed Kakbhushundi flies off without bitterness.
verses.sanskrit_display: उमा जे राम चरन रत बिगत काम मद क्रोध। निज प्रभुमय देखहिं जगत केहि सन करहिं बिरोध ॥
verses.translation: Uma, those devoted to Ram's feet, free of desire, pride and anger, see the whole world filled with their Lord; with whom would they quarrel?
verses.line: When you see the divine in everyone, who is left to quarrel with?

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Mental diseases (manas rog)
