verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi continues listing the diseases of the mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥
verses.translation: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
verses.line: Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Garuda's seven questions
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, on what people do with a rare human life.
verses.sanskrit_display: सो तनु धरि हरि भजहिं न जे नर। होहिं बिषय रत मंद मंद तर॥ काँच किरिच बदलें ते लेहीं। कर ते डारि परस मनि देहीं ॥
verses.translation: Those who gain this body and still do not worship Hari, sunk in the lowest of pleasures, throw away the philosopher's stone from their hand and take shards of glass in exchange.
verses.line: We throw away the philosopher's stone and take shards of glass in exchange.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Garuda's seven questions
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi answers Garuda's questions: what is the greatest sorrow, and the greatest joy?
verses.sanskrit_display: नहिं दरिद्र सम दुख जग माहीं। संत मिलन सम सुख जग नाहीं॥ पर उपकार बचन मन काया। संत सहज सुभाउ खगराया ॥
verses.translation: There is no sorrow in the world like poverty, and no joy like meeting good people. To do good to others in word, thought and deed is the natural way of the good.
verses.line: No sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram says goodbye to his friends
verses.speaker: Angad
verses.setting: Angad, whose father Bali died, pleads not to be sent home after the war.
verses.sanskrit_display: असरन सरन बिरदु संभारी। मोहि जनि तजहु भगत हितकारी॥ मोरें तुम्ह प्रभु गुर पितु माता। जाउँ कहाँ तजि पद जलजाता ॥
verses.translation: Remember your vow to shelter the shelterless and don't abandon me, friend of devotees. You are my lord, teacher, father and mother; leaving your feet, where would I go?
verses.line: You are my teacher, my father and mother now. Where would I go?

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram says goodbye to his friends
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram bids farewell to Guha, the boatmen's chief who helped him into exile.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम्ह मम सखा भरत सम भ्राता। सदा रहेहु पुर आवत जाता॥ बचन सुनत उपजा सुख भारी। परेउ चरन भरि लोचन बारी ॥
verses.translation: You are my friend and a brother like Bharat. Keep coming and going to Ayodhya always. Hearing this, he felt great joy and fell at Ram's feet, eyes full of tears.
verses.line: You are my friend, a brother to me. Keep visiting, always.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Bharat on the nature of the malicious.
verses.sanskrit_display: खलन्ह हृदयँ अति ताप बिसेषी। जरहिं सदा पर संपति देखी॥ जहँ कहुँ निंदा सुनहिं पराई। हरषहिं मनहुँ परी निधि पाई ॥
verses.translation: The hearts of the wicked burn with a special heat: they are always on fire at the sight of someone else's prosperity. Wherever they hear someone being run down, they are delighted, as if they had stumbled on treasure.
verses.line: Envy burns at another's success and feasts on gossip as if it found treasure.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram's address to the citizens
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to the citizens, on how simple the path really is.
verses.sanskrit_display: कहहु भगति पथ कवन प्रयासा। जोग न मख जप तप उपवासा। सरल सुभाव न मन कुटिलाई। जथा लाभ संतोष सदाई ॥
verses.translation: "Tell me, what effort does this path take? No yoga, no sacrifices, no chanting, austerities or fasts. Only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment with whatever comes."
verses.line: No grand effort needed: a simple nature, an honest mind, and contentment with what comes.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, beginning his own story, on why pride is taken from us.
verses.sanskrit_display: नहु राम कर सहज सुभाऊ। जन अभिमान न राखहिं काऊ॥ संसृत मूल सूलप्रद नाना। सकल सोक दायक अभिमाना ॥
verses.translation: Hear Ram's natural way: he never lets pride stay in his devotee, for pride is the root of the cycle of birth and death, the giver of many pains and of every sorrow.
verses.line: Pride is the root of countless pains and every sorrow.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram explains to Kakbhushundi how he loves all beings, using a father's love as the picture.
verses.sanskrit_display: एक पिता के बिपुल कुमारा। होहिं पृथक गुन सील अचारा॥ कोउ पंडित कोउ तापस ग्याता। कोउ धनवंत सूर कोउ दाता ॥ कोउ सर्बग्य धर्मरत कोई। सब पर पितहि प्रीति सम होई॥ कोउ पितु भगत बचन मन कर्मा। सपनेहुँ जान न दूसर धर्मा ॥
verses.translation: One father has many sons, each different in gifts, nature and conduct: one a scholar, one an ascetic, one wise, one rich, one brave, one generous; one all-knowing, one devoted to duty. The father's love is the same for all; but if one is devoted to the father in mind, word and deed, knowing no other duty even in dreams...
verses.line: One parent, many children, each different in gifts and nature, and the love for all is the same.

verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, describing a degraded age, on what teachers and parents pass on.
verses.sanskrit_display: हरइ सिष्य धन सोक न हरई। सो गुर घोर नरक महुँ परई॥ मातु पिता बालकन्हि बोलावहिं। उदर भरै सोइ धर्म सिखावहिं ॥
verses.translation: The teacher who takes his disciple's money but not his sorrow falls into a terrible hell. Parents call their children and teach them only the dharma that fills the belly.
verses.line: Parents call their children and teach them only what fills the stomach.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Brihaspati to Indra
verses.speaker: Brihaspati
verses.setting: The gods' teacher warns Indra not to scheme against Bharat.
verses.sanskrit_display: जद्यपि सम नहिं राग न रोषू। गहहिं न पाप पूनु गुन दोषू॥ करम प्रधान बिस्व करि राखा। जो जस करइ सो तस फलु चाखा ॥
verses.translation: Though Ram is impartial, without attachment or anger, and does not take on anyone's sin, merit, virtue or fault, he has made action the governing law of the world: whatever one does, one tastes the fruit of it.
verses.line: The world runs on action: as you do, so you reap.
verses.misuse: Read as encouragement to act well, not as judgement on anyone's misfortune.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, rainy season similes
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Lakshman, watching the monsoon.
verses.sanskrit_display: छुद्र नदीं भरि चलीं तोराई। जस थोरेहुँ धन खल इतराई॥ भूमि परत भा ढाबर पानी। जनु जीवहि माया लपटानी ॥
verses.translation: Little streams swell and rush along, bursting their banks, the way a petty person swaggers on a little money. Rainwater falling on the ground turns muddy, as the soul is clouded once it is wrapped in illusion.
verses.line: Little streams overflow after one rain, the way small minds swagger after a little money.

verses.ref_label: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand (data 2.165 doha; Gita Press 2.171)
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Bharat has come home to find his father dead and Ram exiled. Vasishtha, grieving too, consoles him.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनहु भरत भावी प्रबल बिलखि कहेउ मुनिनाथ। हानि लाभु जीवनु मरनु जसु अपजसु बिधि हाथ ॥
verses.translation: Listen, Bharat, said the sage, himself in tears: what is to be is powerful. Loss and gain, life and death, honour and dishonour all rest in the Creator's hands.
verses.line: Loss and gain, life and death, praise and blame: much of it was never in your hands.
verses.misuse: Said to lift a grieving son's guilt, not to excuse inaction. Your effort is still one of the five causes of any outcome (Gita 18.14).

verses.collection: The five causes of every action
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verses.sanskrit_display: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verses.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verses.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verses.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram has lain on the shore for three days asking the ocean for a way across. No answer comes.
verses.sanskrit_display: अवलेपः समुद्रस्य न दर्शयति यः स्वयम्। प्रशमश्च क्षमा चैव आर्जवं प्रियवादिता॥ असामर्थ्यफला ह्येते निर्गुणेषु सतां गुणाः।
verses.translation: See the ocean's arrogance: he does not even show himself. Calm, forbearance, straightforwardness and gentle speech, these virtues of the good, are taken by the unworthy as signs of weakness.
verses.line: Calm, patience, honesty and kind words: people who don't value them will read them as weakness.
verses.misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: After three days of patient requests, Ram turns to Lakshman.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षमया हि समायुक्तं मामयं मकरालयः॥ असमर्थ विजानाति धिक्क्षमामीदृशे जने। न दर्शयति साम्ना मे सागरो रूपमात्मनः॥ चापमानय सौमित्रे शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान्। समुद्रं शोषयिष्यामि पद्भयां यान्तु प्लवंगमाः॥
verses.translation: Because I am forbearing, this ocean takes me to be incapable. Shame on forbearance toward such a one. Gentle means have not made him show himself. Lakshman, bring my bow and arrows.
verses.line: My patience was taken for weakness. Gentle asking didn't work. Lakshman, bring my bow.
verses.misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.

verses.collection: Sundar: Three days at the ocean's edge
verses.ref_label: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand (data 5.55 doha; Gita Press 5.57)
verses.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating Ram)
verses.setting: Ram has sat on the shore three days, humbly asking the ocean for a way. The ocean stays silent.
verses.sanskrit_display: बिनय न मानत जलधि जड़ गए तीनि दिन बीति। बोले राम सकोप तब भय बिनु होइ न प्रीति ॥
verses.translation: Three days passed and the stubborn ocean ignored his humble request. Then Ram spoke in anger: without some fear, there is no regard.
verses.line: Three days of humble asking, ignored. Some people only listen once they see you'll act.
verses.misuse: About a stubborn party who ignores repeated humble requests, not a rule for love or for people close to you. Patience comes first; Ram waited three days and forgave the ocean the moment it came.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the opening section on fools: why some people cannot be reasoned with.
verses.sanskrit_display: अज्ञः सुखमाराध्यः सुखतरमाराध्यते विशेषज्ञः । ज्ञानलवदुर्विदग्धं ब्रह्मापि तं नरं न रञ्जयति ॥
verses.translation: An ignorant person is easily won over; an expert, more easily still. But a person puffed up by a scrap of knowledge not even Brahma, the Creator, can satisfy.
verses.line: The ignorant can be taught and the expert persuaded. The half-knower not even God can convince.
verses.misuse: Not a licence to dismiss everyone who disagrees with you as a half-knower; check yourself first.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on fools, on the stubborn mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रसह्य मणिमुद्धरेन्मकरवक्त्रदंष्ट्राङ्कुरा- त्समुद्रमपि संतरेत्प्रचलदूर्मिमालाकुलम् । भुजङ्गमपि कोपितं शिरसि पुष्पवद्धारये- न्न तु प्रतिनिविष्टमूर्खजनचित्तमाराधयेत् ॥
verses.translation: One might wrench a jewel from between a crocodile's teeth, swim an ocean tossing with rows of waves, wear an angry snake on one's head like a flower; but one cannot win over the mind of a fool who has dug in.
verses.line: You can pull a gem from a crocodile's jaws, but you cannot change a mind that has dug in.
verses.misuse: Use it to stop exhausting yourself in arguments, not to write people off.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: The poet looks back on his own youthful arrogance.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं गज इव मदान्धः समभवम् तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः । यदा किञ्चित्किञ्चिद्बुधजनसकाशादवगतम् तदा मूर्खोऽस्मीति ज्वर इव मदो मे व्यपगतः ॥
verses.translation: When I knew a little, I was blind with pride like an elephant in rut, and my mind swelled: 'I know everything.' When, little by little, I learned from the wise, I realised 'I am a fool', and my pride left me like a fever.
verses.line: When I knew a little, I thought I knew everything. Learning from the wise, my fever of pride broke.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of the section on fools.
verses.sanskrit_display: वरं पर्वतदुर्गेषु भ्रान्तं वनचरैः सह । न मूर्खजनसम्पर्कः सुरेन्द्रभवनेष्वपि ॥
verses.translation: Better to wander mountain passes with the creatures of the forest than to keep company with fools, even in the palace of Indra.
verses.line: Better to roam wild hills with animals than to live in a palace among fools.
verses.misuse: About the company you choose to keep, not contempt for people.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning, addressed to proud rulers.
verses.sanskrit_display: हर्तुर्याति न गोचरं किमपि शं पुष्णाति यत् सर्वदा- ऽप्यर्थिभ्यः प्रतिपाद्यमानमनिशं प्राप्नोति वृद्धिं पराम् । कल्पान्तेष्वपि न प्रयाति निधनं विद्याख्यमन्तर्धनं येषां तान् प्रति मानमुज्झत नृपाः कस्तैः सह स्पर्धते ॥
verses.translation: It never comes within a thief's sight; it always nourishes some deep good; given to those who ask, it grows greater; even at the end of an age it does not perish. Kings, drop your pride before those who own this inner wealth called learning. Who can compete with them?
verses.line: Learning is wealth no thief can see. It grows when you give it away and never perishes.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: what fate cannot take.
verses.sanskrit_display: अम्भोजिनीवनविहारविलासमेव हंसस्य हन्ति नितरां कुपितो विधाता । न त्वस्य दुग्धजलभेदविधौ प्रसिद्धां वैदग्ध्यकीर्तिमपहर्तुमसौ समर्थः ॥
verses.translation: An angry Creator may destroy the swan's delight of roaming its lotus pond, but he cannot take away its famous skill of separating milk from water.
verses.line: Fate can take away the swan's lake. It cannot take its gift of telling milk from water.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: the one ornament that lasts.
verses.sanskrit_display: केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वला न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः । वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥
verses.translation: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor necklaces bright as the moon, nor bathing, nor perfume, nor flowers, nor dressed hair. Speech alone, refined and well held, truly adorns a person. Ornaments wear away; the ornament of speech is the real ornament.
verses.line: Jewellery wears out. Well-chosen speech is the one ornament that lasts.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning.
verses.sanskrit_display: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनं विद्या भोगकरी यशस्सुखकरी विद्या गुरूणां गुरुः । विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने विद्या परा देवता विद्या राजसु पूजिता न तु धनं विद्याविहीनः पशुः ॥
verses.translation: Learning is a person's greater beauty, a hidden and guarded treasure. Learning brings enjoyment, fame and happiness; it is the teacher of teachers. In a foreign land learning is your kin; learning is the highest deity. Kings honour learning, not wealth. Without learning a person is little more than an animal.
verses.line: In a foreign land, what you have learned is your family: a treasure no one can see.
verses.misuse: The last phrase is a poet's jab, not a judgement on people without schooling.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: a list of 'if you have this, what need of that'.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षान्तिश्चेत् कवचेन किं किमरिभिः क्रोधोऽस्ति चेद्देहिनां ज्ञातिश्चेदनलेन किं यदि सुहृद् दिव्यौषधैः किं फलम् । किं सर्पैर्यदि दुर्जनाः किमु धनैर्विद्या न वन्द्या यदि व्रीडा चेत्किमु भूषणैः सुकविता यद्यस्ति राज्येन किम् ॥
verses.translation: If you have forbearance, what need of armour? If you have anger, what need of enemies? If you have kinsmen, what need of fire? If a friend, what need of magic medicines? If the wicked are around, what need of snakes? If spotless learning, what need of riches? If modesty, what need of ornaments? If fine poetry, what need of a kingdom?
verses.line: With patience, who needs armour? With anger, who needs enemies? With a true friend, who needs medicine?
verses.misuse: Forbearance protects you; it is not permission for others to keep hurting you.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: on good company.
verses.sanskrit_display: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥
verses.translation: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
verses.line: Good company clears the mind, puts truth in your speech and lifts your spirit. What does it not do?

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: the blessings of a good life.
verses.sanskrit_display: सूनुः सच्चरितः सती प्रियतमा स्वामी प्रसादोन्मुखः स्निग्धं मित्रमवञ्चकः परिजनो निष्क्लेशलेशं मनः । आकारो रुचिरः स्थिरश्च विभवो विद्यावदातं मुखं तुष्टे विष्टपकष्टहारिणि हरौ सम्प्राप्यते देहिना ॥
verses.translation: A son of good conduct, a devoted and loving wife, a gracious master, an affectionate friend, kinsfolk who do not cheat, a mind without a trace of strain, a pleasing form, lasting prosperity, a face bright with learning: these come to the one with whom Hari, remover of the world's troubles, is pleased.
verses.line: A good child, a loving spouse, a kind boss, a true friend, a mind at ease: count these as grace.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: the path every tradition shares.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राणाघातान्निवृत्तिः परधनहरणे संयमः सत्यवाक्यं काले शक्त्या प्रदानं युवतिजनकथामूकभावः परेषाम् । तृष्णास्रोतोविभङ्गो गुरुषु च विनयः सर्वभूतानुकम्पा सामान्यः सर्वशास्त्रेष्वनुपहतविधिः श्रेयसामेष पन्थाः ॥
verses.translation: Refraining from taking life, restraint from seizing others' wealth, truthful speech, timely giving as one is able, silence in gossip about others' wives, breaking the current of craving, humility before elders, compassion for all beings: this is the common path to the good, unbroken in all the scriptures.
verses.line: Harm no one, take nothing that isn't yours, speak truly, give in time, cut craving, be kind to all.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: the three kinds of people.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥
verses.translation: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
verses.line: Some never start for fear of obstacles; some quit when obstacles hit. The best keep going.
verses.misuse: Perseverance is not refusing ever to change course; weigh honestly whether the goal still deserves you.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of the section praising learning: the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
verses.sanskrit_display: असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम् । विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
verses.translation: Do not ask the wicked for favours; do not ask a friend of slender means for money; love a just way of earning; do nothing base even when life is at stake; stand tall in trouble; follow in the footsteps of the great. Who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
verses.line: Don't beg favours from the wicked or money from a struggling friend. Stand tall in hard times.
verses.misuse: 'Even when life is at stake' is the poet's intensity; no principle asks you to harm yourself.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on honour and spirit, contrasting a dog and an elephant.
verses.sanskrit_display: लाङ्गूलचालनमधश्चरणावपातं भूमौ निपत्य वदनोदरदर्शनं च । श्वा पिण्डदस्य कुरुते गजपुङ्गवस्तु धीरं विलोकयति चाटुशतैश्च भुङ्क्ते ॥
verses.translation: The dog wags its tail, falls at the feet of whoever feeds it, rolls on the ground showing its mouth and belly; the lordly elephant looks on steadily and eats only after a hundred coaxing words.
verses.line: The dog grovels before whoever feeds it. The elephant waits with quiet dignity.
verses.misuse: Dignity, not arrogance: it does not mean making others beg you.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: how the world treats someone who has lost money.
verses.sanskrit_display: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥
verses.translation: The same faculties, unimpaired; the same name; the same unclouded mind; the same speech. Yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone else. How strange!
verses.line: Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
verses.misuse: The verse mocks how the world sees you; it does not measure your worth.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: a satire on how money buys reputation.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्यास्ति वित्तं स नरः कुलीनः स पण्डितः स श्रुतवान् गुणज्ञः । स एव वक्ता स च दर्शनीयः सर्वे गुणाः काञ्चनमाश्रयन्ति ॥
verses.translation: Whoever has wealth is well-born, learned, well-read and a judge of merit; he is the eloquent one, the handsome one. All virtues take shelter in gold.
verses.line: Have money and suddenly you are wise, well-born and charming. All virtues seem to lodge in gold.
verses.misuse: Satire on the world's flattery, not advice to chase money.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: how good things are slowly lost.
verses.sanskrit_display: दौर्मन्त्र्यान्नृपतिर्विनश्यति यतिः सङ्गात् सुतो लालनाद् विप्रोऽनध्ययनात् कुलं कुतनयाच्छीलं खलोपासनात् । ह्रीर्मद्यादनवेक्षणादपि कृषिः स्नेहः प्रवासाश्र- यान्मैत्री चाप्रणयात् समृद्धिरनयात् त्यागः प्रमादाद्धनम् ॥
verses.translation: A king is ruined by bad counsel, an ascetic by attachment, a son by spoiling, a brahmin by neglecting study, a family by a wayward son, character by serving the wicked, modesty by drink, farming by neglect, affection by living far away, friendship by lack of warmth, prosperity by bad conduct, and wealth by careless spending.
verses.line: Affection fades with distance, friendship without warmth, wealth with carelessness, a child with spoiling.
verses.misuse: Distance strains affection; it does not doom it. The verse is a call to tend what you love.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth.
verses.sanskrit_display: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥
verses.translation: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
verses.line: Money goes one of three ways: given, enjoyed, or lost. Neither give nor enjoy it, and it is lost.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: how need changes what we value.
verses.sanskrit_display: परिक्षीणः कश्चित्स्पृहयति यवानां प्रसृतये स पश्चात् सम्पूर्णः कलयति धरित्रीं तृणसमाम् । अतश्चानैकान्त्याद्गुरुलघुतयाऽर्थेषु धनिना- मवस्था वस्तूनि प्रथयति च सङ्कोचयति च ॥
verses.translation: A man who has lost everything longs for a handful of barley; later, when full, he counts the whole earth as straw. Because nothing is fixed, a person's condition makes things look great or small.
verses.line: Starving, a handful of grain is everything. Full, the whole earth looks like straw.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth, advice to a ruler on caring for people.
verses.sanskrit_display: राजन् दुधुक्षसि यदि क्षितिधेनुमेतां तेनाद्य वत्समिव लोकममुं पुषाण । तस्मिंश्च सम्यगनिशं परिपोष्यमाणे नानाफलैः फलति कल्पलतेव भूमिः ॥
verses.translation: O king, if you wish to milk this cow, the earth, first nourish the people as one feeds the calf. When they are well and constantly cared for, the earth bears every kind of fruit, like a wish-granting vine.
verses.line: Want results from your people? Nourish them first, as you feed the calf before milking.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: on keeping your dignity before the rich.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्धात्रा निजभालपट्टलिखितं स्तोकं महद्वा धनं तत् प्राप्नोति मरुस्थलेऽपि नितरां मेरौ ततो नाधिकम् । तद्धीरो भव वित्तवत्सु कृपणां वृत्तिं वृथा मा कृथाः कूपे पश्य पयोनिधावपि घटो गृह्णाति तुल्यं जलम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever wealth, small or great, the Creator has written on your forehead, you will get it even in a desert, and no more even on Mount Meru. So be steady; do not play the beggar before the rich for nothing. Look: a pot draws the same water from a well as from the ocean.
verses.line: A pot draws the same water from a well or the ocean. Keep your dignity before the rich.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to stop working or asking for fair pay; a reason not to grovel.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: The poet to the chataka, a bird said to drink only raindrops from clouds.
verses.sanskrit_display: रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयताम् अम्भोदा बहवो वसन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैकादृशाः । केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति धरणीं गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः ॥
verses.translation: Friend chataka, listen carefully for a moment. Many clouds live in the sky, but not all are alike. Some drench the earth with rain; some only thunder for nothing. Do not speak pleading words before every cloud you see.
verses.line: Some clouds bring rain, some only thunder. Don't plead with everyone you meet.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked.
verses.sanskrit_display: दुर्जनः परिहर्तव्यो विद्ययालङ्कृतोऽपि सन् । मणिना भूषितः सर्पः किमसौ न भयङ्करः ॥
verses.translation: A wicked person should be avoided, even if adorned with learning. Is a snake any less frightening because it wears a jewel?
verses.line: Avoid a cruel person even if brilliant. A snake wearing a jewel still bites.
verses.misuse: It means keeping distance from people who harm you, not labelling everyone who annoys you.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: how spite twists every virtue.
verses.sanskrit_display: जाड्यं ह्रीमति गण्यते व्रतरुचौ दम्भः शुचौ कैतवं शूरे निर्घृणता मुनौ विमतिता दैन्यं प्रियालापिनि । तेजस्विन्यवलिप्तता मुखरता वक्तर्यशक्तिः स्थिरे तत्को नाम गुणो भवेत्स गुणिनां यो दुर्जनैर्नाङ्कितः ॥
verses.translation: The modest are called dull; the devout, hypocrites; the pure, frauds; the brave, heartless; the thoughtful sage, a fool; the gentle speaker, servile; the spirited, arrogant; the eloquent, a chatterbox; the steady, weak. What virtue of the virtuous has the wicked not smeared?
verses.line: To a spiteful critic, modesty is dullness and courage is cruelty. No virtue escapes them.
verses.misuse: Not every criticism is spite; use it to stop taking malice personally, not to ignore fair feedback.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: what makes other things unnecessary.
verses.sanskrit_display: लोभश्चेदगुणेन किं पिशुनता यद्यस्ति किं पातकैः सत्यं चेत्तपसा च किं शुचि मनो यद्यस्ति तीर्थेन किम् । सौजन्यं यदि किं गुणैः सुमहिमा यद्यस्ति किं मण्डनैः सद्विद्या यदि किं धनैरपयशो यद्यस्ति किं मृत्युना ॥
verses.translation: If there is greed, what need of other faults? If backbiting, what need of other sins? If truth, what need of austerity? If a pure mind, what need of pilgrimage? If goodness of heart, what need of other virtues? If greatness, what need of ornaments? If true learning, what need of wealth? If disgrace, what need of death?
verses.line: If your mind is pure, what need of pilgrimage? If you speak truth, what need of penance?
verses.misuse: 'Disgrace is worse than death' is old rhetoric about honour, never a reason to harm yourself.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: on rulers ruled by temper.
verses.sanskrit_display: न कश्चिच्चण्डकोपानामात्मीयो नाम भूभुजाम् । होतारमपि जुह्वानं स्पृष्टो दहति पावकः ॥
verses.translation: Rulers with fierce tempers have no one close to them. Fire burns even the priest who feeds it offerings.
verses.line: Fire burns even the hand that feeds it. A raging temper keeps no one close.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: the impossible position of anyone who serves a master.
verses.sanskrit_display: मौनान्मूकः प्रवचनपटुर्वातुलो जल्पको वा धृष्टः पार्श्वे वसति च सदा दूरतश्चाप्रगल्भः । क्षान्त्या भीरुर्यदि न सहते प्रायशो नाभिजातः सेवाधर्मः परमगहनो योगिनामप्यगम्यः ॥
verses.translation: Keep quiet and you are dumb; speak well and you are a babbler or a windbag; stay close and you are pushy; keep away and you lack confidence; be patient and you are a coward; refuse to put up with things and you are ill-bred. The duty of serving another is deep indeed, beyond the reach even of yogis.
verses.line: Quiet, you're dull; talkative, a show-off; patient, weak. Serving a boss is harder than yoga.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: two kinds of friendship.
verses.sanskrit_display: आरम्भगुर्वी क्षयिणी क्रमेण लघ्वी पुरा वृद्धिमती च पश्चात् । दिनस्य पूर्वार्धपरार्धभिन्ना छायेव मैत्री खलसज्जनानाम् ॥
verses.translation: Large at the start and shrinking bit by bit, or slight at first and growing afterwards: like the shade of a day's first and second halves is the friendship of the wicked and of the good.
verses.line: Bad friendships start big and shrink. Good ones start small and keep growing, like afternoon shade.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the good: a portrait of the people worth bowing to.
verses.sanskrit_display: वाञ्छा सज्जनसङ्गमे परगुणे प्रीतिर्गुरौ नम्रता विद्यायां व्यसनं स्वयोषिति रतिर्लोकापवादाद्भयम् । भक्तिः शूलिनि शक्तिरात्मदमने संसर्गमुक्तिः खले येष्वेते निवसन्ति निर्मलगुणास्तेभ्यो नरेभ्यो नमः ॥
verses.translation: A longing for good company, delight in others' merits, humility before a teacher, a passion for learning, love for one's own wife, fear of public disgrace, devotion to Shiva, the strength to master oneself, freedom from bad company: I bow to the people in whom these pure qualities live.
verses.line: Seek good company, delight in others' gifts, love learning, master yourself: bow to such people.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the good: the nature of great souls.
verses.sanskrit_display: विपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा सदसि वाक्पटुता युधि विक्रमः । यशसि चाभिरुचिर्व्यसनं श्रुतौ प्रकृतिसिद्धमिदं हि महात्मनाम् ॥
verses.translation: Steadiness in misfortune, forbearance in success, eloquence in the assembly, courage in battle, a love of good name, a passion for learning: these come naturally to great souls.
verses.line: Steady in bad times, forbearing in good ones, eloquent among people, eager to learn: that is greatness.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the good: the second 'sword's-edge vow'.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
verses.translation: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
verses.line: Give in secret, stay quiet about your favours, praise others' help aloud, stay humble in wealth.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the good.
verses.sanskrit_display: सम्पत्सु महतां चित्तं भवत्युत्पलकोमलम् । आपत्सु च महाशैलशिलासङ्घातकर्कशम् ॥
verses.translation: In prosperity the heart of the great becomes soft as a lotus; in adversity, hard as a mass of mountain rock.
verses.line: In good times be soft as a lotus. In hard times be firm as mountain rock.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the good: how company shapes character.
verses.sanskrit_display: सन्तप्तायसि संस्थितस्य पयसो नामापि न ज्ञायते मुक्ताकारतया तदेव नलिनीपत्रस्थितं राजते । स्वात्यां सागरशुक्तिमध्यपतितं तन्मौक्तिकं जायते प्रायेणाधममध्यमोत्तमगुणः संसर्गतो जायते ॥
verses.translation: Water on red-hot iron leaves not even a name behind; the same water on a lotus leaf shines like a pearl; fallen into a sea oyster under the Svati star, it becomes a pearl. As a rule, low, middling or high qualities come from the company one keeps.
verses.line: One drop vanishes on hot iron, shines on a lotus leaf, becomes a pearl in a shell. Company shapes us.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the good: three rare blessings.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रीणाति यः सुचरितैः पितरं स पुत्रो यद्भर्तुरेव हितमिच्छति तत् कलत्रम् । तन्मित्रमापदि सुखे च समक्रियं यद् एतत् त्रयं जगति पुण्यकृतो लभन्ते ॥
verses.translation: He is a son who pleases his father by good conduct; she is a wife who wishes only her husband's good; that is a friend who is the same in trouble and in happiness. Only those who have done good obtain these three in the world.
verses.line: A true friend is the same in your troubles as in your good times.
verses.misuse: The verse's picture of a wife is one-sided; the card uses only the line on friendship.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of the section on the good.
verses.sanskrit_display: नम्रत्वेनोन्नमन्तः परगुणकथनैः स्वान् गुणान् ख्यापयन्तः स्वार्थान् सम्पादयन्तो विततपृथुतरारम्भयत्नाः परार्थे । क्षान्त्यैवाक्षेपरुक्षाक्षरमुखरमुखान् दुर्जनान् दूषयन्तः सन्तः साश्चर्यचर्या जगति बहुमताः कस्य नाभ्यर्चनीयाः ॥
verses.translation: Rising by bowing low, making their own virtues known by speaking of others', achieving their own aims by working hard for others, shaming slanderers whose mouths are full of harsh words simply by their patience: the good, whose conduct is a wonder, are honoured in the world. Who would not revere them?
verses.line: They rise by bowing, show their worth by praising others, and silence slanderers with patience.
verses.misuse: Patience with slander is strength; it does not mean staying silent about abuse.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Opening verse of the section on helping others.
verses.sanskrit_display: भवन्ति नम्रास्तरवः फलोद्गमै- र्नवाम्बुभिर्दूरविलम्बिनो घनाः । अनुद्धताः सत्पुरुषाः समृद्धिभिः स्वभाव एवैष परोपकारिणाम् ॥
verses.translation: Trees bow low with fruit; clouds hang low with new rain; the good are not puffed up by prosperity. This is the very nature of those who help others.
verses.line: Fruit-laden trees bow low. The truly successful are not puffed up.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on helping others: true ornaments.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रोत्रं श्रुतेनैव न कुण्डलेन दानेन पाणिर्न तु कङ्कणेन । विभाति कायः करुणापराणां परोपकारैर्न तु चन्दनेन ॥
verses.translation: The ear is beautiful through learning, not earrings; the hand through giving, not bracelets; the body of the compassionate shines through helping others, not through sandal paste.
verses.line: Ears shine by listening, hands by giving, the body by helping others, not by ornaments.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on helping others: the marks of a true friend.
verses.sanskrit_display: पापान्निवारयति योजयते हिताय गुह्यं निगूहति गुणान् प्रकटीकरोति । आपद्गतं च न जहाति ददाति काले सन्मित्रलक्षणमिदं निगदन्ति सन्तः ॥
verses.translation: He keeps you from wrong and steers you to what is good; he guards your secrets and makes your good qualities known; he does not leave you in trouble and gives when it is needed. The good call these the marks of a true friend.
verses.line: A true friend stops you doing wrong, keeps your secrets, praises you, and stays when trouble comes.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on helping others: four kinds of people.
verses.sanskrit_display: एते सत्पुरुषाः परार्थघटकाः स्वार्थं परित्यज्य ये सामान्यास्तु परार्थमुद्यमभृतः स्वार्थाविरोधेन ये । तेऽमी मानवराक्षसाः परहितं स्वार्थाय विघ्नन्ति ये ये विघ्नन्ति निरर्थकं परहितं ते के न जानीमहे ॥
verses.translation: Good people serve others' interests, setting their own aside. Ordinary people work for others so long as it does not clash with their own interest. Those who wreck others' good for their own gain are demons in human form. But those who wreck others' good for no gain at all: what to call them, we do not know.
verses.line: Some help at their own cost, some when convenient, some harm for gain. Some harm for nothing at all.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on helping others: a parable of milk and water.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षीरेणात्मगतोदकाय हि गुणा दत्ताः पुरा तेऽखिलाः क्षीरोत्तापमवेक्ष्य तेन पयसा स्वात्मा कृशाणौ हुतः । गन्तुं पावकमुन्मनस्तदभवद् दृष्ट्वा तु मित्रापदं युक्तं तेन जलेन शाम्यति सतां मैत्री पुनस्त्वीदृशी ॥
verses.translation: Milk gave all its qualities to the water that joined it. Seeing the milk being heated, the water offered itself into the fire. Seeing its friend in danger, the milk rose up to follow it into the fire, and settled only when joined with water again. Such is the friendship of the good.
verses.line: Milk boils over to follow water into the fire, and settles when water returns. That is friendship.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on helping others: how the good behave.
verses.sanskrit_display: तृष्णां छिन्धि भज क्षमां जहि मदं पापे रतिं मा कृथाः सत्यं ब्रूह्यनुयाहि साधुपदवीं सेवस्व विद्वज्जनम् । मान्यान् मानय विद्विषोऽप्यनुनय प्रख्यापय प्रश्रयं कीर्तिं पालय दुःखिते कुरु दयामेतत् सतां चेष्टितम् ॥
verses.translation: Cut off craving, practise forbearance, give up arrogance, take no delight in wrong, speak the truth, follow the path of the good, serve the wise, honour those worthy of honour, win over even your enemies, show courtesy, guard your good name, be kind to those in pain: this is how the good behave.
verses.line: Cut craving, forgive, drop arrogance, speak truth, win over even enemies, be kind to those suffering.
verses.misuse: Winning over an enemy is not the same as tolerating harm.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on helping others.
verses.sanskrit_display: मनसि वचसि काये पुण्यपीयूषपूर्णाः त्रिभुवनमुपकारश्रेणिभिः प्रीणयन्तः । परगुणपरमाणून् पर्वतीकृत्य नित्यं निजहृदि विकसन्तः सन्ति सन्तः कियन्तः ॥
verses.translation: Full of the nectar of goodness in mind, speech and body, delighting the three worlds with a stream of kindnesses, always turning the tiniest atom of merit in others into a mountain and blossoming in their own hearts: how many such good people are there?
verses.line: How rare are those who make a mountain out of the smallest good in others.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Opening verse of the section on steadfastness, recalling the churning of the ocean.
verses.sanskrit_display: रत्नैर्महार्हैस्तुतुषुर्न देवा न भेजिरे भीमविषेण भीतिम् । सुधां विना न प्रययुर्विरामं न निश्चितार्थाद्विरमन्ति धीराः ॥
verses.translation: The gods were not satisfied by priceless jewels, nor frightened off by the terrible poison; they did not rest until they had the nectar. The steadfast do not stop short of what they have set out to do.
verses.line: The gods churned past jewels and past poison until they reached nectar. The steady don't stop halfway.
verses.misuse: Steadiness is not refusing to reassess a goal.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on steadfastness.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्वचित् पृथ्वीशय्यः क्वचिदपि च पर्यङ्कशयनः क्वचिच्छाकाहारः क्वचिदपि च शाल्योदनरुचिः । क्वचित् कण्ठाधारी क्वचिदपि च दिव्याम्बरधरो मनस्वी कार्यार्थी न गणयति च दुःखं न च सुखम् ॥
verses.translation: Sometimes he sleeps on the ground, sometimes on a couch; sometimes he lives on greens, sometimes on fine rice; sometimes he wears rags, sometimes heavenly garments. A person of spirit set on a purpose counts neither hardship nor comfort.
verses.line: Floor or bed, greens or fine rice, rags or silk: someone set on a goal counts neither.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on steadfastness: what truly adorns each strength.
verses.sanskrit_display: ऐश्वर्यस्य विभूषणं सुजनता शौर्यस्य वाक्संयमो ज्ञानस्योपशमः श्रुतस्य विनयो वित्तस्य पात्रे व्ययः । अक्रोधस्तपसः क्षमा प्रभवितुर्धर्मस्य निर्व्याजता सर्वेषामपि सर्वकारणमिदं शीलं परं भूषणम् ॥
verses.translation: Courtesy is the ornament of power; restraint in speech, of valour; calm, of knowledge; humility, of learning; giving to the deserving, of wealth; freedom from anger, of austerity; forbearance, of those in authority; sincerity, of dharma. But character, the root of all these, is the highest ornament.
verses.line: Courtesy adorns power, humility adorns learning, calm adorns knowledge. Character adorns everything.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on steadfastness.
verses.sanskrit_display: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verses.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verses.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on steadfastness.
verses.sanskrit_display: पातितोऽपि कराघातैरुत्पतत्येव कन्दुकः । प्रायेण साधुवृत्तनामस्थायिन्यो विपत्तयः ॥
verses.translation: A ball struck down by the hand flies right back up. As a rule, the misfortunes of those who live rightly do not last.
verses.line: A ball knocked down bounces back up. For good people, setbacks rarely last.
verses.misuse: Not a promise that suffering is always short, or that people who suffer long did something wrong.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on steadfastness.
verses.sanskrit_display: आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महारिपुः । नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः कुर्वाणो नावसीदति ॥
verses.translation: Laziness is the great enemy that lives in a person's own body. There is no friend like effort; one who works does not sink.
verses.line: Laziness is the enemy living in your own body. There is no friend like effort.
verses.misuse: Rest is not laziness; burnout needs rest, not more effort.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of the section on steadfastness.
verses.sanskrit_display: छिन्नोऽपि रोहति तरुश्चन्द्रः क्षीणोऽपि वर्धते लोके । इति विमृशन्तः सन्तः सन्तप्यन्ते न लोकेऽस्मिन् ॥
verses.translation: A tree that is cut grows again; the waning moon waxes again in the world. Reflecting on this, the good are not tormented in this world.
verses.line: A cut tree grows back; the waning moon fills again. Remembering this, the wise do not despair.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on fate: the verse that keeps choice alive.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्मायत्तं फलं पुंसां बुद्धिः कर्मानुसारिणी । तथापि सुधिया भाव्यं सुविचार्यैव कुर्वता ॥
verses.translation: The fruit a person reaps depends on past actions, and even the mind follows one's actions. Even so, a wise person should act only after careful thought.
verses.line: Much is shaped by past actions. Still, think carefully before you act.
verses.misuse: Karma is not a reason to stop choosing well; the verse's own point is the second line.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on fate: a lament when a good person is lost too soon.
verses.sanskrit_display: सृजति तावदशेषगुणाकरं पुरुषरत्नमलङ्करणं भुवः । तदपि तत्क्षणभङ्गि करोति चेदहह कष्टमपण्डितता विधेः ॥
verses.translation: The Creator fashions a jewel of a person, a mine of every virtue, an ornament to the earth, and then, if he makes him perish in a moment, alas! what folly in the Creator!
verses.line: Fate shapes a person full of every goodness, then takes them in a moment. Alas, what folly.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Opening verse of the section on action, answering the section on fate.
verses.sanskrit_display: नमस्यामो देवान्ननु हतविधेस्तेऽपि वशगा विधिर्वन्द्यः सोऽपि प्रतिनियतकर्मैकफलदः । फलं कर्मायत्तं यदि किममरैः किञ्च विधिना नमस्तत्कर्मभ्यो विधिरपि न येभ्यः प्रभवति ॥
verses.translation: We bow to the gods, but they are under fate's control. Fate deserves worship, but it only gives the fruit of fixed actions. If the fruit depends on action, what of the gods, what of fate? Salutations to actions themselves, over which even fate has no power.
verses.line: Even fate only delivers the fruit of actions. Bow to what you do.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on action.
verses.sanskrit_display: गुणवदगुणवद्वा कुर्वता कार्यजातं परिणतिरवधार्या यत्नतः पण्डितेन । अतिरभसकृतानां कर्मणामाविपत्ते- र्भवति हृदयदाही शल्यतुल्यो विपाकः ॥
verses.translation: Whether a task is good or bad, a wise person should first carefully weigh its outcome. The result of deeds done in great haste burns the heart like a thorn until one's dying day.
verses.line: Weigh the outcome before you act. Rash deeds leave a thorn that burns for years.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on action: on what is not in our hands.
verses.sanskrit_display: मज्जत्वम्भसि यातु मेरुशिखरं शत्रून् जयत्वावहे वाणिज्यं कृषिसेवने च सकला विद्याः कलाः शिक्षताम् । आकाशं विपुलं प्रयातु खगवत्कृत्वा प्रयत्नं परं नाभाव्यं भवतीह कर्मवशतो भाव्यस्य नाशः कुतः ॥
verses.translation: Let a man dive into the sea, climb to the peak of Meru, conquer his enemies in battle, learn trade, farming, service and every art and science, fly across the vast sky like a bird with all his effort: what is not to be will not happen, by the force of karma, and how can what is to be fail?
verses.line: Dive deep, climb high, master every skill: what is not meant to be still will not happen.
verses.misuse: Show with the verse on effort (Niti 86). This is for letting go after trying, not for not trying.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on action: a riddle of questions and answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: को लाभो गुणिसङ्गमः किमसुखं प्राज्ञेतरैः सङ्गतिः का हानिः समयच्युतिर्निपुणता का धर्मतत्त्वे रतिः । कः शूरो विजितेन्द्रियः प्रियतमा कानुव्रता किं धनं विद्या किं सुखमप्रवासगमनं राज्यं किमाज्ञाफलम् ॥
verses.translation: What is gain? The company of the virtuous. What is sorrow? The company of fools. What is loss? Missing the right moment. What is skill? Love for the heart of dharma. Who is a hero? One who has mastered the senses. Who is a beloved? A faithful wife. What is wealth? Learning. What is happiness? Not having to live abroad. What is a kingdom? Having one's word obeyed.
verses.line: What is real loss? Missing your moment. Who is a hero? One who has mastered himself.
verses.misuse: 'Happiness is not living abroad' voices homesickness; it is not a verdict on emigrants.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on action.
verses.sanskrit_display: अप्रियवचनदरिद्रैः प्रियवचनाढ्यैः स्वदारपरितुष्टैः । परपरिवादनिवृत्तैः क्वचित्क्वचिन्मण्डिता वसुधा ॥
verses.translation: Only here and there is the earth adorned by people poor in harsh words and rich in kind ones, content with their own spouses, who keep away from speaking ill of others.
verses.line: The world is lit, here and there, by people poor in harsh words and rich in kind ones.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on action.
verses.sanskrit_display: कदर्थितस्यापि हि धैर्यवृत्तेर्न शक्यते धैर्यगुणः प्रमार्ष्टुम् । अधोमुखस्यापि कृतस्य वह्नेर्नाधः शिखा याति कदाचिदेव ॥
verses.translation: Even when harassed, the steadfast cannot be robbed of their steadiness. Hold a torch upside down: its flame never points downward.
verses.line: Turn a torch upside down and its flame still rises. Steadiness survives humiliation.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on action: who truly conquers.
verses.sanskrit_display: कान्ताकटाक्षविशिखा न लुनन्ति यस्य चित्तं न निर्दहति कोपकृशानुतापः । कर्षन्ति भूरिविषयाश्च न लोभपाशै- र्लोकत्रयं जयति कृत्स्नमिदं स धीरः ॥
verses.translation: One whose mind is not cut by the arrow-glances of a beloved, not scorched by the burning fire of anger, not dragged by the many senses with nooses of greed: that steady person conquers all three worlds.
verses.line: Whoever isn't burned by anger or dragged by greed has conquered the whole world.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the opening section, 'Censure of Craving': the poet addresses his own craving.
verses.sanskrit_display: उत्खातं निधिशङ्कया क्षितितलं ध्माता गिरेर्धातवो निस्तीर्णः सरितां पतिर्नृपतयो यत्नेन संतोषिताः । मन्त्राराधनतत्परेण मनसा नीताः श्मशाने निशाः प्राप्तः काणवराटकोऽपि न मया तृष्णे सकामा भव ॥
verses.translation: I dug up the earth hoping for treasure, smelted the ores of mountains, crossed the ocean, lord of rivers, worked hard to please kings, spent nights in cremation grounds with my mind fixed on mantras, and I did not get even a broken cowrie. Craving, be satisfied now!
verses.line: I dug, sailed, flattered kings, chased every scheme, and gained not a broken coin. Enough, craving.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Censure of Craving': the poet to his own hope.
verses.sanskrit_display: खलालापाः सोढाः कथमपि तदाराधनपरैः निगृह्यान्तर्बाष्पं हसितमपि शून्येन मनसा । कृतो वित्तस्तम्भप्रतिहतधियामञ्जलिरपि त्वमाशे मोघाशे किमपरमतो नर्तयसि माम् ॥
verses.translation: I somehow put up with the taunts of the wicked while trying to please them; I held back my tears and laughed with an empty heart; I folded my hands even before people whose minds were numbed by money. Hope, futile hope, how much more will you make me dance?
verses.line: I swallowed insults and forced laughter with an empty heart. Hope, how much longer will you make me dance?

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Censure of Craving': doing the right things for the wrong reasons.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षान्तं न क्षमया गृहोचितसुखं त्यक्तं न संतोषतः सोढा दुःसहशीतवाततपनक्लेशा न तप्तं तपः । ध्यातं वित्तमहर्निशं नियमितप्राणैर्न शम्भोः पदं तत्तत्कर्म कृतं यदेव मुनिभिस्तैस्तैः फलैर्वञ्चिताः ॥
verses.translation: We forgave, but not out of forgiveness; we gave up home comforts, but not out of contentment; we bore unbearable cold, wind and heat, but not as austerity; we thought of money day and night with held breath, not of Shiva's feet. We did every act the sages did, and were cheated of every one of their fruits.
verses.line: We forgave, but not out of forgiveness; gave up comforts, but not out of contentment, and missed the fruit.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Censure of Craving'; the most quoted verse of the Vairagyashatakam.
verses.sanskrit_display: भोगा न भुक्ता वयमेव भुक्ताः तपो न तप्तं वयमेव तप्ताः । कालो न यातो वयमेव याता- स्तृष्णा न जीर्णा वयमेव जीर्णाः ॥
verses.translation: We did not enjoy pleasures; pleasures consumed us. We did not perform austerity; we were scorched. Time did not pass; we passed. Craving did not grow old; we grew old.
verses.line: We didn't enjoy pleasures; they consumed us. Time didn't pass; we did. Craving never aged; we did.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Censure of Craving'.
verses.sanskrit_display: वलीभिर्मुखमाक्रान्तं पलितेनाङ्कितं शिरः । गात्राणि शिथिलायन्ते तृष्णैका तरुणायते ॥
verses.translation: The face is overrun by wrinkles, the head marked with grey, the limbs grow slack; craving alone grows young.
verses.line: Wrinkles on the face, grey in the hair, slack limbs. Only craving stays young.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Censure of Craving': old age and the fear of death.
verses.sanskrit_display: निवृत्ता भोगेच्छा पुरुषबहुमानोऽपि गलितः समानाः स्वर्याताः सपदि सुहृदो जीवितसमाः । शनैर्यष्ट्युत्थानं घनतिमिररुद्धे च नयने अहो मूढः कायस्तदपि मरणापायचकितः ॥
verses.translation: The wish for pleasures has gone; the respect people paid us has melted away; our peers have gone to heaven, and friends dear as life are quickly following; we rise slowly with a stick, our eyes clouded with darkness; and still, foolish body, it startles at the approach of death!
verses.line: Friends gone, eyes dim, rising with a stick, and still the body flinches at the thought of death.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of 'Censure of Craving'.
verses.sanskrit_display: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥
verses.translation: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verses.line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: The mockery of giving up pleasures
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'The Mockery of Giving Up Pleasures'.
verses.sanskrit_display: अवश्यं यातारश्चिरतरमुषित्वापि विषया वियोगे को भेदस्त्यजति न जनो यत्स्वयममून् । व्रजन्तः स्वातन्त्र्यादतुलपरितापाय मनसः स्वयं त्यक्ता ह्येते शमसुखमनन्तं विदधति ॥
verses.translation: Pleasures will certainly leave, however long they stay with us. Then what difference is there in parting? Only that people do not let them go themselves. Leaving of their own accord, they bring the mind unequalled torment; given up by oneself, they bring endless peace.
verses.line: Every pleasure leaves someday. Released freely, it brings peace; torn away, it brings torment.
verses.misuse: About things and pleasures; not advice to leave people before they leave you.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: The mockery of giving up pleasures
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'The Mockery of Giving Up Pleasures'.
verses.sanskrit_display: अजानन्दाहात्म्यं पततु शलभस्तीव्रदहने स मीनोऽप्यज्ञानाद्वडिशयुतमश्नातु पिशितम् । विजानन्तोऽप्येते वयमिह विपज्जालजटिलान् न मुञ्चामः कामानहह गहनो मोहमहिमा ॥
verses.translation: Let the moth fall into the blazing flame not knowing that it burns; let the fish swallow the bait not knowing the hook. But we, knowing full well, still do not let go of desires tangled in a net of dangers. Ah, how deep is the power of delusion!
verses.line: The moth doesn't know the flame burns. We know, and still we don't let go.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: The mockery of giving up pleasures
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'The Mockery of Giving Up Pleasures': what we call happiness.
verses.sanskrit_display: तृषा शुष्यत्यास्ये पिबति सलिलं शीतमधुरं क्षुधार्तः शाल्यान्नं कवलयति मांसादिकलितम् । प्रदीप्ते कामाग्नौ सुदृढतरमालिङ्गति वधूं प्रतीकारं व्याधेः सुखमिति विपर्यस्यति जनः ॥
verses.translation: When the mouth dries with thirst, one drinks cool sweet water; pained by hunger, one gobbles rice with meat and the rest; when the fire of desire flares, one holds a woman close. People mistake the cure of a disease for happiness.
verses.line: Drinking when thirsty is relief, not joy. We mistake easing a craving for happiness.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of begging and servility
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Censure of Begging': why a proud man swallows his pride.
verses.sanskrit_display: दीना दीनमुखैः सदैव शिशुकैराकृष्टजीर्णाम्बरा क्रोशद्भिः क्षुधितैर्निरन्नविधुरा दृश्या न चेद्गेहिनी । याञ्चाभङ्गभयेन गद्गदगलत्त्रुट्यद्विलीनाक्षरं को देहीति वदेत्स्वदग्धजठरस्यार्थे मनस्वी पुमान् ॥
verses.translation: If he did not have to see his wife, wretched, her worn clothes tugged by little children with pinched faces crying with hunger, the household without food, what self-respecting man would say 'give', his throat choking with fear of refusal and his words breaking and fading, for the sake of his own wretched belly?
verses.line: A proud man would never beg for himself. For his hungry family, he swallows his pride.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of begging and servility
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Censure of Begging'.
verses.sanskrit_display: ये सन्तोषनिरन्तरप्रमुदितास्तेषां न भिन्ना मुदो ये त्वन्ये धनलुब्धसंकुलधियस्तेषां न तृष्णा हता । इत्थं कस्य कृते कृतः स विधिना कीदृक्पदं सम्पदां स्वात्मन्येव समाप्तहेममहिमा मेरुर्न मे रोचते ॥
verses.translation: Those always delighted by contentment have joy that is undivided; the others, minds crowded with greed for money, never kill their craving. So for whom did fate make wealth, and what kind of place is it? Mount Meru, whose golden glory ends in itself, does not appeal to me.
verses.line: The contented already have their joy; the greedy never quench their thirst. Who is wealth really for?

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the instability of pleasures
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Opening verse of 'On the Instability of Pleasures'.
verses.sanskrit_display: भोगे रोगभयं कुले च्युतिभयं वित्ते नृपालाद्भयं माने दैन्यभयं बले रिपुभयं रूपे जराया भयम् । शास्त्रे वादिभयं गुणे खलभयं काये कृतान्ताद्भयं सर्वं वस्तु भयान्वितं भुवि नृणां वैराग्यमेवाभयम् ॥
verses.translation: In pleasure lies the fear of disease; in high birth, the fear of a fall; in wealth, fear of the king; in honour, fear of humiliation; in strength, fear of enemies; in beauty, fear of old age; in learning, fear of rival debaters; in virtue, fear of the wicked; in the body, fear of death. Everything in this world carries fear; only dispassion is fearless.
verses.line: Wealth fears loss, fame fears disgrace, beauty fears age. Only letting go is free of fear.
verses.misuse: Dispassion is not giving up on life; it is holding things without clutching.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the instability of pleasures
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Instability of Pleasures'.
verses.sanskrit_display: आधिव्याधिशतैर्जनस्य विविधैरारोग्यमुन्मूल्यते लक्ष्मीर्यत्र पतन्ति तत्र विवृतद्वारा इव व्यापदः । जातं जातमवश्यमाशु विवशं मृत्युः करोत्यात्मसात् तत्किं तेन निरङ्कुशेन विधिना यन्निर्मितं सुस्थिरम् ॥
verses.translation: Health is uprooted by hundreds of worries and illnesses of every kind; where fortune arrives, disasters rush in after it as though through open doors; death quickly and helplessly makes everything born its own. What has this unchecked fate made that is stable?
verses.line: Illness, setbacks, loss: what has fate ever made that lasts?

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the instability of pleasures
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Instability of Pleasures'.
verses.sanskrit_display: भोगा मेघवितानमध्यविलसत्सौदामिनीचञ्चला आयुर्वायुविघट्टिताब्जपटलीलीनाम्बुवद्भङ्गुरम् । लोला यौवनलालसास्तनुभृतामित्याकलय्य द्रुतं योगे धैर्यसमाधिसिद्धसुलभे बुद्धिं विधध्वं बुधाः ॥
verses.translation: Pleasures flicker like lightning playing in a canopy of clouds; life is as fragile as water clinging to wind-tossed lotus leaves; the longings of youth are fickle. Knowing this, wise ones, quickly set your minds on yoga, which steadiness and stillness make easy to attain.
verses.line: Pleasures flash like lightning; life trembles like water on a lotus leaf. Turn inward soon.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the instability of pleasures
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Instability of Pleasures'.
verses.sanskrit_display: आयुः कल्लोललोलं कतिपयदिवसस्थायिनी यौवनश्रीः अर्थाः संकल्पकल्पा घनसमयतडिद्विभ्रमा भोगपूगाः । कण्ठाश्लेषोपगूढं तदपि च न चिरं यत्प्रियाभिः प्रणीतं ब्रह्मण्यासक्तचित्ता भवत भवभयाम्बोधिपारं तरीतुम् ॥
verses.translation: Life is restless as a wave; the glow of youth lasts a few days; wealth is as fleeting as a thought; pleasures flash like monsoon lightning; even the embrace of loved ones round the neck does not last long. Set your mind on Brahman to cross the ocean of worldly fear.
verses.line: Life is a wave, youth a few days, money a passing thought. Even embraces end.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the instability of pleasures
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Instability of Pleasures'.
verses.sanskrit_display: व्याघ्रीव तिष्ठति जरा परितर्जयन्ती रोगाश्च शत्रव इव प्रहरन्ति देहम् । आयुः परिस्रवति भिन्नघटादिवाम्भो लोकस्तथाप्यहितमाचरतीति चित्रम् ॥
verses.translation: Old age crouches like a tigress, snarling; diseases strike the body like enemies; life leaks away like water from a cracked pot; and still people do harm. How strange!
verses.line: Life leaks away like water from a cracked pot, and still we spend it hurting each other.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Opening verse of 'On the Greatness of Time'.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा रम्या नगरी महान्स नृपतिः सामन्तचक्रं च तत् पार्श्वे तस्य च सा विदग्धपरिषत्ताश्चन्द्रबिम्बाननाः । उद्वृत्तः स च राजपुत्रनिवहस्ते बन्दिनस्ताः कथाः सर्वं यस्य वशादगात्स्मृतिपथं कालाय तस्मै नमः ॥
verses.translation: That lovely city, that great king, that circle of vassals at his side, that learned court, those moon-faced women, that proud crowd of princes, those bards and their tales: all of it has passed into memory by Time's power. Salutations to that Time.
verses.line: That city, that king, that court, those stories: all of it now only memory. Bow to Time.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Greatness of Time'.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्रानेकः क्वचिदपि गृहे तत्र तिष्ठत्यथैको यत्राप्येकस्तदनु बहवस्तत्र नैकोऽपि चान्ते । इत्थं नेयौ रजनिदिवसौ लोलयन्द्वाविवाक्षौ कालः कल्यो भुवनफलके क्रीडति प्राणिशारैः ॥
verses.translation: Where there were many in a house, one remains; where there was one, many come, and in the end not even one. So Time, rolling night and day like a pair of dice, plays on the board of the world with living beings as its pieces.
verses.line: A full house, then one person, then many, then no one. Time plays dice with our lives.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Greatness of Time'.
verses.sanskrit_display: आदित्यस्य गतागतैरहरहः संक्षीयते जीवितं व्यापारैर्बहुकार्यभारगुरुभिः कालोऽपि न ज्ञायते । दृष्ट्वा जन्मजराविपत्तिमरणं त्रासश्च नोत्पद्यते पीत्वा मोहमयीं प्रमादमदिरामुन्मत्तभूतं जगत् ॥
verses.translation: With the sun's coming and going, life shrinks day by day; with business heavy with many tasks, we do not notice time passing; seeing birth, age, misfortune and death, we feel no alarm. The world has drunk the wine of heedlessness and gone mad.
verses.line: Each sunrise takes a day from us, and, busy with work, we never notice time slipping by.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Greatness of Time'.
verses.sanskrit_display: रात्रिः सैव पुनः स एव दिवसो मत्वा मुधा जन्तवो धावन्त्युद्यमिनस्तथैव निभृतप्रारब्धतत्तत्क्रियाः । व्यापारैः पुनरुक्तभूत विषयैरित्थंविधेनामुना संसारेण कदर्थिता वयमहो मोहान्न लज्जामहे ॥
verses.translation: Thinking 'it is the same night again, the same day', creatures run about in vain, busy as ever with the tasks they have set going; with work full of the same repeated things, tormented by this round of existence, alas, out of delusion we feel no shame.
verses.line: Same night, same day, the same tasks on repeat. We run in circles and call it living.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Greatness of Time': a middle-aged reckoning.
verses.sanskrit_display: विद्या नाधिगता कलङ्करहिता वित्तं च नोपार्जितं शुश्रूषापि समाहितेन मनसा पित्रोर्न सम्पादिता । आलोलायतलोचनाः प्रियतमाः स्वप्नेऽपि नालिङ्गिताः कालोऽयं परपिण्डलोलुपतया काकैरिव प्रेर्यते ॥
verses.translation: I did not gain spotless learning, nor earn wealth; I did not even serve my parents with an attentive mind; I did not hold wide-eyed beloveds even in dreams. Time is driven on, like a crow greedy for others' scraps.
verses.line: I neither learned, nor earned, nor truly cared for my parents. Time slipped away chasing scraps.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Greatness of Time'.
verses.sanskrit_display: वयं येभ्यो जाताश्चिरपरिचिता एव खलु ते समं यैः संवृद्धाः स्मृतिविषयतां तेऽपि गमिताः । इदानीमेते स्मः प्रतिदिवसमासन्नपतना गतास्तुल्यावस्थां सिकतिलनदीतीरतरुभिः ॥
verses.translation: Those who gave us birth are long gone into memory; those with whom we grew up have also passed into memory; and now we, nearer to falling each day, have come to the state of trees on a sandy riverbank.
verses.line: Our parents are memories, our childhood friends too. Now we stand like trees on a crumbling riverbank.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'On the Greatness of Time'.
verses.sanskrit_display: आयुर्वर्षशतं नृणां परिमितं रात्रौ तदर्धं गतं तस्यार्धस्य परस्य चार्धमपरं बालत्ववृद्धत्वयोः । शेषं व्याधिवियोगदुःखसहितं सेवादिभिर्नीयते जीवे वारितरङ्गचञ्चलतरे सौख्यं कुतः प्राणिनाम् ॥
verses.translation: A human life is measured at a hundred years. Half goes in night; of the other half, half again goes in childhood and old age; the rest is spent in sickness, separation and sorrow, in serving others. In a life more restless than a wave, where is happiness for any creature?
verses.line: Half of life goes in sleep, much in childhood and age, the rest in illness and serving others.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of 'On the Greatness of Time'.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षणं बालो भूत्वा क्षणमपि युवा कामरसिकः क्षणं वित्तैर्हीनः क्षणमपि च सम्पूर्णविभवः । जराजीर्णैरङ्गैर्नट इव वलीमण्डिततनुः नरः संसारान्ते विशति यमधानीयवनिकाम् ॥
verses.translation: For a moment a child, for a moment a youth in love, for a moment penniless, for a moment wealthy; then, limbs worn by age and body painted with wrinkles like an actor, man exits behind the curtain of Death at the end of the play.
verses.line: A child, a lover, broke, then rich, then old: like an actor, we exit behind the curtain.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Opening verse of the dialogue between the ascetic and the king.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वं राजा वयमप्युपासितगुरुप्रज्ञाभिमानोन्नताः ख्यातस्त्वं विभवैर्यशांसि कवयो दिक्षु प्रतन्वन्ति नः । इत्थं मानधनातिदूरमुभयोरप्यावयोरन्तरं यद्यस्मासु पराङ्मुखोऽसि वयमप्येकान्ततो निःस्पृहाः ॥
verses.translation: You are a king; we too stand tall with the pride of wisdom gained from serving our teachers. You are famous for your wealth; poets spread our fame in every direction. So the gap between us in honour and riches is not wide. If you turn your face from us, we too are entirely indifferent.
verses.line: You have wealth, I have learning. If you turn away from me, I need nothing from you.
verses.misuse: Self-respect, not contempt for others.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the dialogue between the ascetic and the king.
verses.sanskrit_display: वयमिह परितुष्टा वल्कलैस्त्वं दुकूलैः सम इव परितोषो निर्विशेषो विशेषः । स तु भवतु दरिद्रो यस्य तृष्णा विशाला मनसि च परितुष्टे कोऽर्थवान्को दरिद्रः ॥
verses.translation: We are content here with bark garments, you with silk; the contentment is equal, and the difference makes no difference. He is poor whose craving is vast. When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor?
verses.line: When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor? The poor one has the biggest craving.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the dialogue between the ascetic and the king.
verses.sanskrit_display: विपुलहृदयैरीशैरेतज्जगज्जनितं पुरा विधृतमपरैर्दत्तं चान्यैर्विजित्य तृणं यथा । इह हि भुवनान्यन्ये धीराश्चतुर्दश भुञ्जते कतिपयपुरस्वाम्ये पुंसां क एष मदज्वरः ॥
verses.translation: Great-hearted lords created this world long ago; others held it; others conquered it and gave it away like straw; and even now other heroes enjoy all fourteen worlds. What is this fever of pride in men over lordship of a few towns?
verses.line: Others ruled whole worlds and gave them away like straw. Why this fever of pride over a few towns?

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Opening verse of 'Advice to the Mind'.
verses.sanskrit_display: परेषां चेतांसि प्रतिदिवसमाराध्य बहुधा प्रसादं किं नेतुं विशसि हृदय क्लेशकलितम् । प्रसन्ने त्वय्यन्तः स्वयमुदितचिन्तामणिगणो विविक्तः संकल्पः किमभिलषितं पुष्यति न ते ॥
verses.translation: O heart, why do you enter into weariness, day after day trying to please the minds of others in so many ways, to win their favour? When you are at peace within, your own clear resolve rises by itself like a cluster of wish-granting gems: what wish of yours would it not fulfil?
verses.line: Why exhaust yourself daily winning others' approval? Settle inside, and your own clarity grants every wish.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Advice to the Mind'.
verses.sanskrit_display: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verses.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verses.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verses.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Advice to the Mind': the 'so what?' verse.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राप्ताः श्रियः सकलकामदुघास्ततः किं न्यस्तं पदं शिरसि विद्विषतां ततः किम् । सम्पादिताः प्रणयिनो विभवैस्ततः किं कल्पस्थितास्तनुभृतां तनवस्ततः किम् ॥
verses.translation: You gained fortunes that fulfil every desire: so what? You set your foot on your enemies' heads: so what? You won over friends with your riches: so what? Bodies lasted an aeon: so what?
verses.line: Got every comfort: so what? Beat your rivals: so what? Lived for ages: so what?

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of 'Advice to the Mind'.
verses.sanskrit_display: पातालमाविशसि यासि नभो विलङ्घ्य दिङ्मण्डलं भ्रमसि मानस चापलेन । भ्रान्त्यापि जातु विमलं कथमात्मनीनं न ब्रह्म संस्मरसि निर्वृतिमेषि येन ॥
verses.translation: You plunge into the underworld, leap across the sky, wander round every direction, O mind, out of restlessness. Why do you never, even by mistake, remember that pure Brahman, your own Self, by which you would find peace?
verses.line: Mind, you roam the underworld, the sky and every direction. Why never turn to the stillness within?

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Weighing the lasting and the passing
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Opening verse of 'Weighing the Lasting and the Passing'.
verses.sanskrit_display: किं वेदैः स्मृतिभिः पुराणपठनैः शास्त्रैर्महाविस्तरैः स्वर्गग्रामकुटीनिवासफलदैः कर्मक्रियाविभ्रमैः । मुक्त्वैकं भवदुःखभाररचनाविध्वंसकालानलं स्वात्मानन्दपदप्रवेशकलनं शेषैर्वणिग्वृत्तिभिः ॥
verses.translation: What use are the Vedas, the smritis, reading the Puranas, the vast shastras, and the confusions of ritual that earn a hut in the village of heaven? Apart from the one thing, entry into the bliss of the Self, the fire that burns away the whole burden of worldly sorrow, the rest is merchants' trading.
verses.line: Scripture and ritual without inner peace is just trading. Seek the joy within.
verses.misuse: Not a dismissal of scripture; a warning against religion as a transaction.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Weighing the lasting and the passing
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Weighing the Lasting and the Passing': a portrait of old age.
verses.sanskrit_display: गात्रं संकुचितं गतिर्विगलिता भ्रष्टा च दन्तावलिः- दृष्टिर्नश्यति वर्धते बधिरता वक्त्रं च लालायते । वाक्यं नाद्रियते च बान्धवजनो भार्या न शुश्रूषते हा कष्टं पुरुषस्य जीर्णवयसः पुत्रोऽप्यमित्रायते ॥
verses.translation: The body shrinks, the gait falters, the teeth fall out, sight fades, deafness grows, the mouth drools; relatives pay no heed to his words, his wife no longer looks after him; alas, the misery of an old man: even his son turns hostile.
verses.line: In old age, family stops listening and even a son turns cold. Alas for the aged.
verses.misuse: A lament, not a prediction; read it as a call to keep listening to the old.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Weighing the lasting and the passing
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Weighing the Lasting and the Passing'.
verses.sanskrit_display: यावत्स्वस्थमिदं शरीरमरुजं यावज्जरा दूरतो यावच्चेन्द्रियशक्तिरप्रतिहता यावत्क्षयो नायुषः । आत्मश्रेयसि तावदेव विदुषा कार्यः प्रयत्नो महान् संदीप्ते भवने तु कूपखननं प्रत्युद्यमः कीदृशः ॥
verses.translation: While this body is healthy and free of illness, while old age is far off, while the senses are unimpaired and life has not run down, the wise should make a great effort for their own highest good. Once the house is on fire, what use is digging a well?
verses.line: While you are healthy, do what matters most. No one digs a well once the house is burning.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: Weighing the lasting and the passing
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Weighing the Lasting and the Passing': not knowing how to spend a short life.
verses.sanskrit_display: तपस्यन्तः सन्तः किमधिनिवसामः सुरनदीं गुणोदारान्दारानुत परिचरामः सविनयम् । पिबामः शास्त्रौघानुत विविधकाव्यामृतरसान् न विद्मः किं कुर्मः कतिपयनिमेषायुषि जने ॥
verses.translation: Shall we live as ascetics beside the heavenly river? Or courteously serve our wives, generous in virtue? Or drink the floods of scripture, or the nectar of many kinds of poetry? We do not know what to do, in a human life that lasts a few blinks.
verses.line: Retreat, family, study or art? We cannot choose, and a life lasts only a few blinks.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
verses.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
verses.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva'.
verses.sanskrit_display: महेश्वरे वा जगतामधीश्वरे जनार्दने वा जगदन्तरात्मनि । न वस्तुभेदप्रतिपत्तिरस्ति मे तथापि भक्तिस्तरुणेन्दुशेखरे ॥
verses.translation: Between Maheshvara, lord of the worlds, and Janardana, the inner Self of the world, I see no difference in essence; still, my devotion goes to the one who wears the young moon on his head.
verses.line: I see no real difference between Shiva and Vishnu; still, my heart goes to Shiva.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: The way of the free ascetic
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'The Way of the Free Ascetic'.
verses.sanskrit_display: ब्रह्माण्डं मण्डलीमात्रं किं लोभाय मनस्विनः । शफरीस्फुरितेनाब्धिः क्षुब्धो न खलु जायते ॥
verses.translation: For the high-minded the whole universe is a mere ring; what is there in it to be greedy for? The ocean is not churned up by the flicker of a little fish.
verses.line: The ocean is not stirred by a small fish's flick. Petty things needn't shake you.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: The way of the free ascetic
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'The Way of the Free Ascetic'.
verses.sanskrit_display: महाशय्या पृथ्वी विपुलमुपधानं भुजलता वितानं चाकाशं व्यजनमनुकूलोऽयमनिलः । शरच्चन्द्रो दीपो विरतिवनितासङ्गमुदितः सुखी शान्तः शेते मुनिरतनुभूतिर्नृप इव ॥
verses.translation: The earth is his great bed, his arm a broad pillow, the sky his canopy, the friendly breeze his fan, the autumn moon his lamp; delighted in the company of his bride, Renunciation, the sage sleeps happy and calm, rich beyond measure, like a king.
verses.line: Earth for a bed, an arm for a pillow, the moon for a lamp: the content sleep like kings.

verses.collection: Vairagyashatakam: The way of the free ascetic
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From 'The Way of the Free Ascetic': people arguing over who the wanderer is.
verses.sanskrit_display: चण्डालः किमयं द्विजातिरथवा शूद्रोऽथ किं तापसः किं वा तत्त्वविवेकपेशलमतिर्योगीश्वरः कोऽपि किम् । इत्युत्पन्नविकल्पजल्पमुखरैराभाष्यमाणा जनैः न क्रुद्धाः पथि नैव तुष्टमनसो यान्ति स्वयं योगिनः ॥
verses.translation: 'Is this a chandala? A twice-born? A shudra, or an ascetic? Or some great yogi with a mind skilled in discerning truth?' Talked about like this by people noisy with doubts and chatter, the yogis go their own way, neither angry nor pleased.
verses.line: Let people argue about who you are. Walk on, neither angry nor flattered.
