Tulsi, at that time who but the kind one can calm the terrible pain? Where everything is crisis and the worry seems impossible, there my master Ram keeps me.
verses.line: Where everything is crisis and the worry seems impossible, there I am still kept.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Hanuman Bahuk: "You are the water, I the fish"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, old and in agony from a painful arm, prays to Hanuman.
verses.sanskrit_display: अंबु तू हौं अंबुचर, अंब तू हौं डिंभ, सो न, बूझिये बिलंब अवलंब मेरे तेरिये। बालक बिकल जानि पाहि प्रेम पहिचानि, तुलसीकी बाह पर लामीलूम फेरिये॥
verses.translation: You are the water and I the fish; you are the mother and I the baby. So do not delay, for you are my only support. Knowing the child is in distress, protect him; recognise the love, and stroke Tulsi's aching arm with your long tail.
verses.line: You are the water and I the fish; you the mother, I the child. Stroke the place that hurts.
verses.misuse: Prayer is company in pain, not a substitute for medical care.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Hanuman Bahuk: "Put your hand on my head"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, ill, asks Hanuman for one gentle gesture.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुलसीके माथेपर हाथ फेरो कीसनाथ, देखिये न दास दुखी तोसे कनिगरके॥
verses.translation: Lord of the monkeys, stroke Tulsi's head with your hand. With a protector like you, let your servant not be seen in pain.
verses.line: Put your hand on my head. Let me not be left alone in this pain.
verses.misuse: Prayer is company in pain, not a substitute for medical care.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what Hanuman's name does to fear.
verses.sanskrit_display: संकट सोच सबै तुलसी लिये नाम फटै मकरीके-से जाले।
verses.translation: Tulsi says: all troubles and worries tear apart like spider webs when your name is taken.
verses.line: Troubles and worries tear like cobwebs when you call on the one you trust.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Gitavali: Kausalya holds his little shoes
verses.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating)
verses.setting: After Ram leaves for the forest, his mother Kausalya keeps his childhood things.
verses.sanskrit_display: जननी निरखति बान-धनुहियाँ। बार-बार उर नैननि लावति प्रभुजूकी ललित पनहियाँ॥ कबहुँ प्रथम ज्यों जाइ जगावति कहि प्रिय बचन सँवारे। उठहु तात! बलि मातु बदनपर, अनुज-सखा सब द्वारे॥
verses.translation: The mother gazes at his little bow and arrows. Again and again she presses the Lord's small, lovely shoes to her heart and eyes. Sometimes, as before, she goes to wake him with tender words: "Get up, my child, your mother adores your face; your brothers and friends are all at the door."
verses.line: She held his little shoes to her heart, and some mornings still went to wake him.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: The opening pada of Surdas's songs, sung by a poet who was himself blind.
verses.sanskrit_display: चरन-कमल बंदों हरि-राइ। जाकी कृपा पंगु गिरि लंघे, अंधे कों सब कछु दरसाइ ॥ बहिरौ सुने, गूँग पुनि बोले, रंक चले सिर छत्र धराइ | सूरदास स्वामी करुनामय, बार बार बंदों तिहि पाइ ॥
verses.translation: I bow to the lotus feet of Hari, by whose grace the lame cross mountains and the blind see everything; the deaf hear, the mute speak again, and the pauper walks with a royal canopy over his head. Surdas says: my master is full of compassion; again and again I bow at his feet.
verses.line: By grace the lame cross mountains and the blind see.
verses.reflection: What seems impossible today may not stay so.
verses.misuse: Not a medical promise; a hope that limits are not the last word.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Surdas: companion of those with no one
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on whose side God stands.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथ अनाथनि ही के संगी। दीनदयाल, परम करुनामय, जन-हित हरि बहु-रंगी ॥
verses.translation: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one: kind to the lowly, supremely compassionate, Hari who takes many forms for the good of his people.
verses.line: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Surdas: as the eyelid guards the eye
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas, looking back on hard times, almost misses them for how close God felt.
verses.sanskrit_display: अब वे बिपदा हू न रहीं। मनसा करि सुमिरत हे जब-जब, मिलते तब-तबहीं ॥ अपने दीन दास के हित लगि, फिरते सँग-सँगहीं । लेते राखि पलक गोलक ज्यों, संतत तिन सबहीं ॥
verses.translation: Now even those troubles are gone. Back then, whenever I remembered you in my heart, you met me right then. For the good of your poor servant you walked along beside me, and kept me through all of it as the eyelid keeps the eye.
verses.line: In the hardest days he walked beside me and kept me as the eyelid keeps the eye.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.ref_label: Sursagar vinay pada (Sur Vinay Patrika 167, opening)
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas asks not to be measured.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रभु, मेरे गुन-अवगुन न बिचारों।
verses.translation: Lord, do not weigh my good points and my faults.
verses.line: Lord, do not weigh my good points against my faults. Just keep me.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Surdas: "Good or bad, we are yours"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on belonging that does not depend on being good.
verses.sanskrit_display: जौ हम भले बुरे तो तेरे। तुम्हें हमारी लाज-बड़ाई, बिनती सुनि प्रभु मेरे ॥
verses.translation: Good or bad, we are yours. Our shame and our honour are yours to carry. Hear my plea, my Lord.
verses.line: Good or bad, we are still yours.
verses.reflection: Our shame is not ours to carry alone.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Surdas: the touchstone does not choose
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: The famous bhajan "Prabhu mere avgun chit na dharo".
verses.sanskrit_display: हमारे प्रभु, औगुन चित न धरो । समदरसी है नाम तुम्हारा, सोई पार करौ॥ इक लोहा पूजा में राखत, इक घर बधिक परो। सो दुबिधा पारस नहिं जानत, कंचन करत खरो॥
verses.translation: My Lord, do not hold my faults in your mind. Your name is "the one who sees all alike"; live up to it and carry me across. One piece of iron is kept in the shrine for worship, another lies in a butcher's house; the touchstone knows no such difference, and turns both into pure gold.
verses.line: The touchstone turns any iron to gold, the shrine's or the butcher's.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Surdas, Bhramargeet: "Our eyes rain night and day"
verses.speaker: the gopis
verses.setting: The women of Braj, after Krishna has left, on missing him.
verses.sanskrit_display: निसिदिन बरसत नैन हमारे। सदा रहति पावस ऋतु हम पै जब तें स्याम सिधारे॥
verses.translation: Night and day our eyes keep raining. Ever since Shyam went away, it is always the rainy season for us.
verses.line: "Since he left, it has been monsoon in our eyes."
verses.reflection: Tears for someone you miss are allowed.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.collection: Kabir: the lily and the moon
verses.speaker: Kabir
verses.setting: Kabir on love across distance.
verses.sanskrit_display: जल में बसै कमोदिनी चन्दा बसै अकास। जो है जाको भावता सो ताही के पास॥
verses.translation: The lily lives in the water and the moon lives in the sky; yet whoever is dear to someone is always near them.
verses.line: The lily lives in water, the moon in the sky. Those we love are never far.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.speaker: Kabir
verses.setting: Kabir asks forgiveness as a child asks a father.
verses.sanskrit_display: अवगुन मेरे बाप जो बकसु गरीब निवाज। जो मैं पूत कपूत हौं तऊ पिता को लाज॥
verses.translation: Father, forgive my faults, you who lift up the poor. Even if I am a bad son, I am still my father's to look after.
verses.line: Even if I am a wayward child, I am still my father's child.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.collection: Kabir: whoever has no one has you
verses.speaker: Kabir
verses.setting: Kabir on God's court, where no one is turned away.
verses.sanskrit_display: जिसहि न कोई तिसहि तू, जिस तू तिस सब कोइ । दरिगह तेरी सांईयां , ना मरूम कोइ होइ ॥
verses.translation: Whoever has no one has you; whoever has you has everyone. Master, at your court no one goes away empty-handed.
verses.line: Whoever has no one has you. At your door, no one is turned away.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Kavitakosh states its compilation is not under any licence ("all rights reserved") - treat as a locator/transcription, re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.speaker: Rahim
verses.setting: Rahim on remembrance.
verses.sanskrit_display: रहिमन सुधि सबते भली, लगै जो बारम्बार। बिछुरे मानुष फिरि मिलैं, यहै जानि अवतार॥
verses.translation: Rahim says: remembering is best of all, when it comes again and again. People who were separated meet again; know that this is why God takes birth.
verses.line: Remembering is a kind of nearness. People who were parted do meet again.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.speaker: Rahim
verses.setting: Rahim on telling one's sorrow.
verses.sanskrit_display: दुख नर सुनि हाँसी करैं, धरैं रहीम न धीर। कही सुनैं सुनि-सुनि करैं, ऐसे वे रघुवीर॥
verses.translation: Rahim says: people laugh when they hear of your sorrow and do not keep you steady. Raghuvir listens to what you say, and having listened, acts. That is how he is.
verses.line: People may laugh at your sorrow. There is one who listens, and having listened, helps.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.collection: Rahim: the gift of being low
verses.speaker: Rahim
verses.setting: Rahim on humility after a fall.
verses.sanskrit_display: दिव्य दीनता के रसहिं, का जानै जग अन्धु। भली बिचारी दीनता, दीनबन्धु-से बन्धु॥
verses.translation: What does the blind world know of the divine sweetness of being low? Poor humble lowliness is good: it brings a friend like the Friend of the lowly.
verses.line: Being brought low has one gift: the Friend of the lowly comes close.
verses.misuse: Not a call to accept humiliation; about the closeness found in low times.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.collection: Rahim: the one who lives in your heart
verses.speaker: Rahim
verses.setting: Rahim on a love so close it needs no news.
verses.sanskrit_display: जेहिं रहीम तन-मन दियो, कियो हिए बिच भौन। तासों दुख-सुख कहन की, रही बात अब कौन॥
verses.translation: Rahim says: to the one who has been given body and mind, who has made a home in the heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling?
verses.line: The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.display_ref: Meera pada "Mero darad na jane koy"
verses.ref_label: Meera pada "Mero darad na jane koy"
verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera, mocked by her family for her devotion, on pain no one understands.
verses.sanskrit_display: हे री मैं तो प्रेम-दिवानी मेरो दरद न जाणै कोय। घायल की गति घायल जाणै, जो कोई घायल होय।
verses.translation: Friend, I am mad with love, and no one knows my pain. Only the wounded know what the wounded go through, only one who has been wounded.
verses.line: "No one knows my pain. Only the wounded know the wounded."
verses.reflection: Your pain is real even if unseen.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Kavitakosh states its compilation is not under any licence ("all rights reserved") - treat as a locator/transcription, re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, praising the name of Ram before he begins the story.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥
verses.translation: Tulsi says: if you want light both inside and outside, place the name of Ram like a jewelled lamp on the threshold of your tongue.
verses.line: Want light inside and out? Keep Ram's name like a lamp on the doorstep of your tongue.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on why the name matters even more than the form.
verses.sanskrit_display: रूप बिसेष नाम बिनु जानें। करतल गत न परहिं पहिचानें॥ सुमिरिअ नाम रूप बिनु देखें। आवत हृदयँ सनेह बिसेषें ॥
verses.translation: Even a particular form is not recognised without its name, though it sit in the palm of your hand. But remember the name without seeing the form, and a special love rises in the heart.
verses.line: Remember the name even when you cannot see the form, and love wells up in the heart.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what is left when every other practice feels out of reach.
verses.sanskrit_display: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलंबन एकू॥ कालनेमि कलि कपट निधानू। नाम सुमति समरथ हनुमानू ॥
verses.translation: In this age there is no ritual action, no devotion and no discernment left to lean on; the name of Ram is the one support. In the age of Kali, the name is the clever Hanuman against Kalanemi, the master of deceit.
verses.line: When no practice, devotion or wisdom seems within reach, the name of Ram is still a support.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on the name in a frightening age.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाम कामतरु काल कराला। सुमिरत समन सकल जग जाला॥ राम नाम कलि अभिमत दाता। हित परलोक लोक पितु माता ॥
verses.translation: The name is a wish-fulfilling tree in a terrible time; remembering it stills the whole tangle of the world. In this age the name of Ram gives what the heart rightly wants; it is a well-wisher for this world and the next, a father and a mother.
verses.line: The name of Ram is a father and a mother, a well-wisher in this world and the next.
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, before beginning the story, on how the name works however it is said.
verses.sanskrit_display: भायँ कुभायँ अनख आलस हूँ। नाम जपत मंगल दिसि दसहूँ॥ सुमिरि सो नाम राम गुन गाथा। करउँ नाइ रघुनाथहि माथा ॥॥
verses.translation: Said with love or without it, even in irritation or laziness, repeating the name brings good in all ten directions. Remembering that name, I bow my head to Raghunath and begin his story.
verses.line: With love or without, even irritated or lazy: say the name, and good comes from every side.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas admits his own faults before telling the story.
verses.sanskrit_display: मोरि सुधारिहि सो सब भाँती। जासु कृपा नहिं कृपाँ अघाती॥ राम सुस्वामि कुसेवकु मोसो। निज दिसि देखि दयानिधि पोसो ॥
verses.translation: He will set right everything about me, he whose kindness never tires of being kind. Ram is a good master and I am a poor servant, yet the ocean of compassion looks at it from his own side and cares for me.
verses.line: I am a poor servant; he is a good master who looks from his side and still cares for me.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram remembers his devotees.
verses.sanskrit_display: रहति न प्रभु चित चूक किए की। करत सुरति सय बार हिए की॥ जेहिं अघ बधेउ ब्याध जिमि बाली। फिरि सुकंठ सोइ कीन्हि कुचाली ॥
verses.translation: The Lord does not keep a mistake in his mind; he remembers the heart a hundred times over. The very wrong for which he struck Bali like a hunter, Sugriva later did too.
verses.line: He does not keep your mistake in mind. He remembers your heart a hundred times.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, aware his words are clumsy, trusts that Ram reads the heart.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनि अवलोकि सुचित चख चाही। भगति मोरि मति स्वामि सराही॥ कहत नसाइ होइ हियँ नीकी। रीझत राम जानि जन जी की ॥
verses.translation: Hearing, looking and weighing it with care, my Lord praised the devotion in my mind. What is badly said is still good in the heart; Ram is pleased because he knows what his servant means.
verses.line: Even when it comes out badly, he hears what you meant.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on why he dares to write at all.
verses.sanskrit_display: सठ सेवक की प्रीति रुचि रखिहहिं राम कृपालु। उपल किए जलजान जेहिं सचिव सुमति कपि भालु ॥
verses.translation: Kind Ram will honour the love and the wish of even a foolish servant, he who made stones into boats and monkeys and bears into wise ministers.
verses.line: He made stones float and monkeys wise. He will honour even a clumsy servant's love.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas watches Kausalya with her baby.
verses.sanskrit_display: ब्यापक ब्रह्म निरंजन निर्गुन बिगत बिनोद। सो अज प्रेम भगति बस कौसल्या कें गोद ॥
verses.translation: The all-pervading, stainless, formless Absolute, beyond all play, the unborn one, lies in Kausalya's lap, won over by love and devotion.
verses.line: The infinite one lies in a mother's lap, won over by love.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas bows to every creature before he begins.
verses.sanskrit_display: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥
verses.translation: The eight million four hundred thousand kinds of beings, living in water, on land and in the sky: knowing the whole world to be full of Sita and Ram, I bow to them with folded hands.
verses.line: Seeing the whole world as full of Sita and Ram, I bow to every being with folded hands.

verses.collection: Manas Ayodhya: Valmiki's homes for Ram
verses.speaker: Valmiki
verses.setting: Valmiki ends his list of the hearts Ram lives in.
verses.sanskrit_display: जाहि न चाहिअ कबहुँ कछु तुम्ह सन सहज सनेहु। बसहु निरंतर तासु मन सो राउर निज गेहु ॥
verses.translation: One who never wants anything from you and simply loves you: live in that mind always; it is your own home.
verses.line: The one who wants nothing from you and simply loves you: that heart is your own home.

verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: At Prayag, Bharat, on his way to bring Ram back, asks the holy rivers for a boon.
verses.sanskrit_display: अरथ न धरम न काम रुचि गति न चहउँ निरबान। जनम-जनम रति राम पद यह बरदानु न आन ॥
verses.translation: I have no taste for wealth, duty or pleasure, nor do I seek liberation. Birth after birth, love for Ram's feet: that is the boon, and no other.
verses.line: Not wealth, not pleasure, not even liberation: only love for Ram, life after life.

verses.speaker: Triveni (a voice from the rivers)
verses.setting: Bharat is consumed by shame over the exile; the holy rivers answer him.
verses.sanskrit_display: तात भरत तुम्ह सब बिधि साधू। राम चरन अनुराग अगाधू॥ बादि गलानि करहु मन माहीं। तुम्ह सम रामहि कोउ प्रिय नाहीं ॥
verses.translation: Child Bharat, you are good in every way; your love for Ram's feet is boundless. You torment yourself with guilt for nothing; no one is dearer to Ram than you.
verses.line: You torment yourself with guilt for nothing. No one is dearer to Ram than you.

verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram at Chitrakoot, afraid of being rejected.
verses.sanskrit_display: जौं परिहरहिं मलिन मनु जानी। जौं सनमानहिं सेवकु मानी॥ मोरें सरन रामहि की पनही। राम सुस्वामि दोसु सब जनही ॥
verses.translation: Whether he casts me off, knowing my mind to be soiled, or honours me as his servant, my refuge is Ram's sandals. Ram is a good master; the fault is all his servant's.
verses.line: Whether he turns me away or takes me in, my refuge is still at his feet.
verses.misuse: Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram, slowed by shame, quickened by love.
verses.sanskrit_display: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
verses.translation: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.
verses.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: The whole of Ayodhya arrives at Chitrakoot, each person grieving in their own way.
verses.sanskrit_display: आरत लोग राम सबु जाना। करुनाकर सुजान भगवाना॥ जो जेहि भायँ रहा अभिलाषी। तेहि तेहि कै तसि तसि रुख राखी ॥
verses.translation: The all-knowing, compassionate Lord understood all the people in distress. Whatever each one was longing for, in that very way he met them.
verses.line: He understood each hurting person, and met each one in the way they longed for.

verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat speaks to Ram before the whole assembly at Chitrakoot.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रभु पितु मातु सुहृद गुर स्वामी। पूज्य परम हित अंतरजामी॥ सरल सुसाहिबु सील निधानू। प्रनतपाल सर्बग्य सुजानू ॥ समरथ सरनागत हितकारी। गुनगाहकु अवगुन अघ हारी॥ स्वामि गोसाँइहि सरिस गोसाईं। मोहि समान मैं साइँ दोहाईं ॥
verses.translation: Lord, you are father, mother, friend, teacher and master, worthy of worship, my highest good, knower of my heart; a simple, gentle master, a treasure of good nature, protector of those who bow, all-knowing and wise; mighty, a friend to those who seek refuge, one who values merits and removes faults and sins. There is no master like my master, and, I swear by my master, no one like me.
verses.line: You are father, mother, friend, teacher, master: the one who values what is good in us and lifts our faults.

verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat admits he came to Chitrakoot against his father's order.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोक सनेहँ कि बाल सुभाएँ। आयउँ लाइ रजायसु बाएँ॥ तबहुँ कृपाल हेरि निज ओरा। सबहि भाँति भल मानेउ मोरा ॥
verses.translation: Whether out of grief, love or childishness, I came here against your will. Even then, kind one, you looked at it from your own side and took everything I did as good.
verses.line: I came out of grief and love, even against your wish, and you took it all kindly.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Indra's son Jayant, disguised as a crow, attacks Sita; when he finally falls at Ram's feet, Ram lets him go.
verses.sanskrit_display: कीन्ह मोह बस द्रोह जद्यपि तेहि कर बध उचित। प्रभु छाड़ेउ करि छोह को कृपाल रघुबीर सम ॥
verses.translation: Though out of delusion he had done harm, and punishment would have been just, the Lord let him go out of tenderness. Who is as kind as Raghubir?
verses.line: He had done wrong, and still, when he came for shelter, the Lord let him go out of tenderness.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Sutikshna
verses.setting: The young sage Sutikshna hears Ram is coming and runs to meet him, full of doubt about himself.
verses.sanskrit_display: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥ नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥
verses.translation: 'Will Ram, my master, with his brother, meet me as he would his own servant? There is no firm trust in my heart; no devotion, detachment or wisdom in my mind; no good company, no yoga, chanting or sacrifice, no steady love for his lotus feet. But the ocean of compassion has one habit: the one who has no other refuge is dear to him.'
verses.line: I have no devotion, no wisdom, no steady love. But he loves the one who has nowhere else to go.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Sutikshna, lost in love, wanders and dances on the path; Ram watches.
verses.sanskrit_display: अबिरल प्रेम भगति मुनि पाई। प्रभु देखैं तरु ओट लुकाई॥ अतिसय प्रीति देखि रघुबीरा। प्रगटे हृदयँ हरन भव भीरा ॥
verses.translation: The sage had found unbroken loving devotion; the Lord watched him, hidden behind a tree. Seeing his overflowing love, Raghubir, who removes the fears of the world, appeared in his heart.
verses.line: The Lord hid behind a tree to watch his devotee's joy.

verses.collection: Manas Aranya: Ram's teaching to Lakshman
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram describes the devotee he cannot resist.
verses.sanskrit_display: मम गुन गावत पुलक सरीरा। गदगद गिरा नयन बह नीरा॥ काम आदि मद दंभ न जाकें। तात निरंतर बस मैं ताकें ॥
verses.translation: Singing of my qualities, the body thrills, the voice chokes, tears flow from the eyes; in whom there is no lust, pride or pretence: in their power, brother, I live always.
verses.line: The one whose voice catches and eyes fill at my name, without pride or pretence: I am theirs.

verses.collection: Manas Aranya: Ram's teaching to Lakshman
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram ends his teaching on devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: बचन कर्म मन मोरि गति भजनु करहिं निःकाम। तिन्ह के हृदय कमल महुँ करउँ सदा बिश्राम ॥
verses.translation: Those for whom I am the goal in word, deed and mind, who worship without wanting anything: in the lotus of their heart I rest always.
verses.line: In the heart of the one who loves without wanting anything back, I rest always.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Ram finds the old vulture Jatayu dying after fighting Ravana for Sita.
verses.sanskrit_display: कर सरोज सिर परसेउ कृपासिंधु रघुबीर। निरखि राम छबि धाम मुख बिगत भई सब पीर ॥
verses.translation: Raghubir, the ocean of kindness, touched his head with his lotus hand. Gazing at Ram's face, the home of beauty, all his pain was gone.
verses.line: He touched the dying bird's head, and looking at that face, all his pain was gone.

verses.collection: Manas Aranya: the nine forms of devotion
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram has just said: whoever has even one of the nine forms, woman or man or any being, ...
verses.sanskrit_display: सोइ अतिसय प्रिय भामिनि मोरें। सकल प्रकार भगति दृढ़ तोरें॥ जोगि बृंद दुरलभ गति जोई। तो कहुँ आजु सुलभ भइ सोई ॥
verses.translation: ...that one is most dear to me, good lady; and in you every kind of devotion is firm. The state that is hard even for yogis has today become easy for you.
verses.line: You are most dear to me. What even yogis struggle to reach has become easy for you today.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva tells Parvati what he himself has found.
verses.sanskrit_display: उमा कहउँ मैं अनुभव अपना। सत हरि भजनु जगत सब सपना॥ पुनि प्रभु गए सरोबर तीरा। पंपा नाम सुभग गंभीरा ॥
verses.translation: Uma, I tell you my own experience: worship of Hari is real, and the whole world is a dream.
verses.line: I tell you from my own experience: love for God is real; the rest passes like a dream.
verses.misuse: Not 'nothing in your life matters'; Shiva is naming what lasts.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Narada hesitates to ask Ram for a boon.
verses.sanskrit_display: जानहु मुनि तुम्ह मोर सुभाऊ। जन सन कबहुँ कि करऊँ दुराऊ॥ कवन बस्तु असि प्रिय मोहि लागी। जो मुनिबर न सकहुँ तुम्ह मागी ॥ जन कहुँ कछु अदेय नहिं मोरें। अस बिस्वास तजहु जनि भोरें॥ तब नारद बोले हरषाई। अस बर मागउँ करउँ ढिठाई ॥
verses.translation: 'You know my nature, sage: do I ever hide anything from my own? What thing is so dear to me that you could not ask for it? There is nothing I would withhold from my own; never let go of this trust.' Then Narada, delighted, said: 'I will be bold and ask this boon.'
verses.line: Do I ever hide anything from my own? Never let go of this trust.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Narada asks why Ram stopped his marriage; Ram explains how he guards those who rely on him.
verses.sanskrit_display: तब बिबाह मैं चाहउँ कीन्हा। प्रभु केहि कारन करै न दीन्हा॥ सुनु मुनि तोहि कहउँ सहरोसा। भजहिं जे मोहि तजि सकल भरोसा ॥ करउँ सदा तिन्ह कै रखवारी। जिमि बालक राखइ महतारी॥ गह सिसु बच्छ अनल अहि धाई। तहँ राखइ जननी अरगाई ॥
verses.translation: 'When I wanted to marry, Lord, why did you not let me?' 'Listen, sage, I tell you gladly: those who worship me, giving up every other reliance, I always guard, as a mother guards her child. When the little child runs to grab fire or a snake, the mother pulls it back.'
verses.line: Those who rely on me, I guard always, as a mother pulls her child back from the fire.
verses.misuse: A mother's protection includes saying no; this is not a promise that nothing painful will happen. Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram continues explaining how he cares for different devotees.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रौढ़ भएँ तेहि सुत पर माता। प्रीति करइ नहिं पाछिलि बाता॥ मोरें प्रौढ़ तनय सम ग्यानी। बालक सुत सम दास अमानी ॥ जनहि मोर बल निज बल ताही। दुहु कहँ काम क्रोध रिपु आही॥ यह बिचारि पंडित मोहि भजहीं। पाएहुँ ग्यान भगति नहिं तजहीं ॥
verses.translation: When the son is grown, the mother loves him but no longer as before. The wise are like my grown sons; the humble servant is like my little child. My servant has my strength; the wise one relies on his own. Both face the enemies of desire and anger. Knowing this, the wise worship me, and even after gaining knowledge they do not give up devotion.
verses.line: The humble devotee is like my little child, and has my strength to lean on.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman asks Ram not to let his faults stand between them.
verses.sanskrit_display: जदपि नाथ बहु अवगुन मोरें। सेवक प्रभुहि परै जनि भोरें॥ नाथ जीव तव मायाँ मोहा। सो निस्तरइ तुम्हारेहिं छोहा ॥
verses.translation: Though I have many faults, Lord, let the servant not slip from the master's memory. Lord, every soul is bewildered by your illusion; it is freed only by your tenderness.
verses.line: I have many faults, Lord. Don't let your servant slip from your mind.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman explains why he relies on Ram alone.
verses.sanskrit_display: ता पर मैं रघुबीर दोहाई। जानउँ नहिं कछु भजन उपाई॥ सेवक सुत पति मातु भरोसें। रहइ असोच बनइ प्रभु पोसें ॥
verses.translation: And on top of that, I swear by Raghubir, I know no method of worship. A servant relies on his master, a child on its mother, and lives free of worry; the master has to look after him.
verses.line: A child relies on its mother and stops worrying; she has to look after it.
verses.misuse: Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Hanuman falls at Ram's feet in his true form.
verses.sanskrit_display: अस कहि परेउ चरन अकुलाई। निज तनु प्रगटि प्रीति उर छाई॥ तब रघुपति उठाई उर लावा। निज लोचन जल सींचि जुड़ावा ॥
verses.translation: Saying this he fell at his feet in distress, showing his own form, his heart full of love. Then Raghupati lifted him up, held him to his heart, and cooled him with the tears of his own eyes.
verses.line: Ram lifted him up, held him close, and cooled him with his own tears.

verses.speaker: Sampati
verses.setting: The monkeys despair at the ocean; the old vulture Sampati rouses them.
verses.sanskrit_display: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
verses.translation: Even sinners who remember his name cross the boundless ocean of the world. You are his messengers: give up your timidity, keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verses.line: Drop your timidity. Keep Ram in your heart and find a way.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Sanskrit prayer opening the Sundar Kand, recited daily by many.
verses.sanskrit_display: नान्या स्पृहा रघुपते हृदयेऽस्मदीये सत्यं वदामि च भवानखिलान्तरात्मा। भक्तिं प्रयच्छ रघुपुंगव निर्भरां मे कामादिदोषरहितं कुरु मानसं च ॥
verses.translation: Raghupati, I tell you truly, and you are the inner self of all: there is no other longing in my heart. Give me full devotion, best of the Raghus, and make my mind free of desire and the other faults.
verses.line: There is no other longing in my heart. Give me full devotion, and a mind free of craving.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Mid-leap, the mountain Mainaka rises and offers Hanuman a rest.
verses.sanskrit_display: हनूमान तेहि परसा कर पुनि कीन्ह प्रनाम। राम काजु कीन्हें बिनु मोहि कहाँ बिश्राम ॥
verses.translation: Hanuman touched it with his hand, bowed to it, and said: how can I rest until I have done Ram's work?
verses.line: He thanked the mountain and said: how can I rest before Ram's work is done?
verses.misuse: About commitment to a task that matters; rest is allowed, and Hanuman thanks the one who offers it.

verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan, living among the wicked, wonders if Ram could care for him.
verses.sanskrit_display: तामस तनु कछु साधन नाहीं। प्रीत न पद सरोज मन माहीं॥ अब मोहि भा भरोस हनुमंता। बिनु हरिकृपा मिलहिं नहिं संता ॥
verses.translation: 'I have a demon's body and no spiritual practice, no love for his lotus feet in my mind. But now I have hope, Hanuman: without Hari's grace one does not meet the good.'
verses.line: I have no practice and no love to speak of. But meeting you tells me grace has found me.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman, after joking that no one wants to hear a monkey's name before breakfast, speaks of Ram's kindness to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अस मैं अधम सखा सुनु मोहू पर रघुबीर। कीन्हीं कृपा सुमिरि गुन भरे बिलोचन नीर ॥
verses.translation: Listen, friend: I am that lowly, and yet on me Raghubir showed kindness. Remembering his goodness, his eyes filled with tears.
verses.line: Even on someone as ordinary as me, he showed kindness. Remembering it, Hanuman wept.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman, having given Ram's message, comforts Sita.
verses.sanskrit_display: कह कपि हृदयँ धीर धरु माता। सुमिरु राम सेवक सुखदाता॥ उर आनहु रघुपति प्रभुताई। सुनि मम बचन तजहु कदराई ॥
verses.translation: Hanuman said: 'Hold steady in your heart, mother. Remember Ram, who gives joy to his servants. Bring to mind Raghupati's strength; hearing my words, put away your fear.'
verses.line: Hold steady, mother. Remember Ram, and let my words take away your fear.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Sita doubts that small monkeys can beat Ravana's army; Hanuman answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनु माता साखामृग नहिं बल बुद्धि बिसाल। प्रभु प्रताप तें गरुड़हि खाइ परम लघु ब्याल ॥
verses.translation: Listen, mother: monkeys have no great strength or wisdom. But by the Lord's power even a tiny snake can swallow Garuda.
verses.line: We have no great strength of our own. By the Lord's power, the small can do the impossible.

verses.collection: Manas Sundar: Hanuman in Ravana's court
verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman, a prisoner, tells Ravana himself that the door is still open.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रनतपाल रघुनायक करुना सिंधु खरारि। गएँ सरन प्रभु राखिहैं तव अपराध बिसारि ॥
verses.translation: Raghunayak protects those who bow to him; he is an ocean of compassion. If you go to him for refuge, the Lord will protect you and forget your offence.
verses.line: Even now, go to him for refuge and he will protect you and forget your offence.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Ram asks how Sita keeps herself alive in captivity.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाम पाहरू दिवस निसि ध्यान तुम्हार कपाट। लोचन निज पद जंत्रित जाहिं प्रान केहिं बाट ॥
verses.translation: Your name is the watchman day and night; meditation on you is the door; her eyes are fixed on her own feet. By what way could life leave her?
verses.line: Your name guards her day and night; thinking of you is the door. How could life slip away?
verses.misuse: Speaks of how remembrance kept Sita going through captivity; if you are in danger or despair, reach out for help too.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Hearing of Sita's suffering, Ram's eyes fill with tears.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनि सीता दुख प्रभु सुख अयना। भरि आए जल राजिव नयना॥ बचन कायँ मन मम गति जाही। सपनेहुँ बूझिअ बिपति कि ताही ॥
verses.translation: Hearing of Sita's sorrow, the Lord, home of joy, filled his lotus eyes with tears. 'Can one whose only refuge is me, in word, body and mind, ever meet calamity, even in a dream?'
verses.line: Hearing of her pain, his eyes filled: can one who takes refuge in me ever truly be lost?
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Ram has asked whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: कह हनुमंत बिपति प्रभु सोई। जब तव सुमिरन भजन न होई॥ केतिक बात प्रभु जातुधान की। रिपुहि जीति आनिबी जानकी ॥
verses.translation: Hanuman said: 'Lord, calamity is only this: when remembering and worshipping you does not happen. What is a demon to the Lord? We will defeat the enemy and bring Janaki back.'
verses.line: Real calamity is only this: the moment we stop remembering you.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Ram offers Hanuman anything; Hanuman asks for one thing.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथ भगति अति सुखदायनी। देहु कृपा करि अनपायनी॥ सुनि प्रभु परम सरल कपि बानी। एवमस्तु तब कहेउ भवानी ॥
verses.translation: 'Lord, give me by your kindness the devotion that brings great joy and never leaves.' Hearing the monkey's utterly simple words, the Lord said 'so be it', Bhavani.
verses.line: Offered anything, he asked only for a love that never leaves.

verses.speaker: Sugriva / Ram
verses.setting: Sugriva suspects Vibhishan is a spy and wants him bound; Ram answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: भेद हमार लेन सठ आवा। राखिअ बाँधि मोहि अस भावा॥ सखा नीति तुम्ह नीकि बिचारी। मम पन सरनागत भयहारी ॥
verses.translation: 'The wretch has come to learn our secrets; I think we should bind him.' 'Friend, you have weighed policy well. But my vow is to take away the fear of whoever comes for refuge.'
verses.line: You have reasoned well, friend. But my vow is to take away the fear of whoever comes for refuge.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram explains why he trusts the one who turns up at his door.
verses.sanskrit_display: पापवंत कर सहज सुभाऊ। भजनु मोर तेहि भाव न काऊ॥ जौं पै दुष्ट हृदय सोइ होई। मोरें सनमुख आव कि सोई ॥
verses.translation: It is the natural way of a sinner never to like worshipping me. If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me at all?
verses.line: If they were truly wicked, would they have turned toward me at all?

verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan, standing before Ram, names who he is and asks for shelter.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रवन सुजसु सुनि आयउँ प्रभु भंजन भव भीर। त्राहि त्राहि आरति हरन सरन सुखद रघुबीर ॥
verses.translation: Hearing your good name with my own ears I have come, Lord, breaker of the fear of the world. Save me, save me, remover of distress, Raghubir, whose refuge brings joy.
verses.line: I heard of you and came. Save me, you who take away distress.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, having embraced Vibhishan, asks how he survived in Lanka.
verses.sanskrit_display: खल मंडली बसहु दिनु राती। सखा धरम निबहइ केहि भाँती॥ मैं जानउँ तुम्हारि सब रीती। अति नय निपुन न भाव अनीती ॥
verses.translation: 'You lived day and night among the wicked; how did you keep your goodness, friend? I know all your ways: very wise in conduct, with no taste for wrong.'
verses.line: You lived among the cruel day and night. I know how you kept your goodness.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram tells Vibhishan his own nature.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनहु सखा निज कहउँ सुभाऊ। जान भुसुंडि संभु गिरिजाऊ॥ जौं नर होइ चराचर द्रोही। आवै सभय सरन तकि मोही ॥ तजि मद मोह कपट छल नाना। करउँ सद्य तेहि साधु समाना॥ जननी जनक बंधु सुत दारा। तनु धनु भवन सुहृद परिवारा ॥
verses.translation: Listen, friend, I tell you my own nature, as Bhushundi, Shambhu and Girija know it. If a person who has harmed every living thing comes to me afraid, looking for shelter, and gives up pride, delusion, deceit and trickery, I make him like a saint at once. Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, home, friends and family:
verses.line: Even one who has harmed everyone, if they come afraid and drop their pride, I make good at once.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram describes the devotee who lives in his heart.
verses.sanskrit_display: सब कै ममता ताग बटोरी। मम पद मनहि बाँध बरि डोरी॥ समदरसी इच्छा कछु नाहीं। हरष सोक भय नहिं मन माहीं ॥ अस सज्जन मम उर बस कैसें। लोभी हृदयँ बसइ धनु जैसें॥ तुम्ह सारिखे संत प्रिय मोरें। धरउँ देह नहिं आन निहोरें ॥
verses.translation: Gathering the threads of attachment to all of these, he twists them into one cord and ties his mind to my feet. Even-minded, wanting nothing, with no elation, grief or fear in his mind: such a good person lives in my heart as wealth lives in a miser's heart. Saints like you are dear to me; I take a body for no other reason.
verses.line: Gather every thread of love into one cord, and tie your heart to me.
verses.misuse: Not 'give up your family': it is gathering one's loves into a single devotion. Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.

verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan admits why he first came.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनहु देव सचराचर स्वामी। प्रनतपाल उर अंतरजामी॥ उर कछु प्रथम बासना रही। प्रभु पद प्रीति सरित सो बही ॥
verses.translation: Listen, Lord of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow, knower of hearts: there was some desire in my heart at first; it has been carried away in the river of love for your feet.
verses.line: I came with my own wants. They were carried away in the river of love.

verses.collection: Manas Lanka: Angad in Ravana's court
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Angad walks alone into Ravana's hostile court as Ram's envoy.
verses.sanskrit_display: गयउ सभा दरबार तब सुमिरि राम पद कंज। सिंह ठवनि इत उत चितव धीर बीर बल पुंज ॥
verses.translation: Then he went into the court, remembering Ram's lotus feet, looking this way and that with a lion's gait, steady, brave, a mass of strength.
verses.line: He walked into the hostile room remembering Ram, steady as a lion.

verses.collection: Manas Lanka: Angad in Ravana's court
verses.speaker: Angad (thinking)
verses.setting: Ram sends Angad to Ravana; Angad sees the honour for what it is.
verses.sanskrit_display: स्वयंसिद्ध सब काज नाथ मोहि आदरु दियउ। अस बिचारि जुबराज तन पुलकित हरषित हियउ ॥
verses.translation: 'Every task is already accomplished by itself; the Lord has only given me the honour.' Thinking this, the prince's body thrilled and his heart was glad.
verses.line: The work is already done; I've only been given the honour of carrying it.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Vibhishan showers jewels from the sky; the monkeys put them in their mouths; Ram laughs.
verses.sanskrit_display: मुनि जेहि ध्यान न पावहिं नेति नेति कह बेद। कृपासिंधु सोइ कपिन्ह सन करत अनेक बिनोद ॥
verses.translation: The one whom sages cannot reach in meditation, whom the Vedas call 'not this, not this': that ocean of kindness is joking and playing with monkeys.
verses.line: The one sages cannot reach in meditation is laughing and joking with the monkeys.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva comments on Ram's play with the monkeys.
verses.sanskrit_display: उमा जोग जप दान तप नाना मख ब्रत नेम। राम कृपा नहिं करहिं तसि जसि निष्केवल प्रेम ॥
verses.translation: Uma, yoga, chanting, charity, austerity, sacrifices, vows and rules: none of these win Ram's kindness the way pure love alone does.
verses.line: No practice wins his kindness the way plain love does.

verses.collection: Manas Uttar: Hanuman brings news to Bharat
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: After fourteen years, Hanuman brings Bharat the news that Ram is coming; Bharat has one question.
verses.sanskrit_display: तब हनुमंत नाइ पद माथा। कहे सकल रघुपति गुन गाथा॥ कहु कपि कबहुँ कृपाल गोसाईं। सुमिरहिं मोहि दास की नाईं ॥
verses.translation: Then Hanuman bowed at his feet and told all of Raghupati's virtues. 'Tell me, Hanuman: does the kind master ever remember me, as one remembers a servant?'
verses.line: Tell me: does he ever think of me?

verses.collection: Manas Uttar: Ram's address to the citizens
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, now king, speaks to the people about the human life they have.
verses.sanskrit_display: फिरत सदा माया कर प्रेरा। काल कर्म सुभाव गुन घेरा॥ कबहुँक करि करुना नर देही। देत ईस बिनु हेतु सनेही ॥ नर तनु भव बारिधि कहुँ बेरो। सन्मुख मरुत अनुग्रह मेरो॥ करनधार सदगुर दृढ़ नावा। दुर्लभ साज सुलभ करि पावा ॥
verses.translation: Driven always by illusion, surrounded by time, karma, nature and the qualities, the soul wanders; then sometimes, out of compassion, God, a friend without a reason, gives it a human body. The human body is a boat for the ocean of becoming, my grace is the favourable wind, a true teacher is the steady helmsman: you have been given, easily, what is hard to get.
verses.line: This life is the boat, my grace the wind behind it, a good teacher at the helm.

verses.collection: Manas Uttar: Ram's address to the citizens
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram describes the simple devotee he is won over by.
verses.sanskrit_display: मोर दास कहाइ नर आसा। करइ तौ कहहु कहा बिस्वासा॥ बहुत कहउँ का कथा बढ़ाई। एहि आचरन बस्य मैं भाई ॥
verses.translation: If someone calls himself my servant and still hangs his hopes on others, tell me, what sort of trust is that? Why say more and lengthen the story: it is by this conduct that I am won, brothers.
verses.line: If you call yourself mine and still hang every hope on others, what kind of trust is that?
verses.misuse: Not 'never accept help from people'; it is about where the heart's final reliance rests. Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram continues: what makes someone dear to him is not status.
verses.sanskrit_display: भगति हीन बिरंचि किन होई। सब जीवहु सम प्रिय मोहि सोई॥ भगतिवंत अति नीचउ प्रानी। मोहि प्रानप्रिय असि मम बानी ॥
verses.translation: Even Brahma, without devotion, is dear to me only as any being is. A devoted creature, however lowly, is dear to me as life: this is my word.
verses.line: Without love, even the creator is just another being. With love, the lowliest is dear as life.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram's parable of a father with many sons.
verses.sanskrit_display: कोउ सर्बग्य धर्मरत कोई। सब पर पितहि प्रीति सम होई॥ कोउ पितु भगत बचन मन कर्मा। सपनेहुँ जान न दूसर धर्मा ॥ सो सुत प्रिय पितु प्रान समाना। जद्यपि सो सब भाँति अयाना॥ एहि बिधि जीव चराचर जेते। त्रिजग देव नर असुर समेते ॥
verses.translation: One is all-knowing, one devoted to duty; the father loves them all equally. But one son is devoted to his father in word, mind and deed, and in his dreams knows no other duty: that son is dear to his father as life, though he is unskilled in every way. In this same way are all beings, moving and unmoving, gods, humans and demons.
verses.line: The child who simply loves the father is dear to him as life, though skilled at nothing.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram ends his teaching to Kakbhushundi.
verses.sanskrit_display: पुरुष नपुंसक नारि वा जीव चराचर कोइ। सर्ब भाव भज कपट तजि मोहि परम प्रिय सोइ ॥
verses.translation: Man, woman or of any gender, any being that moves or does not move: whoever worships me with all their heart, giving up deceit, is supremely dear to me.
verses.line: Man, woman, any gender, any being: whoever loves me without deceit is supremely dear to me.

verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Having taught the crow, the child Ram goes back to being a baby and cries for his mother.
verses.sanskrit_display: देखि मातु आतुर उठि धाई। कहि मृदु बचन लिए उर लाई॥ गोद राखि कराव पय पाना। रघुपति चरित ललित कर गाना ॥
verses.translation: Seeing him, the mother rose anxiously and ran, spoke softly to him and held him to her heart. She kept him in her lap and fed him, singing of Raghupati's lovely deeds.
verses.line: The Lord of all cried for his mother, and she ran and held him close.

verses.collection: Manas Uttar: the jewel of devotion
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi compares knowledge to a lamp that can blow out, and devotion to a jewel.
verses.sanskrit_display: कहेउँ ग्यान सिद्धांत बुझाई। सुनहु भगति मनि कै प्रभुताई॥ राम भगति चिंतामनि सुंदर। बसइ गरुड़ जाके उर अंतर ॥ परम प्रकास रूप दिन राती। नहिं कछु चहिअ दिआ घृत बाती॥ मोह दरिद्र निकट नहिं आवा। लोभ बात नहिं ताहि बुझावा ॥
verses.translation: I have explained the principle of knowledge; now hear the power of the jewel of devotion. Devotion to Ram is a beautiful wish-granting gem, Garuda: in whose heart it lives, it is supreme light day and night, needing no lamp, ghee or wick. The poverty of delusion does not come near, and the wind of greed cannot blow it out.
verses.line: Devotion is a jewel that shines day and night; it needs no lamp, no oil, no wick.

verses.collection: Manas Uttar: the jewel of devotion
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi on how devotion reaches people.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम सिंधु घन सज्जन धीरा। चंदन तरु हरि संत समीरा॥ सब कर फल हरि भगति सुहाई। सो बिनु संत न काहूँ पाई ॥
verses.translation: Ram is the ocean, and the steady good are the clouds; Hari is the sandal tree, and the saints are the breeze. The fruit of everything is beautiful devotion to Hari, and no one has found it without the good.
verses.line: The ocean gives rain only through clouds; grace reaches us through good people.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva comments on Garuda's meeting with Kakbhushundi.
verses.sanskrit_display: गिरिजा संत समागम सम न लाभ कछु आन। बिनु हरि कृपा न होइ सो गावहिं बेद पुरान ॥
verses.translation: Girija, there is no gain like the company of saints; and it does not happen without Hari's grace, sing the Vedas and Puranas.
verses.line: No gain is like good company, and good company itself is a grace.

verses.speaker: Shiva / Tulsidas
verses.setting: The Manas ends with its simplest teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: एहिं कलिकाल न साधन दूजा। जोग जग्य जप तप ब्रत पूजा॥ रामहि सुमिरिअ गाइअ रामहि। संतत सुनिअ राम गुन ग्रामहि ॥
verses.translation: In this age of Kali there is no other means, no yoga, sacrifice, chanting, austerity, vow or ritual worship: remember Ram, sing Ram, and always listen to the qualities of Ram.
verses.line: Remember Ram, sing Ram, keep listening to what is good in him.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: The closing prayer of the Ramcharitmanas.
verses.sanskrit_display: मो सम दीन न दीन हित तुम्ह समान रघुबीर। अस बिचारि रघुबंस मनि हरहु बिषम भव भीर ॥
verses.translation: There is no one as poor as I am, and no friend of the poor like you, Raghubir. Thinking this over, jewel of the Raghus, take away the heavy fear of the world.
verses.line: No one is as poor as me, and no one befriends the poor like you. Take this fear away.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: The very last doha of the Ramcharitmanas.
verses.sanskrit_display: कामिहि नारि पिआरि जिमि लोभिहि प्रिय जिमि दाम। तिमि रघुनाथ निरंतर प्रिय लागहु मोहि राम ॥
verses.translation: As a woman is dear to a man full of desire, and as money is dear to a greedy man, so, Raghunath, may you be dear to me always, Ram.
verses.line: As money is dear to the greedy, may you be that dear to me, always.

verses.collection: Valmiki Yuddha: Ram takes in Vibhishana
verses.speaker: Ram (quoting the sage Kandu)
verses.setting: Ram cites an old teaching on protecting whoever asks for shelter.
verses.sanskrit_display: आतॊ वा यदि वा दृप्तः परेषां शरणं गतः। अरिः प्राणान्परित्यज्य रक्षितव्यः कृतात्मना॥
verses.translation: Whether in distress or in pride, an enemy who has come to you for shelter must be protected by a person of steady mind, even at the cost of his own life.
verses.line: Whoever comes to you for shelter, frightened or proud, even a former enemy: protect them.

verses.collection: Valmiki Yuddha: Ram takes in Vibhishana
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram recalls the story of the dove who sheltered the hunter who had caught its mate.
verses.sanskrit_display: स हि तं प्रतिजग्राह भार्याहर्तारमागतम्। कपोतो वानरश्रेष्ठ किंपुनर्मद्विधो जनः॥
verses.translation: That dove received even the one who had carried off its mate when he came to it. If a dove could do that, best of monkeys, how much more a person like me?
verses.line: A dove sheltered even the one who took its mate. How much more should I?

verses.collection: Valmiki Yuddha: Ram takes in Vibhishana
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Ram answers Vibhishana's surrender.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ वचसा सान्त्वयित्वैनं लोचनाभ्यां पिबनिव।
verses.translation: Hearing his words, Ram spoke to him, comforting him with words and seeming to drink him in with his eyes.
verses.line: He comforted him with words and looked at him as if drinking him in with his eyes.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram sends his friends home after his coronation.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं च नित्यशो राजन्सुग्रीवसहितस्त्वया। स्मर्तव्यः परया प्रीत्या गच्छ त्वं विगतज्वरः॥
verses.translation: And my only request, king, is that you always remember me, and Sugriva, with great love. Go now, free from distress.
verses.line: My only request: remember me with love. Now go, free of worry.

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman explains why he wants to keep hearing Ram's story.
verses.sanskrit_display: तच्छ्रुत्वाहं ततो वीर तव चर्यामृतं प्रभो। उत्कण्ठां तां हरिष्यामि मेघलेखामिवानलिः॥
verses.translation: Hearing the nectar of your deeds, hero, Lord, I will clear away my longing for you, as the wind scatters a bank of clouds.
verses.line: Hearing your story will clear my longing for you, as wind clears the clouds.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram rises from his throne, embraces Hanuman and answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: एवमेतत्कपिश्रेष्ठ भविता नात्र संशयः। चरिष्यति कथा यावदेषा लोके च मामिका॥ तावचे भविता कीर्तिः शरीरेऽप्यसवस्तथा। लोका हि यावत्स्थास्यन्ति तावत्स्थास्यन्ति मे कथाः।। एकैकस्योपकारस्य प्राणान्दास्यामि ते कये। शेषस्येहोपकाराणां भवाम ऋणिनो वयम्॥ मदङ्गे जीर्णतां यातु यत्त्वयोपकृतं कपे। नरः प्रत्युपकाराणामापत्स्वायाति पात्रताम्।।२४
verses.translation: So it shall be, best of monkeys, without doubt. As long as my story is current in the world, your fame and your life will last. For each single service you have done me I would give my life, and for the rest we remain in your debt. May what you have done for me be digested within me; a person needs repaying only in times of trouble.
verses.line: For each kindness you did me I'd give my life. May you never be in trouble needing it repaid.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Lakshman, alone with Ram, asks to be taught.
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं प्रपन्नोऽस्मि पदाम्बुजं प्रभो भवापवर्गं तव योगिभावितम् । यथाञ्जसाज्ञानमपारवारिधिं सुखं तरिष्यामि तथानुशाधि माम् ॥
verses.translation: I take refuge at your lotus feet, Lord, which free one from the world and which yogis meditate on. Teach me so that I may easily and happily cross this endless ocean of ignorance.
verses.line: I take refuge at your feet. Teach me how to cross over, simply.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram closes his teaching to Lakshman.
verses.sanskrit_display: यः सेवते मामगुणं गुणात्परं हृदा कदा वा यदि वा गुणात्मकम् । सोऽहं स्वपादाञ्चितरेणुभिः स्पृशन् पुनाति लोकत्रितयं यथा रविः ॥
verses.translation: Whoever serves me in the heart, now and then, whether as beyond qualities or with qualities, becomes me; with the dust of his feet he purifies the three worlds, as the sun does.
verses.line: Whoever turns to me in the heart, even now and then, becomes a light like the sun.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, in a pada to Hanuman.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुमिरत संकट-सोच-व्रिमोचन, मूरति मोद-निधानकी॥ … तुलसी कपिकी कृपा-बिलोकनि, खानि सकल कल्यानकी॥
verses.translation: Remembering him frees one from trouble and worry; his form is a treasury of joy. Tulsi says: the monkey's kind glance is a mine of every blessing.
verses.line: Remember him and worry loosens. His kind glance is a mine of blessings.
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas asks Hanuman to forgive what he said in distress.
verses.sanskrit_display: अति आरत, अति स्वारथी, अति दीन-दुखारी। इनको बिलगु न मानिये, बोलहिं न बिचारी॥ … नाकहि आये नाथसों, साँसति भय भारी। कहि आयो, कीबी छमा, निज ओर निहारी॥
verses.translation: The very distressed, the very needy, the very poor and hurting: do not take offence at them; they speak without thinking. I had reached my limit, Lord; the suffering and fear were heavy. I said what I said; forgive me, looking at it from your side.
verses.line: Don't hold it against the hurting; they speak without thinking. Forgive me, looking from your side.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, after complaining harshly to Hanuman.
verses.sanskrit_display: कटु कहिये गाढे परे, सुनि समुझि सुसाई। करहिं अनभलेउ को भलो, आपनी भलाई॥
verses.translation: In hard straits one says bitter things; a good master hears, understands, and out of his own goodness does good even to the one who wronged him.
verses.line: In hard times we say bitter things. A good master understands and does good anyway.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas urges his own mind to remember the name.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुमिरु सनेहसों तू नाम रामरायको। संबल निसंबलको, सखा असहायको॥ १॥ भाग है अभागेहूको, गुन गुनहीनको। गाहक गरीबको, दयालु दानि दीनको॥ २॥ कुल अकुलीनको, सुन्यो है बेद साखि है। पाँगुरेको हाथ-पाँय, आँधरेको आँखि है॥३॥ माय-बाप भूखेको, अधार निराधारको।
verses.translation: Remember with love the name of King Ram: provision for the one with none, friend of the helpless; the fortune of the unfortunate, the merit of the meritless, a buyer for the poor, the kind giver to the needy; family for the one without family, the Veda bears witness; hands and feet for the lame, eyes for the blind; mother and father for the hungry, a support for the one with no support.
verses.line: Friend of the helpless, luck of the unlucky, mother and father to the hungry: remember that name.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas remembers how Ram first took him in.
verses.sanskrit_display: बूझ्यौ ज्यौ ही, कह्यो, मैं हूँ चेरो ह्वैहौ रावरो जू मेरो कोऊ कहूँ नाहि, चरन गहत हों। मींजो गुरु पीठ, अपनाइ गहि बाँह, बोलि सेबक-सुखद, सदा बिरद बहत हाौं॥
verses.translation: The moment he asked, I said: 'I will be your servant; I have no one anywhere,' and I held his feet. Like a teacher he patted my back, took me by the arm and made me his own, and called me; ever the one who gives joy to servants, he carries that name.
verses.line: I said: I have no one anywhere. He patted my back, took my arm, and made me his own.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas thanks God, then asks for one more thing.
verses.sanskrit_display: हरि! तुम बहुत अनुग्रह कीन्हों। साधन-धाम विबुध दुरलभ तनु, मोहि कृपा करि दीन्हों॥ … तुलसिदास येहि जीव मोह-रजु, जेहि बाँध्यो सोइ छोरै॥
verses.translation: Hari, you have been very kind: out of grace you gave me this body, home of every practice, which even the gods find hard to get. Tulsidas says: the rope of delusion that binds this soul, only the one who tied it can untie.
verses.line: The one who tied this knot is the one who can untie it.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas's prayer for steady love.
verses.sanskrit_display: यह बिनती रघुबीर गुसाई। और आस-बिस्वास-भरोसो, हरो जीव-जड़ताई॥ … कुटिल करम लै जाहि मोहि जहँ जहँ अपनी बरिआई। तहँँ तहँ जनि छिन छोह छाँड़ियो, कमठ-अंडकी नाई॥
verses.translation: This is my prayer, Raghubir, master: take away every other hope, trust and reliance, and the dullness of this soul. Wherever my crooked karma drags me by force, there do not leave off your care even for a moment, as the tortoise keeps watch over its eggs.
verses.line: Wherever my mistakes drag me, don't stop watching over me, as the tortoise watches her eggs.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: thieves in your house
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas complains that greed, anger and pride have broken into his heart.
verses.sanskrit_display: मम हृदय भवन प्रभु तोरा।तहँ बसे आइ बहु चोरा॥ … कह तुलसिदास सुनु रामा।लूटहिं तसकर तव धामा॥ ८॥ चिंता यह मोहिं अपारा। अपजस नहिं होइ तुम्हारा॥
verses.translation: My heart is your house, Lord, and many thieves have come and settled in it. Tulsidas says: listen, Ram, thieves are looting your home; my great worry is only that it will give you a bad name.
verses.line: My heart is your house, and thieves have moved in. Come and see to your own home.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: his hand on my head
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas longs for Ram's hand on his head.
verses.sanskrit_display: कबहुँ सो कर-सरोज रघुनायक ! धरिहौ नाथ सीस मेरे। जेहि कर अभय किये जन आरत, बारक बिबस नाम टेरे॥ … सीतल सुखद छाँह जेहि करकी, मेटति पाप, ताप, माया। निसि-बासर तेहि कर सरोजकी, चाहत तुलसिदास छाया॥
verses.translation: Will you ever place that lotus hand on my head, Raghunayak, the hand that made the distressed fearless when they once called your name helplessly? The cool, comforting shade of that hand removes wrongdoing, pain and illusion; day and night Tulsidas longs for the shade of that lotus hand.
verses.line: Will you ever rest that hand on my head? Day and night I long for its shade.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: I worry and I don't
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas explains why he both worries and doesn't.
verses.sanskrit_display: रामभद्र! मोहिं आपनो सोच है अरु नाहीं। जीव सकल संतापके भाजन जग माहीं॥ १॥ नातो बड़े समर्थ सों इक ओर किधौं हूँ तोको मोसे अति घने मोको एकै तूँ॥
verses.translation: Ramabhadra, I worry about myself, and I don't. Every soul in the world is a vessel of suffering. On one side is my bond with the great and mighty one, and on the other, I: you have many like me, but I have only you.
verses.line: I worry about myself, and I don't. You have many like me; I have only you.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: the court of the poor
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what makes Ram's court different.
verses.sanskrit_display: रघुबर! रावरि यहै बड़ाई। निदरि गनी आदर गरीबपर, करत कृपा अधिकाई॥ … यहि दरबार दीनको आदर, रीति सदा चलि आई
verses.translation: Raghubar, this is your greatness: passing over the rich, you honour the poor and show them more kindness. In this court the poor are respected; that has always been the custom here.
verses.line: In his court the rich are passed over and the poor are honoured. It has always been so.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas admits devotion is hard to live.
verses.sanskrit_display: रघुपति-भगति करत कठिनाई । कहत सुगम करनी अपार जानै सोइ जेहि बनि आई॥
verses.translation: Devotion to Raghupati is hard to practise. It is easy to talk about, but the doing is endless; only the one in whom it has taken root knows.
verses.line: Devotion is easy to talk about and hard to live. Only those who live it know.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: the life I hope to live
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas describes the life he hopes Ram's grace will one day give him.
verses.sanskrit_display: कबहुँक हौं यहि रहनि रहौंगो। श्रीरघुनाथ-कृपालु-कृपातें संत-सुभाव गहौंगो॥ ९॥ जथालाभसंतोष सदा, काहू सों कछु न चहांगो। पर-हित-निरत निरंतर, मन क्रम बचन नेम निबहौंगो॥ … परुष बचन अति दुसह श्रवन सुनि तेहि पावक न दहांगो। बिगत मान, सम सीतल मन, पर-गुन नहिं दोष कहाँगो॥ ३॥ परिहरि देह-जनित चिंता, दुख-सुख समबुद्धि सहोंगो।
verses.translation: Will I ever live like this? By the grace of kind Raghunath, will I take on the nature of a saint: always content with what comes, wanting nothing from anyone, always devoted to others' good, keeping my vow in mind, deed and word; hearing very harsh words and not burning in that fire; free of pride, even and cool of mind, speaking of others' virtues and not their faults; letting go of the body's worries, bearing joy and sorrow with an even mind?
verses.line: Will I ever live like this: content, kind, cool when insulted, speaking of others' good, not their faults?

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas's vow of love.
verses.sanskrit_display: जो तुम त्यागों राम हौं तौ नहिं त्यागो । परिहरि पाँय काहि अनुरागों॥ … हौं तो कुजाचक, स्वामी सुदाता । हौं कुपूत, तुम हितु पितु-माता॥
verses.translation: Even if you leave me, Ram, I will not leave you; leaving your feet, whom would I love? I am a poor beggar and you the good giver; I am a bad son, and you my loving father and mother.
verses.line: Even if you leave me, Ram, I won't leave you. You are my father and mother.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas compares himself to Sugriva, hiding from Bali.
verses.sanskrit_display: केहू भाँति कृपासिंधु मेरी ओर हेरिये। मोको और ठौर न, सुटेक एक तेरिये॥ … करम-कपीस बालि-बली, त्रास-त्रस्यो हौं। चाहत अनाथ-नाथ! तेरी बाह बस्यो हौं॥
verses.translation: Somehow, ocean of kindness, look my way; I have no other place, my one firm support is you. Like Sugriva terrified of mighty Bali, I am terrified of my karma; lord of the helpless, I want to live in the shelter of your arm.
verses.line: Like Sugriva hiding from Bali, I'm afraid. Somehow, look my way; let me live under your arm.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, out of ideas, leaves it to Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: बाप! बलि जाउँ, आप करिये उपाउ सो। तेरे ही निहारे परै हारेहू सुदाउ सो॥४॥ तेरे ही सुझाये सूझै असुझ सुझाउ सो। तेरे ही बुझाये बूझै अबुझ बुझाउ सो॥
verses.translation: Father, I give myself to you: you find the way. By your glance alone a losing throw becomes a winning one; by your showing, what cannot be seen is seen; by your explaining, what cannot be understood is understood.
verses.line: By your glance a losing throw turns into a winning one.
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: walk on saying Ram
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A walking song: the road of life as a long, hard journey.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम कहत चलु, राम कहत चलु, राम कहत चलु भाई रे। नाहिं तौ भव-बेगारि महँ परिहै, छुटत अति कठिनाई रे॥ … मारग अगम, संग नहिं संबल, नाउँ गाउँकर भूला रे। तुलसिदास भव त्रास हरहु अब, होहु राम अनुकूला रे॥
verses.translation: Walk on saying Ram, walk on saying Ram, walk on saying Ram, brother; otherwise you'll be caught in the forced labour of the world, and getting free is very hard. The road is hard, there are no provisions with me, I've forgotten the name of my village. Tulsidas says: take away the fear of the world now, be kind to me, Ram.
verses.line: The road is hard and I've lost my way. Walk on, saying Ram.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: the one true friend
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what happens once someone takes shelter in the name.
verses.sanskrit_display: कैसेउ पाँवर पातकी, जेहि लई नामकी ओट। गाँठी बाँध्यो दाम तो, परख्यो न फेरि खर-खोट॥
verses.translation: However low or sinful a person, once they took the shelter of the name, he tied them into his cloth like a coin and never again tested whether it was true or false.
verses.line: Once you take his shelter, he ties you in his cloth like a coin and never tests you again.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: what is life for
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas questions a life lived only for oneself.
verses.sanskrit_display: लाभ कहा मानुष-तनु पाये। काय-बचन-मन सपनेहुँ कबहुँक घटत न काज पराये॥
verses.translation: What is gained by getting a human body, if in body, word and mind, not even in a dream, one ever helps with someone else's work?
verses.line: What is a human life for, if we never help with someone else's load?

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: if there were anyone else
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas explains why he keeps bringing his troubles to Ram.
verses.sanskrit_display: जो पै दूसरो कोउ होइ। तौ हौं बारहि बार प्रभु कत दुख सुनावौं रोइ॥ … आपसे कहुँ सौंपिये मोहि जो पै अतिहि घिनात। दासतुलसी और बिधि क्यों चरन परिहरि जात॥
verses.translation: If there were anyone else, why would I keep coming back, Lord, to cry my troubles to you? If you find me too distasteful, then hand me over to someone like yourself. How else could Tulsidas leave your feet?
verses.line: If there were anyone else, why would I keep coming to you in tears?

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on his own trust, without judging anyone else's.
verses.sanskrit_display: भरोसो जाहि दूसरो सो करो। मोको तो रामको नाम कलपतरु कलि कल्यान फरो॥ … प्रीति-प्रतीति जहाँ जाकी, तहँ ताको काज सरो। मेरे तो माय-बाप दोउ आखर, हौं सिसु-अरनि अरो॥
verses.translation: Let whoever trusts something else trust it; for me, Ram's name is the wishing tree that bears good fruit in this age. Where a person's love and trust lie, there their work gets done. For me, those two syllables are mother and father, and I am a stubborn child who has dug in his heels.
verses.line: Where your love and trust are, your work gets done. For me those two syllables are mother and father.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas remembers his years as a begging orphan.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाम राम रावरोई हित मेरे। स्वारथ-परमारथ साथिन्ह सों भुज उठाइ कहाँ टेरे॥ … फिरयौ ललात बिनु नाम उदर लगि, दुखउ दुखित मोहि हेरे। नाम-प्रसाद लहत रसाल-फल अब हौं बबुर बहेरे॥
verses.translation: Ram, your name alone is my well-wisher; I say it to all my companions in this life and the next, arms raised. Without the name I wandered, longing for something to fill my belly; even sorrow felt sorry when it looked at me. By the grace of the name, I who was a thorny babul now get mangoes.
verses.line: I wandered hungry; even sorrow pitied me. By the grace of the name, I now bear sweet fruit.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on whose bread he has lived on.
verses.sanskrit_display: गरैगी जीह जो कहौं औरको हौं। जानकी-जीवन! जनम-जनम जग ज्यायो तिहारेहि कौरको हों॥ … तुलसिदास सीतल नित यहि बल, बड़े ठेकाने ठौरको हौं॥
verses.translation: My tongue would rot if I called myself anyone else's. Life of Janaki, birth after birth in this world I have lived on your morsel. Tulsidas is always at peace on this strength: I belong to a great place.
verses.line: I am always at peace on this strength: I belong somewhere great.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on who is truly good in Ram's eyes.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोइ सुकृती, सुचि साँचो जाहि राम! तुम रीझे। गनिका, गीध, बधिक हरिपुर गये, लै कासी प्रयाग कब सीझे॥ … तुलसी सहज सनेह राम बस, और सबै जलकी चिकनाई॥
verses.translation: He alone is virtuous, pure and true with whom you, Ram, are pleased. The courtesan, the vulture and the hunter went to Hari's abode; when were they ever made perfect by Kashi or Prayag? Tulsi says: Ram is won by natural love; everything else is like oil on water.
verses.line: Ram is won by plain, natural love. Everything else just floats on top.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what makes Ram different from every other protector.
verses.sanskrit_display: दीनबंधु ! दूरि किये दीनको न दूसरी सरन। आपको भले हैं सब, आपनेको कोऊ कहूँ, सबको भलो है राम! रावरो चरन॥
verses.translation: Friend of the poor, if you push the poor away they have no other refuge. Everyone is good to their own people, and someone somewhere is good to their own; but your feet, Ram, are good to everyone.
verses.line: Everyone is good to their own. Your feet, Ram, are good to everyone.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: the more I try
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas admits that trying harder seems to push him further away.
verses.sanskrit_display: ज्यों ज्यों निकट भयो चहं कृपालु ! त्यों त्यों दूरि परयो हौं। तुम चहुँ जुग रस एक राम ! हौं हूँ राबरो, जदपि अघ अवगुननि भरो हौं॥
verses.translation: The more I try to come near, kind one, the further away I fall. You are the same in all four ages, Ram; and I too am yours, though I am full of wrongs and faults.
verses.line: The more I try to come close, the further I fall. Still, I am yours.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas lies down at Ram's door like a stubborn child.
verses.sanskrit_display: पन करि हौं हठि आजुतें रामद्वार परयो हौं। “तू मेरो' यह बिन कहे उठिहाँ न जनमभरि, प्रभुकी सौंकरि निरयो हौं॥
verses.translation: I have made a vow: from today I lie stubbornly at Ram's door. I will not get up my whole life until you say 'you are mine'; I swear by the Lord, I have lain down here.
verses.line: I've lain down at your door. I won't get up until you say: you are mine.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas describes how he will know he has been accepted.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम अपनायो तब जानिहौं, जब मन फिरि परिहै। जेहि सुभाव बिषयनि लग्यो, तेहि सहज नाथ सौं नेह छाडि छल करिंहै॥ … प्रभु-गुन सुनि मन हरषिहै, नीर नयननि ढरिहै। तुलसिदास भयो रामको बिस्वास, प्रेम लखि आनँद उमगि उर भरिहै॥
verses.translation: I'll know you have made me your own when my mind turns around: when, with the same ease with which it clung to pleasures, it loves the Lord without deceit. Hearing the Lord's qualities the mind will rejoice, tears will flow from the eyes; Tulsidas will trust Ram, and seeing that love, joy will well up and fill the heart.
verses.line: I'll know you've accepted me when my heart turns toward you as easily as it once turned away.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas remembers begging and being ignored, and what the saints told him.
verses.sanskrit_display: द्वार द्वार दीनता कही, काढ़ि रद, परि पाहूँ। हैं दयालु दुनी दस दिसा, दुख-दोष-दलन-छम, कियो न सँभाषन काहूँ॥ … दुखित देखि संतन कह्यो, सोचै जनि मन माँहू। तोसे पसु-पाँवर-पातकी परिहरे न सरन गये, रघुबर ओर बिनाहूँ॥ ३॥ तुलसी तिहारो भये भयो सुखी प्रीति-प्रतीति बिनाहू। नामकी महिमा, सील नाथको, मेरो भलो बिलोकि अब तें सकुचाहुँ, सिहाहूँ॥
verses.translation: Door to door I told my need, teeth bared, falling at feet; there are kind people in all ten directions, able to end sorrow and fault, and not one spoke to me. Seeing my sorrow, the saints said: 'Don't worry in your heart. The Lord of Raghus has not cast off even beasts, low ones and sinners like you once they took refuge, even without any other side.' Tulsi became yours and was happy, even without love or trust. The glory of the name, the Lord's gentleness: seeing my good fortune now, I am both shy and amazed.
verses.line: Door to door, no one spoke to me. Then good people said: don't worry; he turns no one away.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on the one good thing he has.
verses.sanskrit_display: है तुलसी कें एक गुन अवगुन निधि कहैं लोग। भलो भरोसो रावरो राम रीझिले जोग॥
verses.translation: People call Tulsi a treasury of faults, but he has one virtue: a good trust in you, Ram, which is fit to please you.
verses.line: People call me a heap of faults. I have one virtue: I trust you.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A doha on what love for Ram produces.
verses.sanskrit_display: सूधे मन सूधे बचन सूधी सब करतूति। तुलसी सूधी सकल बिधि रघुबर प्रेम प्रसूति॥
verses.translation: A straight mind, straight words, straight deeds in everything: Tulsi says, all this straightness is born of love for Raghubar.
verses.line: A straight heart, straight words, straight deeds: that is what love for God gives birth to.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A doha on home and renunciation.
verses.sanskrit_display: घर कोन्हें घर जात है घर छाँड़े घर जाइ। तुलसी घर बन बीचहीं राम प्रेम पुर छाइ॥
verses.translation: Making a home, the true home is lost; leaving home, home is lost too. Tulsi says: between home and forest, settle in the city of Ram's love.
verses.line: Clinging to home loses it, fleeing home loses it too. Live in between, in the city of love.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: The opening of Tulsidas's famous chataka (rain-bird) dohas.
verses.sanskrit_display: एक भरोसो एक बल एक आस बिस्वास । एक राम घन स्याम हित चातक तुलसीदास॥
verses.translation: One trust, one strength, one hope and faith: for the chataka Tulsidas, the one dark cloud, Ram, is his friend.
verses.line: One trust, one strength, one hope: like the rain-bird waiting for its one cloud.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A chataka doha: hope that does not depend on being answered.
verses.sanskrit_display: जौ घन बरषे समय सिर जौँ भरि जनम उदास। तुलसी या चित चातकहि तऊ तिहारी आस॥
verses.translation: Whether the cloud rains on time, or stays indifferent my whole life, Tulsi says: this chataka heart still hopes in you.
verses.line: Whether you answer on time or stay silent my whole life, my heart still hopes in you.
