verses.misuse: About trust in God through unanswered seasons; not a reason to stay where a person ignores your needs.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A doha on betrayal.
verses.sanskrit_display: जासु भरोसें सोइऐे राखि गोद में सीस। तुलसी तासु कुचाल तें रखवारो जगदीस॥
verses.translation: When the one you trusted enough to sleep with your head in their lap turns on you, Tulsi says, the Lord of the world is your guardian.
verses.line: When the person you trusted most turns on you, the Lord of the world still guards you.
verses.misuse: Comfort after betrayal; it does not replace getting real-world help or protection.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A doha on Hanuman's devotion.
verses.sanskrit_display: साहब तें सेवक बड़ो जो निज धरम सुजान। राम बाँधि उतरे उदधि लाँघि गए हनुमान॥
verses.translation: The servant who knows his own duty is greater than the master: Ram had to build a bridge to cross the ocean; Hanuman simply leapt across.
verses.line: Ram had to build a bridge to cross the sea. Hanuman, out of love, simply leapt.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram treats his people's faults.
verses.sanskrit_display: अपराध अगाध भएँ जनते, अपने उर आनत नाहिन जू।
verses.translation: Even when his people commit faults beyond measure, he does not take them into his heart.
verses.line: Even when we fail beyond measure, he does not hold it in his heart.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on Ram's way with the hurting.
verses.sanskrit_display: आरत, दीन, अनाथनको रघुनाथु करैं निज हाथकी छाहें॥
verses.translation: For the hurting, the poor and those with no one, Raghunath makes shade with his own hand.
verses.line: For the hurting and the alone, he makes shade with his own hand.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas names everything Ram is to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: रामु हैं मातु, पिता, गुरु, बंधु, औ संगी, सखा, सुतु, स्वामि, सनेही। रामको सौंह, भरोसो है रामको, राम रंँग्यो, रुचि राच्यो न केही॥
verses.translation: Ram is my mother, father, teacher, brother, companion, friend, son, master and beloved. I swear by Ram, my trust is in Ram; I am coloured by Ram, and my heart is taken by no one else.
verses.line: Ram is my mother, father, teacher, brother, friend, child and beloved. My trust is in him.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what life is for, in his own view.
verses.sanskrit_display: मति रामहि सों, गति रामहि सों, रति रामसों, रामहि को बलु है। सबकी न कहै, तुलसीके मतें इतनो जग जीवनको फलु है॥
verses.translation: My mind is with Ram, my goal is with Ram, my love is for Ram, Ram is my strength. I don't speak for everyone; in Tulsi's view, this much is the fruit of living in the world.
verses.line: I don't speak for everyone. For me, this is the fruit of a life: my heart with Ram.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas recalls Prahlad, unharmed by poison, fire and elephants.
verses.sanskrit_display: नेकु बिषादु नहीं प्रहलादहि कारन केहरिके बल हो रे। कौनकी त्रास करै तुलसी जो पै राखिहै राम, तौ मारिहै को रे॥
verses.translation: Prahlad felt not the least despair, because of the strength of the man-lion. Whom should Tulsi fear? If Ram protects, who can kill?
verses.line: If Ram is protecting, whom should I fear?
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas imagines being lost in a wilderness of dangers.
verses.sanskrit_display: संकट कोटि जहाँ 'तुलसी', सुत, मातु, पिता, हित, बंधु न नेरे॥ राखिहैँ रामु कृपालु तहाँ, हनुमानु-से सेवक हैं जेहि केरे। नाक, रसातल, भूतलमें रघुनायकु एकु सहायकु मेरे॥
verses.translation: Where there are a million dangers, Tulsi, and no son, mother, father, friend or kin is near, kind Ram will protect you there, he who has a servant like Hanuman. In heaven, the underworld or on earth, Raghunayak is my one helper.
verses.line: Where a million dangers surround you and no family is near, he is still there, with Hanuman.
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas describes his own life before grace.
verses.sanskrit_display: उँचो मनु, ऊँची रुचि, भागु नीचो निपट ही, लोकरीति-लायक न, लंगर लबारु है। स्वारथु अगमु, परमारथकी कहा चली, पेटकी कठिन जगु जीवको जबारु है॥ चाकरी न आकरी, न खेती, न बनिज-भीरख, जानत न कूर कछु किसब कबारु है। तुलसीकी बाजी राखी रामहीकें नाम,
verses.translation: A high mind, high tastes, and very low luck; no good at worldly ways, a stubborn talker. Selfish gain was out of reach, never mind higher goals; the belly's demands are hard on every living being. No job, no mine, no farm, no trade, no begging; the fool knows no craft or skill. Tulsi's game was saved by Ram's name alone.
verses.line: High hopes, low luck, no job, no trade, no skill. The name of Ram saved my game.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on where Ram can be found.
verses.sanskrit_display: आरतपाल कृपाल जो रामु जेहीं सुमिरे तेहिको तहँ ठाढ़े।
verses.translation: Kind Ram, protector of the hurting: wherever anyone remembers him, there he stands.
verses.line: Wherever anyone remembers him, there he stands.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram responds to his name.
verses.sanskrit_display: अंतरजामिहुतें बड़े बाहेरजामि हैं राम, जे नाम लियेतें। धावत धेनु पेन्हाइ लवाई ज्यों बालक-बोलनि कान कियेतें॥
verses.translation: Greater than the Ram who dwells within is the Ram outside, who comes when his name is called: he runs the way a cow runs, milk flowing, when she hears her calf's cry.
verses.line: Call his name and he comes running, like a cow who hears her calf cry.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Prahlad, his father's sword raised over him.
verses.sanskrit_display: काढ़ि कृपान, कृपा न कहूँ, पितु काल कराल बिलोकि न भागे। “राम कहाँ ?' “सब ठाउँ हें', 'खंभमें ?' ' हा' सुनि हाँक नृकेहरि जागे॥
verses.translation: Sword drawn, no mercy anywhere, the boy did not run on seeing his terrible father. 'Where is Ram?' 'Everywhere.' 'In this pillar?' 'Yes.' Hearing that cry, the man-lion awoke.
verses.line: 'Where is your God?' 'Everywhere.' 'In this pillar?' 'Yes.'

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, after Vibhishan's refuge, on who is welcome.
verses.sanskrit_display: गये राम सरन सबकौ भलो। गनी-गरीब, बड़ो-छोटो, बुध-मूढु, हीनबल-अतिबलो॥ १ ॥ पंगु-अंध, निरगुनी-निसंबल, जो न लहै जाचे जलो। सो निबह्यो नीके, जो जनमि जग राम-राजमारग चलो॥
verses.translation: Whoever goes to Ram for refuge is well: rich or poor, great or small, wise or foolish, weak or very strong. The lame, the blind, those without virtue or provision, who do not get water even when they ask: whoever was born in the world and walked Ram's royal road was looked after well.
verses.line: Rich or poor, wise or foolish, weak or strong: whoever goes to him for refuge is held.

verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan explains why he does not list his troubles.
verses.sanskrit_display: जानत प्रभु दुख-सुख दासनिको, तातें कहि न सुनायो। करि करुना भरि नयन बिलोकहु, तब जानौं अपनायो॥
verses.translation: The Lord knows the joys and sorrows of his servants, so I have not told mine. Look at me with eyes full of kindness; then I'll know you have made me your own.
verses.line: You know my sorrows, so I won't list them. Just look at me kindly, and I'll know I'm yours.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram tells his friends his natural way with those who come to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: सब बिधि हीन-दीन, अति जड़मति जाको कतहुँ न ठाउँ। आयो सरन भजौं, न तजौँ तिहि, यह जानत रिपिराठ॥ … पुनि पुनि भुजा उठाइ कहत हौं, सकल सभा पतिआउ। नहि कोऊ प्रिय मोहि दास सम, कपट-प्रीति बहि जाउ॥
verses.translation: Lacking in every way, poor, very slow-witted, with no place anywhere: if such a one comes for refuge, I care for him and never abandon him; the great sages know this. Again and again I raise my arm and say it, let the whole assembly believe me: no one is as dear to me as my servant; let false love be swept away.
verses.line: Whoever comes with nothing and nowhere to go, I take in and never abandon. I say it, arm raised.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Lakshman lies struck down; Ram, exhausted, speaks to Sugriva.
verses.sanskrit_display: मेरो सब पुरुषारथ थाको। बिपति बँटावन बंधु-बाहु बिनु करौं भरोसो काको॥ … गिरि, कानन जैहें साखा-मृग, हौं पुनि अनुज-सँघाती। ह्वैहै कहा बिभीषनकी गति रही सोच भरि छाती॥
verses.translation: All my strength is spent. Without my brother's arm to share my trouble, whom can I rely on? The monkeys will go back to their hills and forests, and I will go with my brother; but my chest is full of one worry: what will become of Vibhishan?
verses.line: All my strength is spent. And still my chest is full of worry for the one who came to me.
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a specific outcome, and it doesn't replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas describes Hanuman's nature.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुलिस-कठोरतनु जोरपै रोर रन, करुना-कलित मन धारमिक धीरको॥ दुर्जजको कालसो कराल पाल सज्जनको, सुमरि हरनहार तुलसीकी पीरको। सीय-सुखदायक दुलारो रघुनायको, सेवक सहायक है साहसी समीरको॥
verses.translation: A body hard as a thunderbolt, a roar in battle, yet a mind full of compassion, righteous and steady. Terrible to the wicked, protector of the good: remembering him takes away Tulsi's pain. Giver of joy to Sita, darling of Raghunayak, the brave son of the wind is the helper of servants.
verses.line: A body like iron, a heart full of compassion. Remembering him eases my pain.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what Hanuman is to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: रामके गुलामनिको कामतरु रामदूत, मोसे दीन दूबरेको तकिया तिहारिये॥
verses.translation: Messenger of Ram, wishing tree for Ram's servants: for a poor, weak one like me, you are the pillow I lean on.
verses.line: For someone as weak as me, you are the pillow I lean on.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas remembers his begging childhood.
verses.sanskrit_display: टूकनिको घर-घर डोलत कंगाल बोलि, बाल ज्यों कृपाल नतपाल पालि पोसो है। कोन्ही है संभार सार अंजनीकुमार बीर, आपनो बिसारिं न मेरेहू भरोसो है॥
verses.translation: A beggar going house to house for scraps: the kind protector of those who bow called me and raised me like his own child. Brave son of Anjani, you took care of me; do not forget your own, I trust in you too.
verses.line: I went door to door for scraps. You called me and raised me like your own child.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas in severe pain in his arm.
verses.sanskrit_display: औषध अनेक जंंत्र-मंत्र-टोटकादि किये, बदि भये देवता मनाये अधिकाति है॥ … चेरो तेरो तुलसी तू मेरो कह्यो रामदूत, ढील तेरी बीर मोहि पीरतें पिराति है॥
verses.translation: I tried many medicines, charms and remedies, prayed to the gods; it only got worse. Tulsi is your servant; you said 'you are mine', messenger of Ram. Your delay hurts me more than the pain.
verses.line: I've tried every medicine; it keeps getting worse. Your delay hurts more than the pain.
verses.misuse: An honest prayer in illness, not advice to stop treatment. Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas admits the wrong turns of his life.
verses.sanskrit_display: खोटे-खोटे आचरन आचरत अपनायो, अंजनीकुमार सोध्यो रामपानि पाक हौं।
verses.translation: Even while I did bad things, you took me as your own; son of Anjani, you cleansed me and made me fit for Ram's hand.
verses.line: Even while I was doing wrong, you took me as your own and made me fit for Ram.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna, afraid of failing halfway on the inner path, turns to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit_display: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥
verses.translation: Krishna, please cut away this doubt of mine completely. No one but you can remove it.
verses.line: Only you can clear this doubt completely. There is no one else I can ask.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna opens the teaching on knowing him fully.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
verses.translation: Hear, Partha, how with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking refuge in me, you will know me fully, without doubt.
verses.line: Keep your mind attached to me, lean on me, keep practising. You will come to know me fully.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna explains how everything holds together in him.
verses.sanskrit_display: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
verses.translation: There is nothing higher than me, Dhananjaya. All this is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
verses.line: Everything is strung on me like pearls on a single thread.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna has named four kinds of people who turn to him, including the distressed and the one in need.
verses.sanskrit_display: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
verses.translation: All of these are generous souls, but the wise one I regard as my very self, for with mind steadfast he has taken me as the highest goal.
verses.line: Everyone who turns to me, even in need, is noble. The one who loves me is my very self.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna explains how all beings rest in him without being cramped.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् । तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥
verses.translation: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, know that all beings rest in me.
verses.line: As the wind, wherever it blows, always rests in the sky, all beings rest in me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna begins chapter 10, speaking to Arjuna as to someone he loves.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥
verses.translation: Listen once more, mighty-armed, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your good, because you delight in it and are dear to me.
verses.line: Listen again. I am telling you this for your good, because you are dear to me.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Having seen Krishna's greatness, Arjuna remembers years of casual friendship.
verses.sanskrit_display: यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसिविहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु । एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षंतत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, Achyuta, I ask forgiveness of you, the immeasurable.
verses.line: For every careless joke, every time I took you for granted, alone or in company, forgive me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: After the vision, Krishna says what alone makes it possible.
verses.sanskrit_display: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन । ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥
verses.translation: But by undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known like this, seen in truth, and entered into, scorcher of foes.
verses.line: By a love that looks nowhere else, I can truly be known, seen, and entered.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna has asked which devotee is best: lover of the personal God or seeker of the formless.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥
verses.translation: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, ever united, with supreme faith, I consider the most united with me.
verses.line: Those who rest their mind in me, always, with deep trust, I count as closest to me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes those whom he lifts out of the sea of mortality (12.7).
verses.sanskrit_display: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
verses.translation: But those who lay all their actions in me, intent on me, and worship me meditating with single-minded yoga — for them, whose minds are set on me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.
verses.line: Lay your work in me and keep your mind on me; I soon lift you out of the drowning sea.

verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Exiled in the forest, with ten thousand hungry sages arriving and no food left, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: कृष्णकृष्ण महाबाहो देवकीनन्दनाव्यय / वासुदेव जगन्नाथ प्रणतार्तिविनाशन
verses.translation: Krishna, Krishna, mighty-armed son of Devaki, imperishable one, Vasudeva, lord of the world, you who destroy the pain of those who bow to you.
verses.line: Krishna, Krishna... you who take away the pain of everyone who bows to you.
verses.misuse: Calling on God in a crisis is prayer, not a promise that help will come in a particular form or time.

verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi's prayer when Durvasa's sages come to be fed and the pot is empty.
verses.sanskrit_display: वरेण्य वरदानन्त अगतीनां गतिप्रद / पुराणपुरुष प्राणमनोवृत्त्याद्यगोचर
verses.translation: Most worthy, giver of boons, endless one, you who give a way to those who have no way; ancient Person, beyond the reach of breath, mind and thought.
verses.line: You give a way to those who have no way.
verses.misuse: A way, not necessarily the one we wanted; keep taking practical steps too.

verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi's prayer in the forest, with no food and no one to turn to.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वाध्यक्ष पराध्यक्ष त्वामहं शरणं गता / पाहि मां कृपया देव शरणागतवत्सल
verses.translation: Overseer of all, highest overseer, I have come to you for refuge. Protect me in your kindness, O God, you who love those who come for refuge.
verses.line: I have come to you for shelter. Look after me with kindness; you love those who come to you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: After the sages have fled, Krishna explains why he came.
verses.sanskrit_display: भवतामापदं ज्ञात्वा ऋषेः परमकोपनात् / द्रौपद्या चिन्तितः पार्था अहं सत्वरमागतः
verses.translation: Knowing your danger from that very wrathful sage, and because Draupadi thought of me, sons of Pritha, I came quickly.
verses.line: I knew you were in trouble. Draupadi thought of me, so I came quickly.
verses.misuse: Not a promise that every prayer is answered the same day; it shows that being thought of moves him.

verses.speaker: the Pandavas and Draupadi
verses.setting: Relieved after Krishna saves them from Durvasa's anger.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वया नाथेन गोविन्द दुस्तरामापदं विभो / तीर्णाः प्लवमिवासाद्य मज्जमाना महार्णवे
verses.translation: With you as our protector, Govinda, lord, we have crossed this impassable danger, like the drowning who reach a boat in the great ocean.
verses.line: With you beside us we got through it, like drowning people who reach a boat.

verses.collection: Vana: Krishna in the Kamyaka forest
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna visits the exiled Pandavas in the Kamyaka forest; Arjuna has just praised him.
verses.sanskrit_display: ममैव त्वं तवैवाहं ये मदीयास्तवैव ते / यस्त्वां द्वेष्टि स मां द्वेष्टि यस्त्वामनु स मामनु
verses.translation: You are mine alone, and I am yours; those who are mine are yours. Whoever hates you hates me; whoever follows you follows me.
verses.line: You are mine and I am yours. Whoever is mine is yours.

verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Before Krishna's peace mission, Draupadi recalls the dice-hall, where her husbands sat silent.
verses.sanskrit_display: निरमर्षेष्वचेष्टेषु प्रेक्ष्यमाणेषु पाण्डुषु / पाहि मामिति गोविन्द मनसा चिन्तितोसि मे
verses.translation: While the sons of Pandu sat without anger or movement, only watching, I thought of you in my mind, Govinda: 'Protect me!'
verses.line: When those who should have protected me only watched, I called to you in my heart: protect me.
verses.misuse: Draupadi's inner prayer did not replace speaking up: she also challenged the whole court. Prayer is not a reason to stay silent about abuse.

verses.speaker: Vaishampayana
verses.setting: Bhishma, dying on the bed of arrows after the war, begins his hymn to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit_display: भीष्मस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रः कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / शरतल्पगतः कृष्णं प्रदध्यौ प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः
verses.translation: Bhishma, tiger among men, lying on the bed of arrows, pure, with folded hands, fixed his thoughts on Krishna in deed, mind and word.
verses.line: Lying on a bed of arrows, Bhishma folded his hands and turned his whole mind to Krishna.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Near the end of Bhishma's hymn to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit_display: अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पीतवाससमच्युतम् / ये नमस्यन्ति गोविन्दं न तेषां विद्यते भयम्
verses.translation: Those who bow to Govinda, the unfailing one, dark like the flax flower and dressed in yellow, have no fear.
verses.line: Those who bow to Govinda, dark as a flax flower and dressed in yellow, have nothing to fear.
verses.misuse: Fear may still come; devotion is a refuge within it, not a guarantee against bad events.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: From the closing verses of Bhishma's hymn.
verses.sanskrit_display: नमो नरकसंत्रासरक्षामण्डलकारिणे / संसारनिम्नगावर्ततरिकाष्ठाय विष्णवे
verses.translation: Salutations to Vishnu, who draws a protective circle against the terror of hell, the log to cling to in the whirlpools of the river of worldly life.
verses.line: He is the piece of wood to hold on to in the whirlpools of life.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: From the closing verses of Bhishma's hymn.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राणकान्तारपाथेयं संसारोच्छेदभेषजम् / दुःखशोकपरित्राणं हरिरित्यक्षरद्वयम्॥]
verses.translation: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.
verses.line: Food for the long road, medicine, rescue from grief: just two syllables, Ha-ri.
verses.misuse: The name as a place to rest, not a cure that replaces medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma ends his hymn to Krishna, his life's work done, his body pierced by arrows.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वां प्रपन्नाय भक्ताय गतिमिष्टां जिगीषवे / यच्छ्रेयः पुण्डरीकाक्ष तद्ध्यायस्व सुरोत्तम
verses.translation: For the devotee who has taken refuge in you and longs to reach the goal he wants, think, lotus-eyed one, best of gods, of whatever is truly good for him.
verses.line: I've come to you. Whatever is truly best for me, you think of it.
verses.misuse: This surrender comes at the end of Bhishma's long life of effort and duty; it is not a reason to stop making choices.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: The dying Bhishma, pierced by arrows, speaks to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit_display: न दिशः संप्रजानामि नाकाशं न च मेदिनीम् / केवलं तव वीर्येण तिष्ठामि मधुसूदन
verses.translation: I cannot make out the directions, nor the sky, nor the earth. I stand only by your strength, Madhusudana.
verses.line: I can't tell up from down anymore. I'm standing only on your strength.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma answers Krishna's morning question.
verses.sanskrit_display: दाहो मोहः श्रमश्चैव क्लमो ग्लानिस्तथा रुजा / तव प्रसादाद्वार्ष्णेय सद्यो व्यपगतानि मे
verses.translation: The burning, the confusion, the exhaustion, the weariness, the weakness and the pain — by your grace, Varshneya, they left me at once.
verses.line: The burning, the fog, the exhaustion, the pain: by your grace they lifted at once.
verses.misuse: This is Bhishma's experience of grace, not a promise of healing. Keep up medical care.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma, old and wounded, finds new strength to teach.
verses.sanskrit_display: युवेवास्मि समावृत्तस्त्वदनुध्यानबृंहितः / वक्तुं श्रेयः समर्थोऽस्मि त्वत्प्रसादाज्जनार्दन
verses.translation: I feel as if I have become young again, strengthened by meditating on you. By your grace, Janardana, I am able to speak what is good.
verses.line: Thinking of you has made me feel young again. By your grace I can speak.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: At the winter solstice, Bhishma prepares to die and speaks to Krishna one last time.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वद्भक्तं त्वद्गतिं शान्तमुदारमपरिग्रहम् / त्रायस्व पुण्डरीकाक्ष पुरुषोत्तम नित्यशः / अनुजानीहि मां कृष्ण वैकुण्ठ पुरुषोत्तम
verses.translation: Protect always, lotus-eyed Purushottama, your devotee, whose goal you are, calm, generous, owning nothing. Give me leave, Krishna, Vaikuntha, Purushottama.
verses.line: I am yours and you are my goal. Look after me always. Now let me go, Krishna.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: The closing dialogue appended to the Vishnu Sahasranama: Arjuna's prayer.
verses.sanskrit_display: पद्मपत्रविशालक्ष पद्मनाभ सुरोत्तम / भक्तानामनुरक्तानां त्राता भव जनार्दन
verses.translation: Lotus-eyed one with wide eyes, lotus-naveled, best of gods, Janardana, be the protector of the devotees who love you.
verses.line: Lotus-eyed one, be the protector of those who love you.

verses.speaker: Vishnu
verses.setting: In an Anushasana side-story, Vishnu reveals himself to Garuda and speaks of who reaches him.
verses.sanskrit_display: महामोहार्थपङ्के तु निमग्रानां गतिर्हरिः / एकान्तिनो ध्यानपरा यतिभावाद्ब्रजन्ति माम्
verses.translation: For those sunk in the mire of great delusion and the chase for wealth, Hari is the way; the single-minded, intent on meditation, come to me through renunciation.
verses.line: For those stuck deep in the mud of confusion and chasing, Hari is the way out.

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada's prayer of refuge to Vishnu, which Bhishma recounts.
verses.sanskrit_display: लोकनाथं सहस्राक्षमद्भुतं परदं पदम् / भगवन्तं प्रपन्नोऽस्मि भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुम्
verses.translation: I have taken refuge in the Lord, protector of the world, thousand-eyed, wondrous, the highest abode, master of past, future and present.
verses.line: I have taken refuge in the one who holds the past, the present and the future.

verses.speaker: Narayana
verses.setting: The child on the banyan explains to Markandeya why he revealed himself.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वमेकार्णवं दृष्ट्वा नष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम् / विक्लबोसि मया ज्ञातस्ततस्ते दर्शितं जगत्
verses.translation: Seeing everything, moving and unmoving, lost in a single ocean, you were distressed. I knew it, and so I showed you the world.
verses.line: When everything was flooded and you were frightened, I knew. So I showed you the world inside me.

verses.speaker: Markandeya
verses.setting: Markandeya reveals that the child he saw is their own kinsman, Krishna, sitting with them.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः
verses.translation: Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
verses.line: He is father and mother to every being. Go to him for shelter.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: After the war and the Anugita, Arjuna thanks Krishna as they ride to Hastinapura.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथवन्तश्च भवता पाण्डवा मधुसूदन / भवन्तं प्लवमासाद्य तीर्णाः स्म कुरुसागरम् / `भक्तांस्त्वमाश्रितानस्मान्पालयामुत्र चेह च।'
verses.translation: With you as our protector, Madhusudana, we Pandavas crossed the Kuru ocean, using you as our raft. (Protect us, your devotees who rely on you, here and hereafter.)
verses.line: With you as our protector, we crossed an ocean, using you as our raft.

verses.speaker: Kunti
verses.setting: The Pandavas' heir is stillborn, struck by Ashvatthama's weapon; Kunti runs to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit_display: वासुदेव महाबाहो सुप्रजा देवकी त्वया / त्वं नो गतिः प्रतिष्ठा च त्वदायत्तमिदं कुलम्
verses.translation: Vasudeva, mighty-armed, through you Devaki is blessed in her son. You are our way and our ground; this family depends on you.
verses.line: You are our way and the ground we stand on. This family rests on you.
verses.misuse: In the story the child is revived; prayer is not a promise of that outcome. Keep this card away from pregnancy-loss and child-loss contexts.

verses.speaker: the devas
verses.setting: The frightened gods praise Vishnu before asking him to remove their fear.
verses.sanskrit_display: तवैव सत्तया देव ! सत्तावन्तो वयं तव । आश्रिता आपि मूढास्त्वां विस्मरामो हि मायया ॥
verses.translation: By your being alone, O God, we exist and are yours; though we depend on you, we fools forget you through maya.
verses.line: We exist only because of you, and we lean on you. Still we forget you.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas sings of Hari as the friend who shows up in hard times.
verses.sanskrit_display: हरि सो मीत न देख्यौ कोई । विपति-काल सुमिरत, तिहिं औसर आनि तिरीछो होई ॥
verses.translation: I have never seen a friend like Hari. Remember him in a time of trouble, and at that very moment he comes and stands between you and it.
verses.line: I've never seen a friend like Hari. Remember him in trouble, and he comes and stands beside you.
verses.misuse: A friend who stands with you, not a guarantee that the trouble disappears.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on how Govind receives every kind of love; the pada goes on to Shabari's berries and Vidura's banana peels.
verses.sanskrit_display: गोबिंद प्रीति सबनि की मानत | जिहि जिहि भाइ करत जन सेवा, अंतर की गति जानत ॥
verses.translation: Govind accepts everyone's love. In whatever spirit his people serve him, he knows the movement of the heart within.
verses.line: Govind accepts everyone's love, in whatever way they serve. He knows what is really in the heart.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas recalls Krishna washing guests' feet at Yudhishthira's royal sacrifice.
verses.sanskrit_display: जाको चरनोदक सिव सिर धरि, तीनि लोक हितकारी । सोइ प्रभु पांडु-सुतनि के कारन निज कर चरन पखारी ॥
verses.translation: He, the water of whose feet Shiva bears on his head and which blesses the three worlds — that Lord, for the sake of the sons of Pandu, washed feet with his own hands.
verses.line: The Lord whose feet the whole world honours washed others' feet with his own hands.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on trusting the Lord's promise.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रभु तेरो बचन भरोसों साँचों। पोषन भरन विसंभर साहब,
verses.translation: Lord, trust in your word is true: the master who sustains the whole universe feeds and holds us.
verses.line: Lord, your word is worth trusting. The one who holds up the whole world holds you too.
verses.misuse: Trust is not a reason to stop earning or planning; Surdas's next words scold fretting, which the card leaves out.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on being held by Krishna.
verses.sanskrit_display: जाकों मनमोहन अंग करे। ताकौ केस खसे नहिं सिर ते, जो जग बैर परे ॥
verses.translation: The one whom Manmohan takes into his embrace — not a hair falls from his head, even if the whole world turns hostile.
verses.line: When Krishna holds you close, not a hair on your head is harmed, even if the world turns against you.
verses.misuse: Poetic assurance of inner safety, not a guarantee against harm; seek real protection from real threats.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas speaks to his own mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: रे मन, गोबिंद के है रहिये। … दुख, सुख, कीरति, भाग आपने आइ परे सो गहिये।
verses.translation: O mind, stay Govind's. … Sorrow, joy, fame, fortune — whatever falls to you, take it as it comes.
verses.line: Mind, stay Govind's. Sorrow, joy, fame, fortune: take whatever comes your way.
verses.misuse: Accepting what comes is not accepting mistreatment; it is not chasing or dreading outcomes.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on running a household.
verses.sanskrit_display: नंदनंदन करि घर कौ ठाकुर, आपुन है रह चेरो ॥
verses.translation: Make Nandnandan the master of the house, and live in it yourself as his servant.
verses.line: Make Krishna the master of your house, and live there as his helper.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas teaches the mind to love Madhav, using the chatak bird, which drinks only rain.
verses.sanskrit_display: चातक चितवन पारि । घन-आसा सब दुख सहै, (पै) अनत न जाँचे बारि ॥
verses.translation: The chatak, gazing up, bears every hardship in hope of the rain cloud, yet asks no other water.
verses.line: The chatak bears every hardship waiting for the rain cloud, and asks no other water.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on the shelter of the name.
verses.sanskrit_display: बड़ी है राम नाम की ओट | सरन गएँ प्रभु काढ़ि देत नहिं, करत कृपा के कोट ।
verses.translation: Great is the shelter of the name. When you come for refuge, the Lord never turns you out; he builds you forts of kindness.
verses.line: The name is a great shelter. Whoever comes to him is never turned away; he builds walls of kindness.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on singing to Gopal.
verses.sanskrit_display: जो सुख होत गुपालहि गाए । सो सुख होत न जप-तप कीन्हें, कोटिक तीरथ न्हाएं ॥
verses.translation: The joy that comes from singing of Gopal does not come from chanting or austerity, or bathing at ten million holy places.
verses.line: The joy of singing to Gopal doesn't come from rituals or a million pilgrimages.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.collection: Surdas: "The wealth of those with nothing"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas, who owned nothing, on his real wealth.
verses.sanskrit_display: हमारे निर्धन के धन राम । चोर न लेत, घटत नहिं कबहूँ, आवत गाढ़े काम ॥
verses.translation: Ram is the wealth of us who have nothing. No thief takes it, it never runs low, and it comes through in hard times.
verses.line: Ram is the wealth of those with nothing: no thief takes it, it never runs out.
verses.misuse: Inner wealth, not a financial plan: keep paying the bills and asking for help.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas remembers what the Lord has already done for him.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम प्रभु, मोसों बहुत करी | नर-देही दीनी सुमिरन को, मो पापी ते कछु न सरी ॥ गरभ-बास अति त्रास, अधोमुख, तहाँ न मेरी सुधि बिसरी।
verses.translation: Lord, you have done so much for me: you gave me a human body for remembering you, though I, a sinner, achieved nothing with it. In the terror of the womb, head down, even there you did not forget me.
verses.line: You did so much for me. Even in the dark of the womb, you did not forget me.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: At the end of a long confession, Surdas names what makes the Lord great.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुकृती सुचि सेवक जन काहि न जिय भावै। प्रभु की प्रभुता यहै जु दीन सरन पावे॥
verses.translation: Who wouldn't love a virtuous, pure servant? The Lord's greatness is this: that the lowly find shelter.
verses.line: Anyone would love a perfect servant. The Lord's greatness is that the lowly find shelter with him.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas asks for steadiness in love.
verses.sanskrit_display: सोइ कछु कीजे दीन-दयाल ! जातें जन छन चरन न छाँड़े, करुना-सागर, भक्त-रसाल
verses.translation: Do whatever it takes, kind to the lowly, so that your servant never lets go of your feet even for a moment, ocean of compassion, delight of devotees.
verses.line: Do whatever it takes so that I never let go of your feet, not even for a moment.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on how a mother treats her child.
verses.sanskrit_display: अपुने को को न आदर देइ ? ज्यों बालक अपराध कोटि करे, मातु न माने तेइ ॥
verses.translation: Who does not honour their own? A child may do ten million wrongs, and the mother does not count them.
verses.line: Who doesn't honour their own? A child may do a million wrongs; a mother doesn't keep count.
verses.misuse: About God's forgiveness, not a reason to excuse harm done to real people.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on where his strength lies.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम्हरी नाम तजि प्रभु जगदीसर, सु तो कहो मेरे और कहा बल ?
verses.translation: Leaving your name aside, Lord of the world, tell me, what other strength do I have?
verses.line: Apart from your name, Lord, tell me: what other strength do I have?
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas asks to be kept in shelter.
verses.sanskrit_display: अब मोहि सरन राखिये नाथ ! कृपा करी जो गुरुजन पठए, बह्यो जात गह्यो हाथ ॥
verses.translation: Now keep me in your shelter, Lord. By your grace the elders were sent; as I was being swept away, they caught my hand.
verses.line: Keep me in your shelter now. I was being swept away, and your grace sent people who caught my hand.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas, with no one else to tell.
verses.sanskrit_display: कौन सुने यह बात हमारी | समरथ ओर न देखों तुम विनु, कासों विथा कहों बनवारी ॥
verses.translation: Who will hear this matter of mine? I see no one capable but you. To whom shall I tell my pain, Banwari?
verses.line: Who will listen? I see no one else who can help. Who do I tell my pain to, Krishna?
verses.misuse: Telling God is good; telling a person too is also good.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on belonging.
verses.sanskrit_display: मेरी तो गति-पति तुम, अनतहिं दुख पाऊँ। हों कहाइ तेरों, अब कोन कौ कहाऊँ ॥
verses.translation: You are my way and my keeper; anywhere else I find only sorrow. Called yours, whose else could I be called now?
verses.line: You are my way and my keeper. I'm known as yours; whose else could I be?
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.collection: Surdas: "Master of those with no one"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas describes the Lord he trusts.
verses.sanskrit_display: ऐसे प्रभु अनाथ के स्वामी | दीनदयाल, प्रेम-परिंपूरन, सब घट अंतरजामी ॥
verses.translation: Such is the Lord, master of those who have no one: kind to the lowly, brimming with love, knowing every heart from within.
verses.line: He is the protector of those who have no one: kind, full of love, knowing every heart.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on the Lord's readiness.
verses.sanskrit_display: कबहूँ तुम नाहिन गहरु कियो | सदा सुभाव-सुलभ सुमिरन-बस, भक्तनि अमर दियौ ॥
verses.translation: You have never once delayed. By nature easy to reach and won over by remembrance, you have always given your devotees what is undying.
verses.line: You never once delayed. You are easy to reach, and remembering you is enough to win you.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on what pleases the Lord.
verses.sanskrit_display: सरबस प्रभु रीझि देत तुलसी के पाता॥
verses.translation: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives everything.
verses.line: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives everything.
verses.misuse: About the worth of small sincere offerings, not a transaction for material gain.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas asks to be remembered.
verses.sanskrit_display: मेरी सुधि लीजो हो, ब्रजराज । और नहीं जग मैं कोउ मेरो, तुमहि सुधारन काज़ ॥
verses.translation: Remember me, Lord of Braj. I have no one else in the world to set me right but you.
verses.line: Remember me, Lord of Braj. There's no one else to set my life right.
verses.misuse: A prayer from a lonely place, not advice to cut off from people.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on why to serve the Lord of the Yadus.
verses.sanskrit_display: संपति बिपति, बिपति ते संपति, देह कौ यहै सुभाइ ॥ तरुवर फूले, फरे, पतझरे, अपने कालहि पाइ।
verses.translation: Fortune into trouble, trouble into fortune — that is the nature of the body's life. Trees flower, fruit and shed their leaves, each in its season.
verses.line: Good times turn hard and hard times turn good. Trees flower, fruit and shed, each in its season.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.collection: Surdas: "Not all days are the same"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on remembering in good times.
verses.sanskrit_display: सबे दिन एके-से नहि जात। सुमिरन-भजन कियौ करि हरि कौ,जब लों तन-कुसलात॥
verses.translation: Not all days pass the same. Keep remembering and singing of Hari while the body is well.
verses.line: Not every day will be like this one. Remember Hari while you're well.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on the way of one who has tasted Hari.
verses.sanskrit_display: कोमल बचन, दीनता सब सौं, सदा अनंदित रहिये ।
verses.translation: Gentle words, humility with everyone, and always remain joyful.
verses.line: Speak gently, be humble with everyone, and stay joyful.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on how the Lord provides.
verses.sanskrit_display: जो प्रभु के सरनागत आवे। ताकों प्रभु क्यों करि बिसरावे ॥ मातु-उदर में रस पहुँचावत। बहुरि रुधिर तें छीर बनावत ॥
verses.translation: How could the Lord forget one who has come to him for refuge? He sent nourishment to the child in the mother's womb, then turned blood into milk.
verses.line: How could he forget someone who comes to him? He fed you in the womb, then turned blood into milk.
verses.misuse: Trust alongside work and planning; the pada's earlier lines about not caring for food or family are left out.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.collection: Surdas: The bird on the ship
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: One of Surdas's best-known padas.
verses.sanskrit_display: मेरो मन अनत कहाँ सुख पावे । जैसे उड़ि जहाज को पच्छी, फिरि जहाज पर आये ॥
verses.translation: Where else will my mind find happiness? Like the bird on a ship at sea that flies off and comes back to the ship again.
verses.line: Where else will my heart find rest? Like a bird on a ship at sea, it flies off and returns.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on what devotion is to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम्हारी भक्ति हमारे प्रान । छूटि गए केसे जन जीवत, ज्यों पानी बिनु पान ॥
verses.translation: Devotion to you is my very breath. If it were gone, how would your servant live? Like a leaf without water.
verses.line: Loving you is my breath. Without it I'd wither, like a leaf with no water.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.collection: Surdas: The river and the sea
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on a mind given to Nandlal.
verses.sanskrit_display: जैसे सरिता मिले सिंधु को, बहुरि प्रवाह न आवे (हो)। ऐसे सूर कमल-लोचन तें, चित नहिं अनत डुलावै (हो) ॥
verses.translation: As a river that meets the sea never flows back again, so Sur's mind, given to the lotus-eyed one, does not wander elsewhere.
verses.line: Like a river that has reached the sea and never flows back, my heart doesn't wander from him.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: a gopi (Bhramargeet)
verses.setting: In the Bhramargeet, a gopi tells Uddhava she cannot stop remembering Krishna.
verses.sanskrit_display: सूरदास मोहि निमिष न बिसरत मोहन सूरति सोवत जागत॥
verses.translation: Surdas says: I cannot forget Mohan's face for a moment, sleeping or waking.
verses.line: I can't forget his face for a moment, asleep or awake.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Radha (Bhramargeet)
verses.setting: Radha's message to Krishna in Mathura.
verses.sanskrit_display: बारक जाइयो मिलि माधौ। को जानै कब छूटि जायगो स्वाँस, रहै जिय साधौ॥
verses.translation: Come and meet me just once, Madhav. Who knows when the breath may leave; let the heart's wish not remain.
verses.line: Come and see me once, Madhav. Who knows how long there is. Don't leave the wish unfulfilled.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera's 'pain' pada (variant of the famous 'mero dard na jaane koy').
verses.sanskrit_display: मीरा री प्रभु पीर मिटाँगा जब वैद साँवरो होय ॥
verses.translation: Meera's pain will ease only when Saanwara becomes the healer.
verses.line: My pain will ease only when Krishna himself is the healer.
verses.misuse: A love-song image, not medical advice: keep seeing real doctors and counsellors.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Kavitakosh compilation not openly licensed: re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera's pada of refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: अब मैं सरण तिहारी जी, मोहि राखौ कृपा निधान।
verses.translation: Now I am in your shelter; keep me, treasure of kindness.
verses.line: I'm in your shelter now. Keep me, you who are all kindness.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Kavitakosh compilation not openly licensed: re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera waiting for Krishna.
verses.sanskrit_display: पन्थ निहारूँ डगर भुवारूँ, ऊभी मारग जोय।
verses.translation: I watch the road, I sweep the path, standing there looking down the way.
verses.line: I watch the road and sweep the path, standing there, looking for you.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Kavitakosh compilation not openly licensed: re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera inviting Krishna home.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम गुणवंत सुसाहिब कहिये मोमें औगुण सारा।। म्हारे घर आओ प्रीतम प्यारा।। मैं निगुणी कछु गुण नहिं जानूं तुम सा बगसणहारा।।
verses.translation: You are called the virtuous, gracious master; in me are all the faults. (Come to my house, beloved.) I have no merit, I know no virtues; you are the one who forgives.
verses.line: You are all goodness; I am full of faults. I have no merit, but you are the one who forgives.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Kavitakosh compilation not openly licensed: re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera speaks to her own mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: मन रे परसि हरि के चरन। सुभग सीतल कमल- कोमल त्रिविध - ज्वाला- हरन।
verses.translation: O mind, touch Hari's feet: lovely, cool, soft as lotus, taking away the threefold fire.
verses.line: Mind, rest at Hari's feet: cool, soft as a lotus, taking away every burning.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Kavitakosh compilation not openly licensed: re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera's best-known bhajan.
verses.sanskrit_display: पायो जी म्हें तो राम रतन धन पायो। वस्तु अमोलक दी म्हारे सतगुरू, किरपा कर अपनायो॥ जनम-जनम की पूँजी पाई, जग में सभी खोवायो। खरच न खूटै चोर न लूटै, दिन-दिन बढ़त सवायो॥
verses.translation: I have found the jewel-wealth of Ram's name. My true teacher gave me a priceless thing and in kindness made me his own. I found the savings of many lives and lost all the world's. Spending does not exhaust it, no thief can steal it; it grows day by day.
verses.line: I found the treasure of the name. Spending never empties it, no thief can steal it, it grows every day.
verses.misuse: Inner wealth, not a money promise.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Kavitakosh compilation not openly licensed: re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: After long inquiry into what governs our lives, the seer ends with a prayer of refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो ब्रह्माणं विदधाति पूर्वं यो वै वेदांश्च प्रहिणोति तस्मै । तं ह देवं आत्मबुद्धिप्रकाशं मुमुक्षुर्वै शरणमहं प्रपद्ये ॥
verses.translation: He who first brings forth Brahma and hands him the Vedas: to that God, who lights up the understanding of the self, I, longing for freedom, go for refuge.
verses.line: Longing to be free, I take refuge in the God who lights up my understanding.
verses.misuse: Refuge here comes at the end of a whole Upanishad of inquiry and meditation; it is not a substitute for effort.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Describing the one Lord who pervades all, the seer adds what he is to each of us.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । सर्वस्य प्रभुमीशानं सर्वस्य शरणं सुहृत् ॥
verses.translation: He shines through the powers of all the senses yet has no senses; he is the master and ruler of all, the refuge of all, the friend of all.
verses.line: The Lord of everything is also everyone's refuge and everyone's friend.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The seer on where the Lord is found and how one comes to see him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अणोरणीयान् महतो महीयानात्मा गुहायां निहितोऽस्य जन्तोः । तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको धातुः प्रसादान्महिमानमीशम् ॥
verses.translation: Smaller than the small, greater than the great, the Self is hidden in the heart of every creature. One free of grasping sees him, the Lord in his greatness, by the grace of the Creator, and is free of sorrow.
verses.line: The Lord is hidden in your own heart. By his grace one sees him, and sorrow lifts.
verses.misuse: Grace here is not a reward for being good enough; the verse pairs it with letting go of grasping.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Near the end of a hymn to Rudra, the seer speaks as someone frightened by life.
verses.sanskrit_display: अजात इत्येवं कश्चिद्भीरुः प्रपद्यते । रुद्र यत्ते दक्षिणं मुखं तेन मां पाहि नित्यम् ॥
verses.translation: Knowing you as the Unborn, someone afraid comes to you for refuge: Rudra, with that kind, southern face of yours, protect me always.
verses.line: Afraid, I come to you, Rudra. With your kind face, protect me always.
verses.misuse: A prayer for protection, not a promise that nothing bad will happen; it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A Vedic prayer to Rudra, the mountain-dweller, asking to see his gentle side.
verses.sanskrit_display: या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूरघोराऽपापकाशिनी । तया नस्तनुवा शन्तमया गिरिशन्ताभिचाकशीहि ॥
verses.translation: Rudra, that form of yours which is kind, not fearsome, shining with goodness: with that most peaceful form, dweller on the mountain, look upon us.
verses.line: Rudra, turn your gentle, peaceful form toward us, and look upon us.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The seer on the peace that comes from knowing the Lord in whom all things rest.
verses.sanskrit_display: यो योनिं योनिमधितिष्ठत्येको यस्मिन्निदं सं च विचैति सर्वम् । तमीशानं वरदं देवमीड्यं निचाय्येमां शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥
verses.translation: He who alone presides over every source, in whom this whole world comes together and dissolves: knowing that Lord, the giver of blessings, the God worthy of praise, one comes to utter peace.
verses.line: Knowing the kind Lord in whom everything rests, one comes to a peace that does not end.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The seer on finding the kind One in the middle of the world's confusion.
verses.sanskrit_display: सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मं कलिलस्य मध्ये विश्वस्य स्रष्ठारमनेकरूपम् । विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारं ज्ञात्वा शिवं शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥
verses.translation: Subtler than the subtlest, in the midst of chaos, the creator of everything, of many forms, the One who embraces the whole world: knowing him as Shiva, the kind one, one attains peace for ever.
verses.line: In the middle of chaos is the kind One who holds the world. Knowing him brings lasting peace.
verses.misuse: Peace here is inner steadiness, not a promise that the chaos outside will stop.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The seer on the Lord who guards the world through all its ages.
verses.sanskrit_display: स एव काले भुवनस्य गोप्ता विश्वाधिपः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः । यस्मिन् युक्ता ब्रह्मर्षयो देवताश्च तमेवं ज्ञात्वा मृत्युपाशांश्छिनत्ति ॥
verses.translation: He is the guardian of the world in time, the lord of all, hidden in every being, in whom sages and gods are united. Knowing him so, one cuts the nooses of death.
verses.line: He guards the world through time, hidden in every being. Knowing him loosens death's hold.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: One of the best-known verses of the Upanishad, on the God within all.
verses.sanskrit_display: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा। कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥
verses.translation: One God is hidden in all beings: all-pervading, the inner self of every being, overseer of all action, dwelling in all beings, the witness, pure awareness, alone, beyond all qualities.
verses.line: One God is hidden in every being: the inner self of all, the quiet witness of all we do.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A Vedic prayer, shared with the Rig Veda, asking Rudra to spare one's family.
verses.sanskrit_display: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयुषि मा नो गोषु मा न अश्वेषु रीरिषः । वीरान् मा नो रुद्र भामितो वधीर्हविष्मन्तः सदामित् त्वा हवामहे ॥
verses.translation: Do not harm our little ones or our children, our lives, our cattle or our horses. Rudra, in anger do not strike down our brave ones. Bringing offerings, we call on you always.
verses.line: Rudra, spare our little ones, our children, our lives. We call on you always.
verses.misuse: A parent's prayer of fear, not a promise of a particular outcome; it does not replace medical help.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods' hymn to the Goddess, a verse shared with the Vedic Durga Suktam.
verses.sanskrit_display: तामग्निवर्णां तपसा ज्वलन्तीं वैरोचनीं कर्मफलेषु जुष्टाम् । दुर्गां देवीं शरणमहं प्रपद्ये सुतरां नाशयते तमः ॥
verses.translation: She who is fire-coloured, blazing with austerity, radiant, sought by those who act: in Durga, the Goddess, I take refuge. She utterly destroys the darkness.
verses.line: I take refuge in Durga, the blazing Goddess. She clears away the darkness.
verses.misuse: Refuge in the Goddess is strength to face hardship, not a guarantee it will vanish.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods address the Goddess as Mother and see her in every power of the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: नमस्ते अस्तु भगवति भवति मातरस्मान्पातु सर्वतः । सैषाष्टौ वसवः । सैषैकादश रुद्राः। सैषा द्वादशादित्याः ।
verses.translation: Salutations to you, Blessed One. Mother, protect us on every side. She is the eight Vasus; she is the eleven Rudras; she is the twelve Adityas.
verses.line: Goddess, I bow to you. Mother, protect us on every side.
verses.misuse: A child's prayer for protection, not a promise that nothing will go wrong.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods' hymn names what the Goddess is to those who come to her.
verses.sanskrit_display: तामहं प्रणौमि नित्यम् । तापापहारिणीं देवीं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिनीम् । अनन्तां विजयां शुद्धां शरण्यां शिवदां शिवाम् ॥
verses.translation: I bow to her always: the Goddess who takes away pain, giver of both enjoyment and freedom, endless, victorious, pure, the refuge, the giver of good, the kind one.
verses.line: I bow to her always: she takes away pain, she is pure, she is a refuge, she is kind.
verses.misuse: 'Takes away pain' is a devotee's praise, not a promise of a particular outcome; it does not replace care.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: Part of the closing hymn to the Goddess.
verses.sanskrit_display: नमामि त्वामहं देवीं महाभयविनाशिनीम् । महादुर्गप्रशमनीं महाकारुण्यरूपिणीम् ॥
verses.translation: I bow to you, Goddess, destroyer of great fear, who calms great hardship, whose very form is great compassion.
verses.line: I bow to you, Goddess: you end great fear, you ease great hardship, you are compassion itself.
verses.misuse: Praise of the Goddess's compassion, not a promise that hardship will disappear; seek practical help too.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The Upanishad explains the name Durga.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्याः परतरं नास्ति सैषा दुर्गा प्रकीर्तिता । दुर्गात्संत्रायते यस्माद्देवी दुर्गेति कथ्यते ॥
verses.translation: There is nothing higher than her; she is called Durga. Because she rescues from hardship, the Goddess is called Durga.
verses.line: She is called Durga because she carries us safely through hard places.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The hymn ends with a frightened devotee bowing to Durga.
verses.sanskrit_display: तां दुर्गां दुर्गमां देवीं दुराचारविघातिनीम् । नमामि भवभीतोऽहं संसारार्णवतारिणीम् ॥
verses.translation: To that Durga, hard to reach, the Goddess who destroys wrongdoing, who carries us across the ocean of worldly life: afraid of that life, I bow.
verses.line: Frightened by life, I bow to Durga, who carries us across the ocean of the world.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: After the gods' hymn, the Upanishad names the Goddess's nature.
verses.sanskrit_display: एषात्मशक्तिः । एषा विश्वमोहिनी पाशाङ्कुशधनुर्बाणधरा । एषा श्रीमहाविद्या । य एवं वेद स शोकं तरति ।
verses.translation: She is the power of the Self. She enchants the world, holding noose, goad, bow and arrow. She is the great wisdom. Whoever knows this crosses beyond grief.
verses.line: She is the power within the self and the great wisdom. Whoever knows her crosses beyond grief.
verses.misuse: Crossing grief is not being told to stop grieving; it is a direction, not a deadline.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The Skanda Upanishad opens with a devotee thanking Shiva.
verses.sanskrit_display: अच्युतोऽस्मि महादेव तव कारुण्यलेशतः । विज्ञानघन एवास्मि शिवोऽस्मि किमतः परम् ॥
verses.translation: Mahadeva, by a mere trace of your compassion I am unshaken; I am pure knowing; I am Shiva. What could be more than this?
verses.line: Mahadeva, by just a trace of your compassion I stand unshaken. What more could I want?

verses.speaker: Markandeya
verses.setting: Asked how the knowledge of Shiva as teacher dawns, the long-lived sage Markandeya answers with an image.
verses.sanskrit_display: स होवाच । वैराग्यतैलसम्पूर्णे भक्तिवर्तिसमन्विते । प्रबोधपूर्णपात्रे तु ज्ञप्तिदीपं विलोकयेत् ॥ मोहान्धकारे निःसारे उदेति स्वयमेव हि । वैराग्यमरणिं कृत्वा ज्ञानं कृत्वोत्तरारणिम् ॥
verses.translation: In a vessel full of awakening, filled with the oil of detachment and fitted with the wick of devotion, behold the lamp of knowing. In the hollow darkness of delusion it rises of itself. Make detachment the lower fire-stick and knowledge the upper.
verses.line: Fill the lamp with letting go, make devotion its wick, and light rises by itself in the dark.

verses.speaker: Devotee
verses.setting: The well-known meditation verse on Vishnu, printed at the end of the Narayana Upanishad.
verses.sanskrit_display: शान्ताकारं भुजगशयनं पद्मनाभं सुरेशं विश्वाधारं गगनसदृशं मेघवर्णं शुभाङ्गम् । लक्ष्मीकान्तं कमलनयनं योगिभिर्ध्यानगम्यं वन्दे विष्णुं भवभयहरं सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥
verses.translation: Peaceful in form, resting on the serpent, lotus-naveled, lord of the gods, support of the universe, vast as the sky, cloud-coloured, beautiful; beloved of Lakshmi, lotus-eyed, reached by yogis in meditation: I bow to Vishnu, who takes away the fear of worldly life, the one lord of all worlds.
verses.line: I bow to Vishnu, peaceful in form, who takes away the fear of life and holds the universe.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A Vedic prayer about the mind, repeated with the refrain 'may my mind hold good intentions'.
verses.sanskrit_display: यज्जाग्र॑तो दू॒रमु॒दैति॒ दैवं॒ तदु॑ सु॒प्तस्य॒ तथै॒वैति॑ । दू॒रं॒ग॒मं ज्योति॑षां॒ ज्योति॒रेकं॒ तन्मे॒ मनः॑ शि॒वसं॑कल्पमस्तु ॥
verses.translation: That divine mind which travels far when we are awake and likewise when we sleep, the far-going one light among lights: may that mind of mine be of kind and good resolve.
verses.line: My mind wanders far, awake or asleep. May that mind of mine hold only good intentions.

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The last verse of the Shiva Sankalpa prayer.
verses.sanskrit_display: सु॒षा॒र॒थिरश्वा॑निव॒ यन्म॑नु॒ष्या॒न्नेनी॒यते॒ऽभीशु॑भिर्वा॒जिन॑ इव । हृ॒त्प्रति॑ष्ठं॒ यद॑जि॒रं जवि॑ष्ठं॒ तन्मे॒ मनः॑ शि॒वसं॑कल्पमस्तु ॥
verses.translation: Like a good charioteer guiding horses with the reins, the mind leads people; set in the heart, ageless and swiftest: may that mind of mine be of kind and good resolve.
verses.line: The mind steers us like a charioteer steers horses. May my mind hold only good intentions.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva describes how he meets each kind of devotee: the hurting, the seeking, the needy.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदाऽऽर्ताऽर्थाणिजिज्ञासुभक्ता मच्छरणागताः। स्युस्तदा प्रकृतिर्मेऽसौ मातृभावं समाश्रिता ॥ तेभ्यो वै बाञ्छिताः सिद्धीर्दत्त्वाऽग्रे सारयेदिमान्। सर्वतः सर्वथा कल्याः ! नैव कार्योऽत्र विस्मयः ॥
verses.translation: When my distressed, my seeking and my wanting devotees take refuge in me, my nature takes on the feeling of a mother. Giving them the fulfilment they long for, she moves them forward toward me in every way. Do not wonder at this.
verses.line: When the hurting and the seeking take refuge in me, my nature turns toward them like a mother.
verses.misuse: Being met with a mother's care is not a promise of getting every wish; it does not replace practical help.

verses.speaker: The ancestors (pitris)
verses.setting: Ending a long hymn, the ancestors stop asking for anything particular and hand the outcome to Shiva.
verses.sanskrit_display: विहारिन् ! विभो ! भक्तचेतोनिकेते शरण्यं किलैकान्ततस्त्वां व्रजामः । यथा नो भवेदत्र कल्याणमाशु तदेवाधुना देव ! शम्भो ! विधेहि ॥
verses.translation: Dweller in the shrine of devotees' hearts, all-pervading one, we come to you alone for refuge. Do now, divine Shambhu, whatever will quickly bring us good here.
verses.line: You who live in devotees' hearts: we come to you alone. Do whatever is truly good for us.
verses.misuse: Handing over the outcome comes after the effort; it is not a reason to stop acting.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: After telling the ancestors their work needs a mind joined to him, Shiva offers an easier way.
verses.sanskrit_display: उच्यते सुगमोपायः श्रूयतां विश्वभूतिदाः। वरिष्ठं यं समालम्ब्य कृच्छ्राव कृच्छ्रतरेप्वपि ॥ सक्ताः कार्येषु मद्भक्तेर्विमुखा न भविष्यथ । नूनमेकोऽद्वितीयोऽपि स्वभक्तेभ्यो निरन्तरम् ॥
verses.translation: I tell you an easy way; listen. Holding to this best of means, even while engaged in the hardest of tasks, you will not turn away from devotion to me.
verses.line: Here is an easy way: even in the hardest work, you need not drift from devotion.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva lists where he can be found among the things people honour.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रेम्णा स्नेहेन भक्तया च श्रद्धयाऽपि प्रपूरितम् । स्पर्शेषु तु नमस्येष्वालिङ्गनं पितृपुङ्गवाः ! ॥
verses.translation: Among the touches worthy of reverence, O best of ancestors, I am the embrace filled with love, affection, devotion and faith.
verses.line: Among all reverent touches, I am the embrace, full of love, warmth, devotion and trust.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva quotes two Upanishadic sayings about his devotees.
verses.sanskrit_display: तरन्त्यात्मविदो भक्ता निश्चितं शोकसागरम् । सर्वभूतेषु गूढोऽस्ति देव एको न संशयः ॥
verses.translation: Devotees who know the Self surely cross the ocean of sorrow. The one God is hidden in all beings; there is no doubt.
verses.line: Devotees who know the Self cross the ocean of sorrow. One God is hidden in every being.
verses.misuse: Crossing sorrow takes time; this is not an instruction to stop grieving.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva describes the gentle side of his power at work in the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: विश्वं रक्षति मच्छक्तिः सात्त्विकी धर्मरूपिणी। नित्या सा वर्तते नित्यं विश्वकल्याणकारिणी ॥
verses.translation: My gentle power, whose form is dharma, protects the world. She is eternal and always works for the good of the universe.
verses.line: A gentle power, made of goodness, protects the world and always works for its good.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: After defeating the demons, the gods try to praise the Mother and feel their words fall short.
verses.sanskrit_display: परं मनोवेगविमोदिता वयं भावं भवत्या अपि वांगमनोधियाम । अगोचरं द्योतयितुं समुद्यताः क्षमस्व नो दोषममुं दयानिधे ! ॥ अत्र क्षमाप्तावपि कारणं ते महत्यपारास्ति कृपैव मातः! । ब्रह्मस्वरूपे ! जगदम्बिकेऽलं दयामयीं तवां सततं नमामः ॥
verses.translation: Carried away by the rush of feeling, we have tried to put into words what lies beyond word, mind and thought; forgive us this fault, treasure of kindness. Even in this forgiving, the cause is only your great, boundless grace, Mother. Mother of the world, whose form is Brahman, we bow to you, the compassionate, always.
verses.line: Forgive our clumsy words, Mother. Even your forgiving us comes from your boundless grace.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods' hymn on the reach of the Mother's grace.
verses.sanskrit_display: नास्यम्ब ! सीमा तव सत्कृपायाः शक्ता न ये भक्तगणास्त्वदीयाः। तत्त्वप्रबोधस्य प्रपूर्त्यभावाद्रष्टुं हि ते भावमयस्वरूपम् ॥ स्वाभाविकैरेव कृपाकटाक्षैः समीहमाना ह्यनुकम्पितुं तान्। गुणाश्रयायच्छसि दर्शनं स्वं मुक्तिञ्च तेभ्योऽभ्युदयं ददासि ॥
verses.translation: Mother, there is no limit to your true grace. Your devotees who cannot see your form of feeling, for lack of complete understanding, you wish to favour with your natural glances of grace; you show yourself to them and give them both freedom and well-being.
verses.line: Your grace has no limit, Mother. Even those who can't understand you, you look on with kindness.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods' hymn on those who simply love the Mother's feet.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनन्यभक्सैव तु केवलं हि भृङ्गायमाणास्तव पादपद्यमे। विच्योतयस्यम्ब ! न तानपि त्वं स्वदर्शनान्मोक्षखनेः कदापि ॥
verses.translation: Those who, with undivided devotion alone, hover like bees at your lotus feet, Mother, you never let slip from the sight of you, that mine of freedom.
verses.line: Those who stay near your feet like bees near a lotus, Mother, you never let slip away.

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: The Mother explains what happens when beings caught in the world turn to her.
verses.sanskrit_display: परन्तु तेषु जीवेषु शरणं मे गतेषु वै । अहं नानाप्रकारेस्तानाकर्षामि स्वसम्मुखे ॥
verses.translation: But when those beings come to my refuge, I draw them toward me in many different ways.
verses.line: When anyone comes to me for refuge, I draw them toward me in many ways.

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: The Mother describes how her power of knowledge carries a devotee home.
verses.sanskrit_display: ज्ञानिनां मम भक्तानां देवाः ! विद्यास्वरूपिणी। विमुच्य प्रकृतिस्तेभ्यः कर्माणि निखिलानि वै ॥ स्वायत्तानि प्रकुर्वन्ती भक्तानचं विभ्रती। तत्कल्याणकदम्बञ्च विधातुं लीयते मयि ॥
verses.translation: For my wise devotees, gods, Nature in the form of knowledge frees them from all their actions, makes them her own, holds the devotee in her lap, and, to bring about his good, merges into me.
verses.line: Like a mother, she lifts the devotee into her lap and carries him, for his good, to me.

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: Showing her cosmic form, the Mother names herself in words that echo Krishna's in the Gita.
verses.sanskrit_display: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुर्माता निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवालयस्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
verses.translation: I am the goal, the sustainer, the lord, the mother, the dwelling, the refuge, the friend; the origin, the dissolution, the ground, the treasure-house, the imperishable seed.
verses.line: I am your goal, your support, your mother, your home, your refuge, your friend.

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: The Mother tells the gods how to carry their work.
verses.sanskrit_display: मत्परायणतां पुण्यां गृणीताश्रयणं मम । मद्भक्ताः सततं कर्म मयुक्ताः कुरुतामराः ! ॥
verses.translation: Gods, take up that pure dependence on me; take my shelter. As my devotees, always do your work joined to me.
verses.line: Take shelter in me, and do your work with your mind joined to me.
verses.misuse: Shelter does not mean stepping back from the work; the instruction is to keep working.

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: The Mother on what her shelter does to a devotee's way of working.
verses.sanskrit_display: तदाश्रयेण मद्भक्ता द्वन्द्वातीता विमत्सराः । युक्तकर्मरताः सन्तो निषपापा मत्परायणाः ॥
verses.translation: Sheltered by that, my devotees go beyond the pairs of opposites, free of envy, engaged in fitting work; they become free of wrong, devoted to me.
verses.line: Sheltered in her, devotees rise above ups and downs, let go of envy, and do good work.

verses.speaker: Suta
verses.setting: Opening the Dheesh Gita, Suta explains why Ganesha is called Dheesh, lord of the mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: जगत्पिता जगद्वन्धुर्भगवान विश्वपालकः । परे बुद्धे: स्थितो बुद्धिमधिष्ठाय कृपावशात् ॥ मुक्तिं ददाति जीवेभ्यः शरणागतवत्सलः । अतः सम्प्रोच्यते धीश आम्नायैरखिलैरसौ ॥
verses.translation: The Father of the world, its friend, the Lord who protects all, standing beyond the intellect, out of compassion presides over the intellect; loving those who come to him for refuge, he gives beings freedom. So all the Vedas call him Dheesh.
verses.line: Father and friend of the world, he loves those who come to him and sets them free.

verses.speaker: The seers
verses.setting: Seers who had studied every Veda come to Ganesha's world because learning alone left them restless.
verses.sanskrit_display: अतो नेवाभवच्छान्तिरस्माकं चेतसि प्रभो!। वयं शरणमापन्ना भवल्लोकमुपस्थिताः ॥
verses.translation: So no peace came into our minds, Lord. We have come to your world and taken refuge in you.
verses.line: Lord, no peace came to our minds. So we have come to you for refuge.

verses.speaker: Dheesh (Ganesha)
verses.setting: Ganesha tells the seers how a formless God is seen by those who love him.
verses.sanskrit_display: विभुं मामप्यहो भक्ता भावुकाः स्वेच्छया द्विजाः। नानारूपेषु पश्यन्ति कृतकृत्या भवन्ति च ॥ रूपहीनोऽस्म्यहं विप्राः ! श्रद्धावन्तस्तथापि मे । भक्ता मां स्थूलरूपे वा ज्योतीरूपे निरीक्ष्य च ॥
verses.translation: Though I am all-pervading, devotees full of feeling see me in many forms, as they wish, and are fulfilled. I am without form, sages, yet my faithful devotees see me in a bodily form, or as light.
verses.line: I have no form, yet loving devotees see me in the form they long for, and are fulfilled.

verses.speaker: Dheesh (Ganesha)
verses.setting: Ganesha on how living beings are sustained.
verses.sanskrit_display: निश्चितं मातृभावेन विज्ञाः ! धर्ममयेण मे। प्रकृतेः पालिता जीवाः पोपिताश्च निरन्तरम् ॥
verses.translation: Truly, wise ones, by the dharma-filled motherly nature of my Prakriti, beings are protected and nourished without end.
verses.line: All beings are fed and protected, constantly, by a motherly care at the heart of things.

verses.speaker: The seers
verses.setting: The seers' prayer to Ganesha, modelled on the Gayatri.
verses.sanskrit_display: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥
verses.translation: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
verses.line: Ganapati, guard my mind from wrong action, day and night, and turn it toward the good.

verses.speaker: The sages
verses.setting: Told to meditate on his form, the sages admit their minds will not stay still.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रभो! तथोपदेष्टव्यं वातवच्चपलं मन: यथा निगृह्य शक्ष्यामस्त्वां स्मर्तुं चिरशान्तये ॥
verses.translation: Lord, now teach us how to restrain this mind, restless as the wind, so that we can remember you for lasting peace.
verses.line: My mind is restless as the wind. Teach me to steady it, to remember you and be at peace.

verses.speaker: Surya
verses.setting: Surya defines devotion by pointing to loves people already know.
verses.sanskrit_display: स्त्रीमित्रादिषु सः प्रेमा श्रद्धा स जनकादिषु । मय्येव साधकानां स भक्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥
verses.translation: The love one has for a spouse and friends, the reverent trust one has for parents: when seekers turn that toward me, it is called devotion.
verses.line: The love you feel for friends, the trust you feel for parents: turned toward God, that is devotion.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: One of five opening prayers; this one is to Shiva.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुंद इंदु सम देह उमा रमन करुना अयन। जाहि दीन पर नेह करउ कृपा मर्दन मयन ॥
verses.translation: Fair as the jasmine and the moon, beloved of Uma, home of compassion, who loves the lowly: may the destroyer of Kama show me grace.
verses.line: Shiva, home of compassion, loves the lowly. May he be kind to me.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Valmiki, Veda, Shiva-Parvati vandana
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Among his opening salutations, Tulsidas names what Shiva and Parvati are to him.
verses.sanskrit_display: गुर पितु मातु महेस भवानी। प्रनवउँ दीनबंधु दिन दानी॥ सेवक स्वामि सखा सिय पी के। हित निरुपधि सब बिधि तुलसी के ॥
verses.translation: I bow to Mahesh and Bhavani, my teacher, father and mother, friends of the lowly, giving every day; servants, masters and friends of Sita's lord, true well-wishers of Tulsi in every way, without any motive.
verses.line: Shiva and Parvati are my teacher, father and mother: friends of the lowly, giving every day.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Sati doubts, tests and hides it
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Back from testing Ram and lying about it, Sati realises Shiva knows everything.
verses.sanskrit_display: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥
verses.translation: Remembering what she had done, her heart was full of a worry beyond telling. 'Shiva, an ocean of compassion, deep beyond measure, did not speak my fault aloud.'
verses.line: Shiva, an ocean of compassion, never named her mistake aloud.
verses.misuse: Not naming a fault is mercy, not a model for never talking about problems in a relationship.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada tells Parvati's worried parents what Shiva is like.
verses.sanskrit_display: संभु सहज समरथ भगवाना। एहि बिबाहँ सब बिधि कल्याना॥ दुराराध्य पै अहहिं महेसू। आसुतोष पुनि किएँ कलेसू ॥
verses.translation: Shambhu is by nature the all-capable Lord; in this marriage there is good of every kind. Mahesh is hard to win by worship, yet he is quickly pleased when one takes on hardship.
verses.line: Shiva may seem hard to reach, but sincere effort pleases him quickly.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Himavan
verses.setting: Parvati's mother Maina is frantic about her daughter's future. Her husband answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रिया सोचु परिहरहु सबु सुमिरहु श्रीभगवान। पारबतिहि निरमयउ जेहिं सोइ करिहि कल्यान ॥
verses.translation: Beloved, put away all this worry and remember the Lord. He who made Parvati will bring about her good.
verses.line: Let go of this worry and remember God. The one who made our daughter will look after her.
verses.misuse: Himavan then advises a concrete step (Parvati's tapas, 1.68); trust sits beside action, not instead of it.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Voice from the sky (Brahma)
verses.setting: After years of austerity, Parvati is worn thin. A voice from the sky speaks.
verses.sanskrit_display: भयउ मनोरथ सुफल तव सुनु गिरिराजकुमारि। परिहरु दुसह कलेस सब अब मिलिहहिं त्रिपुरारि ॥
verses.translation: Daughter of the mountain king, listen: your longing has borne fruit. Now give up all these unbearable hardships; Tripurari will be yours.
verses.line: Your longing has borne fruit. Put down these hard struggles now; he will be yours.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Shiva's grief and Ram's name
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Shiva wanders, teaching and singing of Ram, after Sati is gone.
verses.sanskrit_display: कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिं ग्याना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥ जदपि अकाम तदपि भगवाना। भगत बिरह दुख दुखित सुजाना ॥
verses.translation: Somewhere he taught knowledge to sages, somewhere he told of Ram's virtues. Though free of all desire, the wise Lord was pained by separation from his devotee.
verses.line: Though beyond all desire, the Lord still grieved at being parted from his devotee.

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: The seven sages come to test Parvati and ask why she is doing such hard tapas.
verses.sanskrit_display: मनु हठ परा न सुनइ सिखावा। चहत बारि पर भीति उठावा॥ नारद कहा सत्य सोइ जाना। बिनु पंखन्ह हम चहहिं उड़ाना ॥ देखहु मुनि अबिबेकु हमारा। चाहिअ सदा सिवहि भरतारा ॥
verses.translation: 'My mind has set itself stubbornly and will not hear advice; it wants to build a wall on water. Taking Narada's word as true, I want to fly without wings. Look at my foolishness, sages: I want only Shiva as my husband, always.'
verses.line: Call it foolish if you like: my heart wants only Shiva, always.

verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: Sitting beside Shiva under the banyan on Kailash, Parvati asks him to clear her old doubt.
verses.sanskrit_display: जासु भवनु सुरतरु तर होई। सहि कि दरिद्र जनित दुखु सोई॥ ससिभूषन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। हरहु नाथ मम मति भ्रम भारी ॥
verses.translation: 'Can one whose home is beneath the wishing tree suffer the pain of poverty? Thinking this over in your heart, Moon-crowned Lord, take away the heavy confusion of my mind.'
verses.line: One who lives under the wishing tree need not suffer want. You are my shelter: clear my confusion.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva answers Parvati's question: how can the formless God be a prince grieving in a forest?
verses.sanskrit_display: सगुनहि अगुनहि नहिं कछु भेदा। गावहिं मुनि पुरान बुध बेदा॥ अगुन अरूप अलख अज जोई। भगत प्रेम बस सगुन सो होई ॥
