verses.translation: There is no difference between God with form and God without form: so say the sages, the Puranas, the learned and the Vedas. The One without qualities, without form, unseen and unborn, takes on form out of love for his devotees.
verses.line: The formless, unseen, unborn One takes on a form out of love for his devotees.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva tells Parvati what Ram's name does.
verses.sanskrit_display: बिबसहुँ जासु नाम नर कहहीं। जनम अनेक रचित अघ दहहीं॥ सादर सुमिरन जे नर करहीं। भव बारिधि गोपद इव तरहीं ॥
verses.translation: Even saying his name helplessly burns away wrongs built up over many lives; and those who remember him with reverence cross the ocean of worldly life as if it were a cow's hoofprint.
verses.line: Those who remember him with love cross life's ocean as easily as a puddle in a hoofprint.
verses.misuse: Praise of remembrance, not a promise that life's problems will vanish; practical help still matters.

verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: Shiva has finished answering; Parvati, holding his feet, tells him what his words did.
verses.sanskrit_display: ससि कर सम सुनि गिरा तुम्हारी। मिटा मोह सरदातप भारी॥ तुम्ह कृपाल सबु संसउ हरेऊ। राम स्वरूप जानि मोहि परेऊ ॥
verses.translation: 'Hearing your words, cool as moonbeams, the heavy autumn heat of my delusion is gone. Kind one, you took away all my doubt, and I came to know Ram's true nature.'
verses.line: Your words fell like cool moonlight. The heat of my confusion is gone; you took away every doubt.

verses.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
verses.setting: His father dead and his demon kin beaten by Vishnu, young Prahlada thinks through what is left.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वात्मना सर्वधिया सर्वसंरम्भरंहसा । स एव शरणं देवो गतिरस्तीह नान्यथा ॥
verses.translation: With all my being, all my mind, all the force of my striving: he alone, that God, is my refuge. There is no other way here.
verses.line: With all my being, all my mind, all my strength: he alone is my refuge.

verses.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
verses.setting: Prahlada makes his decision.
verses.sanskrit_display: अस्मान्निमेषादारभ्य नारायणमजं सदा । संप्रपन्नोऽस्मि सर्वत्र नारायणमयो ह्यहम् ॥
verses.translation: From this very moment I take refuge, always, in Narayana, the unborn. Everywhere, I am full of Narayana.
verses.line: From this moment on, I take refuge in Narayana. Wherever I am, I am full of him.

verses.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
verses.setting: Prahlada describes the prayer that now stays with him.
verses.sanskrit_display: नमो नारायणायेति मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः । नापैति मम हृत्कोशादाकाशादिव मारुतः ॥
verses.translation: The mantra 'Namo Narayanaya', which brings every aim to fulfilment, never leaves the chamber of my heart, as the wind never leaves the sky.
verses.line: 'Namo Narayanaya' never leaves my heart, just as the wind never leaves the sky.
verses.misuse: 'Every aim' is a devotee's praise of the name, not a promise of particular results.

verses.speaker: Prahlada
verses.setting: Vishnu appears in Prahlada's shrine; Prahlada sings a hymn of refuge.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रिभुवनभवनाभिरामकोशं सकलकलङ्कहरं परं प्रकाशम् । अशरणशरणं शरण्यमीशं हरिमजमच्युतमीश्वरं प्रपद्ये ॥
verses.translation: Lovely treasure-house of the three worlds, remover of every stain, the highest light, refuge of those who have no refuge, the shelter-giving Lord: Hari, unborn, unfailing, the Lord, I take refuge in.
verses.line: Refuge of those who have no refuge: Hari, the unfailing one, I take refuge in you.

verses.speaker: Prahlada
verses.setting: Waking into understanding, Prahlada greets what he has found as an old friend.
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मा सर्वपदातीतश्चिरात्संस्मृतिमागतः । दिष्ट्या लब्धोऽसि भगवन्नमस्तेस्तु महात्मने ॥
verses.translation: The Self beyond every word has, after a long time, come back to memory. By good fortune you are found, Lord; salutations to you, great Self.
verses.line: After so long, I remember you. By good fortune, Lord, you are found.

verses.speaker: Prahlada
verses.setting: Vishnu wakes Prahlada from long absorption; Prahlada tells him what has changed.
verses.sanskrit_display: भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन स्थितिः सम्यगथागता । समाधावसमाधौ च रूपेणाहं समः सदा ॥
verses.translation: Lord, by your grace I have come to a rightly settled state. In meditation or out of it, I am always the same.
verses.line: By your grace, Lord, I have found steadiness. In meditation or out of it, I am the same.

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Shiva on true worship
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Shiva has visited Vasishtha's hermitage and asked after his welfare. Vasishtha answers.
verses.sanskrit_display: न किंचिदपि दुष्प्रापं न च काश्चन भीतयः । त्वदनुस्मरणानन्दपरिघूर्णितचेतसाम् ॥
verses.translation: For those whose minds whirl in the joy of remembering you, nothing is hard to reach, and there are no fears at all.
verses.line: For those whose minds are full of the joy of remembering you, nothing is out of reach, nothing feared.
verses.misuse: Remembrance eases fear; it is not a promise that hardship will not come.

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Shiva on true worship
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha keeps telling Shiva what remembering him has meant.
verses.sanskrit_display: तनोति चैष्यतो बीजं त्वदनुस्मरणं प्रभो । ज्ञानामृतैककलशो धृतिज्योत्स्नानिशाकरः ॥ अपवर्गपुरद्वारं त्वदनुस्मरणं प्रभो । त्वदनुस्मरणोदारचिन्तामणिमता मया ॥
verses.translation: Remembering you, Lord, sows the seed of what is to come; it is the one jar of wisdom's nectar, a moon shining with steadiness. Remembering you, Lord, is the door to the city of freedom. Holding the great wish-jewel of remembering you, I...
verses.line: Remembering you, Lord, is a jar of wisdom's nectar, a moon of steadiness, a door to freedom.

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Shiva on true worship
verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva describes inner worship, the kind that needs no temple.
verses.sanskrit_display: गच्छतस्तिष्ठतश्चैव जाग्रतः स्वपतोऽपि च । सर्वाचारगता पूजा नित्यं ध्यानात्मिका त्वियम् ॥
verses.translation: Whether walking or standing, awake or asleep, this worship runs through every activity, always: it is worship made of meditation.
verses.line: Walking or standing, awake or asleep, worship can run through everything you do.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman reaches Sita
verses.speaker: Ram (message)
verses.setting: Hanuman delivers Ram's message to Sita across the sea.
verses.sanskrit_display: सो मनु सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं। जानु प्रीति रसु एतनेहि माहीं॥ प्रभु संदेसु सुनत बैदेही। मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही ॥
verses.translation: And that heart of mine stays with you always. Know that this is the whole of my love. Hearing her Lord's message, Sita was so lost in love she forgot herself.
verses.line: My heart is always with you. That is all you need to know about my love.

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Sita gives Hanuman her message for Ram before he leaves Lanka.
verses.sanskrit_display: कहेहु तात अस मोर प्रनामा। सब प्रकार प्रभु पूरनकामा॥ दीन दयाल बिरिदु संभारी। हरहु नाथ सम संकट भारी ॥
verses.translation: Give him my greeting, friend, and say: Lord, you lack nothing, but kindness to the helpless is your promise. Remember it, and take away my heavy trouble.
verses.line: You are kind to those in trouble. Remember that now, and lift this heavy weight from me.
verses.misuse: A prayer in crisis, not a replacement for practical help.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram comes home
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Bharat, who blamed himself for fourteen years for his mother's scheme, falls at Ram's feet.
verses.sanskrit_display: परे भूमि नहिं उठत उठाए। बर करि कृपासिंधु उर लाए॥ स्यामल गात रोम भए ठाढ़े। नव राजीव नयन जल बाढ़े ॥
verses.translation: Bharat lay on the ground and would not get up when they tried to lift him. The ocean of kindness lifted him by force and held him to his heart. Ram's dark body thrilled, and tears flooded his lotus eyes.
verses.line: He lay on the ground and would not rise. So Ram lifted him up and held him to his heart.

verses.speaker: Shabari and Ram
verses.setting: The old forest woman Shabari, who waited years for Ram, says she is too lowly even to praise him.
verses.sanskrit_display: अधम ते अधम अधम अति नारी। तिन्ह महँ मैं मतिमंद अघारी॥ कह रघुपति सुनु भामिनि बाता। मानउँ एक भगति कर नाता ॥
verses.translation: Shabari: 'Among the lowest of the low, women are counted lowest, and among them I am the dullest, Lord.' Ram said: 'Listen to me, good woman: I recognise only one kinship, the kinship of devotion.'
verses.line: I don't measure people the way the world does. The only kinship I recognise is love.
verses.misuse: The first half is Shabari's harsh self-description, which Ram's reply overturns; never show it on its own.

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Ram has just given the dying vulture Jatayu the final blessing usually sought by sages.
verses.sanskrit_display: कोमल चित अति दीनदयाला। कारन बिनु रघुनाथ कृपाला॥ गीध अधम खग आमिष भोगी। गति दीन्ही जो जाचत जोगी ॥
verses.translation: Raghunath is tender-hearted, kind to the lowly, gracious without needing a reason. To a vulture, a lowly bird that ate flesh, he gave the end that yogis beg for.
verses.line: His heart is tender, and his kindness doesn't need a reason.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Ram sends his friends home
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: The war is over; before flying home, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends back to their homes.
verses.sanskrit_display: निज निज गृह अब तुम्ह सब जाहू। सुमिरेहु मोहि डरपहु जनि काहू॥ सुनत बचन प्रेमाकुल बानर। जोरि पानि बोले सब सादर ॥
verses.translation: Now go home, each of you. Remember me, and don't be afraid of anyone. Hearing this, the monkeys, overcome with love, joined their hands and spoke respectfully.
verses.line: Go home now. Remember me, and don't be afraid of anyone.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, The family council at Chitrakoot
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Before the whole family council, Bharat admits he came against orders and thanks Ram for his kindness.
verses.sanskrit_display: कृपाँ भलाईं आपनी नाथ कीन्ह भल मोर। दूषन भे भूषन सरिस सुजसु चारु चहुँ ओर ॥
verses.translation: Lord, by your own kindness and goodness you have done me good: my faults became like ornaments, and a good name has spread all around me.
verses.line: Through your kindness, even my faults were turned into something good.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Bharat at Bharadwaj's ashram
verses.speaker: Bharadwaj
verses.setting: On his way to find Ram, Bharat confides his grief and guilt to the sage Bharadwaj.
verses.sanskrit_display: भरत बचन सुनि मुनि सुखु पाई। सबहिं कीन्हि बहु भाँति बड़ाई॥ तात करहु जनि सोचु बिसेषी। सब दुखु मिटिहि राम पग देखी ॥
verses.translation: Hearing Bharat's words the sage was happy, and everyone praised him in many ways. 'Child, don't worry so much. All your sorrow will lift when you see Ram's feet.'
verses.line: Don't worry so much. Your sorrow will lift the moment you see him again.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Chitrakoot: Ram to Bharat
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat accepts Ram's wish that he return to Ayodhya, but asks for one thing to carry.
verses.sanskrit_display: अब कृपाल जस आयसु होई। करौं सीस धरि सादर सोई॥ सो अवलंब देव मोहि देई। अवधि पारु पावौं जेहि सेई ॥
verses.translation: Now, gracious one, whatever you command I will do, holding it on my head with respect. But give me something to lean on, Lord, something I can serve, so that I can get through these years.
verses.line: Give me something to hold on to, so I can get through these years.

verses.speaker: Shabari
verses.setting: Shabari shows Ram the hermitage where her teachers lived; they have long since passed on.
verses.sanskrit_display: देवकार्याणि कुर्वद्भिर्यानीमानि कृतानि वै। पुष्पैः कुवलयैः सार्धं म्लानत्वं न तु यान्ति वै॥
verses.translation: The flowers and blue lilies they offered here in their worship have still not withered.
verses.line: My teachers are gone, but the flowers they offered here still haven't withered.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "You are kind, I am in need"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, in his book of petitions to Ram, lists every bond between them.
verses.sanskrit_display: तू दयालु, दीन हौं, तू दानि, हौं भिखारी । हौं प्रसिद्ध पातकी, तू पाप-पुंज-हारी॥ नाथ तू अनाथको, अनाथ कौन मोसो। मो समान आरत नहिं, आरतिहर तोसो॥ ब्रह्म तू, हौं जीव, तू है ठाकुर, हौं चेरो। तात-मात, गुरु-सखा, तू सब बिधि हितु मेरो॥ तोहिं मोहिं नाते अनेक, मानियै जो भावै। ज्यों त्यों तुलसी कृपालु! चरन-सरन पावै॥
verses.translation: You are kind and I am in need; you give and I am a beggar. I am a known wrongdoer and you lift heaps of wrong. Lord, you shelter those who have no one, and who has less than I do? No one hurts as I do, and no one heals hurt as you do. You are the infinite, I a small life; you the master, I the servant. Father and mother, teacher and friend: you wish me well in every way. There are many bonds between us; take whichever one pleases you. Only let Tulsi, somehow, find shelter at your feet.
verses.line: Father, mother, teacher, friend: you are mine in every way. Choose any bond, only keep me close.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "Say once: Tulsidas is mine"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas ends a petition asking for only one thing.
verses.sanskrit_display: तू गरीबको निवाज, हौं गरीब तेरो। बारक कहिये कृपालु! तुलसिदास मेरो॥
verses.translation: You are the one who lifts up the poor, and I am your poor one. Kind one, say it just once: "Tulsidas is mine."
verses.line: You lift up the poor, and I am yours. Just say it once: "You are mine."
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: One of the best-known bhajans of the Vinay Patrika.
verses.sanskrit_display: जाउँ कहाँ तजि चरन तुम्हारे। काको नाम पतित-पावन जग, केहि अति दीन पियारे॥
verses.translation: Where would I go, leaving your feet? Whose name in the world is "the one who lifts the fallen"? To whom are the lowliest so very dear?
verses.line: Where would I go but to you? Who else holds the fallen so dear?
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "Wasted till now, no more"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, after years he feels were lost, resolves to begin again.
verses.sanskrit_display: अबलों नसानी, अब न नसैहौं। राम-कृपा भव-निसा सिरानी, जागे फिरि न डसैहौं॥
verses.translation: Till now it has been wasted; from now it will not be. By Ram's grace the long night is over. Now that I am awake, I will not spread the bed of sleep again.
verses.line: What is lost is lost, but the night is over. Awake now, I begin again.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: not a hair harmed
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what hostility can and cannot do to one who is held.
verses.sanskrit_display: जो पै कृपा रघुपति कृपालुकी, बैर औरके कहा सरै। होइ न बाँको बार भगतको, जो कोउ कोटि उपाय करे॥
verses.translation: If the kind Raghupati's grace is with you, what can anyone's enmity achieve? Not a hair of the devotee is bent, though someone tries a million schemes.
verses.line: When grace is with you, others' ill will cannot even bend a hair.
verses.misuse: Not a promise that harm never happens; a reassurance to steady fear.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: kindness without a reason
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas reminds Ram of everyone he has sheltered.
verses.sanskrit_display: सो धौ को जो नाम-लाज तें, नहिं राख्यो रघुबीर। कारुनीक बिनु कारन ही हरि हरी सकल भव-भीर॥
verses.translation: Who is there that Raghubir did not keep safe, for the honour of his name? The compassionate one, for no reason at all, takes away the whole crowd of fears.
verses.line: The compassionate one needs no reason to take your fears away.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A famous bhajan on a love that asks nothing in return.
verses.sanskrit_display: ऐसो को उदार जग माहीं। बिनु सेवा जो द्रवै दीनपर राम सरिस कोउ नाहीं॥
verses.translation: Who in the world is so generous? There is none like Ram, who melts for the suffering without any service done.
verses.line: Who else melts for the hurting without asking anything first?
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: the tender friend of the lowly
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas opens a list of those Ram embraced: Ahalya, Guha, Jatayu, Shabari.
verses.sanskrit_display: ऐसे राम-दीन हितकारी । अतिकोमल करुनानिधान बिनु कारन पर-उपकारी॥
verses.translation: Such is Ram, the well-wisher of the lowly: utterly tender, a treasury of compassion, doing good to others without any reason.
verses.line: Utterly tender, full of compassion, doing good without needing a reason.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: love that erases big and small
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram's love levels everyone.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम! प्रीतिकी रीति आप नीके जनियत है। बड़ेकी बड़ाई, छोटेकी छोटाई दूरि करै, ऐसी बिरुदावली, बलि, बेद मनियत है॥
verses.translation: Ram, you know the ways of love well. The Vedas praise you as the one who takes away the bigness of the big and the smallness of the small.
verses.line: Love takes away the bigness of the big and the smallness of the small.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: watching the road for grace
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, in a long dry season, waits.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथ ! कृपाहीको पंथ चितवत दीन हौं दिनराति। होइ धौं केहि काल दीनदयालु ! जानि न जाति॥
verses.translation: Lord, day and night this poor one watches the road your kindness will come by. Kind to the lowly, when will it be? I cannot tell.
verses.line: Day and night I watch the road for your kindness. I do not know when, but I wait.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "You have always kept me"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas asks to be kept as he always has been.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम ! राखिये सरन, राखि आये सब दिन। बिदित त्रिलोक तिहुँ काल न दयालु दूजो, आरत-प्रनत-पाल को है प्रभु बिन॥
verses.translation: Ram, keep me in your shelter, as you have kept me every day till now. All three worlds know there has never been another so kind. Who but you protects the hurting who bow before him?
verses.line: Keep me now, as you have kept me every day until now.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "Your name is my mother and father"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, orphaned as a child, on who his family became.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम ! रावरो नाम मेरो मातु-पितु है। सुजन-सनेही, गुरु-साहिब, सखा-सुहृद, राम-नाम प्रेम-पन अबिचल बितु है॥
verses.translation: Ram, your name is my mother and father, my kin and dear ones, my teacher and master, my companion and true friend. My steady love for your name is my unshakeable wealth.
verses.line: Your name is my mother and father, my teacher, my friend, my family.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "As I am, I am yours"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas asks not to be given up on.
verses.sanskrit_display: जैसो हौं तैसो राम रावरो जन, जनि परिहरिये। कृपासिंधु, कोसलधनी! सरनागत-पालक, ढरनि आपनी ढरिये॥ अपराधी तउ आपनो, तुलसी न बिसरिये। टूटियो बाँह गरे परै, फूटेहु बिलोचन पीर होत हित करिये॥
verses.translation: Ram, whatever I am, I am your servant; do not cast me off. Ocean of mercy, lord of Kosala, protector of those who come for shelter, keep to your own nature. Even at fault, I am your own; do not forget Tulsi. A broken arm still hangs at your neck, and an injured eye still aches as your own and is tended with care.
verses.line: A broken arm is still held close in a sling.
verses.reflection: Even at fault, you are still someone's own.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on whom he can turn to.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम तजि हौं कासों कहां, और को हितु मेरे ? दीनबंधु ! सेवक, सखा, आरत, अनाथपर सहज छोह केहि केरे॥
verses.translation: Leaving you, whom would I tell? Who else wishes me well? Friend of the lowly, who else has a natural tenderness for the servant, the friend, the suffering and the one with no one?
verses.line: Who else has such natural tenderness for the hurting and the alone?
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Dohavali: as I am, I am yours
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on the one thing that makes him safe.
verses.sanskrit_display: जैसो तैसो रावरो केवल कोसलपाल। तौ तुलसी को है भलो तिहूँ लोक तिहुँ काल॥
verses.translation: Lord of Kosala, whatever I am, I am yours alone; and so Tulsi is well in all three worlds and all three times.
verses.line: Whatever I am, I am yours. So I am well, now and always.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on belonging without conditions.
verses.sanskrit_display: रामहि डरु करू राम सों ममता प्रीति प्रतीति। तुलसी निरुपधि राम को भएँ हारेहूँ जीति॥
verses.translation: Hold Ram in awe; give Ram your closeness, love and trust. Tulsi says: once you belong to Ram without conditions, even losing is winning.
verses.line: When you belong without conditions, even losing is a kind of winning.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on being protected without knowing it.
verses.sanskrit_display: खेलत बालक ब्याल सँग मेलत पावक हाथ। तुलसी सिसु पितु मातु ज्यो राखत सिय रघुनाथ॥
verses.translation: A child plays with a snake and reaches for the fire; as a father and mother keep that child safe, Tulsi says, so Sita and Ram keep us.
verses.line: As parents pull a child back from the fire, you are kept safe more often than you know.
verses.misuse: Not a promise that nothing bad happens; a reminder of care.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Dohavali: a guardian over every head
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Under the heading "God protects everyone".
verses.sanskrit_display: भागें भल ओड़ेहुँ भलो भलो न घालें घाउ। तुलसी सब के सीस पर रखवारो रघुराउ॥
verses.translation: Better to step away, better to shield yourself; better not to strike a wound. Tulsi says: over everyone's head stands Raghurao, the guardian.
verses.line: Over every head, including yours, there is a guardian.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on his own life, once a beggar boy.
verses.sanskrit_display: घर घर मागे टूक पुनि भूपति पूजे पाय। जे तुलसी तब राम बिनु ते अब राम सहाय॥
verses.translation: I begged for scraps from house to house; later kings bowed at my feet. The Tulsi who was then without Ram now has Ram's help.
verses.line: He once begged for scraps door to door. Where you are now is not where you end.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Kavitavali: lighter than straw, heavier than a mountain
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas remembers a childhood of hunger, wandering door to door.
verses.sanskrit_display: जायो कुल मंगन, बधावनो बजायो, सुनि भयो परितापु पापु जननी-जनकको। बारेतें ललात-बिललात द्वार-द्वार दीन, जानत हो चारि फल चारि ही चनकको॥ तुलसी सो साहेब समर्थको सुसेवकु है, सुनत सिहात सोचु बिधिहू गनकको। नामु राम! रावरो सयानो किधौं बावरो, जो करत गिरीतें गरु तृनतें तनकको॥
verses.translation: Born into a family of beggars, my birth brought my parents only grief. From childhood I wandered door to door, wailing with want, thinking four grains of chickpea were the four great goals of life. Now that same Tulsi is the trusted servant of a mighty master, and even the stars' accountant is amazed. Ram, is your name clever or mad, that it makes one lighter than a straw heavier than a mountain?
verses.line: He once thought four chickpeas were everything. Grace made someone lighter than straw weigh more than a mountain.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Hanuman Bahuk: cared for like a child
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on those who keep Hanuman's call in their heart.
verses.sanskrit_display: बालक-ज्यों पालिहें कृपालु मुनि सिद्ध ताको, जाके हिये हुलसति हाँक हनुमानकी॥
verses.translation: The kind sages and perfected ones will care for him like a child, in whose heart Hanuman's war-cry rings with joy.
verses.line: Whoever keeps that brave call in their heart will be cared for like a child.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna tells Arjuna who he is to every being.
verses.sanskrit_display: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
verses.translation: I am the goal, the sustainer, the master, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend; the origin and the dissolution, the ground, the treasure-house and the undying seed.
verses.line: I am your goal, your support, your witness, your home, your shelter and your friend.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes his relationship to the world.
verses.sanskrit_display: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः । वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥
verses.translation: I am the father of this world, the mother, the one who holds it up, the grandfather; what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.
verses.line: I am the father of this world, and its mother, and the one who holds it all up.
verses.misuse: Not a replacement for a parent who is gone; a reassurance that care runs through everything.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna tells Arjuna how near he is to those who keep him in mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः । तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
verses.translation: O son of Pritha, whoever remembers me constantly, every day, with a mind turned to nothing else, for that steady seeker I am easy to reach.
verses.line: For the one who keeps remembering me, I am easy to reach.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.setting: Terrified by the cosmic vision, Arjuna begs to see his friend again; Krishna returns to his familiar form.
verses.sanskrit_display: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वास्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः । आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनंभूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥
verses.translation: Having spoken so, Vasudeva showed Arjuna his own form once more; the great-souled one, becoming gentle in form again, comforted the frightened Arjuna.
verses.line: Seeing Arjuna frightened, Krishna took his gentle, familiar form again and comforted him.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna sees Krishna's human face again after the overwhelming vision.
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्जुन उवाचदृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन । इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥
verses.translation: Seeing this gentle human form of yours, Janardana, I have now come to myself; my mind is steady and I am back to my natural state.
verses.line: Seeing your gentle human face again, I am calm. I feel like myself again.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Near the end, Krishna tells Arjuna that a busy, working life is no barrier.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः । मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
verses.translation: Even while always doing every kind of work, the one who leans on me reaches the eternal, imperishable home by my grace.
verses.line: Doing all their work while leaning on me, they reach the lasting home, by my grace.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna tells Arjuna where the divine is found.
verses.sanskrit_display: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति । भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥
verses.translation: The Lord dwells in the heart of every being, Arjuna, moving all beings by his power as if mounted on a machine.
verses.line: The divine lives in the heart of every being, yours included.
verses.misuse: The second half is about nature moving us, not fatalism or excusing harm; use the first half as the card.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Before his final words, Krishna tells Arjuna why he is saying them.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
verses.translation: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all: you are deeply loved by me, and so I will tell you what is good for you.
verses.line: Listen once more to my deepest word: you are truly dear to me.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna admits the confusion of the world is hard to get through, and says who gets through it.
verses.sanskrit_display: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
verses.translation: This divine power of mine, made of the three qualities, is very hard to get past. Those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond it.
verses.line: This tangle is hard to get through. Those who take shelter in me get through it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna begins his ladder of practices with the simplest instruction.
verses.sanskrit_display: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
verses.translation: Fix your mind on me alone, let your understanding settle in me; from then on you will dwell in me. Of this there is no doubt.
verses.line: Rest your mind in me, settle your thinking in me, and you will live in me.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: Frightened gods come to Vishnu and say plainly what they need.
verses.sanskrit_display: वयं शरणमापन्नाः शरणागतवत्सल !। भयं नो मोहजं येन विनश्यति तथा कुरु ॥
verses.translation: We have come to you for refuge, you who love those who come for shelter. Do what will make our fear, born of confusion, go away.
verses.line: We have come to you for shelter. Please make this fear, born of confusion, go away.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: In the forest, Draupadi weeps to Krishna about her humiliation in the dice hall; he answers with a vow.
verses.sanskrit_display: पतेद्द्यौर्हिमवाञ्शीर्येत्पृथिवी शकली भवेत् / शुष्येत्तोयनिधिः कृष्णे न मे मोघं वचो भवेत्
verses.translation: The sky may fall, the Himalaya may split, the earth may shatter into pieces, the ocean may dry up, Krishna, but my word will not prove false.
verses.line: The sky could fall and the oceans dry up, but my word to you will not fail.
verses.misuse: In context the vow is that her wrongs will be answered; use it as 'someone stands with you', never as a call to revenge.

verses.collection: Surdas: no one else feels it
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on who truly feels a person's pain.
verses.sanskrit_display: और न काहुहि जन की पीर। जब जब दीन दुखी भयो, तब तब कृपा करी बलबीर॥
verses.translation: No one else feels the pain of his people. Whenever the lowly were in sorrow, every time, Balbir showed them kindness.
verses.line: Every time someone was hurting, kindness came. No one else feels your pain like that.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Surdas: "You already know my joys and sorrows"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on living through ups and downs.
verses.sanskrit_display: जैसे राखहु तैसे रहौं। जानत हौ दुख-सुख सब जन के, मुख करि कहा कहौं ॥ कबहुँक भोजन लहाों कृपानिधि, कबहुँक भूख सहोँ। कवहुँक चढ़ों तुरंग, महा गज, कबहुँक भार बहों ॥
verses.translation: However you keep me, so I will live. You know all the joys and sorrows of your people; why should I say them aloud? Sometimes I get food, kind one, sometimes I go hungry; sometimes I ride a horse or a great elephant, sometimes I carry loads myself.
verses.line: Some days a feast, some days hunger; some days riding high, some days carrying loads. You already know.
verses.misuse: Acceptance is not resignation to mistreatment.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.ref_label: Sursagar vinay pada (Sur Vinay Patrika 256, opening)
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas opens a list of rescues (Gajendra, Draupadi, Parikshit).
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम हरि, सॉकरे के साथी ।
verses.translation: Hari, you are the companion of those in a tight spot.
verses.line: When you are cornered, you are not alone. He is the companion of tight places.
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Surdas, Bhramargeet: Krishna homesick in Mathura
verses.speaker: Krishna (message to Yashoda)
verses.setting: Krishna, now a prince in the city of Mathura, sends word home to his foster mother.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्यपि मथुरा बिभव बहुत है तुम बिनु कछु न सुहाय। सूरदास ब्रजबासी लोगनि भेंटत हृदय जुड़ाय॥
verses.translation: "Though Mathura has great splendour, nothing pleases me without you." Surdas says: meeting the people of Braj, his heart grows cool and calm.
verses.line: "The city has every splendour, but nothing pleases me without you." Even Krishna was homesick.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.collection: Surdas, Bhramargeet: "No one has called me Kanhaiya"
verses.speaker: Krishna (message to Yashoda)
verses.setting: Krishna, far from home in Mathura, sends a message to his mother.
verses.sanskrit_display: नीके रहियो जसुमति मैया। आवैंगे दिन चारि पाँच में हम हलधर दोउ भैया॥ जा दिन तें हम तुमतें बिछुरे काहु न कह्यो 'कन्हैया'। कबहूँ प्रात न कियो कलेवा, साँझ न पीन्हीं धैया॥
verses.translation: Stay well, mother Yashoda. In four or five days we two brothers will come. Since the day I was parted from you, no one has called me "Kanhaiya". I have not had breakfast in the morning, nor warm milk at evening.
verses.line: "Since I left you, no one has called me by my pet name."
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).

verses.display_ref: Meera pada "Tum suno ji mharo arji"
verses.ref_label: Meera pada "Tum suno ji mharo arji"
verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera, cut off by her own family, asks to be heard.
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम सुणो जी म्हारो अरजी। भवसागर में बही जात हूँ काढ़ो तो थारी मरजी।
verses.translation: Please hear my plea. I am being swept away in the ocean of the world; pull me out, if you will.
verses.line: "Hear me. I am being swept away. Pull me out."
verses.reflection: It is all right to ask for help.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Kavitakosh states its compilation is not under any licence ("all rights reserved") - treat as a locator/transcription, re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.collection: Meera: "Look my way, just a little"
verses.display_ref: Meera pada "Tanak Hari chitvau ji mori or"
verses.ref_label: Meera pada "Tanak Hari chitvau ji mori or"
verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera, waiting for an answer that does not come.
verses.sanskrit_display: तनक हरि चितवौ जी मोरी ओर। हम चितवत तुम चितवत नाहीं मन के बड़े कठोर। मेरे आसा चितनि तुम्हरी और न दूजी ठौर।
verses.translation: Hari, look my way, just a little. I keep looking at you, and you do not look back; how hard your heart is! All my hope is in your glance; I have no other place.
verses.line: "Look my way, just a little. All my hope is here." Waiting without an answer is allowed to hurt.
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Kavitakosh states its compilation is not under any licence ("all rights reserved") - treat as a locator/transcription, re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.

verses.display_ref: Meera pada "Hari mere jivan pran adhar"
verses.ref_label: Meera pada "Hari mere jivan pran adhar"
verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera on what holds her up.
verses.sanskrit_display: हरि मेरे जीवन प्राण अधार। और आसरो नांही तुम बिन, तीनू लोक मंझार।।
verses.translation: Hari, you are the support of my life and breath. In all three worlds I have no shelter but you.
verses.line: When nothing else holds you up, there is still a support for your life and breath.

verses.display_ref: Meera pada "Koi kahiyau re prabhu aavan ki"
verses.ref_label: Meera pada "Koi kahiyau re prabhu aavan ki"
verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera, waiting for someone who neither comes nor writes.
verses.sanskrit_display: ए दोउ नैण कह्यो नहिं मानै, नदियां बहै जैसे सावन की।
verses.translation: These two eyes will not listen to me; they flow like rivers in the monsoon.
verses.line: "My eyes will not listen; they flow like monsoon rivers."

prasangs.title_en: The great warriors of both armies are named
prasangs.summary: The blind king Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened at Kurukshetra. Sanjaya describes Duryodhana going to Drona and nervously naming the great warriors on both sides.
prasangs.lesson: Insecurity shows in how we size up rivals before anything has happened.
prasangs.story_hook: The war of the Mahabharata begins not with a battle cry but with a blind old king asking, 'What did they do?'

prasangs.title_en: The conches sound on both sides
prasangs.summary: Bhishma roars and blows his conch; Krishna, Arjuna and the Pandava brothers answer with their own. The sound shakes the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.
prasangs.lesson: Before any hard moment there is noise and bravado; the real test comes after.
prasangs.story_hook: One by one the great conches sounded across the field, each with its own name, until the earth itself seemed to shake.

prasangs.title_en: Arjuna surveys the armies
prasangs.summary: Arjuna asks Krishna to place the chariot between the two armies. Looking across, he sees teachers, uncles, cousins, friends and in-laws ready to fight.
prasangs.lesson: Sometimes the hardest moment is simply seeing clearly who is on the other side.
prasangs.story_hook: Arjuna asked his charioteer for one thing: drive me between the armies so I can see their faces.

prasangs.title_en: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasangs.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.
prasangs.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
prasangs.story_hook: The greatest archer of his age stood between two armies, and his hands began to shake.

prasangs.title_en: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasangs.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasangs.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasangs.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasangs.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasangs.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

prasangs.title_en: Why a warrior must fight: duty
prasangs.summary: Krishna appeals to Arjuna's sense of duty and honour, then tells him to treat victory and defeat alike before he acts.
prasangs.lesson: Decide from steadiness, not from fear of winning or losing.

prasangs.title_en: The yoga of action
prasangs.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasangs.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasangs.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasangs.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasangs.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasangs.title_en: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasangs.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasangs.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

prasangs.title_en: Why action as offering is needed
prasangs.summary: Krishna describes action as offering, the mutual nourishing of humans and gods, and the wrong of taking without giving back.
prasangs.lesson: Life works by give and take; taking only for yourself breaks the cycle.

prasangs.title_en: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasangs.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasangs.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasangs.title_en: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasangs.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasangs.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

prasangs.title_en: Restraining desire
prasangs.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasangs.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

prasangs.title_en: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
prasangs.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago, that he appears whenever goodness declines, and that he meets people on whatever path they come by. He calls the way of action deep.
prasangs.lesson: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.

prasangs.title_en: How the great yogis live
prasangs.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.
prasangs.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

prasangs.title_en: The many kinds of offering and their fruits
prasangs.summary: Krishna lists kinds of sacrifice: of senses, breath, wealth, study, and more, and says all are born of action.
prasangs.lesson: Every act, even eating, can be done as an offering.

prasangs.title_en: The glory of knowledge
prasangs.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasangs.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

prasangs.title_en: Knowledge or action: the verdict
prasangs.summary: Arjuna wants one clear verdict. Krishna says both lead to the good, but selfless action is better, and the true renouncer is the one who neither hates nor craves.
prasangs.lesson: Real letting go is inner: no grudges, no grasping.

prasangs.title_en: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasangs.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasangs.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

prasangs.title_en: The yoga of knowledge
prasangs.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasangs.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasangs.title_en: Meditation with devotion
prasangs.summary: A short sketch of meditation: senses withdrawn, free of desire, fear and anger, knowing the divine as the friend of all beings.
prasangs.lesson: You are not alone: the divine is the friend of every being.

prasangs.title_en: Action, and the one established in yoga
prasangs.summary: The true renouncer is the one who does the work that ought to be done without depending on its fruit, not the one who simply stops.
prasangs.lesson: Quitting isn't renouncing; working without clinging is.

prasangs.title_en: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasangs.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasangs.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

prasangs.title_en: Meditation in detail
prasangs.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasangs.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasangs.title_en: Mastering the mind
prasangs.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasangs.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasangs.title_en: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasangs.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasangs.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasangs.title_en: Knowledge with realisation
prasangs.summary: Krishna promises complete knowledge and describes his lower nature (elements, mind, ego) and higher nature (life itself), on which the world is strung like pearls on a thread.
prasangs.lesson: Everything is held together by one thread.

prasangs.title_en: The Lord as the cause within all things
prasangs.summary: Krishna says he is the taste in water and the light in sun and moon, strength without greed, and desire that does not oppose what is right.
prasangs.lesson: Strength and desire are good when free of greed and within what's right.

prasangs.title_en: The deluded and the devoted
prasangs.summary: Most are deluded by the play of qualities. Four kinds of good people turn to the divine: the distressed, the curious, those in need, and the wise.
prasangs.lesson: Whatever brings you to the search, distress, curiosity or need, is welcome.

prasangs.title_en: Worship of other deities
prasangs.summary: Those who worship other forms with faith have that faith made steady by Krishna, though their gains are limited.
prasangs.lesson: Sincere faith, in whatever form, is strengthened.

prasangs.title_en: Those who miss the Lord and those who know him
prasangs.summary: The deluded see only the outer form; desire and aversion confuse all beings. Those freed from confusion come to know the divine fully.
prasangs.lesson: Pull and push of like and dislike are what confuse us.

prasangs.title_en: Arjuna's seven questions and their answers
prasangs.summary: Krishna defines key terms and says that what one dwells on at death shapes where one goes, so remember the divine always and keep working.
prasangs.lesson: What you dwell on shapes who you become.

prasangs.title_en: The yoga of devotion
prasangs.summary: Krishna describes meditating at the time of death, the cosmic days and nights of Brahma, and the imperishable beyond them.
prasangs.lesson: A mind trained by practice reaches what it rests on.

prasangs.title_en: The bright and the dark paths
prasangs.summary: Krishna describes two paths after death, one of light leading to non-return and one of smoke leading to return.
prasangs.lesson: Know your direction and stay steady.

prasangs.title_en: Knowledge and its power
prasangs.summary: Krishna calls this the king of knowledge and says he pervades all things without being contained by them.
prasangs.lesson: The sacred is closer than it seems.

prasangs.title_en: How the world arises
prasangs.summary: At the end of each cycle beings return to Krishna's nature, and he sends them forth again, unbound by the work.
prasangs.lesson: Change is the nature of the world.

prasangs.title_en: Those who scorn the Lord, and how the devoted worship
prasangs.summary: The deluded overlook the divine in human form; the great-souled worship with steady devotion.
prasangs.lesson: Don't overlook the sacred in the ordinary.

prasangs.title_en: The Lord as the Self of all
prasangs.summary: Krishna lists himself as the ritual, the offering, father, mother, friend, refuge, being and non-being.
prasangs.lesson: The divine is mother, father, friend and refuge.

prasangs.title_en: Worship with and without desire, and their fruits
prasangs.summary: Those who worship for heavenly rewards return when merit runs out; those who think of him alone are carried and protected.
prasangs.lesson: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.

prasangs.title_en: The glory of selfless devotion
prasangs.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasangs.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

prasangs.title_en: The Lord's glories, and the fruit of knowing them
prasangs.summary: Krishna says even gods don't know his origin; understanding, patience, truth, joy, fear and fearlessness all come from him.
prasangs.lesson: All our qualities have one source.

prasangs.title_en: The yoga of devotion and its fruit
prasangs.summary: Devotees talk of the divine with each other and find joy; out of compassion Krishna lights the lamp of knowledge in their hearts.
prasangs.lesson: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

prasangs.title_en: Arjuna praises Krishna and asks to hear his glories
prasangs.summary: Arjuna affirms what he has heard and asks Krishna to describe his manifestations, saying he never tires of hearing.
prasangs.lesson: Curiosity about the sacred is itself a beginning.

prasangs.title_en: Krishna describes his glories
prasangs.summary: Krishna lists his manifestations: among lights the sun, among rivers the Ganga, and ends by saying any excellence is a spark of his splendour.
prasangs.lesson: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

prasangs.title_en: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
prasangs.summary: Thanking Krishna for dispelling his confusion, Arjuna asks to see his imperishable form if he is able.
prasangs.lesson: Ask humbly for what you long to see.
prasangs.story_hook: His confusion gone, Arjuna made a bold request of his friend: show me who you really are.

prasangs.title_en: Krishna describes his cosmic form
prasangs.summary: Krishna invites Arjuna to see countless forms and the whole universe in his body, and grants him divine eyes.
prasangs.lesson: Some truths need new eyes, not more effort.
prasangs.story_hook: 'You cannot see me with these eyes,' Krishna said, 'so I give you divine sight.'

prasangs.title_en: Sanjaya describes the cosmic form to Dhritarashtra
prasangs.summary: Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra of a radiance brighter than a thousand suns and of Arjuna bowing in wonder.
prasangs.lesson: Wonder humbles even the strongest.
prasangs.story_hook: If a thousand suns rose at once in the sky, Sanjaya said, that might resemble the light of that great being.

prasangs.title_en: Arjuna sees the cosmic form and praises it
prasangs.summary: Arjuna sees all beings, gods and worlds in Krishna, and warriors rushing into his mouths like moths into flame. Terrified, he asks who Krishna really is.
prasangs.lesson: Facing something vast can shake you to the core, and that's human.
prasangs.story_hook: Arjuna saw everything at once, and for the first time in his life he could not find his footing.

prasangs.title_en: "I am Time": Krishna urges Arjuna to fight
prasangs.summary: Krishna declares he is Time, the destroyer of worlds; the warriors will die even without Arjuna, so he should rise and be the instrument.
prasangs.lesson: Do your part without imagining everything rests on you.
prasangs.story_hook: 'I am Time,' said the voice from the blazing form, 'grown old, come to end the worlds.'

prasangs.title_en: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form
prasangs.summary: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.
prasangs.lesson: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.
prasangs.story_hook: Arjuna remembered every joke, every careless 'Hey, Krishna!' across years of friendship, and his voice broke.

prasangs.title_en: Krishna returns to his gentle form
prasangs.summary: Krishna tells Arjuna not to fear, and returns to his familiar form to reassure him.
prasangs.lesson: After the storm, kindness and a familiar face restore us.
prasangs.story_hook: Then the vast form folded back into the friend Arjuna knew, smiling, holding the reins.

prasangs.title_en: Only undivided devotion sees him
prasangs.summary: Arjuna is calm again. Krishna says no ritual or study reveals this form, only devotion, and the one free of attachment and enmity towards all reaches him.
prasangs.lesson: Hold no enmity towards any being.

prasangs.title_en: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasangs.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasangs.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

prasangs.title_en: The marks of one dear to God
prasangs.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasangs.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

prasangs.title_en: The field and the knower of the field
prasangs.summary: Krishna calls the body the field and the self its knower, then lists what real knowledge looks like: humility, no pretence, patience, honesty, clear sight of ageing and illness.
prasangs.lesson: Real knowledge shows up as character: humility, patience, honesty.

prasangs.title_en: Nature and spirit
prasangs.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasangs.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

prasangs.title_en: The glory of knowledge; how nature and spirit give rise to the world
prasangs.summary: Krishna calls nature the womb and himself the seed-giving father of all beings.
prasangs.lesson: All beings share one origin.

prasangs.title_en: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
prasangs.summary: Sattva binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas through craving and activity, tamas through laziness and sleep. Each shows itself in recognisable signs.
prasangs.lesson: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

prasangs.title_en: Going beyond the gunas
prasangs.summary: One beyond the qualities does not hate moods when they come or long for them when they go, sits like a witness, and is the same in praise and blame, honour and insult.
prasangs.lesson: Let moods come and go without fighting or chasing them.

prasangs.title_en: The tree of worldly life, and the way out
prasangs.summary: The world is an ashvattha tree with roots above and branches below; cut it with detachment and seek the source. The free of pride and delusion reach it.
prasangs.lesson: Pride and clinging keep us tangled; detachment cuts through.

prasangs.title_en: The individual soul
prasangs.summary: Each living being is an eternal part of Krishna, carrying mind and senses from body to body, seen only by the eye of wisdom.
prasangs.lesson: You are a part of something eternal.

prasangs.title_en: The Supreme Lord and his power
prasangs.summary: Krishna is the light of sun and moon, the nourishment of plants, the digestive fire, and is seated in every heart.
prasangs.lesson: The sacred is seated in every heart.

prasangs.title_en: The perishable, the imperishable and the Supreme Person
prasangs.summary: Krishna distinguishes the perishable, the imperishable, and himself beyond both as the Supreme Person.
prasangs.lesson: Beyond what changes and what lasts, there is more.

prasangs.title_en: Divine and demonic qualities, and where they lead
prasangs.summary: Krishna lists the divine qualities (fearlessness, truth, no anger, compassion, forgiveness, humility) and the demonic ones (hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, harshness), and reassures Arjuna he has the good ones.
prasangs.lesson: Character is a list you can practise: courage, truth, kindness, no arrogance.

prasangs.title_en: The demonic nature and its downfall
prasangs.summary: Krishna portrays people driven by endless desire and worry, bound by hundreds of hopes, always counting 'this I have, that I'll get', proud of wealth and birth.
prasangs.lesson: The mind of 'more' never rests; see it in yourself before it rules you.

prasangs.title_en: Leave what scripture forbids; follow what it guides
prasangs.summary: Desire, anger and greed are the three gates to ruin; leaving them, one does what is truly good. Krishna points to scripture as a guide for what to do.
prasangs.lesson: Desire, anger, greed: close the three gates.

prasangs.title_en: Faith, and harsh austerity against scripture
prasangs.summary: Everyone's faith matches their nature; a person is made of their faith. Harsh self-torment against scripture is condemned.
prasangs.lesson: You become what you deeply believe.

prasangs.title_en: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasangs.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasangs.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

prasangs.title_en: The meaning of Om Tat Sat
prasangs.summary: Om, Tat and Sat name the absolute; acts begun with them and done without wanting reward are good.
prasangs.lesson: Begin with a sacred intention.

prasangs.title_en: What true renunciation is
prasangs.summary: Krishna says good acts shouldn't be dropped; dropping duty out of fear or confusion gains nothing; real renunciation is giving up clinging to results, since no embodied being can stop acting.
prasangs.lesson: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

prasangs.title_en: What makes an action happen
prasangs.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasangs.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

prasangs.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasangs.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasangs.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

prasangs.title_en: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasangs.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasangs.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

prasangs.title_en: Established in knowledge
prasangs.summary: Free of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, one becomes peaceful, neither grieving nor craving, the same to all.
prasangs.lesson: Drop the 'mine' and peace follows.

prasangs.title_en: Action with devotion: surrender
prasangs.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasangs.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

prasangs.title_en: The glory of the Gita
prasangs.summary: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.
prasangs.lesson: Clarity, once found, turns into action.

prasangs.title_en: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasangs.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasangs.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasangs.title_en: Nachiketa questions his father's gift
prasangs.summary: A father makes a show of giving away all he owns, but the cows are old and dry. His young son Nachiketa keeps asking who he will be given to, until the father snaps, 'To Death!' The boy goes, and tells his father to keep his word.
prasangs.lesson: A child's honest question can show up an adult's empty gesture.
prasangs.story_hook: Nachiketa watched his father give away cows too old to give milk, and could not keep quiet.

prasangs.title_en: The three boons and the refused fortune
prasangs.summary: Death, away from home, keeps the boy waiting three days and offers three boons in apology. Nachiketa asks first that his father be calm and not angry with him, then for a sacred fire, then for the truth about death. Yama tempts him with sons, gold, long life and pleasures instead; the boy refuses them all.
prasangs.lesson: Ask for peace with your family first, and don't trade the real question for comfort.
prasangs.story_hook: Death came home to find a boy who had waited three days on his doorstep without food.

prasangs.title_en: The good and the pleasant
prasangs.summary: Yama praises Nachiketa for choosing the good over the pleasant. He explains that both come to every person, and the wise tell them apart, while the foolish choose what is pleasant and lose their way.
prasangs.lesson: Every day offers a choice between what feels good and what is good.

prasangs.title_en: Yama on what does not die
prasangs.summary: Death himself explains that the true self is never born and never dies, and is not killed when the body is. It is found not by cleverness or study but by a calm, honest life.
prasangs.lesson: What you most are cannot be lost, and a quiet, honest life is how you find it.

prasangs.title_en: The chariot of the self
prasangs.summary: Yama pictures a person as a chariot: the self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins and the senses the horses. With a steady mind the horses obey; without it they bolt. He ends with the call to arise and wake.
prasangs.lesson: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

prasangs.title_en: Turning the gaze inward
prasangs.summary: In the second half of his teaching, Yama explains that our senses face outward, so we miss what is within. The wise turn inward and stop looking for lasting things among passing ones; when the knots of the heart are cut, a person is free.
prasangs.lesson: Look inward; what lasts is not out there among passing things.

prasangs.title_en: Shaunaka's question: two kinds of knowledge
prasangs.summary: A wealthy householder asks a sage what single thing, once known, explains everything. Angiras says all our sciences and rituals are the lower knowledge; the higher is knowing the imperishable. He warns against people wise in their own eyes and sends the seeker to a real teacher.
prasangs.lesson: Skills and degrees are real knowledge, but not the deepest kind.

prasangs.title_en: The archer and the target
prasangs.summary: Angiras compares inner practice to archery: take the bow, set the arrow, draw with full attention and hit the target without distraction. When the highest is seen, the heart's knot loosens and doubts are cut.
prasangs.lesson: Single-pointed attention is how anything worthwhile is reached.

prasangs.title_en: Two birds on one tree
prasangs.summary: Two birds sit on one tree: one eats the fruit and grieves, the other simply watches. When the anxious bird sees the calm one beside it, its sorrow falls away. The section goes on to praise truth, effort and freedom from craving.
prasangs.lesson: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.

prasangs.title_en: Six seekers wait a year
prasangs.summary: Six earnest seekers come to the sage Pippalada with questions. Instead of answering, he asks them to live with him for a year in discipline and faith, and only promises to answer what he actually knows.
prasangs.lesson: Readiness matters, and a good teacher only claims what he knows.
prasangs.story_hook: Six seekers arrived with fuel in their hands and questions on their lips, and were told to wait a year.

prasangs.title_en: Sukesha refuses to bluff
prasangs.summary: A prince once asked Sukesha a hard question. Rather than bluff, Sukesha said 'I do not know,' because whoever lies withers to the root. The prince drove off in silence, and Sukesha carried the question to his teacher.
prasangs.lesson: Saying 'I don't know' keeps you honest and keeps you learning.
prasangs.story_hook: A prince pulled up in his chariot and asked Sukesha a question he could not answer.

prasangs.title_en: The graduation address
prasangs.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasangs.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

prasangs.title_en: The measure of joy
prasangs.summary: The Upanishad tries to measure joy: a young, good, strong man owning the whole earth has one unit of human joy, and each higher joy is a hundred times greater, yet each is already held by one free of desire. It ends with the joy before which words turn back, which frees a person from fear and from self-torment over past deeds.
prasangs.lesson: The deepest joy can't be bought, and it frees you from fear and regret.

prasangs.title_en: Bhrigu learns from his father
prasangs.summary: Bhrigu asks his father Varuna to teach him what is ultimate. Varuna gives only a clue and tells him to reflect. Bhrigu comes back four times with answers (food, breath, mind, understanding) and each time is sent back to go deeper, until he discovers that everything is born from joy, lives by joy and returns to joy.
prasangs.lesson: A wise parent lets a child discover the answer instead of handing it over.
prasangs.story_hook: Bhrigu asked his father the biggest question there is, and got only a hint in reply.

prasangs.title_en: Vows of food and hospitality
prasangs.summary: After Bhrigu's discovery come simple household vows: never speak ill of food, never waste it, make it plentiful, and turn no one away from your door.
prasangs.lesson: Respect food and keep your door open.

prasangs.title_en: The three births of a person
prasangs.summary: The Aitareya describes three births: conception and pregnancy, when the mother nourishes the child and must herself be nourished; birth and upbringing, when caring for the child is caring for oneself; and death, when the parent, duties done, departs and the child carries on.
prasangs.lesson: Care for the one who carries and raises the child; raising children continues your life.

prasangs.title_en: Satyakama Jabala, the honest boy
prasangs.summary: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having learned from nature along the way, yet still asks his teacher to teach him.
prasangs.lesson: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.
prasangs.story_hook: Satyakama wanted to study, but first he had to ask his mother a question she could not answer.

prasangs.title_en: The senses argue over who is greatest
prasangs.summary: Speech, sight, hearing and mind each claim to be the most important. Their father says the greatest is the one whose absence hurts the body most. Each leaves for a year and the body manages; when breath starts to leave, all the others are torn loose and beg it to stay.
prasangs.lesson: The quiet one everyone relies on often matters most.
prasangs.story_hook: One day the senses got into an argument about which of them mattered most.

prasangs.title_en: Shvetaketu humbled at the king's court
prasangs.summary: Shvetaketu boasts that his father has taught him everything, then cannot answer a single one of a king's five questions. He runs home and blames his father, who honestly admits he does not know either, and goes to the king himself, refusing wealth and asking only to learn.
prasangs.lesson: A good parent admits what they don't know and goes on learning.
prasangs.story_hook: Shvetaketu walked into the king's assembly sure he knew everything.

prasangs.title_en: Five scholars go to King Ashvapati
prasangs.summary: Five great scholars come to Uddalaka to learn. Knowing he cannot answer everything, he takes them to King Ashvapati instead. The king proudly says his kingdom has no thieves or drunkards and offers gifts, but the scholars politely insist on the purpose they came for.
prasangs.lesson: Point people to someone who knows more, and say plainly what you came for.
prasangs.story_hook: Five of the greatest scholars in the land came to Uddalaka, and he knew he could not answer them all.

prasangs.title_en: Shvetaketu comes home proud
prasangs.summary: After twelve years of study, Shvetaketu returns home at twenty-four full of himself. His father gently asks whether he learned the one thing that makes everything else understood, and the son admits his teachers never taught it.
prasangs.lesson: Learning without humility misses the main thing.
prasangs.story_hook: Shvetaketu came home at twenty-four with every text memorised and his nose in the air.

prasangs.title_en: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
prasangs.summary: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
prasangs.lesson: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

prasangs.title_en: Narada: learned but sad
prasangs.summary: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.
prasangs.lesson: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.
prasangs.story_hook: Narada knew every subject worth knowing, and still came to Sanatkumara feeling sad.

prasangs.title_en: Indra and Virochana with Prajapati
prasangs.summary: Indra of the gods and Virochana of the demons study with Prajapati for 32 years to learn the self. Shown their dressed-up reflections, both leave satisfied; Virochana goes home teaching that the body is everything. Indra stops halfway, sees the flaw, and keeps coming back for 101 years until he learns that the self is not the body.
prasangs.lesson: Don't settle for the first comfortable answer; keep asking until it holds.
prasangs.story_hook: Two rivals, a god and a demon, arrived at Prajapati's door on the same day with the same question.

prasangs.title_en: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasangs.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasangs.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

prasangs.title_en: Maitreyi refuses the inheritance
prasangs.summary: Before leaving home, Yajnavalkya offers to divide his property between his two wives. Maitreyi asks whether all the world's wealth would make her immortal, and when he says no, she asks for what he knows instead. He teaches her that we love husband, wife and children for the self shining in them.
prasangs.lesson: Wealth buys comfort; ask for what lasts.
prasangs.story_hook: Yajnavalkya was leaving home, and he called his wife Maitreyi to divide what he owned.

prasangs.title_en: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court
prasangs.summary: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
prasangs.lesson: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.
prasangs.story_hook: In a hall full of the most learned men in the land, one woman stood up twice.

prasangs.title_en: Janaka asks: what is our light?
prasangs.summary: Yajnavalkya asks the rich, learned King Janaka where he will go when he dies, and the king admits he does not know. Later Janaka asks what light a person lives by: sun, then moon, then fire, then voice, and when all are gone, the self is one's own light.
prasangs.lesson: When every outer light fails, you still have your own.

prasangs.title_en: Yajnavalkya on desire and death
prasangs.summary: Yajnavalkya explains what happens at death with images of a caterpillar and a goldsmith. A person becomes what they desire, will and do; one who knows the self has nothing left to fret about. Know it while you are here, he says, don't brood over many words, and live calm and collected.
prasangs.lesson: You become what you desire and do; know what matters while you are here.

prasangs.title_en: Da Da Da: the voice of thunder
prasangs.summary: Gods, humans and demons finish their studies with their father Prajapati and ask for a parting word. To each he says only 'Da'. The gods hear 'be self-controlled', humans hear 'give', and demons hear 'be compassionate'. The thunder still repeats it.
prasangs.lesson: Each of us hears the lesson we most need: restraint, generosity or compassion.
prasangs.story_hook: When the students asked their father for one last teaching, he gave each of them a single syllable.

prasangs.title_en: Father and son go back to school
prasangs.summary: A patron asks young Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer. He asks his father, who admits he does not know either and suggests they both go to the patron as students. Chitra welcomes Uddalaka for his humility.
prasangs.lesson: A parent who says 'let's learn together' teaches more than any answer.
prasangs.story_hook: When his son came home stumped, Uddalaka did something unusual for a famous teacher.

prasangs.title_en: The father's last gift
prasangs.summary: When a father feels death near, he lies down and his son lies over him, and they exchange words: the father places his speech, breath, sight, hearing, joys and sorrows in the son, and the son receives each one.
prasangs.lesson: Parents pass on far more than property; they pass on themselves.

prasangs.title_en: King Brihadratha's despair
